subject: Fargas Rumblefoot
fact: Fargas Rumblefoot is a halfling adventurer who claims to know the location of a hidden tomb belonging to the half-elf sorcerer Brysis of Khaem, but admits he does not know the precise location—only that it is on the eastern edge of the Darklake. He is under pressure to honor a prior agreement regarding the treasure's location, and his statements are consistent with truthfulness despite ambiguity.
source_quote: In ages past, at the height of Faerûn’s great empires of magic, the half-elf sorcerer Brysis of Khaem was interred in a floating tomb. After the fall of the empire of Netheril and its flying cities, Brysis’s tomb plummeted into a crevasse and wound up in the Underdark, where it has remained for centuries.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a humorous, easily amused party member who finds the names and rituals of the Kuo-toans absurd, yet is motivated by tangible rewards and is quick to negotiate for gold and boats.
source_quote: Grygum mutters, 'Oh great, pit one weird religion against another!'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says the party has temporal needs alongside spiritual ones.
source_quote: “I am all about the spiritual stuff, but the temporal have needs too.”

subject: Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father
fact: Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father is proclaimed as the new god by Bloppblippodd.
source_quote: Bloppblippodd, Ploopploopeen’s daughter, experienced a powerful vision of “Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father,” proclaiming him the new god of her people.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen explains that the Deep Father’s followers make offerings by killing blood sacrifices and casting chum into the Darklake.
source_quote: The followers of the Deep Father have been making an increasing number of offerings on his altar — killing blood sacrifices then casting bloody chum into the waters of the Darklake, where it is consumed by … something.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen explains that the inhabitants of Sloobludop have lived in harmonious service to the will of the Sea Mother for some time.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen explains that the inhabitants of Sloobludop have lived in harmonious service to the will of the Sea Mother for some time.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen explains, 'We are split in two, fighting among ourselves.'
source_quote: We are split in two,' Ploopploopeen explains, 'fighting among ourselves.'

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother.
source_quote: “This is Ploopploopeen, archpriest of the Seamother.”

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says the Sea Mother has answered her prayers.
source_quote: “The Seamother has answered my prayers!”

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says the Sea Mother is the traditional faith of the Kuo-toans and the Deep Father is the real evil.
source_quote: “The Seamother is not a weird religion. It is the traditional faith of the Kuo-toans! It is Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father that is the real evil!”

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen tells Daz not to worry about the number of members in the other faction.
source_quote: “Do not worry yourself about that. All you have to do is distract Bloppblippodd enough. I will take care of her, and my followers will take care of the followers of this false god.”

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen wants to use the party as bait to infiltrate the Deep Father’s cult.
source_quote: “I wish to use you as bait.”

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen will offer them as a 'token of peace and reconciliation' to get closer to the archpriest of the Deep Father — except the adventurers will not be helpless prisoners but infiltrators.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen will offer them as a 'token of peace and reconciliation' to get closer to the archpriest of the Deep Father — except the adventurers will not be helpless prisoners but infiltrators.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: The archpriest of the Sea Mother explains she wants to use them as bait.
source_quote: The archpriest of the Sea Mother explains he wants to use them as bait.

subject: Ploopploopeen, Archpriest of the Sea Mother
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, a traditional Kuo-toan deity, who seeks to use the party as infiltrators to undermine the cult of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father by offering them as 'token of peace' to her daughter Bloppblippodd.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen explains, 'The Seamother has answered my prayers!'

subject: Ploopploopeen, Archpriest of the Sea Mother
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, the traditional faith of the Kuo-toans. She seeks to use the adventurers as infiltrators to disrupt the cult of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father, promising boats, guides, gold, and potions in return.

subject: Sethir
fact: Sethir is a cautious, questioning member of the party who wonders whether to continue engaging with the Kuo-toans, reflecting the group’s uncertainty about their role in this escalating conflict.
source_quote: Sethir mutters, 'Should we continue?'

subject: Sethir
fact: Sethir mutters whether the group should continue.
source_quote: Sethir mutters, “Should we continue?”

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar says the Sea Mother is an old god and the Deep Father is who they should fight against.
source_quote: “No, no, no. The Sea Mother is an old god, the Deep Father, that is who we should fight against. The Deep Mother demands humanoid sacrifices, not the Sea Mother.”

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar sighs and questions why the ambush occurred.
source_quote: Shuushar sighs, “Such an unnecessary battle. Why would this be happening?”

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar suggests talking to Bloppblippodd before taking action.
source_quote: “Perhaps we should talk to his daughter before we take action? I have learned that one must open themselves to all points of view and then only then make decisions and judgments.”

subject: Shuushar the Awakened
fact: Shuushar the Awakened is a Kuo-toan monitor who has experienced enlightenment and now serves as a guide and moral compass for the party, advocating for understanding over violence and emphasizing the legitimacy of the Sea Mother as the traditional faith.
source_quote: Shuushar sighs, 'Such an unnecessary battle. Why would this be happening?'

subject: Shuushar the Awakened
fact: Shuushar the Awakened is a Kuo-toan monitor who provides structured organization over Kuo-toan groups and believes in opening oneself to all points of view before making judgments. He is deeply devoted to the Sea Mother and opposes the Deep Father cult.

subject: Shuushar the Awakened
fact: Shuushar the Awakened says ‘Yes’ to continuing.
source_quote: “Yes,” the Shuushar the Awakened says.

subject: Shuushar the Awakened
fact: Shuushar the Awakened says, 'Yes.'
source_quote: Yes, the Shuushar the Awakened says.

subject: Topsy
fact: Topsy asks if the kuo-toan problems are the party’s concern.
source_quote: “I hear about your problems, and that sounds like a you problem, not like a me problem. What can we help with you?”

subject: Topsy
fact: Topsy is a disengaged, cynical party member who sees the Kuo-toan conflict as a 'you problem' and questions the party’s involvement, reflecting a detached, survivalist attitude.
source_quote: Topsy asks, 'I hear about your problems, and that sounds like a you problem, not like a me problem. What can we help with you?'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a results-oriented member of the party who focuses on material compensation, pressing the archpriest for rewards and showing little interest in theological debates.
source_quote: Zalthir shouts to the archpriest, 'You said reward?'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir looks at Ploopploopeen unimpressed when she offers to use them as bait.
source_quote: Zalthir looks at her, unimpressed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir shouts to the archpriest to confirm the reward.
source_quote: Zalthir shouts to the archpriest, “You said reward?”

subject: 500 gold
fact: Ploopploopeen promises 500 gold as a reward for the party’s aid.
source_quote: The archpriest promises 500 gold and two potions of healing.

subject: Bloody chum
fact: Bloody chum is the sacrificial residue from the Deep Father cult’s blood offerings, cast into the Darklake. It is consumed by an unknown entity, suggesting a deeper, possibly primordial, connection to Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.

subject: guides to navigate the Darklake
fact: Ploopploopeen offers guides to navigate the Darklake as part of the reward.
source_quote: “Two boats and guides to navigate the Darklake?”

subject: hand-held crossbows
fact: A collection of hand-held crossbows, combined with a united team, can create a powerful enough force to take down a formidable group of enemies.
source_quote: a collection of hand-held crossbows, combined with a united team, can create a powerful enough force to take down even a formidable group of enemies.

subject: Hand-held Crossbows
fact: Hand-held crossbows, when used in coordinated formation by a united team, can generate enough force to take down formidable groups of enemies, suggesting tactical synergy over brute strength.
source_quote: In the end, they realize that a collection of hand-held crossbows, combined with a united team, can create a powerful enough force to take down even a formidable group of enemies.

subject: liquid from kuo-toan bodies
fact: Only the application of strength can free a weapon from the liquid glue.
source_quote: Only the application of strength can from a weapon from the glue.

subject: liquid from kuo-toan bodies
fact: The body of the kuo-toans releases a liquid that causes any melee weapon to stick to their bodies.
source_quote: the body of the Kuo-toans releases a particular liquid that causes any melee weapon to stick to their bodies.

subject: Potions of Healing
fact: Two potions of healing are offered by Ploopploopeen as part of the reward package, indicating the party’s anticipated exposure to combat and injury during the infiltration mission.
source_quote: The archpriest promises 500 gold and two potions of healing.

subject: two boats
fact: Ploopploopeen offers two boats as part of the reward after the party is unimpressed with the initial offer.
source_quote: “Two boats and guides to navigate the Darklake?”

subject: Two Boats and Guides
fact: Two boats and experienced guides to navigate the Darklake are offered as part of the reward, essential for the party’s movement through the Kuo-toan-controlled waterways and their infiltration of the Deep Father’s stronghold.
source_quote: 'Two boats and guides to navigate the Darklake?' The escapees nod in agreement.

subject: two potions of healing
fact: Ploopploopeen promises two potions of healing as a reward for the party’s aid.
source_quote: The archpriest promises 500 gold and two potions of healing.

subject: reward offer
fact: The archpriest promises 500 gold and two potions of healing, then adds two boats and guides to navigate the Darklake.
source_quote: The archpriest promises 500 gold and two potions of healing. But she sees how they are unimpressed, “Two boats and guides to navigate the Darklake?”

subject: Bloppblippodd’s Vision
fact: The source and validity of Bloppblippodd’s vision of Leemooggoogoon are unknown — was it divine revelation, psychic trauma, or manipulation by an external force? The party may need to confront her directly to uncover the truth.
source_quote: She has backed up her claims with a tremendous increase in magical power, and new followers have flocked to her.

subject: disruption of rituals
fact: Ploopploopeen wants the party to disrupt the upstart faction’s rituals so her true believers can cut off the head of the cult.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen wants them to disrupt the upstart faction’s rituals, allowing his true believers of the Sea Mother to cut off the head of the cult.

subject: infiltration plan
fact: Ploopploopeen plans to use the party as infiltrators disguised as sacrifices to disrupt the Deep Father’s rituals.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen will offer them as a “token of peace and reconciliation” to get closer to the archpriest of the Deep Father — except the adventurers will not be helpless prisoners but infiltrators.

subject: Ploopploopeen's daughter Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd's vision of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father and her claim of new divine authority are unresolved and central to the factional conflict.
source_quote: A few weeks ago, Bloppblippodd, Ploopploopeen’s daughter, experienced a powerful vision of 'Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father,' proclaiming him the new god of her people. She has backed up her claims with a tremendous increase in magical power, and new followers have flocked to her.

subject: Shuushar’s Philosophical Droning
fact: Shuushar’s tendency to speak at length about openness, perspective, and judgment may delay decisive action — the party must decide whether his wisdom is vital or a dangerous distraction.
source_quote: Shuushar continues to drone on but thankfully walks away.

subject: Shuushar’s transformation
fact: Shuushar has shifted from a monitor focused on control to a seeker of understanding. His growing openness to Bloppblippodd’s perspective may signal a deeper internal conflict or a hidden connection to the Deep Father cult.

subject: The Daughter’s Loyalty
fact: It is unclear whether Bloppblippodd is truly devoted to Leemooggoogoon or is being manipulated — the party may need to confront her directly to determine if she is a zealot, a pawn, or a victim.
source_quote: She has backed up her claims with a tremendous increase in magical power.

subject: The Deep Father’s True Nature
fact: The origin and nature of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father remain unclear — whether a false god, a primordial entity, or a corrupted manifestation — and the party must determine if the cult is truly evil or merely a new evolution of faith.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen says, 'It is Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father that is the real evil!'

subject: The Deep Father's true nature
fact: The origin and true nature of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father remain mysterious. His emergence coincides with Bloppblippodd’s vision and surge in magical power, raising questions about whether he is a genuine deity, a corrupted entity, or a manifestation of collective madness.

subject: The entity in the Darklake
fact: Something consumes the bloody chum cast into the Darklake. Its identity and allegiance are unknown—whether it serves the Deep Father, is an ancient force awakened by the cult, or is a trick of perception.

subject: The identity of the entity consuming the bloody chum
fact: The entity consuming the bloody chum in the Darklake is unspecified and mysterious.
source_quote: The followers of the Deep Father have been making an increasing number of offerings on his altar — killing blood sacrifices then casting bloody chum into the waters of the Darklake, where it is consumed by … something.

subject: The Party’s Role as Infiltrators
fact: The party has been offered as bait by Ploopploopeen to infiltrate the Deep Father cult — their success or failure may determine the balance of power among the Kuo-toans, and their moral alignment may be tested by becoming tools of religious warfare.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen will offer them as a 'token of peace and reconciliation' to get closer to the archpriest of the Deep Father — except the adventurers will not be helpless prisoners but infiltrators.

subject: The Sea Mother’s silence
fact: Despite Ploopploopeen’s claims of divine favor, the Sea Mother has not directly intervened in the schism. This raises doubt about whether her power is fading, or if she is testing her followers through conflict.

subject: The Unseen Consumer in the Darklake
fact: Something unseen consumes the bloody chum cast into the Darklake — a possible avatar of Leemooggoogoon, a primordial entity, or a trapped god — whose nature may hold the key to ending the schism.
source_quote: …where it is consumed by … something.

subject: 1st day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493
fact: The day the escapees arrive in Sloobludop, observe its structure, meet Ploop and Gloog, discover the altars, and begin to understand the religious conflict. The journey ends, and the confrontation begins.
source_quote: 1st day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: 1st day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493
fact: The events of the chapter occur on the first day of the third tenday of Taraskh in the year 1493, marking the beginning of the escapees' involvement in the kuo-toan religious conflict.
source_quote: 1st day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493
fact: The day the Kuo-toan monitor arrives to escort the escapees to the Deep Father’s altar, marking the formal escalation of the conflict and the beginning of the planned confrontation.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493
fact: The events occurred on the 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh, 1493, marking the timeline of the factional conflict and ritual escort.
source_quote: ### 2nd day of the 3rd   Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The session continues on the 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 3rd   Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: Acceptance of Ploop’s Offer
fact: After eating cooked fish and witnessing the rituals, the escapees, including Zalthir, accept Ploop’s offer to remain in Sloobludop and participate in the ritual exchange, abandoning their initial reluctance.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea.

subject: acceptance of Ploop’s offer
fact: The group, including Zalthir, accepts Ploop’s offer after witnessing their customs, eating cooked fish, and being reassured by Gloog’s honor-bound approach.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea... Zalthir is satisfied.

subject: Arrival at Sloobludop
fact: The escapees arrive at Sloobludop after an uneventful journey through tunnels. They are greeted by Kuo-toan sentinels who let them through the walls. They observe the village layout, the two altars, and the strange behaviors of the inhabitants. They are invited into Ploop’s quarters and begin to understand the religious conflict.
source_quote: They snap to attention when Ploop arrives and lets everyone through.

subject: arrival of the monitor and kuo-toa delegation
fact: Twelve kuo-toa led by a monitor arrive at Ploop’s quarters to escort him, his whip, and the prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: attempt to observe the Deep Father’s altar
fact: The escapees sneak to observe the altar of Leemooggoogoon but make noise, alerting the kuo-toans circling the idol and forcing a hasty retreat.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice. 'I say we beat a hasty retreat,' whispers Thorin. 'These guys are spooky. Let’s get out of here,' mutters Zalthir.

subject: combat protocol
fact: You will help us as you, too, see the righteousness of the Deep Mother. But you won’t throw the first punch.
source_quote: You will help us as you, too, see the righteousness of the Deep Mother. No, that would insult the honor of my father and our people. This is our problem, and we must resolve it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz shouts, "We must eat!"
source_quote: We must eat!” he shouts.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz sighs, "Man, we’ve been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing. We busted out of prison, and then what? Ran. We’re being chased, and we keep running. One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing."
source_quote: Daz sighs, "Man, we’ve been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing. We busted out of prison, and then what? Ran. We’re being chased, and we keep running. One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, overcome by the rank smell, has his hand over his mouth and tries to rub the smell out of his nose with his thumb.
source_quote: Daz, overcome by the rank smell, has his hand over his mouth and tries to rub the smell out of his nose with his thumb.

subject: Daz covering his nose from the stench
fact: Daz, overcome by the rank smell of the Sea Mother’s altar, covers his mouth and rubs his nose with his thumb, pretending it is itchy while Ploop watches and smiles weakly.
source_quote: Meanwhile, Daz, overcome by the rank smell, has his hand over his mouth and tries to rub the smell out of his nose with his thumb. Ploop looks at him, and he smiles weakly as he pretends his nose is itchy.

subject: Daz shouting 'We must eat!'
fact: Daz, overwhelmed by the smell and seeking purpose, shouts 'We must eat!' prompting Ploop to reassure them that Kuo-Toans eat cooked fish.
source_quote: "We must eat!" he shouts. Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food, but Ploop, perhaps sensing that, assures him that Kuo Toans eat cooked fish.

subject: Discovery at the Deep Father's Altar
fact: Grygum and the escapees sneak to the altar of Leemooggoogoon and are discovered by the circling kuo-toans. Their attempt at stealth fails, triggering a hostile reaction and forcing a retreat.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice.

subject: Discovery of the Deep Father Altar
fact: The escapees sneak to the Deep Father’s altar, attempting to observe quietly, but are detected. They flee back to Ploop’s house, realizing the danger posed by Bloppblippodd’s followers. This event triggers Gloog’s intervention and the plan to confront the faction.
source_quote: Unfortunately, their attempt to be quiet is anything but. And the kuo-toans circling the Deep Father notice.

subject: Escapees
fact: The escapees notice that many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping.
source_quote: At this point, the escapees notice that many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping.

subject: Escapees
fact: The escapees notice that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.
source_quote: And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Escapees
fact: The escapees sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.
source_quote: they sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.

subject: Escapees
fact: They ignore the Kuo-Toan who stares at them, uncertain if he is awake or asleep.
source_quote: Uncertain if he is awake or asleep, they ignore him.

subject: escort to Deep Father’s archpriest
fact: The archpriest of the Sea Mother, his whip, and prisoners were escorted by a kuo-toa monitor and twelve kuo-toa to meet the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog mutters, "You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd."
source_quote: Gloog is about to sleep, he mutters, "You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog says, "Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority."
source_quote: Gloog burps, "Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog says, "My name is Glooglugogg. Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways. Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness."
source_quote: He says, "My name is Glooglugogg. Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways. Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog says, "No, that would insult the honor of my father and our people. This is our problem, and we must resolve it."
source_quote: Gloog looks at him, "No, that would insult the honor of my father and our people. This is our problem, and we must resolve it."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog says, "Now get rest. In a while, we will have to fight."
source_quote: Gloog turns to him, "Now get rest. In a while, we will have to fight."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog says, "Of course not. You will help us as you, too, see the righteousness of the Deep Mother."
source_quote: Gloog looks at him, "Of course not. You will help us as you, too, see the righteousness of the Deep Mother."

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Gloog’s dislike for his sister becomes increasingly apparent as he enumerates her ills and flaws as a sister, daughter, and former cleric of the Sea Mother.
source_quote: Gloog’s dislike for his sister becomes increasingly apparent as he enumerates her ills and flaws as a sister, daughter, and former cleric of the Sea Mother.

subject: Gloog’s comment on the derro
fact: Gloog remarks that the escapees did not choose to give the Kuo-Toans the derro they tied up, which he finds both honorable and odd.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Gloog’s refusal of first strike
fact: Gloog insists that the escapees will not throw the first punch, as it would insult the honor of his father and people, and that the conflict must be resolved by the Kuo-Toans themselves.
source_quote: No, that would insult the honor of my father and our people. This is our problem, and we must resolve it.

subject: Gloog’s Revelation
fact: Gloog approaches the escapees after they return to Ploop’s house. He reveals his opposition to his sister, explains the political instability in the village, and outlines a plan to resolve the conflict without the escapees striking first. He validates their respect for the Sea Mother and demands they assist in restoring order.
source_quote: I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother...

subject: Gloog’s revelation of internal conflict
fact: Gloog reveals that his sister Bloppblippodd has been given too much deference, has fallen prey to madness, and that the village is divided, requiring immediate action before their support fades.
source_quote: Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness... Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority.

subject: group’s acceptance of the Kuo-Toan cause
fact: The group, previously skeptical, accepts Ploop’s offer after witnessing rituals, eating cooked food, and hearing Gloog’s honorable stance on conflict resolution.
source_quote: At this, even Zalthir is convinced that perhaps helping the Kuo-Toans isn’t a bad idea... Zalthir is satisfied.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that the sacrifice is essential, not the provenance.
source_quote: in the rituals of Leemooggoogoon, the sacrifice is essential, not the provenance.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, "This is like a flag of parley. Have you considered a white flag?"
source_quote: Grygum finally understands, "This is like a flag of parley. Have you considered a white flag?"

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, "Yes, our rituals are different."
source_quote: Grygum nods, "Yes, our rituals are different."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tries to probe if the sacrifice must be willing.
source_quote: Grygum tries to probe if the sacrifice must be willing.

subject: kuo-toan movement
fact: Some kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.
source_quote: some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish

subject: kuo-toan sleep behavior
fact: Many kuo-toans walk around with their eyes open, sleeping.
source_quote: many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping

subject: Kuo-toan Sleep Behavior
fact: The escapees observe that many kuo-toans sleep with their eyes open and some move as if in schools of fish. This unusual behavior is normal for their species and contributes to their eerie, alien presence.
source_quote: At this point, the escapees notice that many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Kuo-toans sleeping with eyes open
fact: The escapees notice that many kuo-toans walk around with their eyes open while sleeping, and some move about as schools of fish.
source_quote: At this point, the escapees notice that many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Morning Confrontation
fact: On the second day, a Kuo-toan monitor arrives at Ploop’s quarters with twelve followers, demanding the escapees accompany them to the Deep Father’s altar. This signals the formal beginning of the confrontation between the two factions, and the escapees are now directly involved in the conflict.
source_quote: Twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters.

subject: Ploop

subject: Bloppblippodd’s Cult
fact: Bloppblippodd leads a splinter faction that has abandoned the ways of the Sea Mother, embraced madness, and retains only a few hard-core supporters.
source_quote: Her hard-core supporters are few, but how many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown.

subject: Followers of Leemooggoogoon
fact: The followers of Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, worship a deity requiring blood sacrifices, preferably unwilling ones. Their idol is a stretched hide of a manta ray with pinned octopuses and a stained altar. They circle the idol in vigil and react violently to intrusions.
source_quote: She needs sacrifices for her false god. An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god.

subject: Followers of the Deep Father
fact: The followers of the Deep Father worship an idol of a manta ray made from hide, with pinned octopuses and a bloodstained altar. They demand unwilling sacrifices and are led by Bloppblippodd. Their numbers are uncertain, but they are a growing threat. Their practices are considered madness by Gloog and others.
source_quote: The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Followers of the Sea Mother
fact: The followers of the Sea Mother revere a scavenger goddess whose altar is adorned with severed crayfish parts, shells, mushrooms, and rotting fish. They believe the perfect offering is regurgitation. Ploopploopeen leads them, and they are the majority in the village. They are seen as traditionalists by Gloog.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Followers of the Sea Mother
fact: The followers of the Sea Mother worship a scavenger goddess who accepts regurgitated offerings. Their central idol is a wooden humanoid female adorned with the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed with gut and piled with shells, stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish. Four kuo-toans guard it constantly.
source_quote: The Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Kuo-toans
fact: The Kuo-toans are a society living between two walls of netting, with a cave wall to the south and the Darklake to the north. They sleep with eyes open, move in schools, and maintain order through designated leaders. Their religion centers on the Sea Mother and Leemooggoogoon, with rituals involving spit-offerings, blood sacrifices, and the use of severed body parts in idols.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Kuo-toan Society
fact: Kuo-toan society is fractured between followers of the Sea Mother and the Deep Father, with Bloppblippodd’s faction threatening collapse. The people sleep while standing, move in schools of fish, and revere idols made from severed body parts. Leadership is maintained by monitors who prevent madness from destroying social order. Rituals involve blood, rot, and unwilling sacrifices, and the existence of their gods is ambiguous.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: The Deep Mother's Followers
fact: The faction loyal to the Deep Mother, including Gloog and his allies, holds the support of the majority in the village and opposes the madness of Bloppblippodd’s followers.
source_quote: How many in the village are on our side? Her side is unknown. This is why it must be dealt with now. While we still have the support of the majority.

subject: Altar of Leemooggoogoon
fact: The altar of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father consists of a large hide stretched between two poles in the shape of a manta ray, with a dead splayed-out manta ray pinned to its center, two dead octopuses draped across the top with tentacles pinned and heads tied together and painted red and blue, reeking of decay and stained dark with blood.
source_quote: They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father. It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles. A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments. The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Altar of the Deep Father
fact: The Altar of the Deep Father is a hide stretched between poles, shaped like a manta ray, with a dead manta ray pinned in the center and two dead octopuses draped across it. The altar is stained dark with blood and reeks of decay. It is surrounded by worshippers who chant and bow, and is guarded by a dozen followers of Bloppblippodd.
source_quote: The idol reeks of decay and the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: Altar of the Sea Mother
fact: The Altar of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden statue of a humanoid female, with a severed giant albino crayfish head and claws lashed on with gut. It emits a powerful stench of rotting shellfish and is piled with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish. It is guarded by four alert Kuo-toans and worshipped by many villagers.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish.

subject: Altar of the Sea Mother
fact: The altar of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden statue of a humanoid female, with its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed on with gut strands and emitting a rotting shellfish stench, with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish piled at its feet and strung around its neck.
source_quote: Ploop stops in front of the sizeable nine-foot-tall statue. The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish. Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: Darklake
fact: The Darklake borders the northern edge of Sloobludop, with docks and some boats. It is a source of food and transportation, but also a place of mystery and danger. The water is associated with the Deep Father’s cult and the unnatural movement of Kuo-toans who swim in schools.
source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty.

subject: Darklake
fact: The Darklake is a body of water bordering the northern edge of Sloobludop. It features docks with boats, some occupied, some empty. Groups of kuo-toan leaders walk along its shore, maintaining societal order.
source_quote: The Darklake side has docks. Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty. Walking along the docks are groups of Kuo-Toans.

subject: Guardians of the Deep Father's Altar

subject: Guardians of the Sea Mother's Altar
fact: Four stern kuo-toans slowly circle the Sea Mother's altar, alert and on guard. They are part of the cult's permanent vigil and react to any disturbance near the idol.
source_quote: Four stern kuo-toa slowly circle the statue, alert and on guard...

subject: Kuo-toa
fact: Twelve kuo-toa accompanied their monitor to Ploopploopeen’s quarters as part of a formal escort mission to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters.

subject: Kuo-toa Monitor
fact: A kuo-toa monitor led twelve kuo-toa to Ploopploopeen’s quarters and was admitted by the archpriest of the Sea Mother to escort him, his whip, and the prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Kuo-toan Guardians
fact: Four stern Kuo-toans slowly circle the Sea Mother’s statue, alert and on guard. Others move about, bowing and chanting. They are not ordinary worshippers but specialized sentinels, likely trained to protect sacred sites. Their behavior is unnatural and deeply unsettling to the escapees.
source_quote: Four stern kuo-toa slowly circle the statue, alert and on guard, while a few others move about, gazing up at the statue and bowing repeatedly while chanting.

subject: Kuo-toan Monitor
fact: A Kuo-toan monitor arrives at Ploopploopeen’s quarters with twelve followers, signaling formal authority. Monitors are responsible for maintaining order and preventing societal collapse from madness. This monitor is acting on behalf of the Deep Father’s leadership and has come to escort the escapees to the altar of Leemooggoogoon.
source_quote: Twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is Gloog’s sister; she has been granted excessive deference by their father, has fallen prey to madness, and shows no respect for their society’s ways.
source_quote: Our society is torn to pieces by my sister Bloppblippodd. Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much. She has no respect for our ways. And she has fallen prey to this madness.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father and Ploopploopeen’s daughter, whose relationship with her father is strained and whose devotion to the Deep Father is questioned.
source_quote: My daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father and daughter of Ploopploopeen. She demands offerings for her deity and is the catalyst for the planned attack on the escapees. Her relationship with her father is troubled.
source_quote: In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd is the high priestess of the Deep Father, Ploopploopeen’s daughter, who has fallen into madness and is seen as a threat to Kuo-toan society. She demands sacrifices for her false god, insists on unwilling offerings, and has amassed a faction of followers. Her relationship with her father is strained and unclear, and her existence as a legitimate cleric is questioned.
source_quote: She needs sacrifices for her false god.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an escapee who finds purpose in helping the Kuo-toans after a long history of running and loss. He is repulsed by the stench of the altars but pretends to be itchy to hide his discomfort. He is moved by the idea of having a goal after prison and death.
source_quote: Man, we've been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an escapee who finds purpose in helping the Kuo-toans after years of running and loss. He is repulsed by the stench of the Sea Mother’s altar but pretends it’s an itch. He shouts for food, is convinced by the promise of cooked fish, and sees the conflict as a meaningful end to their despair.
source_quote: Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz, having escaped prison and witnessed the death of a group member, finds purpose in helping the Kuo-Toans and declares that having something to focus on is less depressing than running.
source_quote: Man, we’ve been running for days. Having a purpose in life is a good thing. We busted out of prison, and then what? Ran. We’re being chased, and we keep running. One of our group got killed by another of our group. Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: Deep Father
fact: The Deep Father is the deity of Bloppblippodd, worshipped with a manta-ray hide idol and blood-stained altar, and is contrasted with the Sea Mother’s scavenger nature.
source_quote: The idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father... She has fallen prey to this madness.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg is known as Gloog to his friends; he disapproves of his father's decision to allow outsiders to meddle in their affairs, but acknowledges the party's respect for the Sea Mother and their understanding of their ways.
source_quote: Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg, called Gloog, is a Kuo-toan who disapproves of his sister Bloppblippodd’s rule and believes she has corrupted their traditions. He supports the escapees’ involvement in resolving the conflict, insists on honor-bound action without the first punch, and acknowledges the group’s respect for the Sea Mother. He is uncertain whether the escapees chose to spare the derro they captured.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Glooglugogg
fact: Glooglugogg, who goes by Gloog, is a kuo-toan who disapproves of his sister Bloppblippodd’s actions and believes she has fallen prey to madness and disrespect for their ways.
source_quote: My name is Glooglugogg. Gloog is what my friends call me. I do not approve of Father’s choice to have outsiders meddle in our affairs, but you showed respect to the Sea Mother, and thus, I see that you respect and understand our ways.

subject: Glooglugogg's Father
fact: Gloog’s father is the patriarch who has shown excessive deference to Bloppblippodd, enabling her descent into madness and fracturing their society.
source_quote: Father has shown her too much deference, offered her too much, and let her get away with too much.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an escapee who recalls lore about the Deep Sea Mother and understands that regurgitation is a sacred offering. He spits on the altar, gains Ploop’s trust, and helps the group navigate Kuo-toan customs. He wonders what Ploop has heard and is aware of the ambiguity surrounding Leemooggoogoon’s existence.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is one of the escapees who begins to understand Kuo-toan rituals and misconceptions. He recognizes the altar of the Sea Mother as a scavenger deity and participates in the spit-offering. He is skeptical of Leemooggoogoon's existence and attempts to negotiate peace with symbols of parley.
source_quote: This is like a flag of parley. Have you considered a white flag?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalls that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is the perfect form of offering, and he spits on the altar to demonstrate respect.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering. Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understands that this is like a flag of parley.
source_quote: Grygum finally understands, "This is like a flag of parley."

subject: Kuo-toan monitor
fact: The kuo-toan monitor leads twelve kuo-toa to Ploopploopeen’s quarters and is admitted to oversee the transfer of prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: In the morning, twelve kuo-toa led by a kuo-toa monitor arrive at Ploopploopeen’s quarters. The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Leemooggoogoon
fact: Leemooggoogoon is the Deep Father, a deity whose existence is questioned by Zalthir, worshipped by Bloppblippodd, and whose altar is marked by a manta-ray hide idol stained with blood.
source_quote: It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists... They sneak out just close enough to see the idol of Leemooggoogoon the Deep Father.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother who has been ordered to accompany the monitor, his whip, and prisoners to the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother who stares unblinkingly at the escapees and realizes the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen, the archpriest of the Sea Mother, stares unblinkingly at the escapees.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, currently hosting the escapees in Sloobludop and attempting to broker a ritual exchange with the followers of Leemooggoogoon. He has strained relations with his daughter, Bloppblippodd, and is uncertain whether Leemooggoogoon actually exists.
source_quote: I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen is the archpriest of the Sea Mother, who seeks to mediate between his people and outsiders, but struggles with communication and familial tension with his daughter Bloppblippodd. He believes offerings to the Sea Mother require regurgitation and spitting, and he is delighted when Grygum and Thorin comply. He sleeps standing and is observed walking outside while asleep.
source_quote: Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen realizes that the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.
source_quote: Ploopploopeen realizes that the Tongues spell didn’t translate his intent as well as he would like.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god."
source_quote: No. An unwilling sacrifice is better. This is an evil god.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "I tried that, but she didn’t bite. She needs sacrifices for her false god."
source_quote: I tried that, but she didn’t bite. She needs sacrifices for her false god.

subject: Ploopploopeen
fact: Ploopploopeen says, "You will arrive in Sloobludop and stay in my quarters. I will send message to the followers of Leemooggoogoon that I have an offering for him. In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering. I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack. Your role in this will be over."
source_quote: No, this is wrong. You will arrive in Sloobludop and stay in my quarters. I will send message to the followers of Leemooggoogoon that I have an offering for him. In the morning, my daughter, Bloppblippodd, the high priestess of the Deep Father, will demand to see the offering. I will present you to her, and I will insist that I come with you. She will accept. And then all of my followers will attack. Your role in this will be over.

subject: Sea Mother
fact: The Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess whose statue is made of wood and severed giant albino crayfish parts, and whose worship includes spitting and regurgitation as offerings.
source_quote: Grygum recalls from somewhere that the Deep Sea Mother is a scavenger goddess and that regurgitating and spitting on her altar is perhaps the perfect form of offering.

subject: Shuushar
fact: Shuushar is referenced as having explained that the Kuo-Toans walking along the docks are leader types responsible for ensuring the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.
source_quote: These leader types that Shuushar explained are responsible for ensuring that the madness of the Kuo-Toans doesn’t rip the society apart.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an escapee who questions the effectiveness of Kuo-toan defenses and is wary of their food. He spits on the Sea Mother’s altar and is concerned about the nature of sacrifices. He is the first to suggest retreat when discovered at the Deep Father’s altar.
source_quote: I say we beat a hasty retreat.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an escapee who questions the effectiveness of Kuo-toan defenses, worries about food, and observes the unnatural behaviors of the Kuo-toans. He spits on the altar, is convinced by the promise of cooked fish, and later suggests retreat when the Deep Father’s altar is discovered.
source_quote: Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food, but Ploop... assures him that Kuo Toans eat cooked fish.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is wary of raw rotting food, questions the effectiveness of nEttin g walls, and participates in spitting on the Sea Mother’s altar.
source_quote: Thorin is worried that this will be some raw rotting food... Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader... Ploop is delighted when Grygum and Thorin both spit on the altar.

subject: Topsy and Turvy
fact: Topsy and Turvy are escapees who recognize the chaos of the situation as an opportunity for theft. They are not directly involved in ritual discussions but are attuned to the potential for looting.
source_quote: A free-for-all is an excellent opportunity to steal.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a member of the party who seeks clarification on their role in the conflict; he is satisfied after learning they will assist without initiating violence.
source_quote: So when we go there, our job is just to sit around and do nothing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an escapee initially indifferent to the Kuo-toans' plight, seeing their conflicts as irrelevant. He is skeptical of their rituals but is eventually convinced by the promise of cooked fish and the group's acceptance of Ploop's offer.
source_quote: They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an escapee who initially sees no value in helping the Kuo-toans, questions his role repeatedly, and seeks clarity on whether he must fight. He is swayed by the promise of cooked food and the honor-bound nature of Gloog’s plan, and he is wary of the supernatural behaviors of the Kuo-toans.
source_quote: So when we go there, our job is just to sit around and do nothing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is skeptical of the Kuo-Toans’ cause, questions the existence of Leemooggoogoon, and initially sees no value in helping them until convinced by their customs.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why they should bother. They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern... It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

subject: altar condition
fact: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.
source_quote: the broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood

subject: blood-stained altar
fact: The broad stone altar below the idol of Leemooggoogoon is stained dark with blood, indicating frequent ritual use.
source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: blood-stained stone altar
fact: The broad stone altar beneath the Deep Father’s idol is stained dark with blood, indicating violent ritual practices.
source_quote: The broad stone altar below the idol is stained dark with blood.

subject: dead manta ray
fact: The dead manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide on the altar of Leemooggoogoon, forming the core of the idol.
source_quote: A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide.

subject: dead octopuses
fact: Two dead octopuses are draped across the top of the Leemooggoogoon idol, their tentacles pinned and artfully arranged, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.
source_quote: Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: Deep Father Idol
fact: The Deep Father idol is a hide stretched between poles in the shape of a manta ray, with a dead manta ray pinned to its center and two dead octopuses draped across it, their heads painted and tied together. It is stained with blood and emits a foul odor. It is the central object of worship for Bloppblippodd’s faction.
source_quote: It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles.

subject: docks condition
fact: Some of the docks have boats; some are empty.
source_quote: Some of the docks have boats. Some are empty

subject: dried vegetable matter
fact: The ceilings of homes in Sloobludop are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter, a material common to all dwellings in the village.
source_quote: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: gut strands
fact: Gut strands are used to lash the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish onto the statue of the Sea Mother, contributing to its overpowering stench.
source_quote: These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish.

subject: gut-strung garlands
fact: Garlands of gut hold shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish around the neck of the Sea Mother’s statue.
source_quote: Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: house materials
fact: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.
source_quote: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter

subject: idol dimensions
fact: The idol of Leemooggoogoon consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles.
source_quote: It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles

subject: idol offerings
fact: A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.
source_quote: A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments

subject: idol stench
fact: The idol reeks of decay.
source_quote: The idol reeks of decay

subject: Leemooggoogoon's Idol
fact: The idol of Leemooggoogoon is a hide stretched on cords between two poles, shaped like a manta ray. It is pinned with a dead manta ray and two dead octopuses, their tentacles artfully arranged and their heads painted red and blue. The altar below is stained with blood.
source_quote: It consists of a large hide cut roughly in the shape of a manta ray and stretched out on cords between two support poles. A dead, splayed-out manta ray is pinned to the center of the hide. Two dead octopuses are draped across the top, their tentacles pinned and artfully arrayed, their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: nEttin g
fact: nEttin g is a material used to construct walls in Sloobludop, described as ineffective against determined invaders, and guarded by Kuo-toans who snap to attention when Ploop arrives.
source_quote: There is a wall made of nEttin g guarded by Kuo-toans... Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader.

subject: N-Ettin Wall
fact: The western entrance to Sloobludop is guarded by a wall made of n-Ettin g, which Thorin notes is ineffective against a determined invader. It is manned by kuo-toans who snap to attention upon Ploop’s arrival.
source_quote: There is a wall made of nEttin g guarded by Kuo-toans. Thorin notes that the nEttin g isn’t an effective wall against a determined invader.

subject: Net Wall
fact: The eastern boundary of Sloobludop is a second wall of nets, separating the village from the Deep Father’s altar. It is part of the ritual geography of the town and likely serves both defensive and symbolic purposes.
source_quote: Past the walls are the huts of the kuo-toans, and at the other end of the town, almost 500 feet away, is another wall of nets.

subject: red and blue pigments
fact: Red and blue pigments are used to paint the heads of the two dead octopuses on the altar of Leemooggoogoon, artfully arrayed and tied together.
source_quote: Their heads tied together and painted with red and blue pigments.

subject: Sea Mother's Idol
fact: The idol of the Sea Mother is a nine-foot-tall wooden humanoid statue, its head and forearms composed of the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, bound with gut. It is decorated with brightly colored stones, mushrooms, shells, and rotting fish in garlands and piles.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut and emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish. Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.

subject: Sea Mother Statue
fact: The Sea Mother statue is a nine-foot-tall wooden idol carved in the shape of a humanoid female, with severed crayfish head and claws lashed on with gut. It emits a foul stench and is adorned with shells, colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish. It is the central object of worship for the Sea Mother’s followers.
source_quote: The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female, its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Sea Mother altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck

subject: statue dimensions
fact: The statue of the Deep Sea Mother is roughly nine feet tall, carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female.
source_quote: the sizeable nine-foot-tall statue. The statue is roughly carved from wood in the shape of a humanoid female

subject: statue materials
fact: The statue's head and forearms are formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish, lashed on with strands of gut.
source_quote: its head and forearms formed from the severed head and claws of a giant albino crayfish. These parts are lashed on with strands of gut

subject: statue offerings
fact: Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck.
source_quote: Shells, brightly colored stones, mushrooms, and rotting fish are piled at the statue’s feet and strung in garlands around its neck

subject: statue size
fact: The statue is sizeable and nine feet tall.
source_quote: the sizeable nine-foot-tall statue

subject: statue stench
fact: The statue emits an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish.
source_quote: emit an overpowering stench of rotting shellfish

subject: the whip
fact: The whip carried by the archpriest of the Sea Mother is being taken with him on the escort to the archpriest of the Deep Father, suggesting ceremonial or punitive significance.
source_quote: he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: unidentified dried vegetable matter
fact: This material is used for ceilings in all homes in Sloobludop, and its nature remains unknown to the escapees.
source_quote: Each home has mud walls, and the ceilings are made from an unidentified dried vegetable matter.

subject: whip
fact: The whip is carried by the archpriest of the Sea Mother and accompanies him and the prisoners to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.
source_quote: The archpriest of the Sea Mother admits the monitor and informs him that he, his whip, and the prisoners will accompany them to see the archpriest of the Deep Father.

subject: derro prisoners
fact: The party had previously tied up derro prisoners, an act Gloog finds both honorable and odd, suggesting unresolved tension or mystery around their capture and fate.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Existence of Leemooggoogoon
fact: It is unclear whether Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, is a real deity or a construct used to justify ritual violence. Grygum and others suspect the god may not exist, but the cult’s fervor and the bloodstained altar suggest otherwise.
source_quote: It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

subject: Existence of Leemooggoogoon
fact: It is unclear whether Leemooggoogoon, the Deep Father, is a real deity or a delusion of Bloppblippodd’s. The escapees and even Gloog question the legitimacy of the god, and the rituals surrounding the idol may be the product of madness rather than faith.
source_quote: It’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

subject: Kuo-toan Sleep Behavior
fact: Kuo-toans sleep while standing and move in schools of fish, suggesting they are not entirely human or are under supernatural influence. This behavior is normal to them but deeply disturbing to the escapees, and may hint at deeper magical corruption or transformation.
source_quote: Many kuo-toans just walk around with their eyes open, sleeping. And that some other kuo-toans are moving about as schools of fish.

subject: Leemooggoogoon
fact: It’s unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.
source_quote: it’s also unclear if a god named Leemooggoogoon even exists.

subject: Ploopploopeen and Bloppblippodd's relationship
fact: Ploopploopeen and his daughter have problems with their relationship.
source_quote: He and his daughter have problems with their relationship.

subject: Purpose After Escape
fact: The escapees are searching for meaning after years of running, prison, and death. Daz’s declaration that having a purpose is less depressing than aimless flight resonates with the group, making them willing to engage in the kuo-toan conflict.
source_quote: Having something to focus on would be much less depressing than just doing what we are doing.

subject: The Derro’s Fate
fact: The escapees captured a derro but chose not to hand them over to the Kuo-toans. Gloog finds this both honorable and odd, suggesting that the derro’s fate remains unresolved and may have consequences for future alliances or betrayals.
source_quote: You didn’t choose just to give us the derro whom you tied up? That is both honorable and odd.

subject: Zalthir's role
fact: Zalthir wonders why they should bother. They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders why they should bother. They have their problems, and the issues of these two warring tribes are not their concern.

subject: 2nd day of the 3rd tenday of Taraskh
fact: The day on which the ritual was performed, the kuo-toa civil war erupted, and Demogorgon was summoned. It is the day the escapees ceased being prisoners and became survivors of an apocalypse.

subject: 2nd day of the 3rd tenday of Taraskh
fact: The ritual occurs on the 2nd day of the 3rd tenday of Taraskh, a significant temporal anchor in the campaign calendar.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 3rd tenday of Taraskh

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occur during a session of play, following the completion of a ritual and the emergence of a cosmic horror. The timeline is immediate and continuous, with no temporal breaks between observation, realization, and manifestation.
source_quote: The battle continues to rage... Daz observes the madness... Thorin then notices... Grygum thinks for a moment... Just then, he hears...

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 2nd day of the 3rd Tenday of Taraskh.
source_quote: 2nd day of the 3rd tenday of Taraskh

subject: Blopp
fact: Blopp screams at one of the Kuo Toans to stop the escapees from running.
source_quote: Blopp screams at one of the Kuo Toans to stop the escapees from running.

subject: Bloppblippodd
fact: Bloppblippodd calls for the sacrifices to be brought forth.
source_quote: Just then, he hears Bloppblippodd call for the sacrifices to be brought forth.

subject: Blopp's second in command
fact: Her second in command advances to block one route of escape.
source_quote: Her second in command advances to block one route of escape.

subject: Buppido
fact: Buppido mutters, 'ahd m.'
source_quote: ahd m.

subject: Cleric of Bahamut
fact: The cleric of Bahamut says, 'Gold to buy things and nothing to buy?'
source_quote: Gold to buy things and nothing to buy?

subject: Completion of the Ritual
fact: The ritual was completed when the archpriest of the Deep Father slew Blopp and uttered 'Leemooggoogoon.' This act triggered the manifestation of Demogorgon from the Darklake, fulfilling the prophecy of evil rituals summoning terrible outcomes.
source_quote: Grygum thinks for a moment and realizes that the ritual is complete. Usually, when an evil cult completes a cruel ritual, something terrible happens.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz announces, 'We’re all going to come out of this alive.'
source_quote: We’re all going to come out of this alive.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz notices the cleric running and runs after him.
source_quote: Daz notices the cleric running and runs after him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observes the madness and walks towards the boat with a confident swagger, looking as if he knows what he is doing and that nobody should mess with him.
source_quote: Daz observes the madness and walks towards the boat with a confident swagger, looking as if he knows what he is doing and that nobody should mess with him.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz shouts, 'We should check to see if we can find any supplies anywhere.'
source_quote: We should check to see if we can find any supplies anywhere.

subject: Duergar
fact: The duergar looks at Grygum, surprised yet somehow comforted.
source_quote: The duergar looks at Grygum, surprised yet somehow comforted.

subject: Duergar
fact: The duergar says, 'I am Hemeth.'
source_quote: Hemeth.

subject: Duergar
fact: The duergar says, 'What? You are just going to show up here and die?'
source_quote: What? You are just going to show up here and die?

subject: Duergar
fact: The duergar sighs, 'Very well. Tell me when to act. And if we get out of here alive, find me in Gracklstugh.'
source_quote: Very well. Tell me when to act. And if we get out of here alive, find me in Gracklstugh.

subject: Duergar
fact: The duergar's desire to live overcomes his innate cultural cynicism.
source_quote: His desire to live overcomes his innate cultural cynicism.

subject: Duergar Realization
fact: Hemeth, the duergar, realizes the escapees are not passive victims and that the ritual may not proceed as the cultists believe, prompting him to seek information and a chance to survive.
source_quote: The duergar looks at Grygum, surprised yet somehow comforted. ... 'There’s more than meets the eye.' ... 'Very well. Tell me when to act.'

subject: Emergence of Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon bursts from the Darklake, thirty feet tall, with two baboon-like heads, tentacles, and blazing red eyes, heralding the ultimate evil outcome of the ritual.
source_quote: A thick, oily tentacle bursts forth, followed by another. ... two monstrous heads break the surface, resembling hideous, enraged baboons with wickedly curved tusks. ... It throws back both its heads and lets out a mighty roar!

subject: Emergence of Demogorgon
fact: Demogorgon emerged from the Darklake after the ritual’s completion, bursting forth with oily tentacles, foaming water, and two monstrous baboon heads with tusks and blazing red eyes. The creature stands thirty feet tall and radiates bloodlust and madness.
source_quote: A thick, oily tentacle burst forth, followed by another. Two monstrous heads broke the surface... water cascading down its back and shoulders.

subject: escapee consensus
fact: The escapees, including Jimjar, collectively conclude they have survived the ordeal alive, despite the chaos and impending threat.
source_quote: Jimjar mutters, 'We all made it alive.'

subject: escapee exodus
fact: The escapees, led by Daz’s swaggering confidence, mimic his posture and walk toward the boat away from the battle, ignored by the warring Kuo-Toans.
source_quote: Daz shouts, 'We should check to see if we can find any supplies anywhere.' ... Daz notices the cleric running and runs after him. ... Everyone is both pleased and disappointed... They walk towards the boat, away from the battle, with the swagger of righteous, powerful, and dangerous adventurers.

subject: Escapee exodus to the boat
fact: The escapees mimic Daz’s swagger and walk toward the boat, away from the battle, appearing as righteous, powerful, and dangerous adventurers.
source_quote: Daz walks towards the boat with a confident swagger, looking as if he knows what he is doing and that nobody should mess with him. ... The other escapees, seeing that, mimic him.

subject: Escape from the Cavern
fact: The escapees, led by Daz’s bravado and Grygum’s tactical insight, fled the chaos toward the eastern boat. They used the distraction of the kuo-toa infighting and Demogorgon’s arrival to slip away, abandoning the altar, the dead, and the madness behind them.

subject: factional betrayal
fact: Ploop betrays his daughter and attacks her along with his allies, triggering a genocidal battle between followers of the Sea Mother and the Deep Father.
source_quote: Ploop has betrayed his daughter, not the escapees, and attacks her along with his allies.

subject: fish-people massacre
fact: Kuo-Toans fishing in the Darklake are suddenly attacked by an unseen underwater enemy, resulting in their deaths and bloodied foam on the lake’s surface.
source_quote: Thorin then notices several Kuo-Toans who were previously in the water fishing and are now screaming. ... the screaming stops, and the water foams with blood. The fish people are no longer.

subject: free-for-all chaos
fact: The Kuo-Toans engage in a free-for-all melee, attacking each other while ignoring the escapees, allowing the group to flee unnoticed.
source_quote: Kuo-Toans are attacking other Kuo-Toans. And the sacrifices are now ignored. ... The Kuo Toans engaged in the melee ignore them.

subject: Free-for-all melee
fact: Kuo-Toans attack each other; sacrifices are ignored; the battle becomes a chaotic free-for-all.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum concludes, 'No, this is going to be one of those conventional slit-their-throats with-knife sacrifices. Normally, the victims would be disarmed, but I guess they figure that part of the ritual is some of the cultists dying in the attempt?'
source_quote: No, this is going to be one of those conventional slit-their-throats with-knife sacrifices. Normally, the victims would be disarmed, but I guess they figure that part of the ritual is some of the cultists dying in the attempt?

subject: Grygum

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum looks at him and thinks, 'It would be cheating to let one of us die. Would he cheat?'
source_quote: It would be cheating to let one of us die. Would he cheat?

subject: Grygum

source_quote: This is bad, but it can’t be what I think it is.

subject: Grygum

source_quote: He points to a boat in the far eastern part of the cave, guarded by a small group of isolated Kuo-Toans.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realizes that this creature doesn’t know the plan and recognizes that this may be an opportunity to take advantage of this poor creature.
source_quote: Grygum realizes that this creature doesn’t know the plan and recognizes that this may be an opportunity to take advantage of this poor creature.

fact: Grygum says, 'I take that back; this is bad.'

source_quote: Let’s see if there is anything we can take from Ploop. After all he promised to pay us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, 'There’s more than meets the eye.'
source_quote: There’s more than meets the eye.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum sees a thick, oily tentacle burst forth, followed by another.
source_quote: And then a thick, oily tentacle bursts forth, followed by another.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum shouts, 'Demogorgon, Prince of Demons, powerful, dangerous, and we need to run.'
source_quote: Demogorgon, Prince of Demons, powerful, dangerous, and we need to run.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum stares at the point in the lake as two monstrous heads break the surface, resembling hideous, enraged baboons with wickedly curved tusks.
source_quote: He stares at the point in the lake as two monstrous heads break the surface, resembling hideous, enraged baboons with wickedly curved tusks.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks for a moment and realizes that the ritual is complete.
source_quote: Grygum thinks for a moment and realizes that the ritual is complete.
