fact: Droki is the central figure in the corruption at the Deepking’s court, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly elements of the Clan Lairds. His discovery is essential to proving the conspiracy.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow is from Menzoberranzan and views Duergar violence as crude and artless compared to the refined politicking of his homeland. He is disgusted by the lack of style in Duergar conflict and contrasts their brutality with the elegance of drow intrigue.
source_quote: The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow says, 'Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me.'
source_quote: At this point, the Drow sitting next to the Halfling splutters, “Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me.”

subject: Drow at Darklake Brewery
fact: The Drow from Menzoberranzan criticizes Duergar culture as brutish and styleless, contrasting it with Drow politicking, and implies deeper cultural tensions in the Underdark.
source_quote: The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar... It’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art... It’s disgraceful.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar gives the Stone Giant the briefest of scowls, showing how much they don’t want to give this non-Duergar permission to visit their city.
source_quote: The dwarf watches how the Duergar gives the Stone Giant the briefest of scowls, showing how much they don’t want to give this non-Duergar permission to visit their city.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar says, 'And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.'
source_quote: There is a pause, “And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.”

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar turns to the others on his patrol, briefly discusses, and says, 'We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.'
source_quote: The Duergar turns to the others on his patrol, briefly discusses, and says, “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.”

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is the guardian of the city against corruption, linked to the Council of Savants and possibly the Clan Lairds, and holds the key to uncovering the conspiracy centered on Droki. She can guarantee freedom and safe passage in exchange for Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is the captain of the Stone Guards on the lake, commanding authority through stern presence. She seeks covert assistance to locate the rogue Duergar Droki without provoking war with the Derro, and she navigates diplomacy with a mix of threat and charm.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'And I can offer one more thing. If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here. As you think about which group to work with, remember I am the one that can guarantee your freedom.'
source_quote: She then smiles very evilly, “And I can offer one more thing.” ... “If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here. As you think about which group to work with, remember I am the one that can guarantee your freedom.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.'
source_quote: “As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.'
source_quote: “I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live. If we were to go there in force, it would provoke a violent reaction. So we need someone who isn’t us to find him.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.'
source_quote: “It is my job to protect the city from corruption. So yes, it is for the city.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds. Discovery of this conspiracy will earn me great favor with the Deepking. And when that happens, I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.'
source_quote: “There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds. Discovery of this conspiracy will earn me great favor with the Deepking. And when that happens, I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, 'Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.'
source_quote: Errde smiles, “Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.”

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull, captain of the Stone Guards, manipulates Thorin’s party into investigating corruption, offers payment and protection, and implies authority over Drow slave claims; her motives are ambiguous.
source_quote: I can tell them that they are not here... I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.

subject: Gartokkar's status
fact: Gartokkar is the chief of the Keepers of the Flame and one of the Deepking’s most prized advisors.
source_quote: We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors.

subject: Gartokkar's title
fact: Gartokkar is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, responsible for tending Themberchaud — a fire dragon that burns stone-hot to fuel Gracklstugh’s furnaces. He is literal-minded, misunderstood sarcasm, laughed at a joke for the first time in long memory, and offered Zalthir safe passage through the city in exchange for a service. He warned that the offer expires tomorrow and that future interactions may be hostile if declined.
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.'
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.'
source_quote: “The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.'
source_quote: There is a moment of hesitation, “The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs. And we are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors. We need someone like you.'
source_quote: Gartokkar is a Duergar, and he is literal and misses the sarcasm, “Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs. And we are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors. We need someone like you.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn says, 'Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city. And as long as you did nothing that the Deepking would disapprove of and would not require me to do too much, I could keep you out of the prisons.'
source_quote: “Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh. If you were to come to the Keepers of the Flame headquarters and do me a service, I could give you safe passage through the city. And as long as you did nothing that the Deepking would disapprove of and would not require me to do too much, I could keep you out of the prisons.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, operates the dragon-lighter system for Gracklstugh’s furnaces and recruits outsiders; he laughs at jokes and makes conditional offers of protection.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot... We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors... We need someone like you.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame, is literal, values humor, and recruits outsiders to serve the Keepers of the Flame; he is a high-ranking advisor to the Deepking.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... We are the most prized of the Deepking’s advisors.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum hears from within the darkness the sound of Zalthir’s fists hitting the giant and the blade of Thorin, but still, the giant stands.
source_quote: Grygum hears from within the darkness the sound of Zalthir’’s fists hitting the giant and the blade of Thorin, but still, the giant stands.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc who sneaks peeks to gather intelligence, speaks with pragmatic humor, and is perceived as non-threatening despite his appearance. He is trusted by Daz as a companion in navigating dangerous social terrain.
source_quote: Grygum, who sneaks a quick peek, says that inside is a pretty dour place where people talk only in hushed whispers.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum jokes, 'We do have some kindling here.'
source_quote: Zalthir hears Grygum’s joke, “We do have some kindling here.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device the Duergar are holding, a tube that connects to a bottle on their back, with a small flame sitting outside the tube, produced by a magic concoction lit by a tiny flame when the Duergar operator pulls a lever.
source_quote: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device they are holding. It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes the battle, interprets Daz’s magic as deliberately weakened, hears Zalthir’s attacks, and rushes in to strike the giant with his mace; he later witnesses Thorin praying and the Duergar shrinking.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.' ... Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace. ... Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead. ... Grygum looks up, and the enlarged Duergars have shrunk to their standard size.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace.
source_quote: So Grygum rushes in to strike with his mace.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thinks, 'Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.'
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.
source_quote: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant at the hands of Duergar using a magical flame device, observed Thorin’s attempt to subdue it, noted Daz’s deliberate weakening of his spells, and heard Zalthir’s fists and Thorin’s blade striking the giant — ultimately rushing in to strike with his mace. He watched Thorin mourn the giant and saw the Duergar shrink to standard size after the giant’s death.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Guard
fact: The guard sensing that asks, 'Someone who does not follow orders and engages in anti-social behavior, but does it in a way that will bring them no profit and certain doom?'
source_quote: The guard sensing that asks, “Someone who does not follow orders and engages in anti-social behavior, but does it in a way that will bring them no profit and certain doom?”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling is an outsider in the Underdark who survives by appearing harmless, avoiding political entanglements, and sharing information with those not 'in the game.' He is well-informed about factional conflicts, the Deepking’s madness, and the Keepers of the Flame’s predicament.
source_quote: I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'It all began with the Deepking’s madness.'
source_quote: “It all began with the Deepking’s madness.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.'
source_quote: “I’m an outsider. And what do I know? Not very much. And as long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat. And I can share what I know with those not in the game. And you are not part of the game, nor am I.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.'
source_quote: Now, they don’t. It’s as if he is detached from reality.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'The red dragon keeps the stones hot enough for the furnaces to burn. Are you wondering about its horde? The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem, and you’re right to wonder, is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon. There is also the problem of the dragon becoming more powerful over time. So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.'
source_quote: “The red dragon keeps the stones hot enough for the furnaces to burn. Are you wondering about its horde? The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him. The problem, and you’re right to wonder, is that Red Dragons dislike playing second fiddle. And so, at some point, the Dragon discovers it’s not in charge. Then, the Keepers of the Flame have to kill the dragon. There is also the problem of the dragon becoming more powerful over time. So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.'
source_quote: He pauses, searching for a phrase, “What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling says, 'You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.'
source_quote: “You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.”

subject: Halfling at Darklake Brewery
fact: The Halfling is an outsider who avoids faction involvement, provides key intelligence on Deepking’s madness and faction conflicts, and understands the danger of being perceived as a player.
source_quote: I’m an outsider... As long as I stay an outsider, no one considers me a threat... Not relevant to the game.

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is Dorhun’s companion, a Stone Giant and former apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam; his role is passive but confirms the legitimacy of Dorhun’s request.
source_quote: I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is a stone giant and companion of Dorhun, also an apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam. He accompanied Dorhun when he met Thorin and was present when Dorhun granted passage through the city. He did not speak but was part of the authoritative presence that commanded the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says to the Duergar with the stone weapons, 'Stone Guards, you are to let them through.'
source_quote: Turning to the Duergar with the stone weapons, he says, “Stone Guards, you are to let them through.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?'
source_quote: The Stone Giant doesn’t smile, “No. But then again, I don’t know many. Who are you?” ... Then he says, “I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.'
source_quote: Then he says, “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant says, 'We have qualified immunity if a Stone Giant is rampaging through our city.'
source_quote: “We have qualified immunity if a Stone Giant is rampaging through our city,” one explains.

subject: Stone Giant
fact: The Stone Giant stares at Thorin, whose body and blade show that he fought and perhaps killed the two-headed giant.
source_quote: The Stone Giant stares at Thorin, whose body and blade show that he fought and perhaps killed the two-headed giant.

subject: Stonespeaker Hgraam
fact: Stonespeaker Hgraam was the mentor of Dorhun and Rihuud; his death is implied to be connected to the stone giant’s rampage and the city’s deeper mysteries.
source_quote: We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam. Did you kill him?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue the two-headed stone giant, pleaded with the Duergar not to kill it, and later prayed for the dead. He inquired about unusual behavior among giants, used a precise definition of anti-social, non-profitable madness to communicate with the Duergar, and was directed by Dorhun — a stone giant apprentice of Stonespeaker Hgraam — to visit Cairngorm Cavern. He confirmed that he tried to subdue Hgraam, not kill him, and was granted safe passage by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: “Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him,” shouts Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempts to subdue the stone giant, prays for the dead, questions Duergar about 'crazy' behavior, learns of increased incidents of anti-social giants, and is approached by Dorhun who requests a visit to Cairngorm Cavern; he later negotiates with Errde Blackskull and seeks clarity on whether he serves the city or the Stone Guards.
source_quote: Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him," ... "Are there more crazy people about?" ... "I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city." ... "It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!" ... "Are we helping you? Or the city?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a traveler who is tempted to join the Stone Guards but is wary of factional entanglements. He is influenced by the halfling’s warnings and struggles to distinguish between helping the guards and serving the city’s interests.
source_quote: Are we helping you? Or the city?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is seeking clarity on whether to align with the Stone Guards or the City, and is being manipulated by Errde’s promises of freedom and rewards in exchange for action against Droki.
source_quote: Look, we want to know if this is for the Stone Guards or the City?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is tempted to work for the Stone Guards, but the warnings of the halfling worry him.
source_quote: Thorin is tempted to work for the Stone Guards. After all, they are friends of the Stone giants, but the warnings of the Halfing worry him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is unfamiliar with the patterns of behavior of the Duergar, and finds the madness of a stone giant unheard of.
source_quote: Although Thorin is unfamiliar with the patterns of behavior of the Duergar, the madness of a stone giant is unheard of.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not talkative and may take a long time before they initiate a conversation as they ponder all possible things.
source_quote: Thorin remembers that Stone Giants are not talkative and may take a long time before they initiate a conversation as they ponder all possible things.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin says, 'It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!'
source_quote: Thorin grabs his sword and wonders where exactly they will run to because it’s not clear how they can beat the entire stone guard, but the effect Daz was hoping for is achieved. Errde is taken aback and smiles, “Of course not. It is a friendly conversation.” ... Thorin shouts, “It’s just a friendly meeting. Not that kind of meeting!”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin shouts, 'Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him.'
source_quote: “Don’t kill him! There’s something wrong with this giant! Let’s try and subdue him,” shouts Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin turns to one of the Duergar, 'Are there more crazy people about?'
source_quote: He turns to one of the Duergar, “Are there more crazy people about?”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin whispers prayers for the dead after the duergars kill the giant.
source_quote: Grygum watches as a distraught Thorin whispers prayers for the dead.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is targeted by Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame, who offers him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service; the offer expires tomorrow and carries implied threats.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame... Your skill set would be of great value to the city of Gracklstugh... The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.
source_quote: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks, 'I gotta get me some of that ability.'
source_quote: “I gotta get me some of that ability,” he thinks.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was focused on survival against being burned, crushed, or arrested. He encountered Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for a service. Gartokkar revealed the city’s use of a fire dragon to fuel furnaces, misunderstood sarcasm about being a ‘lighter,’ and laughed at Grygum’s joke about kindling. Zalthir was warned the offer expires tomorrow and that future encounters may not be friendly.
source_quote: “I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.”

subject: Zalthir's observation
fact: Zalthir notices Gartokkar has four notches on his ears, which do not look self-inflicted.
source_quote: Zalthir immediately notices the scars on his ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as a reward for initial cooperation, with another 175 gold pieces contingent on delivering Droki and proof of corruption.
source_quote: As a reward, I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: Dragon eggs
fact: Dragon eggs are available for purchase and can be hatched, enabling the Keepers of the Flame to replace the Red Dragon when necessary. This knowledge informs Daz’s understanding of the cycle of control and violence in the city.
source_quote: Daz wonders... how Dragon eggs can be purchased and hatched.

subject: Flame Device
fact: The flame device is a magical apparatus used by Duergar to control and project fire, consisting of a tube connected to a bottle on the back, with a small external flame produced by a magic concoction lit when a lever is pulled. It was used to kill the two-headed stone giant and is a signature tool of the Duergar militias.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: flame tube and bottle device
fact: A Duergar-held device consisting of a tube connected to a bottle on the back produces a persistent flame through magic; it is used to burn and kill the stone giant.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: reward offer
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment from the armory as initial reward, with another 175 gold pieces upon success.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: reward structure
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces upfront and another 175 gold pieces upon successful delivery of Droki and proof.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. When you bring me Droki and the proof I need, then I will give you 175 more.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a fire dragon kept by the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh. It burns stone-hot and is used to fuel the city’s furnaces, replacing the need for large amounts of kindling. It is a living, controlled weapon of industrial power, and its care is the most prized duty in the Deepking’s service.
source_quote: “we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.”

subject: corruption inquiry
fact: Errde seeks proof of corruption linked to Droki, the Council of Savants, and Clan Lairds.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: corruption of the Deepking’s court
fact: A hidden corruption is eating at the heart of the Deepking’s court, linked to Droki, the Council of Savants, and Clan Lairds; its nature and resolution remain unresolved.
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: Deepking’s madness
fact: The Deepking’s rule has become increasingly arbitrary and detached from reality, leading to the collapse of logical law in Gracklstugh. This madness is the root cause of current factional instability and the Keepers of the Flame’s desperation.
source_quote: It all began with the Deepking’s madness.

subject: Dorhun’s invitation to Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun invited Thorin to visit Cairngorm Cavern before leaving the city, implying that Hgraam’s legacy, the stone giants’ history, or a deeper secret lies there. This is an unresolved thread that may connect to the mystery of the giant madness, the Duergar’s control, or the origins of the fire dragon.
source_quote: “I ask you to visit me at Cairngorm Cavern before you leave the city.”

subject: Droki’s corruption
fact: Droki is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds, but the nature of this corruption is not yet proven.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Drow slave escape
fact: A group of escaped Drow slaves may be in the city; Errde Blackskull offers to deny their presence, implying the party may be harboring them or could be targeted by Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: escaped slaves
fact: A group of Drow may be searching for escaped slaves; Errde can deny their presence in the city, and her ability to provide this cover is a leverage point for Thorin’s freedom.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: Gartokkar’s offer to Zalthir
fact: Gartokkar offered Zalthir safe passage and protection in Gracklstugh in exchange for a service, with the offer expiring tomorrow. Failure to accept may result in hostile future encounters. The nature of the service is unspecified, creating a pending plot thread that could lead Zalthir into the heart of the Keepers of the Flame’s operations.
source_quote: “The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.”

subject: identity and fate of Droki
fact: Droki, a Duergar living in the West Cleft District, is the central figure in the corruption investigation; his connection to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds is unverified.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki... Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption.

subject: mystery of the stone giant madness
fact: A surge of anti-social, non-profitable madness among stone giants has been reported by Duergar, with no known cause. This phenomenon has increased militia work and may be tied to a clan leader’s hidden knowledge. Thorin and Dorhun’s encounters suggest this is a systemic issue with deep roots in the city’s power structure.
source_quote: “We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior... And we know of no underlying cause. Although a clan leader may have information they have chosen not to share with us.”

subject: Not relevant to the game
fact: The phrase 'Not relevant to the game' has emerged as a cryptic mantra among outsiders who avoid factional entanglements. It defines a survival philosophy in the Underdark, separating observers from participants.
source_quote: What is that expression? It's -- Not relevant to the game.

subject: origin of the dragon-lighter system
fact: The origin of the red dragon’s forced servitude as a flame source for Gracklstugh’s furnaces is unexplained, and the cycle of killing and replacing dragons raises ethical and strategic questions.
source_quote: The Keepers of the Flame give him a horde, and they pamper him... the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: proof of corruption
fact: Errde claims Daz’s description of the Blade Bazaar’s behaviors constitutes proof of corruption, linking systemic lawlessness in commerce to political decay.
source_quote: You have found me proof!

subject: The Halfling’s outsider status
fact: The halfling refuses to become involved in the city’s factions because he wants to remain an outsider who watches, not participates.
source_quote: I like to watch. I would avoid such encounters and actions.

subject: The Red Dragon’s fate
fact: The Keepers of the Flame must kill and replace the red dragon over time because it becomes more powerful and resents its role, but the source of new dragons is unexplored.
source_quote: So the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one.

subject: Thorin’s allegiance
fact: Thorin is torn between aiding the Stone Guards, the city, or remaining neutral; his moral compass conflicts with the city’s authoritarian structure and hidden agendas.
source_quote: Are we helping you? Or the city?" ... "I am tempted to work for the Stone Guards... but the warnings of the Halfing worry him.

subject: Zalthir’s desire for power
fact: Zalthir wants to acquire the ability he saw used by Gartokkar, but his intention to do so is unspoken beyond his internal thought.
source_quote: I gotta get me some of that ability," he thinks.

subject: Zalthir’s recruitment
fact: Zalthir has been offered a role in the Keepers of the Flame, but the cost, timing, and consequences of acceptance remain unknown.
source_quote: Your skill set would be of great value... I could give you safe passage... I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: On this date, the assassination of Werz Saltbaron occurred, magic was used in combat, and Werz vanished invisibly, marking a turning point in the investigation.
source_quote: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493
fact: On this day, the party’s entanglement in the triple-agent web reaches critical mass: assassinations are witnessed, Themberchaud claims them as agents, Gartokkar reveals the dragon egg theft, and the true power structure of Gracklstugh is exposed.
source_quote: The dragon roars, 'Gartokkar, come.'

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during a single, tense session in Gracklstugh — a critical turning point where Thorin’s survival strategy shifts from evasion to open confrontation, and the fate of the egg, Themberchaud, and the city hangs in the balance.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur during a single session following the group’s arrival at Gracklstugh, after resting and prior to any mission execution.
source_quote: And after resting, he heads out to the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493 DR.
source_quote: 10th day of the 1st Tenday of Myrtul 1493

subject: agent recruitment
fact: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.
source_quote: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.

subject: assassination attempt
fact: Two assassins, wearing face coverings and wielding glowing weapons, strike the other man.
source_quote: Two assassins, wearing face coverings and wielding glowing weapons, strike the other man.

subject: Assassination Attempt on Werz Saltbaron
fact: Two masked assassins wielding glowing weapons attacked Werz Saltbaron on the pier; the party intervened, killing the assassins, but found no weapons — only a charcoal drawing of the merchant on one corpse, suggesting he was the target — or the killer.
source_quote: He presents it to the Duergar. 'Oh my, I was.'

subject: Assassination of Werz Saltbaron
fact: Werz Saltbaron was attacked by two psychic assassins on the pier near the inn; the attackers vanished without leaving weapons, and the victim had no physical wounds despite being struck.
source_quote: Two assassins... strike the other man... The Duergar merchant has no wound on his body.

subject: association with undesirables
fact: Thorin has been seen associating with individuals of questionable character, including other surface dwellers and individuals who may be considered enemies of the state.
source_quote: Association with Undesirables: Thorin has been seen associating with individuals of questionable character, including other surface dwellers and individuals who may be considered enemies of the state. Such associations can raise suspicion and lead to accusations of conspiracy, aiding, and abetting.

subject: Badge Distribution
fact: Gartokkar distributes gold badges to the group under Themberchaud’s command; the act serves as a ritual of enrollment and a tangible symbol of the dragon’s authority, though its material value remains uncertain.
source_quote: Give these humanoids some of the gold badges.

subject: Cavern Tremor and Voice
fact: A thunderous voice echoes through the cavern as Themberchaud emerges, accompanied by a seismic tremor; the spectacle reinforces his dominance and the supernatural weight of his presence.
source_quote: Gartokkar," the voice calls as a reptilian behemoth comes into view.

subject: cleric of Bahamut's outrage at Themberchaud's treatment
fact: Grygum, as a cleric of Bahamut, is appalled at how Themberchaud is treated and agrees to the plan.
source_quote: Grygum smiles, “As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.”

subject: Daz
fact: Daz replies that the faction thinks they are working for them, but whether they do is up to them.
source_quote: Daz, who has experience with the twisted, machiavellian politics of the Drow, replies, "The faction thinks we are working for them. Whether we do is up to us."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, "I think gathering intelligence is just as important," dismissing Jimjar’s suggestion to leave.
source_quote: Daz dismisses him, "I think gathering intelligence is just as important."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, "The faction thinks we are working for them. Whether we do is up to us."
source_quote: Daz, who has experience with the twisted, machiavellian politics of the Drow, replies, "The faction thinks we are working for them. Whether we do is up to us."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz says, "We never technically accepted an offer. He assumed we accepted. We would like to understand the nature of the offer?"
source_quote: Daz gets their first, "We never technically accepted an offer. He assumed we accepted. We would like to understand the nature of the offer?"

subject: Daz
fact: Daz speaks the words for scorching rays, feels intense heat, and launches fiery energy at an assassin while Zalthir’s darkness hides the flash.
source_quote: Daz speaks the words for scorching rays and feels the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested. He points with his index finger, uses his thumb to sight, squints, and lets the rays loose...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thinks, "And perhaps that’s why," he’s being attacked, right before the assassination occurs.
source_quote: "And perhaps that’s why," Daz thinks, "he’s being attacked."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thinks, "Wererats," when he notices the other escapees are missing.
source_quote: "Wererats," thinks Daz.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz turned to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges and said, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?'
source_quote: Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, 'So we flash the right one at the right time?'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz utters mystical words and causes motes of light to appear above his hand, launching magic missiles at an assassin.
source_quote: When Daz utters the mystical words, motes of light appear above his hand, and three fingers point at one of the assassins. A silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles...

subject: Daz
fact: Daz walks to the piers near the inn and observes a Duergar man looking into the darkness of the Darklake.
source_quote: Daz leaves the inn and walks to the piers near the "inn." On one of the piers, a Duergar man appears, looking into the darkness of the Darklake.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz watches two assassins strike a Duergar man with glowing weapons and wonders if they are psychic weapons.
source_quote: As Daz watches, two assassins, wearing face coverings and wielding glowing weapons, strike the other man. "Psychic weapons?" he wonders.

subject: disaster of revealing the egg
fact: Gartokkar says sharing the egg’s existence would be a disaster.
source_quote: Gartokkar turns dark and then smiles, “You joke? Sharing that would be a disaster.”

subject: double agent status
fact: We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: dragon egg theft
fact: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: dragon’s age and replacement
fact: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: dragon's breath
fact: The dragon roars, 'If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them.' And with that, he breathes fire in a circle around the cavern. When nobody dies or screams, the dragon laughs.
source_quote: The dragon roars, 'If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them.' And with that, he breathes fire in a circle around the cavern. When nobody dies or screams, the dragon laughs.

subject: espionage investigation
fact: The espionage investigation is referenced as the grave offense Thorin is suspected of, due to his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including Themberchaud and the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: Given his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud, Thorin is suspected of espionage or gathering intelligence for potentially hostile entities.

subject: fabrication of charges against Thorin
fact: Gartokkar has prepared a list of eight fabricated legal transgressions against Thorin under Gracklstugh law, including public disturbance, interference with the city watch, questioning authority, unauthorized access, and suspicion of espionage — all to justify his arrest if needed.
source_quote: Let me enumerate a list of potential transgressions that the dwarf, Thorin, has committed...

subject: factional deception
fact: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: flashing the right badge at the right time
fact: Daz asks if they should flash the right badge at the right time.
source_quote: Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges, “So we flash the right one at the right time?”

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar enumerates potential transgressions committed by Thorin that could warrant punitive action under Gracklstugh law.
source_quote: Let me enumerate a list of potential transgressions that the dwarf, Thorin, has committed, which could warrant significant punitive action within the laws of Gracklstugh.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar explains that the Keepers of the Flame lost the red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement, and that Themberchaud doesn’t know about it.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement... He doesn’t know.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar hands out gold badges and holy symbols of Laduguer to the group.
source_quote: Let me give you this holy symbol of Laduguer and these gold pins featuring Themberchaud’s profile.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar looked at Thorin and said, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar paused and asked, 'Is that enough?'
source_quote: Gartokkar pauses, 'Is that enough?'

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar reveals that Themberchaud thinks the Keepers of the Flame work for him, but in truth, he works for them.
source_quote: Gartokkar smiles conspiratorially, "Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn't realize is that he works for us."

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world."
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "He doesn’t know."
source_quote: He doesn’t know.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "I am so delighted to see that you accepted Themberchaud’s offer to be an agent of ours."
source_quote: Gartokkar sits down in his chamber and says, "I am so delighted to see that you accepted Themberchaud’s offer to be an agent of ours."

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "Let me enumerate a list of potential transgressions that the dwarf, Thorin, has committed, which could warrant significant punitive action within the laws of Gracklstugh."
source_quote: Let me enumerate a list of potential transgressions that the dwarf, Thorin, has committed, which could warrant significant punitive action within the laws of Gracklstugh.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us."
source_quote: Gartokkar smiles conspiratorially, "Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn't realize is that he works for us."

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki."
source_quote: We have identified an agent of the Grey Ghosts. His name is Droki.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement."
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar says, "Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards."
source_quote: Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar tells Thorin that Themberchaud will eventually "move on" because he wants to see more of the world.
source_quote: Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar threatens to turn the group over to the Stone Guards if they refuse to accept the agent role.
source_quote: Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards.

subject: Gartokkar
fact: Gartokkar turned dark and then smiled and said, 'You joke? Sharing that would be a disaster.'
source_quote: Gartokkar turns dark and then smiles, 'You joke? Sharing that would be a disaster.'

subject: Gartokkar’s list of transgressions
fact: Gartokkar threatens Thorin with a list of potential transgressions under Gracklstugh law to coerce compliance.
source_quote: Let me enumerate a list of potential transgressions that the dwarf, Thorin, has committed, which could warrant significant punitive action within the laws of Gracklstugh.

subject: Gartokkar’s revelation about Themberchaud’s replacement
fact: Gartokkar reveals that the Keepers of the Flame are waiting for Themberchaud to 'move on' so a new dragon can be hatched from the stolen egg, and that Themberchaud believes he is in control.
source_quote: The egg is for when Themberchaud moves on. His replacement. Eventually, the Dragon moves on because he wants to see more of the world.

subject: general suspicion
fact: As a non-Duergar, Thorin is already subject to suspicion and scrutiny within Gracklstugh, and any deviation from expected behavior can lead to arrest and imprisonment.
source_quote: General Suspicion: As a non-Duergar, Thorin is already subject to suspicion and scrutiny within Gracklstugh. Any deviation from expected behavior or any action that could be interpreted as threatening to the city's stability can lead to arrest and imprisonment.

subject: group’s forced acceptance as agents
fact: The group is declared agents of Themberchaud without their consent, and later learns they are also being manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame, making them triple agents.
source_quote: We never technically accepted an offer. He assumed we accepted.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum mutters that they are double agents or triple agents, working for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: Grygum, standing next to Thorin, mutters, "I suppose we are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum pushes the first assassin’s corpse into the water.
source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum rushes one of the assassins trying to toss him into the water and fails.
source_quote: As Daz watches, Grygum rushes one of the assassins, trying to toss him into the water. He fails.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, "I suppose we are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame."
source_quote: Grygum, standing next to Thorin, mutters, "I suppose we are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, "It’s like when parents say that the pet puppy left even when it dies."
source_quote: Grygum turns to Thorin, "It’s like when parents say that the pet puppy left even when it dies."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum says, "We have people who will come looking for us!" to Themberchaud.
source_quote: Grygum shouts, "We have people who will come looking for us!"

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum smiled and said, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.'

subject: interference with city watch
fact: Thorin attempted to influence and direct the actions of the Duergar City Watch during the incident with the stone giant, which can be seen as obstruction.
source_quote: Interference with City Watch: Thorin attempted to influence and direct the actions of the Duergar City Watch during the aforementioned incident with the stone giant. While he claims he was trying to help, any interference with the watch's official duties can be seen as obstruction and a challenge to their authority.

subject: interrogation by Stone Guards
fact: The interrogation by Stone Guards is referenced by Thorin as the event that will occur if they are arrested, during which they will have to tell the truth about the egg.
source_quote: Thorin stares at him. 'I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?'

subject: Invisibility of Werz Saltbaron
fact: After being healed, Werz Saltbaron became invisible and departed, suggesting he possesses magical means of evasion and may be hiding his true intentions.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible.

subject: Jimjar
fact: Jimjar says, "Very well," after shrugging at Daz’s refusal to leave.
source_quote: Jimjar shrugs and slumps into one of the beds. He sighs, "Very well."

subject: magic missiles cast by Daz
fact: Daz casts magic missiles, causing motes of light to appear above his hand, three fingers pointing at an assassin, followed by a silent rush of air and a burst of light and crackling sound upon impact.
source_quote: When Daz utters the mystical words, motes of light appear above his hand, and three fingers point at one of the assassins. A silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles, and when they strike, a burst of light and a crackling sound fills the area.

subject: possession of unauthorized items
fact: If Thorin is found to own any items considered contraband or restricted within Gracklstugh, such as certain weapons or magical items, he will violate the law.
source_quote: Possession of Unauthorized Items: If Thorin is found to own any items considered contraband or restricted within Gracklstugh, such as certain weapons or magical items, he will violate the law.

subject: psychic blade assassination
fact: Two assassins strike Werz Saltbaron with glowing weapons, leaving no entrance or exit wounds, consistent with psychic blade attacks described in Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs.
source_quote: Two assassins, wearing face coverings and wielding glowing weapons, strike the other man. 'Psychic weapons?' he wonders.

subject: public disturbance and disorder
fact: Thorin was involved in the altercation with the deranged stone giant, contributing to the ensuing public disorder.
source_quote: Public Disturbance and Disorder: Thorin was involved in the altercation with the deranged stone giant. While he claims to have wanted to subdue the giant, his actions could be interpreted as contributing to the ensuing public disorder.

subject: pushing assassins’ corpses into the Darklake
fact: Grygum and Zalthir push the assassins’ corpses into the Darklake to conceal evidence before the guard arrives.
source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water. Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.

subject: questioning authority
fact: Thorin has repeatedly questioned the authority and motives of various Duergar individuals and factions, including the Keepers of the Flame, which is not tolerated.
source_quote: Questioning Authority: Thorin has repeatedly questioned the authority and motives of various Duergar individuals and factions, including the Keepers of the Flame. Such questioning can be perceived as dissent and disrespect, which is not tolerated within Gracklstugh's hierarchical society.

subject: Recruitment by Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud forcibly recruited the party as his agents without consent, using intimidation and false authority, while the Keepers of the Flame simultaneously claimed them as their own — creating a layered deception that traps the party in triple-agent status.
source_quote: I wish for you to be my agent. And as my agents, you will have my protection.

subject: request for the egg and proof of the Gray Ghosts
fact: Gartokkar tells Thorin to find the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.

subject: Revelation of the Dragon Egg Theft
fact: Gartokkar reveals the Keepers of the Flame lost the dragon egg meant to replace Themberchaud to the Gray Ghosts, and that Themberchaud is unaware he is being groomed for replacement — a secret the party now holds.
source_quote: The egg is for when Themberchaud moves on. His replacement.

subject: riding the Dragon out of Gracklstugh
fact: Thorin proposes riding the Dragon out of the city, laying waste to everything behind them, as factions are playing them against each other.
source_quote: Thorin nods. And then he has a peculiar glint in his eye. He turns to Grygum, “I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?”

subject: scorching rays cast by Daz
fact: Daz casts scorching rays, feeling intense heat, pointing with his index finger, using his thumb to sight, squinting, and releasing the rays, which leave a streak of heat haze and burn flesh despite Zalthir’s darkness.
source_quote: He speaks the words for scorching rays and feels the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested. He points with his index finger, uses his thumb to sight, squints, and lets the rays loose. They travel quickly, leaving a streak of heat haze.

subject: shared disclosure of the egg
fact: Thorin says if they get arrested, they will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg.
source_quote: Thorin stares at him. “I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?”

subject: suspicion of espionage
fact: Given his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud, Thorin is suspected of espionage or gathering intelligence for potentially hostile entities.
source_quote: Suspicion of Espionage: Given his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud, Thorin is suspected of espionage or gathering intelligence for potentially hostile entities. This is a grave offense with severe consequences.

subject: theft of the red dragon egg
fact: The red dragon egg, believed to be the replacement for Themberchaud, was stolen by the Gray Ghosts agent Droki. The theft caused a major disturbance in the Underdark and has become the focal point of a multi-faction power struggle.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud asks Daz if he is from Menzoberranzan and laughs when Daz says yes.
source_quote: The dragon asks if Daz is from Menzoberranzan... Daz says he is. The dragon laughs, "Excellent! You have no family associations and nobody that can be blackmailed."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud asks Zalthir if he is a gold dragonborn and says he never liked gold dragons.
source_quote: The dragon turns to Zalthir, "You are a gold dragonborn?" "No, a bronze." "Good. I never liked gold dragons."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud breathes fire in a circle around the cavern and laughs when nobody dies or screams.
source_quote: The dragon bellows, "If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them." And with that, he breathes fire in a circle around the cavern. When nobody dies or screams, the dragon laughs.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud declares the group his agents and whispers that their first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask, but report to him first.
source_quote: The dragon whispers, "Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "Excellent! You have no family associations and nobody that can be blackmailed."
source_quote: The dragon laughs, "Excellent! You have no family associations and nobody that can be blackmailed."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "Good. I never liked gold dragons."
source_quote: "Good. I never liked gold dragons."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "I wish to speak to them alone."
source_quote: The dragon roars, "I wish to speak to them alone."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them."
source_quote: The dragon bellows, "If I catch anyone spying, I will kill them."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "You are a gold dragonborn?"
source_quote: The dragon turns to Zalthir, "You are a gold dragonborn?"

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud says, "Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first."
source_quote: The dragon whispers, "Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first."

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud tells Gartokkar to give the group gold badges and commands the rest to follow Gartokkar’s orders.
source_quote: Gartokkar, come... Give these humanoids some of the gold badges... And the rest of you do what Gartokkar says.

subject: Themberchaud’s fire circle
fact: Themberchaud breathes fire in a circle around his cavern, and when no one dies or screams, he laughs, demonstrating his control and theatricality.
source_quote: And with that, he breathes fire in a circle around the cavern. When nobody dies or screams, the dragon laughs.

subject: Themberchaud's Recruitment
fact: Themberchaud unilaterally declares Zalthir and his companions his agents without seeking consent, using intimidation, psychological dominance, and symbolic gifts (gold badges) to enforce compliance.
source_quote: I wish for you to be my agent. And as my agents, you will have my protection.

subject: The Party’s Triple-Agent Status
fact: The party is now simultaneously bound — by coercion, deception, and circumstance — to the Stone Guards (Errde), the Keepers of the Flame (Gartokkar), and Themberchaud, with no clear allegiance, no escape, and no certainty of who is manipulating whom.
source_quote: We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin and Gartokkar stood outside the building that houses Gartokkar’s office.
source_quote: As they stand outside the building that houses Gartokkar’s office, Daz turns to Thorin while looking at his collection of badges...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks Gartokkar what the rights and responsibilities of being an agent are.
source_quote: "What are the rights and responsibilities for this position?" growls Thorin, outraged to be working for a dragon.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had a peculiar glint in his eye and turned to Grygum and said, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'
source_quote: Thorin nods. And then he has a peculiar glint in his eye. He turns to Grygum, 'I have an idea. These factions are all trying to play us against each other, and this Dragon is one of us. So what if we ride this Dragon out of here, laying waste to everything behind us?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin nodded in response to Daz’s question.
source_quote: Thorin nods.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin rushes into the fight alongside Grygum.
source_quote: Grygum rushes into the fight, and so does Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin says, "God, what I wouldn’t do for a bath and listening to whale sounds."
source_quote: The dwarf smiles, "Scented candles!" And then he says, "God, what I wouldn’t do for a bath and listening to whale sounds."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin says, "I want to be my faction."
source_quote: Thorin is exasperated and almost shouts, "I am sorry, I can't deal with these factions. I can't keep track of who we are working for and which faction we are double-crossing. I want to be my faction."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin stared at Gartokkar and said, 'I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?'
source_quote: Thorin stares at him. 'I am just putting all of our cards on the table. So if we get arrested, we will have to tell the Stone Guards about the egg, right?'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin weighs a gold badge given by Gartokkar and asks Daz how much gold it is.
source_quote: Gartokkar hands out some gold badges. Thorin weighs it in his hands. Daz turns to him and asks, "How much gold is this?"

subject: Thorin’s plan to ride Themberchaud
fact: Thorin and Grygum have devised a radical plan to use Themberchaud as a weapon to escape Gracklstugh, destroying everything behind them. This plan represents a direct challenge to Duergar authority, combining rebellion, sacrilege, and strategic violence — a turning point from passive survival to active revolution.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: triple agent status
fact: We are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: I suppose we are double agents, or is it triple agents? We work for the Stone Guards and the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: unauthorized access
fact: Thorin may have entered areas restricted to non-Duergar citizens without proper authorization, even with the passes.
source_quote: Unauthorized Access: Depending on his movements within the city, Thorin may have entered areas restricted to non-Duergar citizens without proper authorization, even with the passes. Any unauthorized access to restricted areas is a violation of city ordinances.

subject: Use of Magic Missiles and Scorching Rays
fact: Daz cast magic missiles and scorching rays during the assassination, using visual sighting and precise targeting; the spells struck the assassins with visible light and heat, but Zalthir’s Darkness concealed the flashes.
source_quote: Motes of light appear above his hand... a silent rush of air accompanies the flight of the magic missiles... the rush of intense heat as the fiery energy is manifested.

subject: Werz Saltbaron’s invisibility
fact: Werz Saltbaron becomes invisible after being healed by Grygum, confirming his identity as a covert operative.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.
source_quote: Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts Darkness to cover the area and hides the flash of Daz’s scorching rays.
source_quote: Zalthir covers the area with Darkness.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir casts Darkness to cover the area and mutters that area-of-effect spells are useful because he can't see.
source_quote: Zalthir covers the area with Darkness. "I can't see. And this is why area of effect spells are useful," he mutters.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds a box of scented candles among the assassins' corpses and passes them to Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir starts to rifle through the assassins' corpses and finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles. He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds a charcoal drawing of the Duergar merchant on one of the assassins' corpses and presents it to him.
source_quote: Zalthir scrutinizes him and concludes that Holl may not have been lying... He presents it to the Duergar.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds coins, bloodstained gloves, and a box of scented candles among the assassins' corpses and passes the candles to Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir starts to rifle through the assassins' corpses and finds some coins, a pair of bloodstained gloves, and a box of candles. He notices they have a pleasant smell and passes them to Thorin.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir hears a body falling into the water and says, "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."
source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water. "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir helps push the second assassin’s corpse into the water.
source_quote: Zalthir agrees and helps push the other body into the water.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir nods in agreement when Grygum says they have people looking for them.
source_quote: Zalthir nods, "Of course."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir offers to create an illusion of whale sounds for Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir chuckles, "I could create that illusion for you."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir overhears Daz and asks Grygum if Themberchaud plays chess, recalling Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs.
source_quote: Zalthir overhears Daz and asks Grygum, "Do you think this dragon also plays chess? According to Milo Goodbarrel’s memoirs, chess played a significant role in negotiating with the metallic dragons."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir reflects that deals with red dragons are never good deals.
source_quote: Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinks Zalthir.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "Convenient," after the Duergar merchant becomes invisible.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible. "Convenient."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinking to himself.
source_quote: Deals with red dragons are never good deals," thinks Zalthir.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "I could create that illusion for you," offering to make whale sounds for Thorin.
source_quote: Zalthir chuckles, "I could create that illusion for you."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."
source_quote: Just then, Zalthir hears a body falling into the water. Grygum has pushed the first corpse into the water. "We must get out of here before the guard shows up."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir watches the Duergar merchant become invisible after thanking them.
source_quote: Zalthir watches as the Duergar becomes invisible.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wonders if Daz is lying about being from Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: Zalthir wonders as well. Daz says he is. But Zalthir isn’t convinced that is the truth.

subject: Duergar
fact: The Duergar are a reclusive subterranean race known for austere living conditions, dark clothing, and occasional displays of hidden wealth, and are suspected of internal conflict and possible involvement in psychic assassinations.
source_quote: The Ghohlbrorn’s Lair... offers the kind of accommodations one could expect from a Duergar: unpleasant, cold, and austere.

subject: Duergar City Watch
fact: The Duergar City Watch is referenced as the entity Thorin attempted to influence and direct during the incident with the stone giant, and whose official duties interference is seen as obstruction.
source_quote: Thorin attempted to influence and direct the actions of the Duergar City Watch during the aforementioned incident with the stone giant.

subject: Duergar City Watch
fact: The Duergar City Watch is the official law enforcement body of Gracklstugh, tasked with maintaining order and enforcing city ordinances. It is viewed as an authoritarian institution that tolerates no interference, and its authority is absolute. Thorin’s attempts to influence its actions are considered obstruction.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a mysterious, possibly outlawed or hidden faction in Gracklstugh, whose existence is suspected but unconfirmed. Gartokkar demands proof of their involvement, indicating they are tied to a larger conspiracy, possibly involving the egg or Themberchaud.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a secretive and dangerous faction responsible for stealing the red dragon egg and creating chaos in the Underdark. They are enemies of the Keepers of the Flame and are actively opposed by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the egg and created a great disturbance in the Underdark.

subject: Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are referenced by Gartokkar as the group whose proof must be found alongside the egg.
source_quote: Gartokkar looks at him, 'Just find me the egg and the proof of the Gray Ghosts.'

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a Duergar psionic order that claims spiritual and political authority over Gracklstugh. They manipulate Themberchaud, orchestrate the theft of the red dragon egg, and use fabricated legal charges to control outsiders.
source_quote: The powers of the Keepers of the Flame derive an equal measure from our psionic abilities, the leadership of the Deepking, and our influence over Themberchaud.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a powerful Duergar religious or political faction within Gracklstugh, associated with divine authority and the suppression of dissent. Thorin’s repeated questioning of their motives has marked him as a threat to their doctrinal control and social hierarchy.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a secretive organization believed to be in possession of a Red Dragon held in peculiar captivity, and are the subject of Grygum and Daz’s intelligence-gathering efforts.
source_quote: Daz wants to learn about the Keepers of the Flame, and Grygum wants to know about this Red Dragon that is kept in some kind of peculiar captivity by the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a secretive, ritualistic order based in the southeastern cave; they are subordinate to Themberchaud but act as the immediate authority over the agents, creating a dual-layered chain of command.
source_quote: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.

subject: Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are referenced as the group Thorin has repeatedly questioned, and whose authority and motives are perceived as dissent and disrespect.
source_quote: Thorin has repeatedly questioned the authority and motives of various Duergar individuals and factions, including the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are an external force to which Grygum claims the group has ties; their existence introduces a third, potentially hostile layer of allegiance, making the group’s position ambiguous and precarious.
source_quote: We have people who will come looking for us!

subject: Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are the official law enforcement of Gracklstugh, tasked with maintaining order and pursuing criminals like Droki. They are manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame and used as a threat against non-Duergar like Thorin.
source_quote: Well we will turn you over to the Stone Guards.

subject: The Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a rogue faction that stole the dragon egg intended to replace Themberchaud, destabilizing the balance of power in Gracklstugh, and are now hunted by both the Keepers of the Flame and the Stone Guards.
source_quote: The Gray Ghosts stole the egg and created a great disturbance in the Underdark.

subject: the Gray Ghosts
fact: The Gray Ghosts are a thieves’ guild that stole the red dragon egg intended to hatch Themberchaud’s replacement, causing a disturbance in the Underdark.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: the Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a psionic faction that controls Themberchaud, believes he works for them, and seeks to replace him with a new dragon hatched from a stolen egg.
source_quote: Themberchaud thinks we work for him. What Themberchaud doesn’t realize is that he works for us.

subject: The Keepers of the Flame
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are a psionic sect in Gracklstugh that secretly control Themberchaud, manipulate agents through holy symbols and coercion, and are locked in a cold war with the Gray Ghosts over the stolen dragon egg meant to replace the current Wyrmsmith.
source_quote: We lost face when the Gray Ghosts stole the valuable red dragon egg that would hatch Themberchaud’s replacement.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is a dragon, likely a red dragon, held in oppressive or exploitative conditions by the Duergar of Gracklstugh. Grygum’s outrage at its treatment and Thorin’s plan to ‘ride it out’ suggest it is not merely a beast but a sentient entity with symbolic or strategic value — possibly a prisoner, weapon, or sacred being.

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Themberchaud is referenced by Grygum as the entity he is appalled at how they treat, and by Gartokkar as one of the city's affairs Thorin is suspected of gathering intelligence on.
source_quote: Grygum smiles, 'As a cleric of Bahamut, I am appalled at how they treat Themberchaud. Let’s do it.' ... Given his questioning and interest in the city's affairs, including the Keepers of the Flame and Themberchaud, Thorin is suspected of espionage...

subject: Themberchaud’s Agents
fact: Themberchaud believes he has recruited the party as his personal agents, but they are unaware they are being manipulated by the Keepers of the Flame, who use his authority as cover for their own agenda — making the party unwitting triple agents.
source_quote: Your first mission is to do whatever the Keepers of the Flame ask you to, but report to Themberchaud first.

subject: Themberchaud’s agents
fact: Themberchaud claims the group as his agents without consent, offering protection in exchange for obedience, but they are unaware he is himself manipulated.
source_quote: I am Themberchaud, and I wish for you to be my agent. And as my agents, you will have my protection.

subject: Themberchaud's Regime
fact: Themberchaud's regime operates as a coercive, personality-driven faction that assumes loyalty, offers protection as a privilege, and demands unquestioning obedience; its power is rooted in terror, illusion of choice, and the exploitation of agents' dependencies.
source_quote: You will have my protection.

subject: The Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are Errde Blackskull’s enforcement arm, tasked with internal security, hunting the Gray Ghosts agent Droki, and suppressing knowledge of psychic assassins — a threat they believe is real but publicly deny.
source_quote: Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, is looking for [Droki].

subject: the Stone Guards
fact: The Stone Guards are led by Errde Blackskull and are searching for Droki, an agent of the Gray Ghosts.
source_quote: This is the same person Errde, Captain of the Stone Guards, is looking for.

subject: Thieve’s Guild
