fact: T'sarran goons are hostile non-noble enforcers associated with House T'sarran, encountered and burned by the party prior to the Duskryn sisters' intervention; they are treated as a tactical hazard rather than a strategic threat.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: T'sarran goons
fact: T'sarran goons are unnamed enforcers or mercenaries loyal to House T'sarran, previously engaged and burned by the party, indicating prior violent conflict and establishing their role as immediate threats.
source_quote: Hired to protect me — specifically, me — from Ilvara's House and from the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning.

subject: T'sarran goons count
fact: Multiple T'sarran goons were present and were burned by the party.
source_quote: the T'sarran goons we'd just finished burning

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is a past event or entity tied to Daz’s escape and subsequent months of running, representing a dangerous encounter or threat in his history.
source_quote: The whole of it — the capture, the escape, Velkynvelve, the months of running — threading back to a single point.

subject: vrock count
fact: Two vrock demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is a deity whose influence is manifest in the pulsing fungal growth that infected Ilvara’s ritual chamber, and whose reach is sensed as a slow, rhythmic corruption.
source_quote: the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach...

subject: Zuggtmoy's fungal growth
fact: Zuggtmoy's fungal growth is a pulsing, slow-rhythmic mass that crept up stone surfaces in Ilvara’s chamber, infused with her reach, and required acid to collapse into ash.
source_quote: the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach, slow and rhythmic like breathing... the fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash...

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a Lolth cleric who declared herself in charge after a chaotic escape, displaying unwavering confidence and divine self-justification, ultimately killed by Zalthir to prevent her from invoking further divine power.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a Lolth cultist who declared herself in charge after surviving chaos, and was killed by Zalthir with the Eldritch Claw Tattoo after a failed grapple by Thorin.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!... I stepped in. The Eldritch Claw Tattoo doesn't announce itself... Asha Vandree did not get another word out.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who became indistinguishable from Zuggtmoy’s rot, and was looted with efficient respect after her theological problem was resolved.
source_quote: So I looted her with the efficient respect one extends to a theological problem that has been resolved.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who became indistinguishable from the rot she served, and was looted with efficient respect after her death.
source_quote: She had been a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who declared herself in charge after surviving chaos, and was silenced by a decisive strike that prevented her from praying, commanding, or cursing. She was contained only as long as her mouth was covered, and her eyes conveyed she was already composing her next prayer.
source_quote: I am blessed by Lolth!

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree was a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.
source_quote: Asha Vandree had been a cleric of Lolth who had also become, in some capacity, a cleric of Zuggtmoy, and in the end she had been indistinguishable from the rot she served.

subject: Blingdenstone
fact: Blingdenstone was the site of a prior ooze crisis that Glabbagool survived, marking it as a significant location in the group’s history and Glabbagool’s endurance.
source_quote: Glabbagool had survived Blingdenstone, the ooze crisis...

subject: Brother Harren
fact: Brother Harren is a former instructor at the monastery who taught a class on decisive action under moral uncertainty, which Zalthir recalls but cannot remember the content of.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Decisive action under moral uncertainty — the ethics of necessary violence, or something like that. I think it was Brother Harren, the one who never sat down, who taught it. I don't remember what he said.

subject: Brother Quellin
fact: Brother Quellin was possibly the one who taught the class on material impermanence — the transience of tools, the attachment to implements, something about a bowl and an empty hand.
source_quote: I think it was Brother Quellin, or possibly the tall one whose name I never quite caught, the one who always had chalk dust on his robe. The transience of tools. The attachment to implements. Something about a bowl and an empty hand.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz accepted that the Duskryn sisters were not entirely wrong to be skeptical of his possible noble lineage.
source_quote: The uncomfortable truth is that they were not entirely wrong to be skeptical.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz acknowledged that he carried unresolved questions about his identity alongside the party’s other burdens.
source_quote: I had an unanswered question about my own identity sitting unresolved in my chest, a pair of Drow mercenaries who found me either fascinating or ridiculous, and a sunblade that had just been persuaded to participate in something it found philosophically objectionable.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz admitted he literally had no idea why there was so much focus on him.
source_quote: I said what I actually believed, which is a thing I do less often than I probably should: 'I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz appreciated that Nym used the past tense when referring to his concern for his safety.
source_quote: I appreciated the past tense. It did a lot of work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that a third 'bravo' is never sincere.
source_quote: Three *bravos*. I have found, as a general principle, that a third *bravo* is never sincere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that asking the obvious question was important because the answer was rarely the obvious answer.
source_quote: You always ask the obvious question, because the answer is rarely the obvious answer.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that someone in Menzoberranzan had paid a lot to keep him alive, and that the anonymity implied the payer had something to hide.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that level of insulation around a financial transaction means exactly one thing: the payer has significant reason not to be associated with the purchase.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believed that the fact someone hired professionals rather than acting directly was the most interesting part of the situation.
source_quote: That last part was the interesting part.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz came through last, the way Daz always came through last, already observing before he was fully present, already composing the analysis before his feet had cleared the threshold.
source_quote: Daz came through last, the way Daz always came through last, already observing before he was fully present, already composing the analysis before his feet had cleared the threshold.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considered himself a nobody — with no house, no lineage, no claim to Drow societal currency.
source_quote: I had no house. No lineage with the right names. No claim on any of the structures that give a Drow life its currency in Menzoberranzan.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz emerged last, already observing and composing analysis before fully exiting, and is directing the group’s next steps toward Candlekeep to research House T'sarran, Jimjar’s disappearance, and his own hidden history — framing decisions as group discussions while subtly guiding them to his conclusions.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry. The decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz's call, framed as a group discussion but with Daz's particular analytical gravity already pulling it toward a conclusion before the conversation began.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz felt he was standing at the edge of the question that changes everything, as described by Milo Goodbarrel.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed away the observation that the two Drow had decided they weren't worth the effort.
source_quote: The two of them hadn't lowered their weapons so much as they'd decided we weren't worth the effort. I filed that away.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed the question of his identity away to return to it at inconvenient moments.
source_quote: I filed the question where I file most things that don't have immediate answers — in the part of my mind that I return to at inconvenient moments — and let the conversation move on.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz had been running a list in the back of his head since Velkynvelve of entities that wanted him dead.
source_quote: I'd been running a list in the back of my head since Velkynvelve — the kind of list you keep when your life depends on knowing who wants what.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a Drow who refuses to accept easy narratives about his identity, preferring to pursue truth through investigation rather than fantasy, and whose quiet dignity contrasts with the skepticism of others.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?... Which was, I thought, the most restrained thing he could possibly have said in that moment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan who studied magic, held private opinions that would have gotten him killed if voiced aloud, and ended up in Velkynvelve's cages alongside a dwarf raised by giants and a dragonborn who doesn't talk much. He is confused about why powerful Drow houses are targeting him with such orchestrated attention, and he does not believe he is a person of consequence.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence. I am a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan who studied magic, held private opinions that would have gotten him killed if voiced aloud, and eventually ended up in Velkynvelve's cages alongside a dwarf raised by giants and a dragonborn who doesn't talk much.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan with no known noble lineage, yet he is the target of a high-value contract orchestrated by House T'sarran, suggesting his true value is hidden or misunderstood.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence... And yet, powerful Drow houses do not spend this kind of resource on nobodies.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan, formerly imprisoned at Velkynvelve, whose mysterious value triggered a high-cost contract from House T'sarran to extract him alive, despite his lack of known lineage or consequence.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence. I am a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan who studied magic, held private opinions that would have gotten him killed if voiced aloud, and eventually ended up in Velkynvelve's cages alongside a dwarf raised by giants and a dragonborn who doesn't talk much.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate with no noble house affiliation and no apparent strategic value, yet was the subject of a costly contract to protect him from Ilvara's House and the T'sarran goons.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a male Drow apostate with no noble house affiliation, no known lineage, and no apparent strategic value in Menzoberranzan, yet someone has paid a significant sum — described as 'they interrupt you, a lot' — to ensure his survival.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a non-noble, background-less Drow who has been the target of a high-value protective contract from an unknown patron in Menzoberranzan, and he is actively questioning why such resources were expended on him.
source_quote: I literally have no idea why there's all this focus on me.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a pragmatic, analytical Drow who avoids emotional displays, treats mysteries as data to be audited, and seeks collective understanding over personal revelation.
source_quote: I think... we should investigate this together. Whatever we find... we split the proceeds.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is an elf with no known noble house affiliation, mysterious background, and sudden appearance prior to a high-value contract to extract him alive and unharmed. He possesses no overt signs of noble lineage but is the target of a contract orchestrated by House T'sarran.
source_quote: So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is reflecting on being protected by an anonymous, powerful entity in Menzoberranzan, and privately realizes he is the unexpected center of a larger, unresolved plot involving his survival and purpose.
source_quote: I considered what remained. Someone in Menzoberranzan had spent generously — *they interrupt you, a lot* — to ensure that a male Drow apostate with no house affiliation and no apparent strategic value survived long enough to do whatever it was I was apparently supposed to do.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz meant seriously when he said, 'We've come a long way.'
source_quote: He said it lightly. He meant it seriously.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Nym and Kaelira regarded him with skepticism that was precise, not cruel.
source_quote: Nym and Kaelira regarded me with the specific expression that Drow reserve for people they find simultaneously interesting and beneath consideration. The tone was sardonic in the way that only people trained in the same school of thought as me can manage — not cruel, just precise.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that Thorin’s use of the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard was an effective tool for negotiating with Dawnbringer.
source_quote: I noted the outburst, noted Thorin's expression — the particular patience of a man who has had this conversation before and expects to have it again — and watched.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that Dawnbringer refused to be used as a religious symbol for purification.
source_quote: I'm not some kind of magical wizard thingy that purifies things. I am a high-quality sunblade. I kill things. I will not be treated like a religious symbol to be used and waved over corrupt—

subject: Daz
fact: Daz possessed the Stonespeaker Crystal and was suspected of drafting journal entries; he led the group’s decision-making regarding the months ahead, steering them toward Candlekeep and research into House T'sarran, Jimjar’s disappearance, and his own hidden history.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz possesses the Stonespeaker Crystal, a key artifact from their Underdark journey, and is using it as part of his ongoing research into the group’s mysteries and his own past.
source_quote: The Stonespeaker Crystal was Daz's. But I noted the response. Filed it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately acknowledges the possibility that his perceived value stems from noble blood he never earned, and finds such speculation embarrassing, preferring any answer to be more interesting than inherited status.
source_quote: I have, privately, catalogued that possibility and found it embarrassing. Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately catalogued the possibility of noble blood as embarrassing and preferred a more interesting answer.
source_quote: I have, privately, catalogued that possibility and found it embarrassing. Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately found Nym's elegant indifference toward Asha reassuring.
source_quote: Nym dismissed it with a kind of elegant indifference that I found, privately, somewhat reassuring.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz privately thought that the entire chain of events might have started because someone decided to be friends with the wrong drow.
source_quote: The thought had a particular shape. Elegant, in the way that retrospective clarity sometimes is. The whole of it — the capture, the escape, Velkynvelve, the months of running — threading back to a single point. Me. A nobody. A nobody that someone in Menzoberranzan had interrupted their schedule over, more than once.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz proposes that the group jointly investigate the mystery of his value, suggesting they audit the financial and contractual records behind the contract to extract him, and offers to split any proceeds.
source_quote: "I think," I said, keeping my voice very even, "that we should investigate this together. Whatever we find — whoever is behind this, whatever they think I'm worth — we split the proceeds. Audit their books. Understand the ledger before anyone decides whether to collect the debt."

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized that until this moment, the list of entities wanting him alive and protected had been empty.
source_quote: Entities with motive to see me alive and sufficiently protected to require hired blades from Menzoberranzan — that list had, until approximately this moment, been empty.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized that Thorin and Dawnbringer’s exchange had the comfortable rhythm of repetition — they had been here before.
source_quote: They had been here before, the dwarf and his sword. They would be here again.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz remained expressionlessly neutral throughout the confrontation, quietly calculating the situation with intense focus, suggesting he was weighing options without committing to any.
source_quote: Daz's face was carefully neutral in the way that meant he was calculating very quickly.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz resolved to investigate his origins together with the party and split any proceeds from the discovery.
source_quote: I think,' I said, keeping my voice very even, 'that we should investigate this together. Whatever we find — whoever is behind this, whatever they think I'm worth — we split the proceeds.'

subject: Daz
fact: Daz thought that Kaelira’s puzzlement was genuine and not theatrical.
source_quote: And then she looked at me, and there was genuine puzzlement in it — not contempt, not theater. Actual, professional confusion at an anomaly that didn't fit the pattern she'd been given.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was cataloguing the room and paying close attention to implications of recovered items.
source_quote: Daz looked over from where he was already cataloguing the rest of the room. Daz was paying attention in the way he pays attention to things — still, cataloguing, already working the implications.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was suspected of already drafting a journal entry while standing in the Overbright.
source_quote: Daz was, I suspected, already drafting a journal entry.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was the subject of a high-value contract by House T'sarran to extract him alive and unharmed, implicating him as a target of significant interest. His true identity remains unknown.
source_quote: There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz wondered why powerful Drow houses would spend so much to extract him, given his lack of consequence.
source_quote: I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence. I am a male Drow apostate from Menzoberranzan... My lineage is not distinguished. My House, if I ever truly had one, is not significant. I do not possess anything worth this level of orchestrated attention.

subject: Daz age
fact: Daz has been a prisoner for fifteen years.
source_quote: fifteen years a prisoner

subject: Daz count
fact: One Drow apostate, Daz, is the subject of the contract.
source_quote: a nobody

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth emerged with the rest of the surviving crew, but her specific actions and reactions are not detailed beyond her presence in the group's transition to the surface.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth was part of the moltley crew that followed, having survived the journey through the Underdark.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Eldeth
fact: Eldeth was part of the moltley crew who survived the journey and emerged after Daz.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool had not been in sunlight before, and his eyes — whatever they were structurally — were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made Zalthir’s response to the Overbright seem measured.
source_quote: He had not been in sunlight before. None of us were entirely sure what Glabbagool's eyes were, from a structural standpoint, but they were wide and present and sweeping across the surface world with an attention that made my own response to the Overbright seem, by comparison, measured.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze, the most improbable relationship any of us had formed in the Underdark.
source_quote: Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze, the most improbable relationship any of us had formed in the Underdark, which was saying something given the competition.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a gelatinous ooze transformed into a grey ooze, experienced sunlight for the first time and reacted with curiosity rather than retreat, his wide, present eyes sweeping the surface world with attention that contrasted with the group’s measured responses.
source_quote: Glabbagool had peered out. There is no other word for it. He peered. He had not been in sunlight before.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the gelatinous ward turned grey ooze and improbable companion, emerged from the bag of holding to experience sunlight for the first time, reacting with wide-eyed curiosity rather than fear — a response that contrasted with the group’s own awe and impressed Zalthir.
source_quote: Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze... had peered out. He had not been in sunlight before. He took it in the way a child takes in a first ocean.

subject: Gorg'Bahamut
fact: Gorg'Bahamut was the narrator's mentor, who would have wanted a pious ritual performed over the dead.
source_quote: My mentor Gorg'Bahamut would have wanted me to.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum attempted to subdue Asha with divine light but missed, and later expressed reluctance to kill, seeking alternatives. He was visibly shaken by the outcome and preferred nonlethal resolution.
source_quote: I don't like killing people if I don't have to.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum attempted to use divine light against Asha Vandree but missed, and later expressed a preference for non-lethal solutions.
source_quote: He leveled something at her — a directed burst of divine light that should have taken her off her feet — and it missed... I would prefer not to kill anyone and was trying very hard to think of an alternative.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Ilvara had not resisted the corruption documented in her prayer book.
source_quote: She had not resisted it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed acknowledging the craft of terrible objects is not the same as endorsing what they served.
source_quote: There is a tradition... of displaying items that are terrible in origin and remarkable in craft, on the theory that acknowledging the craft is not the same as endorsing what the craft served.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the thing that undoes you isn't the opponent you've been studying — it's the thing you didn't know to look for.
source_quote: Sometimes the thing that undoes you isn't the opponent you've been studying — it's the thing you didn't know to look for.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum destroyed the pulsing fungal growth clinging to the platform, using acid to purge Zuggtmoy’s corruption, demonstrating his intolerance for lingering evil.
source_quote: He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter... collapsed into ash in the time it takes to exhale.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum emerged next, blinking with something that looked less like discomfort and more like relief, the earnest half-orc having what appeared to be a genuine spiritual moment with direct sunlight.
source_quote: Grygum next, blinking with something that looked less like discomfort and more like relief, the earnest half-orc having what appeared to be a genuine spiritual moment with direct sunlight.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum feared that Ilvara had written the marginalia herself in a state so altered her handwriting had changed.
source_quote: Or — and this was the reading that settled in my stomach like cold stone — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt the particular weight of irony settle in his chest when holding the jailer's keys.
source_quote: I turned them over in my hands and felt the particular weight of irony settle in my chest.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum had pamphlets on his mind — he would look up the lore of Bahamut, pick up pamphlets, and be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.
source_quote: Grygum had pamphlets on his mind. This was entirely consistent. Grygum was the only one among us who had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read, and Candlekeep was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage. He would look up the lore of Bahamut. He would pick up pamphlets. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum intended to examine Ilvara's prayer book gingerly because it was dangerous.
source_quote: I'll examine it gingerly.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric who examines and documents the relics of Ilvara’s corruption with methodical care, recognizing their significance as evidence of supernatural influence; he takes notes rather than speak, indicating a professional restraint and deep awareness of the danger in the artifacts.
source_quote: I had so much I could have said about any of them. I took notes instead.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a divine caster who attempted to use holy light against Asha Vandree, failed, and later expressed reluctance to kill, preferring alternatives — reflecting his theological ethics and discomfort with lethal force.
source_quote: Let's put a period after that 'now that I'm in charge' thing.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is processing a theological observation about mysterious dispensations and later shows thoughtful consideration when Daz proposes auditing the books, indicating his reflective nature.
source_quote: Grygum was probably filing away some theological observation about mysterious dispensations. ... Grygum looked thoughtful, which is his equivalent.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the individual who dealt with the platform and used acid to destroy the fungal growth infused with Zuggtmoy’s reach, collapsing it into ash.
source_quote: Behind me, Grygum was dealing with the platform... Grygum was not the sort to leave corruption breathing. He opened his mouth, and the acid came out clean and decisive, and the fungal matter that had spent months becoming something wrong collapsed into ash...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum looked thoughtful when Daz suggested auditing the books of the mysterious payer.
source_quote: No one laughed. Grygum looked thoughtful, which is his equivalent.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that the marginalia in Ilvara's prayer book were in a different hand, indicating a second mind at work.
source_quote: A different hand. That detail mattered to me more than any of the specific words.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum opened the bag of holding just enough to allow Glabbagool to peer out, and later engaged in what appeared to be sincere prayer, while also accumulating pamphlets and planning to research Bahamut’s lore at Candlekeep.
source_quote: Grygum had opened the bag of holding just enough, and Glabbagool — our companion, our gelatinous ward who was now a grey ooze — had peered out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled seeing similar handwriting in a merchant who had been Tongued by a bardic curse.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum suspected the wax pouch was the more interesting item after taking it from Asha Vandree's body.
source_quote: I had the wax pouch, and I suspected it was the more interesting item.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought of Stroud sitting across from Protanther and realized even long preparation can leave blind spots.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the Living Serpent Head Scourge was a great museum piece.
source_quote: The Living Serpent Head Scourge sounds... It sounds like a great museum piece.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the ambiguity of whether Ilvara knew she wasn't resisting her corruption was the most troubling part.
source_quote: That ambiguity was the most troubling part.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the keys would have been very useful at the very beginning.
source_quote: You know, they would have been very useful in the very beginning,

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the theological text in the wax pouch was tedious and boring (being diplomatic).
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration... It's very tedious and boring.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that the prayer book told him things he did not want to know.
source_quote: It told me things I did not want to know.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was probably filing away a theological observation about mysterious dispensations.
source_quote: Grygum was probably filing away some theological observation about mysterious dispensations.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was very tired immediately after reading the contents of the wax pouch.
source_quote: I was right. I was also, immediately, very tired.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum wondered whether the theological text was pre-craziness or post-craziness.
source_quote: Is this pre-craziness or post-craziness, do you think?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum, the earnest half-orc, experienced a genuine spiritual moment in direct sunlight, opened the bag of holding, and is now focused on acquiring pamphlets and lore about Bahamut at Candlekeep, treating the Great Library as both research and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was doing something with his hands that was probably prayer and probably sincere. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets. This was Grygum.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara collected the tooth of Thorin as a trophy to assert power over captives, using it as evidence of her dominance, and anchored a corrupted fungal mass as part of a ritual.
source_quote: Ilvara had made a point of collecting trophies... she'd taken my tooth... as a ritual anchor.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara had been carrying Thorin’s tooth around the Underdark as a trophy of ownership.
source_quote: she had been carrying his tooth around the Underdark. She had collected it like a curiosity.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a High Priestess who built an elevated ritual site, used fungal growth as a conduit for Zuggtmoy’s influence, collected trophies including Thorin’s tooth, and became something that served two masters and understood neither.
source_quote: Ilvara had built herself something elevated, which made a certain kind of sense — High Priestesses don't stand at floor level, they stand at the level where everyone has to look up at them... the fungal growth that had crept up the stone was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach... Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a High Priestess who built rituals around a fused sigil of Lolth and Zuggtmoy, indicating her devotion to two conflicting deities. She is now dead, her madness made physical in the stitched cloth found in the chamber.
source_quote: It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth subverted by Zuggtmoy, whose prayer book documented a slow, ambiguous corruption through marginalia in a second handwriting.
source_quote: The marginalia told the story... Two hands because two minds had been working the same pen.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.
source_quote: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth who had been actively subverted by Zuggtmoy.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was a high priestess of Lolth, ambitious and politically dangerous, who was subtly and irreversibly corrupted by Zuggtmoy; she did not resist the influence and may not have recognized her own transformation, as evidenced by the evolving marginalia in her prayer book.
source_quote: She had not resisted it. I could not tell from the text whether she had known she wasn't resisting or whether she had genuinely believed she was still moving in her own direction. That ambiguity was the most troubling part.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, a High Priestess, used a fungal mass as a ritual anchor and wove Lolth’s web into Zuggtmoy’s sigil on a cloth artifact, revealing her dual allegiance and descent into madness.
source_quote: It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara, a high priestess, had been carrying confiscated prisoner belongings, including Thorin's tooth, as trophies of ownership.
source_quote: Ilvara had been carrying it. Of course she had — she was exactly the sort of high priestess who would keep trophies, who would drag along evidence of her ownership of people the way some clerics keep relics.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira applauded the killing of Asha Vandree with deliberate, mocking praise, framing it as proof that Asha wasn’t completely defenseless — her tone implying the act was necessary and long overdue.
source_quote: Well done, well done, well done! See, he wasn't completely defenseless.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a Drow mercenary from House Duskryn, co-hired with Nym to protect Daz; she is analytically sharp, visibly puzzled by the anomaly of Daz’s value, and uninterested in self-mythologizing narratives, yet acknowledges the financial weight behind his protection.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery... Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a Drow mercenary who expresses professional puzzlement at the scale of expenditure on Daz’s protection, noting that his lack of lineage makes the payment inexplicable.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody. Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a calm, professional Drow sister who analyzes evidence with detached precision and offers brutally honest assessments, prioritizing duty over speculation.
source_quote: Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is a professional, reserved investigator who analyzes evidence without speculation. She prioritizes facts over theory and acknowledges the limits of their mandate.
source_quote: Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is one of the Duskryn sisters, hired through cutouts to extract Daz, and she regards him with a mixture of interest and condescension. She has seen the performance of self-deluded Drow claiming noble lineage before and finds it sardonic.
source_quote: They had opinions, the sisters, about mysterious orphans who arrive at adulthood convinced they have noble blood waiting somewhere. They had seen this particular performance before, apparently.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is one of the Duskryn sisters, who is still and professional, reading burned documents with focused precision, and states the most honest thing in the chamber: they are not paid to think too hard.
source_quote: Kaelira was the opposite — still and professional, reading the burned pages with the focus of someone who was paid to be good at exactly this... "Perhaps, but we're not paid to think that hard."

subject: Kaelira Duskryn
fact: Kaelira Duskryn is a Drow mercenary who, alongside her sister Nym, was contracted to protect Daz; she expresses professional confusion at the inexplicable scale of investment in a non-noble outsider and dismisses Daz's self-mythologizing as typical drow delusion.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is a halfling author whose writings Daz has read extensively; his phrase 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything' resonates with Daz’s current existential realization.
source_quote: He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is a halfling whose book contains the phrase 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything,' which the narrator associates with his current existential state.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it 'standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.'

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, a halfling whose writings Daz has read extensively, coined the phrase *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything* to describe the feeling of being at the center of a pivotal, self-referential plot.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel, that relentlessly hopeful halfling whose book I'd read too many times to admit, had a phrase for the sensation I was experiencing. He called it *standing at the edge of the question that changes everything.*

subject: Nym
fact: Nym criticized Thorin’s grapple as tactically naive against a Lolth cleric, asserting that the only proper response is to sever the head with a blade. She expressed disbelief at the party’s survival given their flawed tactics.
source_quote: When attacking a cleric of Lolth, one does not just simply grapple them. One takes your blade and cuts their heads off.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a Drow mercenary from House Duskryn, hired to protect Daz from House Mizzrym and House T'sarran, who speaks with the practiced tone of Menzoberranzan’s elite, displays professional detachment, and dismisses theological threats as irrelevant to her contract.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a Drow mercenary who speaks with the tone of Menzoberranzan’s natural courtesy, dismisses threats with elegant indifference, and states that the contract terms were to prevent other drow factions from killing Daz.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is a sharp, expressive Drow sister who is deeply skeptical of Daz’s mysterious origins and dismissive of noble bloodline theories, yet professionally engaged in the investigation.
source_quote: That is an excellent question... Do you have daddy issues? Do you have mommy issues? Every drow thinks there's some noble things.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is an expressive, skeptical individual who questions Daz’s origins and dismisses the idea of hidden noble lineage as a common delusion among drow. She is irritated by the scale of the contract and the lack of transparency.
source_quote: That is an excellent question. You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up, and all of a sudden, we're contracted to protect a nobody.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is one of the Duskryn sisters, hired through cutouts to extract Daz, and she regards him with a mixture of interest and condescension. She has seen the performance of self-deluded Drow claiming noble lineage before and finds it sardonic.
source_quote: They had opinions, the sisters, about mysterious orphans who arrive at adulthood convinced they have noble blood waiting somewhere. They had seen this particular performance before, apparently.

subject: Nym
fact: Nym is one of the Duskryn sisters, whose face grows more expressive when irritated, and who is skeptical of Daz’s possible noble origins, dismissing them as typical orphan fantasies.
source_quote: Nym had the kind of face that gets more expressive the more irritated she becomes, and right now she was very expressive... "Yes, yes, yes, that's what every orphan thinks. Do you have daddy issues? Do you have mommy issues? Every drow thinks there's some noble things."

subject: Nym Duskryn
fact: Nym Duskryn is a Drow mercenary hired in Menzoberranzan to protect Daz from House Ilvara and House T'sarran, and she dismisses the threat of a low-level Lolth cultist as irrelevant to the contract's value.
source_quote: Our terms of our contract were to make sure that the other drow factions didn't get you killed.

subject: party member count
fact: Eight individuals emerged from the tunnel: the narrator, Thorin, Grygum, Daz, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and two others.
source_quote: The others emerged around me. Thorin first... Grygum next... Daz came through last... The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks

subject: prisoners count
fact: Ten other prisoners are held in the dungeon.
source_quote: ten other prisoners

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther was the subject of Stroud’s long preparation and eventual blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait emerged with the group, but no specific actions, dialogue, or reactions are described beyond being part of the surviving crew.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait was part of the moltley crew that followed, having survived the journey through the Underdark.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait was part of the moltley crew who survived the journey and emerged after Daz.
source_quote: The rest of our moltley crew followed, Eldeth, Spiderbait, and the rest of the folks who had survived this journey.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud sat down across from Protanther after four hundred years of preparation and still had a blind spot.
source_quote: I thought, briefly, of Stroud sitting down across from Protanther. Four hundred years of preparation. Still had a blind spot.

subject: Stroud's preparation duration
fact: Stroud had been preparing for four hundred years before his blind spot was exposed.
source_quote: Four hundred years of preparation

subject: The Narrator
fact: The Narrator made the decisive, irreversible choice to kill Asha Vandree with a precise, monastic strike that silenced her before she could cast. They acted without hesitation, acknowledging their action as necessary and morally unambiguous, unlike the others’ indecision.
source_quote: Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to retain the services of the Duskryn sisters after their contract was fulfilled, asking about cost — a request met with a definitive refusal that implied their fee was beyond the party's means.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, tried to retain them. He asked what it would cost. Nym's answer was three words and they landed like a portcullis.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue Asha Vandree with a grapple and hand over her mouth, but was corrected by Nym for failing to kill a Lolth cleric properly.
source_quote: I also put my hand across her mouth so she can't talk, so... When attacking a cleric of Lolth, one does not just simply grapple them.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue Asha Vandree with a grapple, clamping his hand over her mouth to prevent spellcasting, but failed to neutralize the threat permanently. He later claimed he could have killed her if he wanted to, revealing his moral hesitation.
source_quote: I could have taken her out if I wanted to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin carried Dawnbringer and contemplated its suffering through months of darkness, seeking a 'sword whisperer' to tend to the blade, and calculated the sun’s position relative to the year while standing still at the surface’s edge.
source_quote: Thorin, characteristically, was thinking about Dawnbringer... He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considered Daz’s response to Nym’s skepticism to be the most restrained thing he could have said.
source_quote: Daz looked at her with something behind his eyes that I couldn't quite read. He let a beat pass, and then he said: 'So then maybe there's more to me than meets the eye?' Which was, I thought, the most restrained thing he could possibly have said in that moment.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin decided the necromantic pearl was necromantic, based on its sensation, like the smell from a giant's larder.
source_quote: I decided, necromantic, the same way you decide the smell coming from the back of a giant's larder means something died in there a while ago.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin emerged first, as he always led from the front, always had, it was as close to instinct as that dwarf ever got.
source_quote: Thorin first, which was correct — he always led from the front, always had, it was as close to instinct as that dwarf ever got.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt recognition and then something quieter beneath it when Grygum mentioned his tooth.
source_quote: Thorin looked up. Something shifted in his face — recognition, and then something quieter beneath it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt the bundle of ritual items was not equipment but evidence of Ilvara's madness.
source_quote: It wasn't equipment. It was evidence. It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt the debt of his stolen tooth was now settled because he had recovered it.
source_quote: It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had his tooth collected as a trophy by Ilvara, and reclaimed it from her confiscated belongings after recognizing its significance.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back. He held it for a moment without saying anything.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin had mentioned a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with dwarvish seriousness that meant he believed this person existed and should be found.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about, which meant he believed this person existed and should be found.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intended to keep silent about the significance of the tooth and the pearl because speaking would add nothing to the next ten seconds.
source_quote: I didn't say any of that out loud. Thorin Giantfriend, radical transparency, except when the thing being said wouldn't add anything to the next ten seconds.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intended to take the necromantic pearl because he would not leave anything useful in the cavern.
source_quote: I didn't need a name for it. It was worth something to the right buyer, and I was not going to leave anything useful in this cavern, so I pocketed it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf who travels with the sentient sunblade Dawnbringer and has developed a patient, repetitive negotiation dynamic with it. He uses the Vaultmaster Locking Scabbard as a diplomatic tool to manage the blade’s objections.
source_quote: Thorin reached, unhurriedly, for the scabbard. "Do I need to show you the scabbard again?"

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a member of the party who attempted to subdue Asha Vandree via grapple, believing non-lethal restraint sufficient, but was corrected by the Drow mercenaries for misunderstanding the lethal nature of Lolth clerics.
source_quote: I could have taken her out if I wanted to." ... "I don't like killing people if I don't have to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is displaying his characteristic contemplative stance, hesitating between action and stillness as he weighs the next move in a situation that demands careful judgment.
source_quote: Thorin had that look he gets — the one where he's deciding whether to charge at the problem or stand very still and wait for it to explain itself.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin led the group out of the tunnel, always instinctively at the front, and is now contemplating the history of Dawnbringer — a sword forged for radiance that endured prolonged darkness — and seeking a 'sword whisperer' to restore its connection to light.
source_quote: Thorin stood with his face at an angle that suggested he was calculating the sun's position relative to the year. He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realized the signet ring and documents proved House T'sarran had contracted to extract Daz alive.
source_quote: The documents were worse. What was left of them... confirmed what we'd been trying to piece together since the mage had arrived with her mercenary escort. There had been a contract. Extract Daz alive and unharmed. House T'sarran behind it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin reclaimed his tooth from Ilvara's collection and remarked on its sentimental value.
source_quote: 'Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.' He held it for a moment without saying anything. Then: 'Very sentimental.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to kill Asha Vandree without necessity, stating he didn't like killing people if he didn't have to.
source_quote: I don't like killing people if I don't have to," Thorin said. "I mean, you know...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to pray over the dead soldiers of House Mizzrym because he had nothing to say to them.
source_quote: I didn't pray over them. They'd come here doing what they were told by someone who had already lost her mind, and I had nothing to say to them that wasn't just 'better luck in another life.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembered Ilvara taking his tooth at Velkynvelve as a trophy and a symbol of power.
source_quote: When we'd first found ourselves hanging in nets at Velkynvelve, Ilvara had made a point of collecting trophies. It was the kind of thing a person does when they want their captives to understand the power relation clearly — she'd taken my tooth.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin tried to retain the Drow sisters and asked what it would cost.
source_quote: Thorin, to his credit, tried to retain them. He asked what it would cost.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understood the necromantic pearl was not in the wrong place by accident — someone had placed it there.
source_quote: The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted his tooth back after Grygum mentioned it.
source_quote: Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin was thinking about Dawnbringer — what it had been through, months of darkness, a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.
source_quote: Thorin, characteristically, was thinking about Dawnbringer. Not what to do with it; he would never give it up, and the sword would never go quietly. But what it had been through. Months of darkness, months of the deep, a blade whose nature was radiance forced to endure the complete absence of the thing it was built to carry.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin’s tooth had been taken and carried by Ilvara as a trophy of ownership.
source_quote: 'like your tooth, Thorin.'... Oh, yeah. I want my tooth back.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend is a man of radical transparency who chooses silence when speech adds nothing to the next ten seconds, and who carries the necromantic pearl and his reclaimed tooth as symbols of a journey from captivity to agency.
source_quote: Thorin Giantfriend, radical transparency, except when the thing being said wouldn't add anything to the next ten seconds... I didn't say any of that out loud.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend is carrying the necromantic pearl and the recovered tooth, having reclaimed them from Ilvara's ritual anchor and trophies, and is now preparing to clear the next chamber.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket... I had the tooth back. And I had the pearl that had been buried in the heart of whatever she'd turned this place into.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend is referenced as the radical transparency practitioner who recovered a necromantic pearl from the heart of Ilvara’s corrupted fungal ritual site and reclaimed his own tooth, the trophy she took during his capture at Velkynvelve.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket. I'd already turned over the question of what it meant — something this finished, this dense, at the core of a corrupted fungal mass that Ilvara had been using as a ritual anchor... I had the tooth back. And I had the pearl that had been buried in the heart of whatever she'd turned this place into.

subject: Thorin Giantfriend
fact: Thorin Giantfriend recovered a necromantic pearl from the heart of Ilvara's corrupted fungal ritual site and reclaimed his stolen tooth, marking the beginning and escalation of the corruption they faced.
source_quote: I had the necromantic pearl in one pocket... I had the tooth back. And I had the pearl that had been buried in the heart of whatever she'd turned this place into.

subject: Thorin's age or tenure
fact: Thorin has carried stranger things out of stranger places in the last several months.
source_quote: I've carried stranger things out of stranger places in the last several months

subject: Thorin's imprisonment duration
fact: Thorin has been a prisoner for fifteen years.
source_quote: fifteen years a prisoner

subject: Tongued merchant
fact: A merchant once known to the narrator had been Tongued by a bardic curse, producing correspondence eerily similar to Ilvara’s marginalia.
source_quote: I had seen something like this before, in a completely different context — a merchant I once knew who had been Tongued by a bardic curse, whose correspondence from that period was eerily similar.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir agreed with the group’s decision to spend their gold on adventuring gear rather than business ventures.
source_quote: We agreed on the gear.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed that Thorin's reluctance, Nym and Kaelira's calculation, Grygum's preference for alternatives, and Daz's neutrality were all reasonable and true.
source_quote: All of it was reasonable. All of it was true. I just happened to also be true.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the monastery curriculum’s focus on non-combat topics had not worked itself out for him.
source_quote: It had not, in fact, worked itself out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not look at Asha's body after killing her.
source_quote: I didn't look at the body.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir emerged into the Overbright after months of Underdark travel, having stopped trusting the surface world would be real, and now observes the group's reactions with quiet analysis, noting the transformation in others and himself.
source_quote: I stood and let the light happen to me. I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir felt the sunlight was a kind of violence, not pain, but the body registering that something fundamental had changed.
source_quote: what I felt when it touched my face was a kind of violence, or close to it. Not pain. Just the body registering that something fundamental had changed, the same way a deep-water creature might register the pressure dropping.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found Glabbagool’s curiosity toward the surface world admirable, though he would not say it out loud.
source_quote: I found that admirable in a way I was not going to say out loud.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had been thinking about the Overbright intermittently for months, not with anticipation but like a theory he had not yet been able to test.
source_quote: I had been thinking about this moment, intermittently, for months. Not with anticipation exactly — anticipation implies you trust the thing to happen. More the way you might think about a theory you have not yet been able to test.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had no opinion on sword whisperers but noted the category and moved on.
source_quote: I had no opinion on sword whisperers. I noted the category and moved on.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had stopped counting steps around the third hour of climbing because counting had started to feel like superstition, and had stopped trusting the Overbright would be real — but it was real.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had stopped trusting that the Overbright would be real.
source_quote: I had stopped trusting it would be real.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a Drow who made the decisive call to kill Asha Vandree using the Eldritch Claw Tattoo, believing someone had to act when others hesitated.
source_quote: I'm making a call... I stepped in... Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a combat-trained individual with an Eldritch Claw Tattoo, who decisively killed Asha Vandree to neutralize a clerical threat, acting when others hesitated, and accepting the moral weight of the choice without justification.
source_quote: I'm making a call." ... "I didn't look at the body.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is quietly observing the unfolding situation, embodying a passive but perceptive presence without verbal or active intervention.
source_quote: Zalthir, characteristically, was simply watching.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the one who stopped counting steps around the third hour of climbing because counting had started to feel like superstition, like measuring distance against the possibility of failure.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew Grygum had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read and would treat Candlekeep as both research and pilgrimage.
source_quote: Grygum was the only one among us who had accumulated a list of things he wanted to read, and Candlekeep was going to be, for him, something between research and pilgrimage. He would look up the lore of Bahamut. He would pick up pamphlets. He would be genuinely delighted by the availability of pamphlets.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in sunlight.
source_quote: I knew that Drow cloaks disintegrated in the sunlight.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir made the decision to kill Asha Vandree because he believed someone had to make the call.
source_quote: I'm making a call," I said. ... I just happened to also be true. Someone had to make the call. I made it. That's all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled a saying from the Garden Shadow about the most dangerous person being the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: I've read rooms like this before. The Garden Shadow had a saying — or possibly Brother Quellin did, the one with the dusty robes who taught something about pressure points of social authority ... that the most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered Thorin’s serious belief in the existence of a sword whisperer for Dawnbringer.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up, delivered with the particular dwarvish seriousness that Thorin applied to things he actually cared about, which meant he believed this person existed and should be found.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembered a class on decisive action under moral uncertainty taught by Brother Harren, though he didn't recall what was said.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Decisive action under moral uncertainty — the ethics of necessary violence, or something like that. I think it was Brother Harren, the one who never sat down, who taught it. I don't remember what he said. I remember it went on for a long time.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at the sky, having survived the Underdark and now facing the unknown with measured observation, noting the actions of others without voicing his own opinions.
source_quote: I stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything I had navigated in months, and I thought: this is where we were going.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stopped counting steps because counting had started to feel like superstition, as if he were measuring distance against the possibility of failure.
source_quote: I had stopped counting the steps somewhere around the third hour of climbing — not because I lost track, but because counting had started to feel like superstition, like I was measuring the distance against the possibility of failure.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought Asha's confidence was the problem because she had already decided she'd won.
source_quote: She said it with the absolute confidence of someone who had just survived something she shouldn't have — chaos, screaming, close calls that she'd already reframed as divine favor — and that confidence was the problem. *Excellent! Now that I am in charge!* ... Asha had already decided.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought, as he stood at the tunnel’s mouth, that they had made it — and now there was everything else.
source_quote: I stood at the entrance to the surface world, squinting at a sky that went farther than anything I had navigated in months, and I thought: this is where we were going. We had made it. Now there was everything else.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree's body without objection.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow — and I did not begrudge him that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree's body, and Grygum did not begrudge him that.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing... and I did not begrudge him that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir took the Drow cloak from Asha Vandree’s body.
source_quote: Zalthir took the Drow cloak she'd been wearing — the fine spider-silk kind that drinks shadow.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz’s call, framed as a group discussion but pulled by Daz’s analytical gravity.
source_quote: The decision about what to do with the months was largely Daz's call, framed as a group discussion but with Daz's particular analytical gravity already pulling it toward a conclusion before the conversation began.

subject: Ilvara's marginalia
fact: The marginalia in Ilvara's prayer book showed a gradual shift from formal prayer to associative, unstructured writing, indicating psychological corruption.
source_quote: Then, gradually, around the margins, a second voice crept in. Less structured. More associative. The sentences didn't always end. Some of them were questions that answered themselves with other questions.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book is a standard Lolth prayer book with marginalia in a different hand, documenting the gradual corruption by Zuggtmoy; the early entries are formal and liturgical, but the marginalia become associative, fragmented, and self-answering, indicating a shift in consciousness.
source_quote: It told me things I did not want to know. The marginalia told the story. A different hand. Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book was a standard Lolth devotional text with marginalia in a different hand, documenting her corruption timeline.
source_quote: The main text was a standard Lolth prayer book — the kind of thing they give to promising young acolytes in the outer sanctums of any major drow religious house. The marginalia told the story. A different hand. That detail mattered to me more than any of the specific words.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book

subject: Ilvara's tooth

source_quote: It was the kind of thing a person does when they want their captives to understand the power relation clearly — she'd taken my tooth. A chip broken off in the capture, displayed in her chest like a piece of evidence of what she could do... It was settled now. I had the tooth back.

Inside: incense cones, a silver bowl small enough to fit in one hand, and a cloth that had been stitched with two sigils — Lolth's web worked into the eight-fold geometry of Zuggtmoy's mark, one woven inside the other.

source_quote: Smooth. Dense. Fist-sized. The weight of it was wrong for something grown — too even, too finished, like a stone that had been worked by a hand that knew what it was doing.

subject: necromantic pearl

source_quote: something this finished, this dense, at the core of a corrupted fungal mass... The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it.

subject: necromantic pearl
fact: The necromantic pearl is a smooth, dense, fist-sized object, unnaturally finished like a worked stone, found at the core of the fungal mass in the chamber once used by Ilvara as a ritual anchor, radiating a necromantic sensation akin to standing before a door to an unwanted room.
source_quote: Smooth. Dense. Fist-sized. The weight of it was wrong for something grown — too even, too finished, like a stone that had been worked by a hand that knew what it was doing. And the sensation coming off it wasn't heat or cold exactly. More like standing next to a door that opens into a room you don't want to know about. Necromantic, I decided...

fact: Daz intends to uncover the truth about why he was targeted, even if the answer is not noble blood.
source_quote: Whatever the answer to this question turns out to be, I prefer it to be something more interesting than inherited blood I didn't earn.

subject: Daz's identity and targeting
fact: Daz is unresolved about why he is being targeted by powerful, anonymous Drow forces. He questions whether his perceived value is real or imagined, and whether his lineage or past actions are the cause — a mystery that remains unexplained and emotionally burdensome.
source_quote: I had no idea why. I am not, by any meaningful measure, a person of consequence... And yet.

subject: Daz's purpose
fact: Daz is the unexpected focal point of a larger scheme — someone in Menzoberranzan intervened repeatedly to ensure his survival, but his ultimate purpose remains unknown.
source_quote: to ensure that a male Drow apostate with no house affiliation and no apparent strategic value survived long enough to do whatever it was I was apparently supposed to do.

subject: Daz's true identity
fact: Daz's origins are completely unknown, and his sudden appearance alongside a high-value protective contract has led the Duskryn sisters to suspect either a noble house game or his own self-delusion — but the truth remains unconfirmed.
source_quote: Yes, yes, yes, that's what every orphan thinks. Do you have daddy issues? Do you have mommy issues? Every drow thinks there's some noble things.

subject: Daz's true identity
fact: Daz’s mysterious value to House T'sarran, despite his apparent insignificance, creates an unresolved thread about his origins, potential hidden lineage, or undisclosed role.
source_quote: The gap between what I know about myself and what someone apparently believes about me was large enough to be, frankly, concerning.

subject: Daz's true identity
fact: Daz’s origins are completely unknown. He has no noble lineage, no documented background, and yet he was the target of a high-stakes contract by a powerful house. His true identity and why he was targeted remain unresolved.
source_quote: You don't belong to any noble house, your background is a complete mystery, you suddenly show up...

subject: duration of journey
fact: The exact duration of the journey through Velkynvelve, Gracklstugh, the Darklake, and Blingdenstone is unknown — the narrator cannot tell how many months it had been.
source_quote: I genuinely cannot tell you how many months it had been.

subject: House Mizzrym's concern
fact: House Mizzrym's sealed orders revealed frantic concern over Ilvara's disappearance, unaware of her corruption.
source_quote: Where are you? What have you been doing? Respond — kind of thing. You've gone missing. Followed by more frantic: where are you, where are you?

subject: House T'sarran's motive
fact: The reason House T'sarran sought to extract Daz alive — rather than kill him — is unknown. Their motive, beyond the contract, and their connection to the mage and the chamber’s events, remain unexplained.
source_quote: Somebody had spent a significant amount of gold to ensure that the elf standing to my left made it out of this cavern breathing.

subject: identity of the marginalia writer
fact: It is unclear whether the second handwriting in Ilvara’s prayer book was her own altered self or an external influence, leaving the nature of her corruption unresolved.
source_quote: Someone else had written in her prayer book. Or — she had written in it herself but in a state so altered that the handwriting had changed.

subject: Ilvara's corruption
fact: Ilvara's corruption timeline was legible in the marginalia of her prayer book, showing a gradual shift from normal devotion to altered thinking.
source_quote: The corruption timeline was legible if you knew how to read it. Ilvara had been normal... and then something had found the edge of her and started pulling.

subject: Ilvara's dual devotion
fact: Ilvara’s fusion of Lolth and Zuggtmoy’s sigils suggests a heretical synthesis of two opposing deities. The implications of her transformation and whether she was acting alone or under external influence are unresolved.
source_quote: It was Ilvara's madness made physical — the thing she'd built her rituals around while she was becoming something that served two masters and understood neither.

subject: Ilvara's dual worship
fact: Ilvara’s fusion of Lolth and Zuggtmoy in ritual artifacts suggests a deeper, unexplained syncretic heresy that may extend beyond her personal madness.
source_quote: She'd been using as a ritual anchor... and the fungal growth... was still pulsing with Zuggtmoy's reach.

subject: Jimjar's disappearance
fact: Jimjar vanished under mysterious circumstances linked to House T'sarran and the Duskryns — his fate is a key unknown the group seeks to unravel at Candlekeep, possibly tied to Daz’s own past.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance and whatever the various cutouts and hired Duskryns were ultimately pointing at regarding Daz's own history

subject: Jimjar's Disappearance
fact: Jimjar’s fate remains unknown, linked to House T'sarran and the Duskryns, and is a central mystery motivating the group’s research at Candlekeep.
source_quote: research into House T'sarran and Jimjar's disappearance...

subject: moral uncertainty in lethal action
fact: The party’s division over whether to kill Asha Vandree — between necessity, mercy, and tactical ignorance — remains unresolved. Each perspective is reasonable, but none is sufficient to prevent future crises.
source_quote: All of it was reasonable. All of it was true. I just happened to also be true.

subject: mystery patron
fact: An unknown patron in Menzoberranzan has paid a substantial sum to contract the Duskryn sisters to protect Daz, a non-noble individual with no known lineage — raising the question of why such resources were allocated to him.
source_quote: Do you know how much money that required us to get, for us to do? A lot. Like, they interrupt you. A lot.

subject: Neverlight Grove's missed meeting
fact: The letter from Neverlight Grove confirmed Ilvara's political alliance had dissolved because she was lost to Zuggtmoy's influence.
source_quote: A missed meeting. Political correspondence that had gone nowhere, because the person it was addressed to had gone somewhere else — somewhere a Demon Queen's influence had been a stronger pull than any political alliance.

subject: origin of Ilvara’s corruption
fact: The source of Ilvara’s subversion remains unknown — whether induced by another entity or self-initiated through altered consciousness — and the ambiguity is deeply troubling.
source_quote: I could not tell from the text whether she had known she wasn't resisting or whether she had genuinely believed she was still moving in her own direction.

subject: out of the dark and into the darkness
fact: The party has moved from one state of obscurity into another, with no clear resolution or destination yet identified.
source_quote: Chapter 49: Out of the dark and into the darkness.

subject: pre-craziness or post-craziness
fact: It is uncertain whether the author of the theological treatise wrote it before or after descending into madness.
source_quote: Is this pre-craziness or post-craziness, do you think?

subject: Sword Whisperer
fact: Thorin’s belief in the existence of a 'sword whisperer' to restore Dawnbringer is an unfulfilled thread, suggesting a future quest to locate this specialist and heal the sword’s suffering.
source_quote: He had mentioned something about a specialist — the phrase *sword whisperer* had come up...

subject: the identity of the anonymous patron
fact: An anonymous, powerful entity in Menzoberranzan has funded Daz's survival through cutouts, ensuring even hired blades don't know who paid — creating a central unresolved mystery driving the plot.
source_quote: They had done this anonymously. Through cutouts. In a manner that ensured even the hired blades didn't know who was paying.

subject: the monastery curriculum
fact: Zalthir recalls a forgotten lesson on material impermanence — possibly taught by Brother Quellin or a chalk-dusted instructor — that emphasized detachment from tools, a philosophical undercurrent that contrasts with the group’s reliance on gear and artifacts.
source_quote: There was a class for this. Some form of material impermanence — I think it was Brother Quellin... Something about a bowl and an empty hand.

subject: The necromantic pearl
fact: Thorin suspects the pearl is a key to understanding Ilvara’s ritual corruption, but has not yet named its origin.
source_quote: The pearl wasn't in the wrong place by accident. Someone had put something like it there, or something like it had grown there because the conditions were exactly right for it. Either answer was a problem that needed a name.

subject: theological implications of Lolth-Zuggtmoy unity
fact: The treatise claiming Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same entity challenges the foundations of drow theology and may represent a new, dangerous heresy.
source_quote: It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad.

subject: theological treatise on Lolth and Zuggtmoy
fact: A written theological treatise argues that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same being — a conclusion reached by backward reasoning from a desired doctrine, considered both well-argued and completely mad.
source_quote: It's basically a long theological exploration of why Zuggtmoy and Lolth — and claiming that Lolth and Zuggtmoy are the same thing... It was very well-argued. It was also completely mad.

subject: the origin of the plot
fact: The entire sequence — capture, escape, Velkynvelve, months of running — may have originated from an unexpected act of solidarity: someone in Menzoberranzan decided to befriend or protect a nobody.
source_quote: for all you know, the reason this all got started was because they all decided to be friends with the wrong drow.

subject: the purpose of the necromantic pearl
