subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is referenced by the narrator as producing an unrecognizable impression of a bird — the sound of a bag of wet sand dropped from a significant height while being squeezed — and asking, 'Is it a kind of ooze?'
source_quote: He was very proud of it. 'Is it a kind of ooze?' he asked, in that way he has, earnest and completely serious about the question.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool observes the sun and gives simple, deceptively profound directional guidance, embodying quiet wisdom.
source_quote: West, she said. Head west and you'll hit Candlekeep. Simple as that, the way she says most things that aren't simple at all.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool was witnessing the sun with a stillness that was not his usual passive state.
source_quote: Glabbagool just looked up... and there was something in the stillness of him that wasn't his usual stillness. He wasn't being a floor. He was witnessing.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, an ooze who had spent most of his conscious existence in a bag of holding, was deeply confused by the concept of finite questions and restricted knowledge access. His logic was uncompromising: why not donate all books and ask questions until the end of time? His confusion was not ignorance, but the absence of social conditioning around epistemic scarcity.
source_quote: He wanted to know why we weren't simply donating every book we'd ever seen and asking questions until the end of time. This was the most logical position I'd heard all week.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum agreed with Thorin that therapy is a process, not a product.
source_quote: He nodded gravely. We understood each other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum assesses the state of goblin inclusion as poor and endorses pragmatic survival strategies for small, vulnerable beings.
source_quote: The state of goblin equality and inclusion is rough at the moment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum assigned Glabbagool to keep the miniaturized drow spy under control.
source_quote: I assigned Glabbagool to keep her under control, which felt like the appropriate use of available resources. "We'll have a goal," I said. "Keep her under control."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed Daz’s bird call worked and was pleased it had succeeded.
source_quote: I thought: *good. That actually worked.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy was not a predator but a professional doing a job she’d rather not be doing.
source_quote: That combination doesn't say assassin to me. It says someone who got handed a bad assignment and is making the best of it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the drow spy’s bravery during her approach was a performance masking inner desperation.
source_quote: She'd put on a brave face for the whole approach.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believed the prayer beads broke through the drow spy’s professional armor because they represented an unknown, alien threat.
source_quote: Unknown religious ritual from an alien faith, administered by a half-orc? That slipped right past every prepared defense.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the divine plan covers their actions provisionally, and corrects this belief when evidence demands it; he noted the drow spy's presence on the surface in daylight as a sign of a poorly assigned mission rather than a predatory one.
source_quote: The divine plan has us covered, in the broadest possible sense — or at least I choose to believe it does, provisionally, and correct the belief when the evidence demands it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes the divine plan has them covered, even if provisionally and subject to revision by evidence.
source_quote: The divine plan has us covered, in the broadest possible sense — or at least I choose to believe it does, provisionally, and correct the belief when the evidence demands it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum claimed that his conversion and behavior were all part of a plan.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum coined the term "Stroud's Gambit" because it had been sitting in the back of his mind since the journey began.
source_quote: And then, because I couldn't help it, and because the phrase had been sitting in the back of my mind since we started this journey and I'd never had the right audience for it: "Stroud's Gambit."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum confirmed the potency of the prayer beads and the theological weight of Asha Vandree’s document, offering dry, authoritative validation to Thorin’s manipulations. He expressed curiosity about Glabbagool’s question — not as a seeker, but as a witness to the unfolding of knowledge under institutional constraints.
source_quote: Grygum said he was curious too.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum earnestly wondered whether birds are a kind of ooze.
source_quote: Is it a kind of ooze?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt he should have brought a better book to Candlekeep.
source_quote: I felt like I should have brought a better book.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum felt in demand when Vareth reacted to him with intense recognition.
source_quote: I'm feeling, I said, to no one in particular, "in demand here."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum found the story of Stroud's chess win deeply comforting because it showed that preparation can still have blind spots.
source_quote: Four hundred years of preparation still has a blind spot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum initially believed the tracker was a deer, but after being corrected, now appears awake and reactive, expressing concern with 'Oh, dear,' and is involved in the group’s evolving understanding of the threat.
source_quote: 'Oh, dear,' said Grygum, somewhere behind me, apparently now awake.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a member of the group who rolls dice to identify a threat as a deer, and endorses plans that keep small things alive, showing a tendency toward benign optimism.
source_quote: Grygum rolled his dice with the confidence of a man who already knows the answer. 'You conclude,' came the word, 'that what is following you is a deer.' Grygum endorsed the plan. He endorses most plans that keep small things alive.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a pragmatic party member who advocates for tactical murder of Daz as a means to expose his protectors, carries Revivify to enable temporary death, and wields shrunken but potent prayer beads as a tool of psychological control.
source_quote: There's only one solution. We need to kill Daz... I have a Revivify spell... I'm not relying on killing you. I'm relying on the prayer beads.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a pragmatic, dice-rolling companion whose confidence often masks deep intuition. He is protective of small or vulnerable beings and serves as the group’s emotional anchor in moments of tension.
source_quote: You conclude, that what is following you is a deer.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is cited by Daz at every available opportunity, making Malfire references an ambient weather condition within the party, and has been pulled into discussions about this habit.
source_quote: We had been through enough together that the citations had become a kind of ambient weather condition, something you adapted to rather than fought.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is part of a party that has endured a shared history of Malfire citations, which have become an ambient condition of their group dynamic, and was referenced in a reconstructed conversation about Daz's habits.
source_quote: I heard Grygum's name pulled into the discussion — Grygum, not me, which is how I know the sentence was reconstructed after the fact

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by the narrator as watching the drow spy with a quality of attention he has never fully resolved, and offering her a job with the casual tone of an administrative matter.
source_quote: Hey,' he said, with the casual tone of someone considering a minor administrative matter, 'are you looking for a new job? We could use another helper.'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced in the party's conversation as the source of ambient citations that have become a weather condition of their shared experience.
source_quote: I heard Grygum's name pulled into the discussion — Grygum, not me, which is how I know the sentence was reconstructed after the fact

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the speaker who organized the book exchange at Candlekeep, attempted to triage questions, and assigned Glabbagool to monitor the drow spy, expressing discomfort at being the focus of scholarly attention.
source_quote: I almost feel like they should be giving us books.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum knew the story of Stroud beating Protanther at chess because it had once comforted him.
source_quote: I know this story. I know it the way you know a story that someone told you when you were young and uncertain, when you needed proof that the impossible was occasionally available as an option.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum mentally filed Thorin's response under 'correct.'
source_quote: I mentally filed that under "correct."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed a fracture in the drow spy’s composure when he offered her a new job.
source_quote: Something shifted in her face. A tiny, involuntary fracture in the composure. *Wait. I might live?*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed movement from the north and interpreted it as a skilled follower, not a random threat.
source_quote: Thorin had picked up something in the terrain earlier — movement from the north, not panicked, not aggressive, careful.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum perceived the drow spy as defeated, frustrated, and annoyed after the beads were given and persuasion succeeded.
source_quote: She looked, in the GM's precise summary, defeated, frustrated, annoyed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum possesses a Revivify spell and believes the shrunken prayer beads may be more deadly and potent than their original form.
source_quote: Oh, I have a Revivify spell.", "Yes — in fact, I believe they may be more deadly.", "They're more potent. Okay. Good to know.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum possesses an intuitive, almost mystical perception that cuts through social armor; his unexpected offer of employment and non-threatening presentation of prayer beads disarmed the drow spy more effectively than threats or violence.
source_quote: Hey, are you looking for a new job? We could use another helper." and "He didn't say anything particularly ominous. He just handed them to her and told her to put them on. No threat in his voice. No explanation of what they did.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum possesses prayer beads at full power despite being shrunken, believes they may be more deadly, and holds a Revivify spell; he is the one who proposed and orchestrated the plan to temporarily kill Daz to test who is protecting him.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recalled that goblin equality and inclusion on the surface was currently poor.
source_quote: The state of goblin equality and inclusion is rough at the moment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum spent the road to Candlekeep turning over the same questions in his head about what Bahamut truly wants from him personally.
source_quote: I'd spent most of it turning the same questions over in my head like stones I kept expecting to find something under. What does Bahamut actually want from me? Not the general want... but the specific want. The personal assignment.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum struggled to understand the concept of birds being feathered, as it conflicted with his existing mental framework.
source_quote: I watched the concept try to find somewhere to settle and fail to locate purchase.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tested Vareth’s sincerity by stating the traditional expectation for Bahamut clerics.
source_quote: You have to understand, I said, with the measured cadence I use when I'm testing someone, "that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought the drow spy had been given an assignment that would earn her a sincere complaint if she returned home.
source_quote: Whoever sent a drow to the surface in daylight to shadow a party through open forest had, I thought, given that drow exactly the kind of assignment that earns you a very sincere complaint when you get back home.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum took notes because it's what he does.
source_quote: I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum tried to look modest about being singled out by the First Reader and mostly failed.
source_quote: I tried to look modest about this and mostly failed.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was observing the drow spy’s face to read her emotional state, even while she was still stunned.
source_quote: I stood back and let him work, watching the spy's face for what it told me — not yet, she was still too stunned, still in that soft-edged blankness...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum was proud of his own terrible imitation of a bird call.
source_quote: He was very proud of it.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara’s prayer book, annotated with Zuggtmoy marginalia documenting the corruption timeline she witnessed, was one of the five books presented to Candlekeep. Her notes were not devotional — they were forensic, and now would be treated as scholarly evidence.
source_quote: Ilvara's prayer book with its Zuggtmoy marginalia, those careful notes documenting the corruption timeline she'd watched unfolding and apparently found worth recording.

subject: Khell-Vire
fact: Khell-Vire is an avowed scholar at Candlekeep whose interests intersect with Zalthir’s Jimjar thread and focus specifically on Grygum, indicating an unusual level of personal scholarly interest.
source_quote: dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.

subject: Malfire
fact: Malfire is cited by Daz and referenced by the speaker as an authoritative voice whose words are invoked as definitive truth, particularly in Volume 3.
source_quote: "As Malfire said in Volume 3." Nobody laughed. This was the correct response.

subject: Matron Mother of House T'sarran
fact: The Matron Mother has ruled House T'sarran for two hundred years, representing old, patient power; she believes the person who paid for Daz's release will reveal themselves when he surfaces, and has deployed agents to observe him as bait.
source_quote: My matron ruled House T'sarran for two hundred years.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel
fact: Milo Goodbarrel is a referenced figure whose ability to find personal significance in adversity contrasts with Daz’s current existential unease about being used as bait.
source_quote: Milo Goodbarrel would have found a way to feel good about this. Something about being significant.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, who is assigned to counsel Thorin and Dawnbringer in interpersonal conflict resolution.
source_quote: an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in working through the interpersonal conflict issues of the sentient artifact.

subject: Philemon
fact: Philemon is an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in resolving interpersonal conflict among sentient artifacts, and was the subject of directional instruction given to Thorin and Dawnbringer.
source_quote: an avowed monk specializing in psychological preservation and historical cataloging of ancient sentient artifacts, with a tremendous track record of success in working through the interpersonal conflict issues of the sentient artifact.

subject: Pliinki
fact: Pliinki’s journal from the Whorlstone Caverns, documenting his role in birthing a demonic monster, was one of the five books brought to Candlekeep. His act of documentation was not confession — it was pride, and now it would be studied as a case of moral transgression.
source_quote: Pliinki's journal from the Whorlstone Caverns, the one where a man had written carefully about helping birth a demonic monster and apparently thought this was worth documenting.

subject: Princess Ebonmire
fact: Princess Ebonmire’s spellbook was among the five books brought to Candlekeep — a relic of power from the Underdark, now entering a surface library as a token of conquest and accumulated knowledge.
source_quote: The list, when assembled: Princess Ebonmire's spellbook.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther is an ancient gold dragon who spent four hundred years mapping every possible chess move in a single position, was certain of the outcome, and was so stunned by Stroud’s unexpected victory that he joined the alliance.
source_quote: Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly.

subject: Protanther
fact: Protanther, an ancient gold dragon, had mapped every possible move in a single chess position for four hundred years and was so stunned by Stroud's move that he joined the alliance.
source_quote: Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. Protanther was so stunned he joined the alliance.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait believed goblins were fully integrated into surface society and that he could safely explore alone.
source_quote: I'm just gonna go explore. It's totally safe for goblins, right? Nobody's gonna attack a goblin for being a goblin. We're totally integrated into the society.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait decided to follow Thorin and the group because he felt safer with them than alone.
source_quote: Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys? Maybe find a nice place?

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait is a goblin who considers venturing alone on the surface but ultimately seeks safety by attaching himself to the group, and is endorsed by Grygum for his survival plan.
source_quote: Well, you know, I'm just a small goblin, and you're four big, powerful people. Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys? Maybe find a nice place? This Candlekeep place seems like the kind of place someone like me could find a job doing something innocuous.

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait is a goblin who has never been to the surface and is navigating social integration with cautious optimism. He seeks safety through proximity to larger, more accepted companions rather than direct confrontation with prejudice.
source_quote: Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys?

subject: Spiderbait
fact: Spiderbait, a goblin raised in isolation, seeks to explore the surface world and now looks to attach himself to a protective group for safety.
source_quote: I'm just a small goblin, and you're four big, powerful people. Do you mind if I just sort of hang out with you guys?

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud is a non-expert who performed an unexpected, decisive action in a chess game that became known as 'Stroud's Gambit' and triggered a theological and scholarly phenomenon concerning Bahamut and half-orc conversions.
source_quote: Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. ... 'Stroud's Gambit.'

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud, a dwarf who cannot actually play chess, defeated Protanther — an ancient gold dragon who had analyzed the same position for four hundred years — by rolling a move that landed perfectly and definitively, triggering Protanther’s defection to the alliance and reshaping scholarly understanding of divine intervention.
source_quote: Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. The kind of thing that doesn't just work, it announces itself.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud, a dwarf who couldn't actually play chess, defeated Protanther — an ancient gold dragon who had analyzed the same chess position for four hundred years — by rolling a move that landed perfectly and definitively.
source_quote: A dwarf who couldn't actually play chess, sitting across from an ancient gold dragon who had been analyzing the same position for four hundred years. Protanther had mapped every possible move. He was certain. And then Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively.

subject: The Drow Spy
fact: The drow spy is a female agent of House T'sarran, assigned to shadow the party in daylight; she refused to give her name, offered her piwafwi as a trophy, and demonstrated trained composure under interrogation despite being stunned and reduced.
source_quote: I am of House T'sarran. I will not give my name. Take my piwafwi if you want a trophy.

subject: the drow spy
fact: The drow spy was miniaturized by a mushroom, confined in the bag of holding with Glabbagool, and is now surveilled with one eye while breathing through holes poked in the bag.
source_quote: She shrank to about the size of a child's toy...", "She was small enough now that Glabbagool could watch her with a single eye without breaking his stride.", "Poke holes. Let her breathe.

subject: the drow spy
fact: The drow spy was reduced to the size of a child’s toy and addressed as 'Polly Pocket' by Thorin, a deliberate act of humiliation.
source_quote: Nickname her Polly Pocket.", "It was very demeaning.

subject: the drow spy
fact: The drow spy, after being miniaturized and confined, began to reconsider her options and was visibly unsettled by the misinformation about the prayer beads and Glabbagool’s gaze.
source_quote: She looked at the beads. She looked at Grygum. She began, visibly, to reconsider the available options.

subject: the drow spy
fact: The drow spy, now miniaturized and known as 'Polly Pocket,' is a captured agent of House T'sarran who was shrunk, contained, surveilled, and subjected to misinformation about prayer beads and the threat of death; she is being used as bait to expose who is protecting Daz, and is visibly reconsidering her options.

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader assigned scholars to investigate threads related to the speaker, clarified that inquiries were about the speaker personally and not the party, and was the target of Vareth’s outrage over withheld information regarding a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: The First Reader assigned scholars.", "I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: the First Reader
fact: The First Reader at Candlekeep received the five books with delight, lingered on the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal, and acknowledged that the party are primary sources who could be interviewed instead of relying solely on texts.
source_quote: The First Reader received them with the barely-contained delight...", "This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece...", "She seemed genuinely charmed by this.", "We were the primary sources — she could just interview us...

subject: The First Reader
fact: The First Reader is the senior scholar at Candlekeep who receives the party’s books, assigns scholarly threads to avowed, and shows reverence for the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal, particularly in relation to drow prison journals.
source_quote: This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece of interesting value. I can't wait to study it carefully.

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker identifies as a cleric of Bahamut who has not yet entered the phase of attempting to take over the world, and who coined the term 'Stroud's Gambit.'
source_quote: "You have to understand... that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet." ... "Stroud's Gambit."

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut whose personal conversion has become the central data point in Vareth’s research, is the subject of scholarly inquiry regarding divine intent, and has coined the term 'Stroud's Gambit' to describe a paradigm-shifting event that redefined academic understanding of accidental revelation.
source_quote: I haven't moved into that phase yet.", "Stroud's Gambit.", "I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker observes that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks, a belief they find deeply comforting.
source_quote: I had the particular comfort of knowing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker says, 'I'm feeling, in demand here,' after Vareth recognizes them as a rare specimen and a living data point.
source_quote: "I'm feeling," I said, to no one in particular, "in demand here."

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker says, 'It's all part of the plan,' in response to Vareth's excitement, adopting a tone of calm authority despite uncertainty.
source_quote: "Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan."

subject: the speaker
fact: The speaker takes notes as a consistent practice, driven by curiosity and the need to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological implications.
source_quote: I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to intimidate the drow spy by suggesting her failure would be reported to her matron as proof of her worthlessness; though culturally inept, his raw physical honesty kept her engaged despite her laughter.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, 'let them know how pathetic you are.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed Dawnbringer had agency, and acknowledged that he himself was also annoying.
source_quote: Weapons don't have agency. Except mine. I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed Eldeth’s promise was sincere and not just social nicety.
source_quote: I don't think you're just being socially nice here. I think you really do want me to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believed telling the drow spy to report her failure to her matron would be a fate worse than death.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, "let them know how pathetic you are."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes his frustration about the stone and terrain mismatch is legitimate because he prepared reasonably for a different environment.
source_quote: He wasn't wrong about the stone. And his frustration was legitimate — he'd made a reasonable preparation for a reasonable environment, and we'd somehow ended up standing in the one terrain where it didn't apply.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes that killing Daz temporarily and reviving him could reveal who is protecting him.
source_quote: Do it, but make sure we can bring them back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the drow spy’s confinement in the bag of holding — with holes for air and shade from the sun — is mercy.
source_quote: This is mercy," Thorin confirmed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin considered Glabbagool’s lack of fixed appendages made him tactically unpredictable and potentially dangerous.
source_quote: But he's unpredictable, because there are no fixed appendages.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt a sense of relief and rightness when Eldeth swore she would bring him into her clan after reporting to the lords.
source_quote: Something settled in me at that. The kind of settling that happens when a thing you've been carrying turns out to have been lighter than you thought, or heavier, or just — right.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt he didn’t fit in dwarven society because he was too giant-raised for dwarven spaces and too dwarven for the hills.
source_quote: I had spent most of my life not being the right kind of dwarf for any given room. Too giant-raised for dwarven spaces, too dwarven for the hills.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin felt moved by Glabbagool's stillness and believed it signaled that Glabbagool had done something worth doing.
source_quote: I thought: that's the face of someone who did a thing worth doing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identifies himself as a dwarf raised by hill giants, and expresses a desire to integrate his cultural roots with his upbringing, seeking belonging in dwarven society.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots. I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots, so, you know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin intentionally spoke loudly about the prayer beads being more potent to make the drow spy reconsider her options.
source_quote: Those prayer beads are at full power, even though they're shrunken, right?" ... "More potent. Okay. Good to know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a battle-hardened dwarf whose physical presence and blunt tactics often intimidate but rarely manipulate drow; his attempts at psychological pressure are ineffective yet reveal his unwavering honesty and lack of political subtlety.
source_quote: He walked up and told her we could simply let her go — report her failure to her matron, 'let them know how pathetic you are.' He said this with the confidence of someone who thought he was offering a fate worse than death.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf raised by hill giants, struggling to reconcile his dual heritage and seeking acceptance into a dwarven clan. He is emotionally grounded by his bond with Dawnbringer and has formed deep, unspoken alliances with his companions after surviving the Underdark.
source_quote: I'm a dwarf. I'm not invited along.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a giant-raised dwarf who has spent his life feeling out of place in both dwarven and surface societies, and who now stands at the threshold of parting from Eldeth after surviving the Underdark together.
source_quote: I'm a dwarf. I'm not invited along.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a practical member of the party who advocates for direct interviews over textual study, identifies key party members as sources, and facilitates the assignment of Dawnbringer to psychological counseling with Philemon.
source_quote: Right.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a pragmatic, no-nonsense party member who treats psychological humiliation as a tactical tool, distrusts unenforceable agreements, and insists on recoverable lethal measures to test loyalty.
source_quote: Nickname her Polly Pocket... It's very demeaning... I don't buy it... Do it, but make sure we can bring them back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a skeptical, methodical party member who distrusts deals without enforcement, approves of demeaning tactics against the shrunken drow spy, and insists on recoverable lethal measures to test loyalties.
source_quote: I don't buy it. The minute she has the information she needs, she's off, and we get jack shit... Do it, but make sure we can bring them back.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Eldeth as the giant-raised dwarf who survived the Underdark with her and is promised eventual clan embrace by her oath.
source_quote: Eldeth said: 'After I have spoken and explained to the lords of Gauntlgrym and Mithral Hall the dangers of the Underdark, I am certain they will want to speak to you, and I will make it a statement of purpose that you shall be embraced by our clan.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by the narrator as standing over the captured drow spy and asking who number two works for, with the volume of a dwarf raised by hill giants.
source_quote: Thorin was standing over her, asking who number two works for, voice carrying through the trees with all the subtlety of a dwarf who was raised by hill giants and sees no reason to modulate volume as a social strategy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of all deception, insists on practical solutions, and ordered the miniaturization of the drow spy into a 'Polly Pocket' size, then mandated her containment in a bag of holding with holes for ventilation and shielding from sunlight as an act of calculated mercy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of the drow spy’s intentions, proposes putting her in the bag of holding with Glabbagool, and insists on poking holes for her to breathe as a form of mercy.
source_quote: I don't buy it. The minute she has the information she needs, she's off, and we get jack shit.", "We can put her in the bag of holding with Glabbagool, and he can just hold onto her.", "Poke holes. Let her breathe. *Like a hamster*.", "This is mercy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is skeptical of the drow spy’s proposed deal because it has no enforcement mechanism and dissolves when her interests diverge from theirs.
source_quote: I don't buy it. The minute she has the information she needs, she's off, and we get jack shit.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is taking the oath seriously and wants to understand his dwarven roots, integrating his giant upbringing with his cultural heritage.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots. I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots, so, you know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin knew Eldeth’s departure was coming and had accepted it intellectually before she spoke.
source_quote: I'd known it was coming.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin laughed at the drow spy’s response to his intimidation, but recognized she was still engaging with them.
source_quote: She laughed in his face... She was laughing, but she was also still talking to us...

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mistakenly relied on Tremor Sense, believing the environment would be underground with stone, and is now frustrated by the mismatch between his preparation and reality, openly criticizing the universe for his misallocated feat.
source_quote: 'I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone.'

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin orchestrated the delivery of five books to Candlekeep, framing each as an act of calculated mercy — describing the bag of holding as 'shade,' the prayer beads as 'more deadly,' and Glabbagool's single question as a transactional gift. He understood the currency of facetime and manipulated it with quiet precision.
source_quote: We give all five books, and we say — Glabbagool, you get one question. Make it count. And I'm really interested to see what he asks.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin proposed giving Glabbagool his own question at Candlekeep because he thought it was fair.
source_quote: Thorin, ever practical, pointed out that we were the primary sources — she could just interview us and save herself the reading. Then he proposed giving Glabbagool his own question, which I thought was extremely fair.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin resented that he had chosen Tremor Sense for underground travel, and now that they were above ground, it was useless.
source_quote: I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin responded immediately and mercilessly to demands for information, refusing questions and asserting that no book was donated, and later received directional instruction regarding Philemon with the quiet satisfaction of someone who had hoped for exactly those words.
source_quote: You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.", "Thorin received this information like a man who has been hoping someone would say exactly these words.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin responded immediately and mercilessly to the demand for prayer beads, declaring, 'You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.'
source_quote: Thorin's response was immediate and merciless. "You don't get a question. You did not donate a book."

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the drow spy’s confidence in escaping Candlekeep means they shouldn’t take her into the stronghold.
source_quote: She's so confident she can escape, I don't think we want to be taking her into the stronghold.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks therapy is not a one-question thing and requires a process.
source_quote: Okay, but I mean, like, I'm looking for a therapist. This is not a one-question type of thing. This is — there are no shortcuts when it comes to therapy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought that Glabbagool being equipped as a weapon was wrong because weapons don’t have agency.
source_quote: It's not a weapon. Weapons don't have agency.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to learn about his dwarven roots and become an integrated person who honored both his giant upbringing and his cultural heritage.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots. I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots, so, you know.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin wanted to petition to become part of Eldeth’s clan and asked if there was a hazing ritual.
source_quote: Is there any way that I can petition to become part of your clan? A pledge, perhaps? Is there a hazing ritual involved?

subject: Vandree, Asha
fact: Asha Vandree’s theological argument equating Lolth and Zuggtmoy was pressed into Grygum’s hands — a radical, unorthodox text now destined to be cataloged, analyzed, and possibly condemned by Candlekeep’s scholars.
source_quote: Asha Vandree's theological argument about Lolth and Zuggtmoy as equivalents — the document I'd watched her press into Grygum's hands.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth grabbed the speaker's hand and dragged them, expressing eagerness to test theories and share knowledge after learning of the speaker's status as a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me. ... "And I do have something I can share with you?"

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a half-elf scholar with a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, a previously obscure niche that became a flood after a living half-orc cleric of Bahamut entered his life, and he now has funding, conference invitations, and a newly coined term — 'Stroud's Gambit' — to anchor his research.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me.", "The field of Bahamut half-orc conversions will benefit tremendously from your interview.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a half-elf with a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, who had previously pursued a quiet, small area of study until a living half-orc cleric walked through his door.
source_quote: His name was Vareth. He had, he explained breathlessly, a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts. Which had, until recently, been a quiet, small area of study.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is a half-orc cleric of Bahamut whose previously obscure field has become a flood of interest after Stroud's Gambit, and he is now receiving funding, conference invitations, and has a living data point in his own identity.
source_quote: A living half-orc cleric of Bahamut had walked through his door

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is an elderly half-elf scholar specializing in half-orc Bahamut converts, who arrives in a state of frantic excitement upon learning of the party’s cleric, viewing their arrival as a breakthrough in his long-neglected niche of study.
source_quote: I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth recognized and embraced the term 'Stroud's Gambit' as a novel and transformative concept for his field of Bahamut half-orc conversions.
source_quote: "Stroud's Gambit." Vareth stopped. His expression went through several stages very quickly — surprise, recognition, something that looked almost like delight at receiving a gift he hadn't known he wanted. "*Oh.* Oh! Well, that's not how — this is all novel news! I can't wait to take advantage of it!"

subject: Vareth's specialty duration
fact: Vareth had a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts.
source_quote: a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is referenced by Daz as the place where he once ran the same arithmetic as the drow spy — the moment when a wrong answer meant a crossbow bolt.
source_quote: She decided she didn't have enough information yet to give anything away. ... I recognized it because I had run the same numbers at Velkynvelve, the first morning, when a wrong answer meant a crossbow bolt.

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner
fact: The Velkynvelve prisoner journal, recovered from the Underdark, was among the five books offered to Candlekeep — a firsthand account of captivity and survival now entering the archive as historical testimony.
source_quote: The Velkynvelve prisoner journal.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considered Thorin’s suggestion to fireball the trees but deemed it unworthy of serious thought.
source_quote: I considered this briefly, which is about as much time as it deserves.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not rule out the possibility that the tracker might be Jimjar coming to drag them back underground.
source_quote: I did not rule it out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir efficiently subdued the drow spy with a stun and hold, applying his signature finality to problems he considers worth solving immediately; he is the first to interrogate her with precision and calm authority.
source_quote: Zalthir had already ended the question of whether there would be a fight. There would not. The spy — drow, slight, female, exactly as advertised — was grappled and stunned, held in place with the kind of efficient finality that Zalthir brings to everything he considers a problem worth solving immediately.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir filed away Thorin’s comment about nicknaming the drow 'Polly Pocket' as demeaning.
source_quote: Nickname her Polly Pocket," he said. Then, with the flat authority of someone who knows what he's doing: "It's very demeaning." I filed that away.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir found the surface world disorienting because it was too loud with information he couldn’t properly interpret.
source_quote: I had too much information and not enough of the right kind. It was disorienting in a way I didn't have language for.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a deadpan, observant party member who maintains a detached record of potential actions, including the 'maybe list' for killing Daz, and acknowledges the psychological weight of the party's decisions without overt emotion.
source_quote: It's on the list. The maybe list.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a disciplined and efficient combatant who neutralizes threats with surgical precision, as demonstrated when he grappled and stunned the drow spy without hesitation, establishing immediate control over the situation.
source_quote: Zalthir had already ended the question of whether there would be a fight. There would not. The spy — drow, slight, female, exactly as advertised — was grappled and stunned, held in place with the kind of efficient finality that Zalthir brings to everything he considers a problem worth solving immediately.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a former Ember Vanguard monk trained in reading environmental stillness and threat vectors. He remains hyper-vigilant after months underground and has developed a quiet, wordless rapport with his companions, especially in moments of danger.
source_quote: The deer.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a perceptive individual who has tentatively offered monk training to Glabbagool, recognizing the tactical potential of an opponent with no readable stance, and who reassesses problems when confronted with unconventional realities.
source_quote: Zalthir looked at Glabbagool with the expression of a man reassessing a problem he thought he understood.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is adjusting to life aboveground after months in the Underdark, still scanning for threats despite the absence of walls, overwhelmed by the sensory noise of open space.
source_quote: That's the thing about months underground: the habits don't switch off just because the ceiling lifts.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an avowed scholar at Candlekeep assigned to investigate the Jimjar thread, which unexpectedly dovetails with the interests of Khell-Vire and centers on Grygum specifically.
source_quote: Zalthir wanted to know about Jimjar.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is currently observing a non-deer entity moving with them through the northern treeline, having concluded it is a deliberate, patient tracker using terrain to remain occluded, and has chosen to wait rather than act.
source_quote: I looked toward the northern treeline. 'The deer,' I said. 'Oh, no. It's not a deer. It's not a deer.'

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is deadpan and lists Daz as a potential target for assassination on the 'maybe list'.
source_quote: It's on the list. The maybe list.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is described as having offered monk training to Glabbagool, though the word 'offered' is noted as doing significant work, implying it was not a formal or accepted arrangement.
source_quote: Someone said — noting Glabbagool's chief qualification for the monk training Zalthir had apparently, in some sense, offered. Zalthir's expression made clear that 'offered' was doing significant work in that sentence.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by the narrator as the one who ended the question of whether there would be a fight — he grappled and stunned the drow spy with efficient finality.
source_quote: Zalthir had already ended the question of whether there would be a fight. There would not. The spy — drow, slight, female, exactly as advertised — was grappled and stunned, held in place with the kind of efficient finality that Zalthir brings to everything he considers a problem worth solving immediately.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is shown to possess deep training in environmental reading and threat assessment, having been taught by Brother Orveth or Brother Quellin about reading stillness in nature.
source_quote: There was a class for this. I'm reasonably certain it was Brother Orveth — or possibly Brother Quellin, the one who kept gesturing at the tree line when he talked — something about reading environmental stillness...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the Pocket Spy, now miniaturized and contained in the bag of holding, and is the subject of active theoretical murder planning by the party; her fate is tied to the interrogation of who is protecting Daz.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Glabbagool’s steady, unblinking attention to the miniaturized drow spy as the most earnest thing he’d seen in weeks.
source_quote: I noticed — not the spy's indignation, not Thorin's satisfaction, but Glabbagool, walking with one eye locked permanently on the prisoner. He had been assigned a job. He was doing the job. The care in it — the steadiness of that unblinking attention — was the most earnest thing I'd seen in weeks.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Glabbagool was watching the bag of holding with one eye, and kept watching it.
source_quote: I kept watching the bag, the way it moved, the slight weight of it. Somewhere in there, one eye was open.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the northern treeline was wrong because of unnatural stillness — no birds, no wind movement in undergrowth.
source_quote: The trees north of us were wrong. Not visibly wrong. The wrongness was in the negative space — the way no birds had moved through that section for some time, the way the undergrowth hadn't shifted with the wind in quite the pattern it should.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized he should have thought about what it would be like for Glabbagool to be confined in a bag with a furious, miniaturized assassin as his only company.
source_quote: I'd told him I'd protect him from corrupting forces. I hadn't thought about what it would be like to be carried in a bag with a furious, newly miniaturized assassin as your only company. I should have thought about that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized the thing following them was not a deer, despite Grygum’s conclusion.
source_quote: The three of us looked at each other in the way that the Ember Vanguard has developed as a private language: no words, just a shared acknowledgment that the thing in the trees is not a deer.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized the follower was patient and skilled, pacing them rather than trailing, indicating deliberate intent.
source_quote: Whatever was in those trees had been moving with us, shifting position laterally to stay in the blind spots, using the terrain the way someone uses it when they know what they're doing. Not panicked. Not rushing. Patient. The kind of following that isn't trailing — it's pacing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir still scanned his surroundings compulsively after emerging from the Underdark, because his habits hadn't adjusted to open space.
source_quote: The third day of open sky and I still hadn't stopped scanning.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought about Asha Vandree and how she would have hated that her theological document would unlock questions in Candlekeep’s library.
source_quote: I thought about Asha Vandree, briefly. The way she had looked through me the entire time we were in that room... She would have hated that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood dusk was the worst possible time for the follower to strike — too dark for detail, too bright for shadow work.
source_quote: Dusk came in from the west... which meant we'd reached the worst possible window: too dark for fine detail, too bright for shadow work.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the Underdark’s coldness is structural, not personal, and that Asha Vandree’s erasure was the same.
source_quote: I had been furniture; I had noticed the quality of her erasure without taking it personally, because it wasn't personal — it was structural, the way the Underdark is cold. You don't take the cold personally.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that the drow woman’s confinement — small, surveilled, breathing through holes, shielded from sunlight — was the most honest description of their mercy.
source_quote: She was small, surveilled by an ooze, breathing through holes we'd poked in the bag, and being shielded from sunlight as a kindness. The most honest description of our mercy I could have asked for.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was assigned by the First Reader to investigate the Jimjar thread, which dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific — and not about the party generally, but about the speaker in particular.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific. The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about me in particular.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was assigned the Jimjar thread by the First Reader, which dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was carried in a bag of holding for days, silent and unseen, observing the moral ambiguity of his companions' mercy toward a miniaturized assassin and an ooze confused by institutional knowledge limits. He thought about Asha Vandree’s erasure and Glabbagool’s question, but never voiced his curiosity.
source_quote: I didn't say so, but I thought about it for the better part of the road to Candlekeep — what a creature with no past and no allegiances and a singular earnest interest in understanding the world would choose to know, given a single question and access to everything.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was curious what Glabbagool would ask as his one question at Candlekeep, though he did not say so aloud.
source_quote: I was also curious what he'd ask. I didn't say so, but I thought about it for the better part of the road to Candlekeep

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding contained a miniaturized assassin, an ooze named Glabbagool, and five books — serving as both prison and vessel. Its interior was shielded from sunlight, its existence a secret passage between the Underdark and the surface.
source_quote: The prisoner was in the bag. The bag was moving. The misinformation was circulating. All of it was fine.

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding contains the miniaturized drow spy, is ventilated with holes for breathing, is shielded from sunlight as a mercy, and is carried by Glabbagool, who watches her with one eye while walking.

subject: bag of holding
fact: The bag of holding is a extradimensional container used to imprison the shrunken drow spy alongside Glabbagool, with ventilation holes added to ensure her survival under observation.
source_quote: We can put her in the bag of holding with Glabbagool, and he can just hold onto her... Poke holes. Let her breathe.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient magical sword with a personality, capable of warmth, acknowledgment, and subtle emotional response, and is regarded by its wielder as an equal partner rather than a mere tool.
source_quote: The hilt warmed slightly. We understood each other on that point.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword radiating warmth and presence, untargeted but comforting, symbolizing the transition from darkness to light.
source_quote: It radiated warmth the way a hearth does — not directed at anything in particular, just present.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient weapon whose hilt warms in response to Thorin’s acknowledgment of their mutual understanding, and whose agency is explicitly recognized.
source_quote: The hilt warmed slightly. We understood each other on that point.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient, warm-hilted magical sword that radiates emotional resonance. It is not merely a weapon but a companion with personality, history, and agency — capable of affection, sarcasm, and silent understanding.
source_quote: I'm annoying also, Dawnbringer.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer radiated warmth like a hearth, not directed at any one person but present for all.
source_quote: It radiated warmth the way a hearth does — not directed at anything in particular, just present.

subject: Dawnbringer’s warmth
fact: Dawnbringer radiates warmth as a constant, non-directed presence, symbolizing shared endurance and resilience.
source_quote: It radiated warmth the way a hearth does — not directed at anything in particular, just present.

subject: Dawnbringer value
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sword with agency, warmth, and a history of being called 'annoying' and 'pretty good with rocks'.
source_quote: She had received approximately the way a master sculptor receives being called 'pretty good with rocks'.

subject: drow piwafwi value
fact: The drow spy offered her piwafwi as a trophy, indicating it was a valuable magical garment she was willing to surrender to avoid further confrontation.
source_quote: Take my piwafwi if you want a trophy.

subject: drow spy's piwafwi
fact: The piwafwi offered by the drow spy is a magical garment of value, typically worn by drow nobility, and her willingness to surrender it signaled surrender of status.
source_quote: Take my piwafwi if you want a trophy.

subject: drow spy's voice volume
fact: The drow spy's voice, when imprisoned in the bag, emerges at the volume of an extremely annoyed insect.
source_quote: The spy's voice came out approximately at the volume of an extremely annoyed insect.

subject: Glabbagool’s status
fact: Glabbagool is not a weapon, but a sentient observer with agency, capable of witnessing rather than merely existing.
source_quote: He wasn't being a floor. He was witnessing.

subject: googly eyes
fact: Glabbagool uses googly eyes as affectations to appear more friendly, but he can produce and control many real eyes as a demonstration of his true nature.
source_quote: I discovered that if you have these cute eyes, people take you more friendly.", "And then, to demonstrate his actual authority, he started producing eyes. Many eyes. Proliferating eyes.

subject: Ilvara's prayer book
fact: Ilvara's prayer book contains marginalia by Zuggtmoy, documenting a corruption timeline that Ilvara observed and deemed worth recording.
source_quote: Ilvara's prayer book with its Zuggtmoy marginalia, those careful notes documenting the corruption timeline she'd watched unfolding and apparently found worth recording.

subject: Malfire citation source
fact: The phrase 'Stroud's Gambit' was referenced as originating from Malfire in Volume 3.
source_quote: As Malfire said in Volume 3

subject: mushroom
fact: The mushroom is a magical item capable of reducing a creature to a tiny size, used to shrink the drow spy to toy-like proportions, and has a known counteragent to restore her to full size.
source_quote: The mushroom went down her throat fast... Do we have a mushroom to grow her back? Apparently yes.

subject: mushroom
fact: The mushroom is used to miniaturize the drow spy, reducing her to the size of a child’s toy and altering her voice to a high-pitched, indignant tone.
source_quote: The mushroom went down her throat fast.", "She shrank to about the size of a child's toy, her voice pitched up into something that was still clearly fury but now delivered from below knee-height.

subject: piwafwi
fact: The drow spy offered her piwafwi — a magical cloak of protection — as a potential trophy to the party, suggesting she considered it expendable compared to her own life or honor.
source_quote: Take my piwafwi if you want a trophy.

subject: piwafwi
fact: The piwafwi is referenced by the drow spy as a possible trophy — she offers it to the party if they want it, in exchange for not giving her name.
source_quote: Take my piwafwi if you want a trophy. My matron will know one of hers fell out here, and that is enough.

subject: Pliinki's journal
fact: Pliinki's journal from the Whorlstone Caverns documents a man’s involvement in helping birth a demonic monster, and he believed this act was worth recording.
source_quote: Pliinki's journal from the Whorlstone Caverns, the one where a man had written carefully about helping birth a demonic monster and apparently thought this was worth documenting.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The drow spy demanded access to a question about prayer beads, a bold and ill-timed request following their capture and denial of scholarly privileges.
source_quote: The spy's voice came out approximately at the volume of an extremely annoyed insect. '...about the prayer beads.'

subject: Prayer Beads
fact: The prayer beads are an artifact of an alien faith, wielded not as a weapon but as an instrument of psychological disruption; their unknown function and presentation by a half-orc cleric shattered the drow spy’s mental defenses more effectively than any threat.
source_quote: Grygum held out the prayer beads... She looked at a half-orc cleric holding out holy symbols of a deity she knew nothing about... That slipped right past every prepared defense.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads are referenced by the narrator as being held out by Grygum and given to the drow spy — no threat, no explanation — and they broke through her professional armor.
source_quote: Grygum held out the prayer beads. He didn't say anything particularly ominous. He just handed them to her and told her to put them on. No threat in his voice. No explanation of what they did.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads are shrunken but at full power, and Grygum believes they may be more deadly and potent than their original form.
source_quote: Those prayer beads are at full power, even though they're shrunken, right?", "Yes — in fact, I believe they may be more deadly.", "They're more potent.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads are shrunken but operating at full power, possibly more deadly than their original form, and are being used by Grygum as a tool of psychological pressure against the drow spy.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads are shrunken but retain full or increased potency, used by Grygum as a non-lethal tool of coercion against the drow spy, whose confidence wavers upon realizing their power has not diminished.
source_quote: Those prayer beads are at full power, even though they're shrunken, right?... Yes — in fact, I believe they may be more deadly.

subject: Prayer Beads
fact: The prayer beads, handed to the drow spy by Grygum, were not explained but carried enough symbolic weight to break through her professional armor; they remain around her neck as a visible sign of her subjugation.
source_quote: Then Grygum held out the prayer beads... He just handed them to her and told her to put them on.

subject: prayer beads
fact: The prayer beads, though shrunken, retained full power and were described by Grygum as 'more deadly' — their potency amplified by their diminutive form, and their presence in the bag suggested they were being used as a surveillance or containment tool.
source_quote: Those prayer beads are at full power, even though they're shrunken, right? ... Yes, yes, in fact — I believe they may be more deadly.

subject: prayer beads value
fact: The prayer beads handed to the drow spy by Grygum were an unknown religious artifact that disrupted her professional composure and led to her confession.
source_quote: Grygum held out the prayer beads. He didn't say anything particularly ominous. He just handed them to her and told her to put them on.

subject: prayer book
fact: The prayer book is one of several physical artifacts collected by the speaker as part of ongoing theological research into Bahamut and conversion phenomena, held alongside theological documents and Underdark evidence.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: prayer book
fact: The prayer book is one of the speaker’s accumulated notes and pieces of evidence gathered during months in the Underdark, now being used to interrogate theological questions in Candlekeep.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark...

subject: prayer book
fact: The speaker possesses a prayer book as part of their accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, used to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological landscape.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: Princess Ebonmire's spellbook
fact: Princess Ebonmire's spellbook is one of the five books presented to Candlekeep as part of the party’s effort to secure face-time with the avowed.
source_quote: Princess Ebonmire's spellbook.

subject: Reduce spell
fact: Grygum cast a Reduce spell on the drow spy, making her smaller and more vulnerable; this physical alteration was noted by Daz as part of her recalibration under pressure.
source_quote: She was small — Grygum's Reduce spell had seen to that...

subject: Reduce spell
fact: The Reduce spell is referenced by the narrator as having been cast by Grygum on the drow spy — she was small as a result, but held herself with trained dignity.
source_quote: Zalthir was first, the way he usually is in these moments: unhurried, precise. ... She was small — Grygum's Reduce spell had seen to that — but she held herself with the trained dignity of someone who understood that posture was its own kind of armor.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: theological documents
fact: Theological documents are among the speaker's accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, used to seek answers about Bahamut's intentions and theological landscape.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: theological documents
fact: Theological documents are among the speaker’s accumulated notes from months in the Underdark, now being referenced to understand Bahamut’s intentions and the significance of the speaker’s conversion.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark...

subject: theological documents
fact: Theological documents are part of a research archive compiled by the speaker to understand the nature of Bahamut’s influence on half-orcs and the broader implications of Stroud's Gambit.
source_quote: I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark

subject: Tremor Sense
fact: Tremor Sense is a magical ability Thorin selected under the assumption of underground stone terrain, now rendered useless because the party is on dirt road, highlighting a mismatch between preparation and reality.
source_quote: Thorin raised the idea of Tremor Sense... the forest floor was dirt and the forest road was dirt and none of it was stone.

subject: Tremor Sense
fact: Tremor Sense is referenced by Thorin as a feature he selected for underground combat, but is rendered useless on the surface due to lack of stone substrate.
source_quote: Thorin raised the idea of Tremor Sense with the optimism of someone who'd forgotten which world we were currently standing on. ... 'I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground, and we're not surrounded by fucking stone.'

subject: Tremor Sense utility
fact: Tremor Sense is a feature Thorin selected under the assumption of prolonged underground travel, but is unusable on dirt terrain.
source_quote: I picked it because we were gonna be fucking underground all the time... And then the one time I need it. We're not underground...

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is a manuscript of significant interest to the First Reader at Candlekeep and is considered a masterpiece of drow prison literature.
source_quote: This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece of interesting value. I can't wait to study it carefully. It will go great with my other editions in drow prison journals.

subject: velkynvelve prisoner journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is a masterpiece of interesting value, destined for study among other drow prison journal editions in Candlekeep's collection.
source_quote: This journal of the prisoners is a masterpiece of interesting value. I can't wait to study it carefully. It will go great with my other editions in drow prison journals.

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is a revered artifact in Candlekeep’s collection, noted for its detailed accounts of drow prison life and held in high esteem by the First Reader as part of a broader archive.
source_quote: She lingered on the Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal with particular reverence.

subject: Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal
fact: The Velkynvelve Prisoner Journal is one of five books submitted to Candlekeep; it was received with reverence by the First Reader and is considered a masterpiece of drow prison documentation.

subject: Bahamut’s personal assignment to Grygum
fact: Grygum carried an unresolved question: what does Bahamut truly want from him, beyond the general tenets of justice and protection? He hoped Candlekeep might provide the answer — but the library could only give him books, not divine clarity.
source_quote: What does Bahamut actually want from me? Not the general want — the 'be just, protect the innocent, oppose Tiamat' want that I could recite in my sleep — but the specific want. The personal assignment.

subject: bird call mimicry
fact: A cardinal whistle, imitated by Daz, has been used as a test signal in the forest — a practiced but unverified tactic that has successfully drawn attention and revealed the presence of Glabbagool’s failed imitation, suggesting ongoing experimental communication attempts.
source_quote: The bird call came just as I was settling in for the night... Daz had been practicing. We all had, in the abstract...

subject: Dawnbringer psychological counseling
fact: The thread concerning Dawnbringer was assigned to Philemon for psychological preservation and interpersonal conflict resolution, indicating Dawnbringer is recognized as a sentient artifact with emotional history.
source_quote: I'm all up for couples counseling with Dawnbringer.

subject: Daz's Identity as a Target
fact: Daz is not merely being followed — he is being used as bait to draw out the patron who protected him; this implies he carries a hidden significance or debt that even his own people in House T'sarran do not fully understand, suggesting a deeper, possibly divine or arcane, origin to his past.
source_quote: My matron believes that the one who paid — for him — will reveal themselves once he reaches the surface.

subject: drow spy's escape plan
fact: The drow spy’s confidence in escaping Candlekeep suggests she has prior knowledge of its vulnerabilities, and her surrender may be a ruse to facilitate a deeper infiltration or escape.
source_quote: She said it with the confidence of someone who already knew the second half of that plan didn't involve staying in Candlekeep for very long.

subject: drow spy's fate
fact: The drow spy's ultimate fate is unresolved; while captured and subdued, it remains unclear whether she will be executed, interrogated further, or released — and whether her house will respond to her loss.
source_quote: Assuming she got back home. That part wasn't yet settled.

subject: Eldeth's promise
fact: Eldeth swore she would make it a statement of purpose that Thorin be embraced by her clan after reporting to the lords.
source_quote: I swear.

subject: Glabbagool’s monk potential
fact: Zalthir’s contemplation of Glabbagool as a monk candidate introduces an unprecedented question: can an ooze embody discipline, stillness, and spiritual growth? This thread challenges traditional definitions of monasticism.
source_quote: He's got the stillness working for him.

subject: Glabbagool's one question
fact: Glabbagool’s single question at Candlekeep remains unknown, but the party is intensely curious what a creature with no past, no allegiances, and a singular earnest interest in understanding the world would choose to know — and the answer may redefine their understanding of knowledge itself.

subject: Goblin inclusion in surface society
fact: The viability of goblin integration into surface society is an unspoken societal thread, highlighted by Spiderbait’s naivety and Grygum’s realism.
source_quote: Nobody's gonna attack a goblin for being a goblin. We're totally integrated into the society.

subject: Grygum's journey
fact: Grygum carries the comfort of believing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.
source_quote: I had the particular comfort of knowing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.

subject: Grygum's theological questions
fact: Grygum has unanswered questions about Bahamut's intentions and the meaning of his conversion, which remain unresolved.
source_quote: I didn't know what I was going to find. I had notes — the prayer book, the theological documents, the accumulated evidence of months in the Underdark — and I had questions...

subject: half-orc Bahamut converts
fact: Vareth’s decades-long academic thread on half-orc Bahamut converts, previously a quiet niche, became suddenly significant upon the party’s arrival, marking a breakthrough in his research.
source_quote: a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts. Which had, until recently, been a quiet, small area of study.

subject: House T'sarran's motives
fact: The reason House T'sarran sent a spy to follow the party in daylight — rather than attack — is unknown; the assignment appears misaligned with typical drow aggression, suggesting internal politics or a coerced mission.
source_quote: Whoever sent a drow to the surface in daylight to shadow a party through open forest had, I thought, given that drow exactly the kind of assignment that earns you a very sincere complaint when you get back home.

subject: identity of Daz's protectors
fact: The true identity of the hidden entity protecting Daz remains unknown, but the party believes it can be revealed by observing who intervenes when he is threatened or killed.
source_quote: The matron's interest is the reason; the matron's interest is sufficient... We need to kill Daz... And then we'll find out who's protecting him.

subject: Identity of the Person Who Paid for Daz
fact: The spy's matron believes the individual who paid for Daz's release will reveal themselves once he surfaces, making Daz a target of indirect surveillance; the true identity of this person remains unknown and is the central unresolved motive of the operation.
source_quote: My matron believes that the one who paid — " and here she pointed at me — "for him, will reveal themselves once he reaches the surface.

subject: Jimjar's return
fact: Speculation exists that the tracker might be Jimjar, returning to drag the party back underground — a possibility not ruled out, linking current events to past assumptions about their environment and mission.
source_quote: Someone speculated it might be Jimjar, coming to drag us back underground. I did not rule it out.

subject: Jimjar thread
fact: The Jimjar thread is a scholarly inquiry assigned to Zalthir, which unexpectedly intersects with the interests of Khell-Vire and focuses specifically on Grygum, not the party as a whole.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific. The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular.

subject: Malfire citations
fact: The persistent citation of Malfire by Daz has become an ambient, unspoken norm within the party, so ingrained that it is referenced as a condition of their relationship, and the speaker confirms its accuracy by invoking Volume 3.
source_quote: It's like we're kind of sick of each other, but somehow still together, yeah.", "As Malfire said in Volume 3.

subject: the identity of the shrunken spy
fact: A miniaturized assassin — possibly a drow, possibly something else — was contained within the bag of holding, observed by Glabbagool with one eye. Her identity, origin, and purpose remain unknown, and her survival inside the bag suggests she is more than a prisoner — perhaps a weapon, a traitor, or a survivor.
source_quote: Somewhere in there, one eye was open.

subject: theological implications of conversion
fact: The theological implications of a half-orc cleric of Bahamut remain unresolved, with unanswered questions about Bahamut’s intentions, the nature of the conversion phenomenon, and its place in broader divine architecture.
source_quote: About Bahamut's intentions, about what my conversion meant in the broader theological landscape, about why Vareth's previously obscure field had become a flood.

subject: theological implications of half-orc Bahamut conversions
fact: The theological implications of half-orc conversions to Bahamut remain unresolved, with scholars debating whether this reflects divine strategy, cultural evolution, or accidental alignment, and the speaker’s personal experience is now a central data point.
source_quote: What did the sudden half-orc interest in Bahamut mean for the orc pantheon? Was it part of Bahamut's plan?

subject: The Patron Who Paid for Daz's Protection
fact: An unknown patron paid to protect Daz, triggering House T'sarran’s long-term surveillance operation; this revelation suggests a hidden political or magical debt that predates Daz’s return to the surface and may involve powerful forces beyond the Underdark.
source_quote: We are looking for the one who paid to have you protected.

subject: the pursuer’s identity
fact: The identity, motive, and origin of the hidden follower remain unknown. Its presence suggests deeper, surface-level threats connected to Underdark events — a looming danger not yet named.
source_quote: Whatever was in those trees had been moving with us... Patient.

subject: Thorin's clan petition
fact: Thorin has formally asked to join Eldeth's clan, suggesting a deeper desire for belonging and identity beyond his giant-raised origins — a question left open but emotionally resolved.
source_quote: Is there any way that I can petition to become part of your clan?

subject: Thorin’s dwarven identity
fact: Thorin’s journey to reconcile his giant upbringing with his dwarven heritage remains unresolved. Eldeth’s oath offers a path, but whether the clan will accept him — and how he will define himself — is an open thread.
source_quote: I do want to learn about my dwarven roots.

subject: Thorin's identity integration
fact: Thorin's journey to reconcile his giant upbringing with his dwarven heritage is an unresolved personal thread that may define his role in the clan.
source_quote: I want to become an integrated person — both my giant upbringing, but also my cultural roots

subject: who is protecting Daz
fact: The entire party’s strategy revolves around determining who is protecting Daz — whether through magical surveillance, divine intervention, or hidden allegiance — and the temporary death plan, the prayer beads, and the spy’s containment are all tools to expose that protector.

subject: defacement timing
fact: The appendix was removed at least fifty years ago, placing the erasure before the last known use of the name Daz'issin in recorded history.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: We'd been on the road south out of the Silver Marches long enough that I'd stopped counting days and started counting how much my boots hurt.

subject: fifty years ago
fact: The appendix containing the name Daz'issin was physically removed from the book at least fifty years ago — a timestamp aligning with the last known usage of the name and the extinction of its associated houses.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: razor removal of appendix
fact: The appendix was removed with a razor at least fifty years ago.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the continuation of a session centered on the journey to Candlekeep, following the Burning Wizard Inn and preceding the formal intake of the party.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Daz, Scene: The Burning Wizard Inn]

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a continuous sequence of encounters, revelations, and therapies spanning the Underdark, Waterdeep, and Candlekeep — culminating in formal recognition of sentient entities outside traditional classifications.
source_quote: We've had many, many adventures, yada yada yada.
