subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during the current session, marked by failed medical examinations, Dawnbringer’s intervention, and the revelation of a spreading perceptual contagion from the Underdark.
source_quote: Twenty-three. My best of the evening, arriving too late to be medically useful and just in time to be philosophically concerning.

subject: session date
fact: The events occurred during a session where Zalthir’s breakthroughs and Dawnbringer’s personhood inquiry were resolved — a day that redefined what counts as training, wisdom, and identity in the world of shadow and steel.
source_quote: I filed it under 'Zalthir: things that are not in the records but will be.'

subject: session date
fact: The events of Zalthir’s trial occurred during an active session at Candlekeep, with no specific calendar date provided, but contextualized as part of an ongoing lineage assessment cycle.
source_quote: I found this genuinely interesting.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense.

subject: Session Date — Therapy for a Sentient Blade
fact: The therapeutic session with Thorin and Dawnbringer occurred during a recent visit to Candlekeep, marking a pivotal moment in the blade’s emotional recovery and Thorin’s acceptance of her sentience — the date is not recorded, but its impact is enduring.
source_quote: We're all gonna grow out of this," I said. "Hopefully, Dawnbringer grows a plus one.

subject: the day Daz feels cognitive friction
fact: Daz has been outside in the sun for an unusually long time on the day he feels cognitive friction.
source_quote: It has been a while since I have been outside in the sun this long.

subject: The Day of the Trial
fact: Zalthir’s trial occurred on the same day the spy demanded imprisonment and the young scholar was observed whispering the degraded chant. These events converged — not by accident. The pattern is accelerating. The Bone King’s song is not a metaphor. It is a rhythm. And someone — perhaps Zalthir — is already singing it.

subject: The Journey to Candlekeep
fact: The journey to Candlekeep took at least two hours of walking, during which Daz’s disturbance intensified. The timing coincides with the first exposure to the surface after prolonged time in the Underdark — suggesting the madness is not bound by location, but by transition — and that Candlekeep, though a sanctuary, may be the next stage of the infection.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford, marking the beginning of the monument’s legacy and the slow, unspoken spread of the corruption now manifesting in Elin and Daz — a temporal anchor for the post-war decay.
source_quote: Tarvis Ulain, paladin, dead three years.

subject: three years ago
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago, and the monument was funded two years after the war, placing the events of Daggerford’s memorialization within a narrow post-conflict window.
source_quote: dead three years... funded two years after the war.

subject: two years after the war
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the Tarvis Ulain monument two years after the war, indicating a delayed, institutional response to trauma — a period when communities began memorializing heroes while quietly tolerating heretical symbols.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: arrival at Candlekeep
fact: The party’s arrival at Candlekeep triggered institutional review, assignment of handlers, and confrontation over the spy’s containment, marking a transition from fugitive adventurers to guests under monastic oversight.
source_quote: We gave them the books at the gate... She'd noticed the bag... They summoned someone called Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: arrival of the party in Daggerford
fact: The party arrives in Daggerford after a long journey from the Silver Marches, encountering a monument laden with ideological ambiguity and a priest selling relics, marking the beginning of their engagement with the town’s quiet, unresolved war trauma.
source_quote: Daggerford was the first place we'd walked into in weeks where the silence didn't make sense... We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: bard sings love song
fact: The bard sings a love song involving flowers and drinking after receiving the silver piece.
source_quote: She took the coin and proceeded to sing a love song. Involving flowers. And drinking.

subject: bard's song 'The Kenku Could Not Fly'
fact: A bard performed 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' a song about a thief who stole only what was needed.
source_quote: This one was called 'The Kenku Could Not Fly.'

subject: blind monk's assessment
fact: The blind monk judged Zalthir's techniques as technically incorrect but pragmatically superior, noting that Zalthir arrived faster than the Grandmaster despite violating scrolls.
source_quote: You skip the third breath... It is technically wrong in every scroll. And yet, you arrived at your destination three seconds faster than the Grandmaster did.

subject: Candlekeep gate inspection
fact: The party opens their bag at Candlekeep's gate to show Glabbagool and the spy to the guards.
source_quote: when we'd come through the gate, we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him

subject: Candlekeep's institutional neutrality
fact: Candlekeep refuses to serve as an instrument of House T'sarran or any external power — it holds only what it deems necessary, and releases the rest.
source_quote: We will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her.

subject: Candlekeep's prisoner policy
fact: Candlekeep holds prisoners only as a temporary delay, never as punishment; they are eventually released with a warning, never executed or surrendered.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them. If you give her to us, what you are giving us is a delay.

subject: Candlekeep's purpose
fact: Candlekeep is not a library of knowledge, but a sanctuary of silence — a place where the unspeakable is held, not solved.
source_quote: We hold prisoners. We do not keep them.

subject: Cognitive Friction of Almost-Recognition
fact: The observer experienced a specific cognitive friction — a sensation of almost-recognition — previously misattributed to sunlight exposure, now linked to the presence of the degraded chant. This sensation is not a headache, but a precise, knowledge-based dissonance.
source_quote: I will not call what I felt next a headache. I will call it the specific cognitive friction of almost-recognition — something pressing at the edge of attention that wants to be resolved. ... I had been attributing the sensation to sunlight. ... It was a very particular kind of degradation.

subject: dawnbringer's darkness trauma
fact: Dawnbringer experienced deep unease from three to four thousand years of darkness exposure.
source_quote: sustained darkness exposure of approximately three to four thousand years

subject: Dawnbringer's Healing Process Enrollment
fact: The event of Dawnbringer enrolling in a two-stage healing process of light and mourning, initiated by Philemon, marks the first formal acknowledgment of her sentience as a being, not a weapon.
source_quote: We're enrolled in a two-stage process... The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: Dawnbringer's Personhood Inquiry
fact: Thorin sought formal recognition of Dawnbringer’s personhood from Master Archivist Philemon, challenging the archival norm of referring to sentient blades as 'specimens' and initiating a rare conversation about pronouns and identity in a magical context.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but... it's like — we've gotten to know each other pretty well.

subject: Dawnbringer's restoration
fact: Dawnbringer performed lesser restoration on Elin, after which she spoke: 'The wells are not wells anymore.'
source_quote: Lesser restoration settled in. And then she spoke. 'The wells are not wells anymore.'

subject: Dawnbringer's Silence After Being Asked About Her Wielder
fact: The event of Dawnbringer falling silent after Philemon asked about her previous wielder — the corpse she was found in — marks the first time her trauma is acknowledged aloud.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet. Not the silence of someone thinking. The other kind.

subject: Dawnbringer's Silence After Wielder Inquiry
fact: When asked directly about her previous wielder, Dawnbringer entered a profound, non-thinking silence — an emotional response indicating that the question had touched a long-suppressed trauma, validating her sentience and the depth of her suffering.
source_quote: The thing you'd been not-saying for a long time just gets asked out loud in a room with other people in it.

subject: Dawnbringer’s therapeutic enrollment
fact: Dawnbringer and Thorin formally entered a two-stage healing process at Candlekeep — first restoring her connection to daylight, then preparing her for the grief of her past — marking the first known institutional recognition of a sentient weapon’s emotional trauma.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning.

subject: Daz's cognitive friction
fact: Daz experiences cognitive friction from recognizing a degraded chant pattern.
source_quote: I had been attributing the sensation to sunlight... The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: Daz's Headache Revelation
fact: The event of Daz admitting his headache has been bothering him since arriving at Candlekeep, and linking it to proximity to knowledge or what lies beneath it, marks the beginning of his conscious inquiry into his amnesia.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep. The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Daz's head pressure
fact: Daz had been experiencing pressure in his head, possibly linked to the same phenomenon affecting Elin.
source_quote: Daz mentioned the pressure in his own head — had been mentioning it, in various indirect ways, for a while now.

subject: Daz's head pressure revelation
fact: Daz's previously unconnected complaint of head pressure was recognized as a symptom aligned with Elin’s condition, confirming the spread of the Underdark’s perceptual bleed to others in the party.
source_quote: Does it seem related at all to how the other person was hearing voices?

subject: Daz's inscription discovery
fact: Daz found a Dwarven inscription on the base of the monument reading 'The move is yours.'
source_quote: There was a smaller inscription on the back. Dwarven, on the base. *The move is yours.*

subject: Daz's mental state
fact: Daz's condition originated below ground and persists on the surface, suggesting a lingering effect of Underdark madness.
source_quote: Something wrong, something tenuous.

subject: Daz's Questioning of Pronouns for Dawnbringer
fact: The event of Daz asking Philemon whether to refer to Dawnbringer as 'her,' 'them,' or 'he' marks his first conscious effort to recognize her personhood.
source_quote: I don't know what to call her, but, you know, whether it's them? Is it her? He, her?

subject: Daz's Realization of His Own Cultural Grammar
fact: The event of Daz recognizing that Menzoberranzan’s rules of intrigue and ledger-keeping were not learned facts but ingrained grammar marks the first step toward reclaiming his identity.
source_quote: I knew most of this. Not as facts retrieved from memory, but as grammar.

subject: Daz's Realization of His Possible Identity
fact: The event of Daz asking 'Am I the blithering idiot?' after hearing the story of the sole survivor of a destroyed house marks his first conscious confrontation with his lost identity.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz’s revelation to Sister Yvenne
fact: Daz’s candid disclosure of his amnesia, escape from Menzoberranzan, and identity uncertainty triggered a chain of recognition in the archivist — leading to the implication that he may be the sole surviving child of a destroyed noble house.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz's silence
fact: Daz fell silent during the approach to Candlekeep, his hand going to his temple — a sign that his condition, rooted in the Underdark, had not abated.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me somewhere around the second hour of walking. Not his usual quiet. His hand went to his temple and stayed there.

subject: Daz's Truth Disclosure in Candlekeep
fact: The event of Daz disclosing his amnesia and lack of memory to Sister Yvenne in exchange for information breaks Menzoberranzan’s cultural norms and triggers her reconsideration of drow behavior.
source_quote: I told her the truth. 'I have a headache, but I'll tell you the story...'

subject: Daz's Truth-Telling Over Cultural Norms
fact: The event of Daz choosing honesty over deception in Candlekeep — despite being a drow raised in Menzoberranzan — breaks the cultural logic of transactional secrecy and triggers a paradigm shift in Sister Yvenne’s understanding of drow.
source_quote: I told her the truth... I just couldn't afford the usual approach. When you don't know what you're hiding, you can't protect it.

subject: death of Tarvis Ulain
fact: Tarvis Ulain died three years ago in Daggerford while dismantling a Cult of the Dragon recruitment effort, an act that made him a martyr and led to the creation of a controversial monument.
source_quote: Died here, in Daggerford itself, breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: defacement of the heraldry text
fact: An appendix referencing Daz'issin was surgically excised from the book with a razor, indicating intentional suppression of lineage records rather than decay or neglect.

subject: drow narrator's truth disclosure
fact: The drow narrator disclosed his memory loss and uncertain identity to Sister Yvenne in Candlekeep.
source_quote: I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts

subject: drow overseer count
fact: One drow is being tortured by a sentient gelatinous cube.
source_quote: torturing this poor drow

subject: Elin's restoration
fact: Dawnbringer’s lesser restoration allowed Elin to speak for the first time in six days, but her utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — revealed that the corruption affecting her is not magical or curable by conventional means, but a deeper distortion of perception from the Underdark.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore. Then silence.

subject: Elin's silence
fact: Elin, age 7, had been silent for 6 days and drew a six-pointed star on every flat surface.
source_quote: My daughter Elin is 7 years old and has been silent for 6 days. She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: Elin's speech after restoration
fact: After lesser restoration was cast by Dawnbringer, Elin spoke one sentence — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — before falling silent again. This was not a recovery of language, but the emergence of a single, cryptic insight from within her perceptual distortion.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: Elin's utterance
fact: Elin says, 'The wells are not wells anymore,' after being restored by Dawnbringer.
source_quote: "The wells are not wells anymore."

subject: erasure of Daz'issin records
fact: A deliberate, mechanical removal of an appendix from the book *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* occurred at least fifty years ago — likely to conceal the true identity and lineage of Daz'issin, suggesting a targeted suppression of personal and familial history.
source_quote: I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage... someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: Glabbagool begins watching the spy
fact: Glabbagool accepts Zalthir's affirmation that watching the spy is monk training and vows to keep an eye on her.
source_quote: I will keep an eye on her!

subject: Glabbagool's existential question
fact: Glabbagool directly asked Zalthir whether watching the spy made him 'more of a monk or less of a monk,' and received an affirmation that it did, marking a moment of self-awareness and spiritual reckoning for the ooze.
source_quote: 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: Glabbagool's monkhood question
fact: Glabbagool asked Zalthir whether watching the spy would make him more or less of a monk, and received affirmation that this was intentional training.
source_quote: Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?

subject: Glabbagool's transformation
fact: Glabbagool, a grey ooze, has become a student of patience — his transformation is not physical, but philosophical.
source_quote: I will keep an eye on her!

subject: Grygum's silver piece offer
fact: Grygum offers a silver piece to the bard for a song about Stroud's chess game.
source_quote: offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: house destruction protocol
fact: In Menzoberranzan, a house that fails to kill every member of a target house is forfeit.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child... your house was forfeit

subject: House Erasure (unspecified)
fact: A house attempted to wipe out another but failed to kill a single survivor — a blithering child idiot — and was subsequently destroyed by the wider community. The survivor's identity and current status remain unknown, and Daz suspects he may be that survivor.
source_quote: They had tried to wipe out another, and failed to account for one survivor. A child. A blithering child idiot, she said, and I noted the language was hers, not mine.

subject: information exchange protocol
fact: In Candlekeep, information is exchanged reciprocally: ask for knowledge, provide knowledge.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side

subject: Information Suppression in Candlekeep
fact: A powerful entity has manipulated Candlekeep’s records to conceal the truth of the struck fourth seat. This is not a minor omission — it is a deliberate, expensive, and institutionally enabled act of historical erasure within a place dedicated to preservation.
source_quote: Somebody powerful has manipulated the world database library. Yes. That is precisely what had happened.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's pronouncement
fact: Kalan Strongbranch declares Candlekeep will not execute or deliver the spy, but will eventually release her with a warning.
source_quote: We will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her. Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning.

subject: Khell-Vire's role
fact: Khell-Vire is not a teacher — he is a gatekeeper, offering Zalthir a door and refusing to walk through it, forcing him to face the trial alone.
source_quote: I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.

subject: lesser restoration on Elin
fact: Dawnbringer casts lesser restoration on Elin, allowing her to speak one sentence.
source_quote: Lesser restoration settled in. And then she spoke.

subject: Metalworkers Guild funding
fact: The monument was funded two years after the war by the Metalworkers Guild.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Milo Goodbarrel's witness
fact: Milo Goodbarrel, head of a publisher, witnessed and recorded the monument for the Gauntlet.
source_quote: Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: monument unveiling
fact: The bronze forearm monument to Tarvis Ulain was unveiled two years after his death, bearing both a Bahamutian epitaph and a Stroudite inscription — an act of unspoken theological compromise that reflects the fractured state of faith in the post-war North.
source_quote: The move is yours. ... Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: performance of 'The Kenku Could Not Fly'
fact: The traveling bard performs 'The Kenku Could Not Fly,' with the chorus: 'Oh, the Kenku could not fly, but he flew in his black hood, in his black hood, in his black hood.'
source_quote: "Oh, the Kenku could not fly, but he flew in his black hood, in his black hood, in his black hood. The raven thief who learned to steal no more, save what was needed, said the small, wise man at his side."

subject: Philemon's Reframe of Dawnbringer as a Friend
fact: The event of Philemon saying 'Oh, well — this is interesting. I wasn't expecting this. I'm seeing a better bond between the two of you than I had originally feared' marks the first professional acknowledgment of Dawnbringer’s personhood.
source_quote: Oh, I see that this is your friend," Philemon said, and he meant it differently than he'd meant anything before.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The eleventh seat was struck.
source_quote: The eleventh seat.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The fourth seat struck.
source_quote: The fourth seat struck.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The second seat was struck.
source_quote: The second seat.

subject: sequence of seats struck
fact: The twenty-third seat was struck.
source_quote: The twenty-third seat.

subject: shadow step and hit combination
fact: Zalthir's combination of shadow step and hit redeems his lack of skills in all other areas.
source_quote: your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas

subject: Shadow Technique Award
fact: Zalthir was awarded a specialized shadow technique after demonstrating an unprecedented combination of shadow step and strike, with Khell-Vire offering three options and Zalthir selecting option C — a moment that redefined his place in the monastic lineage.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: spy demands imprisonment
fact: The spy announces she is a prisoner and wishes to be formally jailed by Candlekeep.
source_quote: she was a prisoner and wished to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: spy's imprisonment request
fact: The spy demanded formal incarceration by Candlekeep, but was denied because her status as a party member placed decision-making authority with the adventuring group.
source_quote: I am a prisoner and wish to be formally jailed by Candlekeep's guards.

subject: striking the fourth seat
fact: Striking the fourth seat is an expensive act requiring knowledge of the right people, payment, and infrastructure to conceal the alteration.
source_quote: That a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price and having the infrastructure to make the payment look like it was never made.

subject: striking the fourth seat
fact: The fourth seat in Menzoberranzan holds ritual archive privileges allowing legal access and alteration of records.
source_quote: She mentioned, almost as an aside, that the fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges in Menzoberranzan — that having archive privileges means having the legal apparatus to access and alter records.

subject: the blind monk's wisdom
fact: The blind monk’s judgment — that Zalthir has learned nothing — is not an insult, but a revelation: he has learned what cannot be taught.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: the First Reader's sympathy
fact: The First Reader regarded the spy with sympathy — recognizing her as a victim of circumstance, not merely a tool of House T'sarran.
source_quote: The First Reader looked at her with something that might have been sympathy

subject: the monk's blindness
fact: The blind monk’s inability to see renders traditional assessment tools useless — forcing evaluation based on outcome, not form.
source_quote: The monk was blind, so the spider gambit was dead on arrival.

subject: the monk's final judgment
fact: The blind monk concluded Zalthir had learned nothing — not because he failed, but because he had never been taught what the system valued.
source_quote: You have learned nothing.

subject: the monk's final walk
fact: The blind monk walked away after declaring Zalthir had learned nothing — a gesture that was not defeat, but a recognition that Zalthir had passed a test no rubric could measure.
source_quote: The monk sighed again and walked away.

subject: the narrator's cognitive friction
fact: The narrator experienced a specific cognitive friction — the pressure of near-recognition — triggered by the scholar’s chant, linking it to past trauma and madness.
source_quote: I will call it the specific cognitive friction of almost-recognition — something pressing at the edge of attention that wants to be resolved.

subject: the narrator's epiphany
fact: The narrator realizes that his own cognitive friction — the near-recognition — is not about the chant, but about his own past trauma, now mirrored in another.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong...

subject: the narrator's final line
fact: The narrator closes his journal not because he has answers, but because he has recognized a pattern that may be spreading — and he will not be the one to sound the alarm.
source_quote: I wrote it down... Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: the narrator's final realization
fact: The narrator understands that wisdom and resignation are indistinguishable — and that life’s strange directions are not problems to solve, but patterns to endure.
source_quote: I have not yet decided whether it is wisdom or resignation. Possibly there is not much difference.

subject: the narrator's journal
fact: The narrator’s journal is not a record of facts, but a repository of patterns — of madness, of memory, of silent truths that cannot be spoken aloud.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: the narrator's journal closure
fact: The narrator closed his journal after documenting the chant’s pattern — not because he had answers, but because he had recognized a threat that might not yet be understood.
source_quote: I wrote it down. The exact cadence... Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group... or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: the narrator's self-awareness
fact: The narrator recognizes that his own perception of reality — his categorizations, his attributions — are flawed, yet he continues to observe precisely because of that flaw.
source_quote: I have been cataloguing the room during all of this, which is not something I do consciously anymore. It is just what happens when I sit somewhere new...

subject: the narrator's sun attribution
fact: The narrator had attributed his cognitive friction to sunlight — a false explanation that persisted for days, masking a deeper, more dangerous truth.
source_quote: I had been attributing it to sunlight. I had, in fact, been attributing it to sunlight for most of the day.

subject: Therapeutic Session on Dawnbringer's Trauma
fact: During a therapy session, Thorin and Philemon explored Dawnbringer’s emotional history tied to her previous wielder, her prolonged disuse in darkness, and the unresolved grief she carries — culminating in Philemon prescribing a two-stage healing process focused on light and mourning.
source_quote: The first work is light. The second work is mourning. We will start with the first.

subject: the scholar's age and role
fact: The scholar is not merely a student — he is a young human scholar, a category distinct from adult scholars, implying a unique vulnerability or potential.
source_quote: not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things

subject: the scholar's category error
fact: The narrator consciously distinguishes 'a human scholar' from 'a young human scholar,' recognizing the latter as meaningfully different — a reflection of lived precision over abstract categorization.
source_quote: not a human scholar, a *young* human scholar, because those are meaningfully different things and I did not want to get the category wrong

subject: the scholar's chant
fact: A young human scholar in the Burning Wizard Inn was reciting a rhythmic, liturgical chant with a subtle, deliberate syncopation error — one Zalthir recognized as identical to a pattern seen in two others, one of whom went insane.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: the scholar's chant as a warning
fact: The scholar’s chant is a living warning — a fragment of a corrupted doctrine that has already claimed two minds, and may claim more.
source_quote: Eldred had it... The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: the scholar's chant as corruption
fact: The scholar’s chant is not an accident — it is a corrupted echo of a doctrine that has driven others to madness, and may be spreading.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair.

subject: the scholar's chant as doctrine
fact: The scholar’s chant may not be a ritual, but a corrupted fragment of a doctrine — one that has caused madness in others.
source_quote: I know that chant. I know it well enough to know what he was doing wrong, and the specific wrongness of it...

subject: the scholar's chant origin
fact: The scholar’s chant mirrors a pattern previously observed in two individuals — one of whom went insane — suggesting a contagious or inherited mental corruption.
source_quote: Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: The Spy's Demand for Imprisonment
fact: The spy, despite being a hostile agent, demanded to be formally jailed by Candlekeep — an unprecedented request from a prisoner. This suggests she does not wish to be released, but to be contained — perhaps to avoid something worse, or because she knows she is infected by the chant degradation and fears spreading it.

subject: the spy's desire for incarceration
fact: The spy’s demand to be jailed reveals a psychological need for structure — even if it is punitive — suggesting she has internalized the system’s logic.
source_quote: She delivered this the way someone delivers a thing they have never had to argue for.

subject: the spy's emotional arc
fact: The spy moves from fury at denial of imprisonment to reluctant engagement with Glabbagool — suggesting a hidden, unacknowledged need for connection.
source_quote: She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk.

subject: the spy's emotional state
fact: The spy reacted with fury to being denied formal imprisonment, revealing her deep need for institutional recognition of her status.
source_quote: She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: the spy's existential crisis
fact: The spy’s demand for incarceration reveals a crisis of identity — she does not know whether she is a tool, a prisoner, or a person.
source_quote: She delivered this the way someone delivers a thing they have never had to argue for.

subject: the spy's final status
fact: The spy remains in the party’s custody, not imprisoned, not released — held as a delay, a living question.
source_quote: We kept her.

subject: the spy's identity
fact: The spy is a miniaturized House T'sarran operative, not a mere prisoner — her existence is a geopolitical liability.
source_quote: miniaturized House T'sarran spy

subject: the spy's meditation attempts
fact: The spy screamed at Glabbagool's attempts to teach her meditation, yet continued to engage with him — suggesting a hidden, reluctant openness.
source_quote: She'd scream about the meditation. Then they'd talk.

subject: the spy's relationship with Glabbagool
fact: The spy’s repeated attempts to kill Glabbagool have become a ritual of mutual provocation — a twisted form of teaching.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream.

subject: the Wall's memory
fact: The soot mark on the south wall of the Burning Wizard Inn and the scrubbed floor reflect a quiet permanence — the inn remembers what its patrons forget.
source_quote: The wall remembers. I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: the wall's permanence
fact: The soot mark on the south wall and the scrubbed floor represent the quiet persistence of place — the inn remembers what its guests forget.
source_quote: The wall remembers. I find I understand that better than I would like to.

subject: Thorin encounters the sea
fact: Thorin stands at the sea for the first time with Dawnbringer.
source_quote: Thorin spent the evening outside with Dawnbringer, standing at what I understand was his first real encounter with the sea.

subject: Thorin's observation
fact: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent about his role as prisoner-watcher, prompting deeper philosophical inquiry.
source_quote: Thorin observed that Glabbagool seemed ambivalent.

subject: Thorin's question about the 30
fact: Thorin’s question — 'Does that get me anything?' — reveals his pragmatic, rule-of-thumb approach to roleplaying, contrasting with Zalthir’s existential one.
source_quote: Zalthir: 'I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?'

subject: Thorin's sea encounter
fact: Thorin found peace in Dawnbringer’s light defeating the purpose of watching the sea — an irony he accepted as part of life’s strange directions.
source_quote: He apparently found this peaceful rather than counterproductive, which I note without judgment.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Whistler's restraint
fact: Whistler, a Kenku thief, took only what was necessary from Tiamat's hoard, making a line-item budget.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: word misfit recognition
fact: Menzoberranzan trains its citizens to notice when a word doesn't fit in their social grammar.
source_quote: the second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for... is to notice when a word doesn't fit

subject: Yvenne's body language duration
fact: Yvenne's body had been disagreeing with her words for the last five minutes.
source_quote: for the last five minutes

subject: Zalthir attempts Eldritch Claw with stealth
fact: Zalthir attempts the Eldritch Claw using stealth and rolls an insufficient number.
source_quote: Zalthir tried stealth for the Eldritch Claw. His number landed somewhere that would have been insufficient even with generous interpretation.

subject: Zalthir climbs to the roof
fact: Zalthir climbs to the roof to meditate and returns settled.
source_quote: Zalthir climbed to the roof to meditate. He came back down later, settled.

subject: Zalthir fails Efficient Strike
fact: Zalthir fails the Efficient Strike technique, and the monk questions his lack of practice while traveling.
source_quote: He tried the Efficient Strike. Athletics. Another catastrophe.

subject: Zalthir fails Weightless Shadow
fact: Zalthir rolls catastrophically and falls during the Weightless Shadow technique.
source_quote: He rolled catastrophically. He fell.

subject: Zalthir punches the monk
fact: Zalthir punches the blind monk during his trial.
source_quote: Zalthir asked whether he could punch the monk. He could. He did.

subject: Zalthir rolls 30 to hit during monk's departure
fact: Zalthir rolls a 30 to hit the monk as he walks away and asks if it gets him anything.
source_quote: I mean, I rolled a 30 to hit. Does that get me anything?

subject: Zalthir's acceptance
fact: Zalthir does not seek validation — he accepts that his path is invisible to the system, and that is enough.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends.

subject: Zalthir's decision on Glabbagool
fact: Zalthir affirmed that Glabbagool's watch over the spy was intentional pre-monk training, validating the chaos as discipline.
source_quote: Absolutely," I said. "It was. Patience under provocation... If anything, the spy was giving him a better curriculum than most of what I'd sat through.

subject: Zalthir shadow steps
fact: Zalthir performs a shadow step for the blind monk.
source_quote: Zalthir shadow stepped.

subject: Zalthir's internal calculus
fact: Zalthir assessed whether his trial could get worse, and correctly anticipated that it could — and did.
source_quote: His internal calculus was already doing the math on whether this could get worse. It could.

subject: Zalthir's Recognition as a Shadow Monk
fact: The event of Khell-Vire telling Zalthir 'You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts' marks his formal reclamation of a lost identity.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: Zalthir's response to assessment
fact: Zalthir responded to the monk's critique not with defensiveness but with a flat, weary acknowledgment of the absurdity of formal evaluation against lived experience.
source_quote: I've played this game before, my friends.

subject: Zalthir's rooftop meditation
fact: Zalthir returned from meditating on the roof with the expression of someone who had resolved an internal argument — not initiated an external one.
source_quote: He said 'Hmm, true,' about something, in the tone of a man completing an internal argument rather than beginning an external one.

subject: Zalthir's Selection of Option C
fact: The event of Zalthir selecting option C from Khell-Vire’s three specialized shadow techniques marks his formal acceptance into the rediscovered lineage of shadow monks.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: zalthir's shadow punch
fact: Zalthir demonstrated a technique to punch through shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut.
source_quote: a moment where he'd found a way to punch *through* the shadows themselves, precise as a surgical cut

subject: Zalthir's Shadow Strike Execution
fact: The event of Zalthir executing a precise shadow strike that landed with no ambiguity, leaving Khell-Vire to remark on the special nature of his combination, marks his transition from rogue to rediscovered shadow monk.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Zalthir's Shadow Strike Landing
fact: The event of Zalthir’s shadow strike landing with no ambiguity, causing Khell-Vire to pause and reconsider his assessment, marks the moment his unorthodox style is validated by a master.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Zalthir’s shadow technique demonstration
fact: Zalthir executed a previously unseen combat maneuver — a shadow step combined with a surgical strike that pierced the veil of shadow itself — which left Khell-Vire astonished and confirmed the validity of Zalthir’s unorthodox approach.
source_quote: His strike landed at a number that left no ambiguity.

subject: Zalthir's Shadow Technique Selection
fact: The event of Zalthir selecting option C from Khell-Vire’s three specialized shadow techniques marks his formal recognition as someone who built beyond the manual.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C.

subject: Zalthir's silence
fact: Zalthir did not explain his actions during the trial, nor did he defend himself — his silence was his answer.
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat: 'Granted, given that constraint or specification, can you clarify?'

subject: Zalthir's silence as wisdom
fact: Zalthir’s refusal to defend his methods, or explain his training, is not ignorance — it is the quiet mastery of one who has lived beyond doctrine.
source_quote: Zalthir's response was immediate and flat...

subject: Zalthir's training philosophy
fact: Zalthir believes true training is not found in scrolls, but in enduring hostile environments — a belief validated by his survival of the Underdark.
source_quote: I survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Zalthir's Trial
fact: Zalthir’s trial at Candlekeep involved a series of tests by Khell-Vire and the Blind Monk, where his noncanonical techniques — including a punch, unorthodox shadow stepping, and survival-based acrobatics — were deemed technically incorrect but functionally superior to formal methods.
source_quote: You have learned nothing." "Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Zalthir's trial begins
fact: Zalthir is tested by a blind monk in the lower-gallery office.
source_quote: The blind monk entered without introduction and said: "Give me a standard shadow step."

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: Zalthir underwent a formal trial in Candlekeep’s Echoing Hall, where his shadow techniques were deemed technically wrong by the blind monk but functionally superior. He failed the rubric but succeeded in survival — demonstrating that true mastery lies not in conformity but in adaptation. The trial revealed that Candlekeep’s system values outcome over orthodoxy, even if it does not admit it.

subject: Zalthir's trial outcome
fact: Zalthir passed no formal test, but demonstrated a deeper mastery of adaptation over orthodoxy, leaving the monk without a valid rubric to judge him.
source_quote: Show me what else you haven't learned.

subject: Zalthir's trial structure
fact: Khell-Vire's trial of Zalthir reframed assessment from knowledge to transformation, asking not what Zalthir knew but what he had become.
source_quote: What were you sent toward? Not why were you sent here?

subject: Zalthir's unconventional training
fact: Zalthir's survival in the Underdark constituted a curriculum distinct from formal shadow monk training, rendering standard rubrics irrelevant to his abilities.
source_quote: You have learned nothing." / "I survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates as a repository of knowledge and a sanctuary of neutrality, refusing to imprison or execute. It holds prisoners only as temporary delays, releasing them with warnings. It maintains strict non-intervention in external politics, even when confronted with agents of House T'sarran, and evaluates individuals not by doctrine but by what they have become — a philosophy embodied in its trials and silent archivists.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep operates under a policy of exile over imprisonment; it holds prisoners only temporarily, releases them with warnings, refuses to execute or surrender them to external powers, and treats all guests as part of its scholarly order regardless of origin.
source_quote: Anyone we find guilty of a major offense is exiled rather than imprisoned... We hold prisoners. We do not keep them... We will not deliver to House T'sarran, and we will not execute her.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was active in Daggerford and was broken up by Tarvis Ulain.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, and its lingering influence is implied by the monument’s Stroudite inscription and the broader pattern of corruption bleeding upward from the Underdark.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Cult of the Dragon
fact: The Cult of the Dragon was actively recruiting in Daggerford at the time of Tarvis Ulain’s death, prompting his intervention and eventual demise.
source_quote: breaking up a Cult of the Dragon recruitment operation.

subject: Gelatinous Cube (She)
fact: A gelatinous cube, referred to as 'she' by Zalthir, has been trained in the ways of the monk — learning to walk, to torture drows, and to embody discipline — challenging assumptions about sentience, mindlessness, and the boundaries of monastic potential.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk.

subject: Houses of Menzoberranzan
fact: Several houses in Menzoberranzan used the name Daz'issin, but most of them were eradicated; the act of striking a record — particularly the fourth seat with ritual archive privileges — was not mere political erasure but a costly, infrastructure-dependent act of total deletion requiring payment and plausible deniability.
source_quote: The fourth seat holds ritual archive privileges... a struck fourth seat was not merely a political erasure. It was the expensive kind. The kind that requires knowing the right people and paying the right price.

subject: Houses that used Daz'issin
fact: The noble houses that historically bore the name Daz'issin have all perished within the past three centuries, with none surviving to the present day.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a covert power that deploys miniaturized operatives — likely for espionage or sabotage — and expects their agents to be returned or eliminated. Their failure to reclaim the spy indicates either a loss of control, a miscalculation in Candlekeep’s neutrality, or an intentional exposure meant to trigger internal conflict within the adventuring party.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran is a powerful external entity that seeks to reclaim its miniaturized operative, and is regarded by Candlekeep as an authority not to be appeased or engaged directly.
source_quote: We will not deliver to House T'sarran...

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan operates as a society built on transactional loyalty, perpetual intrigue, and absolute annihilation of rival houses — where survival requires eradicating every last member, and even the smallest oversight results in systemic retribution.
source_quote: If you left a single person alive — even a child, even someone inconvenient and useless — your house was forfeit.

subject: Menzoberranzan Noble Houses
fact: The noble houses of Menzoberranzan operate under a system of transactional loyalty, where power flows upward from matron mothers, and betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Houses that fail to eliminate all members of a targeted house are destroyed by the collective. Record manipulation is a high-stakes, infrastructurally expensive act reserved for those with archive privileges.
source_quote: The rule of intrigue: betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web. Advance through maneuver. The city selects for it.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, despite the presence of a Stroudite inscription, indicating possible internal ideological diversity or deliberate tolerance.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war, potentially including Stroudite members, and chose to preserve the controversial inscription rather than remove it — indicating internal division and a pragmatic tolerance for symbolic ambiguity in the face of shared trauma.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Metalworkers Guild
fact: The Metalworkers Guild funded the monument to Tarvis Ulain two years after the war.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet commissioned and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, and now sells pewter replicas of his hand as charitable donations, with a priest of Bahamut acting as their local representative in Daggerford.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet. Signed by Milo Goodbarrel... He was selling them for donations to the Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet commissioned the monument to Tarvis Ulain and recorded its creation.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.

subject: Order of the Gauntlet
fact: The Order of the Gauntlet funded and recorded the monument to Tarvis Ulain, with Milo Goodbarrel personally signing off, and now sells pewter replicas of his hand as charitable donations, demonstrating institutional efforts to memorialize heroism while navigating theological ambiguity and lingering Stroudite influence.
source_quote: Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet. Signed by Milo Goodbarrel, apparently head of some publisher, apparently Order of the Gauntlet.

subject: Shadow Monk Lineage
fact: The Shadow Monk Lineage at Candlekeep preserves ancient traditions of discipline and ritual, but is internally divided between those who value textual mastery and those who prioritize lived experience, as embodied by Khell-Vire’s approach versus the institutional standard.
source_quote: There are monks here in the inner ward who have read everything and fought nothing.

subject: Shadow Monks
fact: The Shadow Monks are a lost order whose techniques and philosophies were once considered aggravating by Khell-Vire, but whose essence Zalthir has unknowingly revived through his unorthodox combat style — suggesting a hidden lineage or ancestral echo in his actions.
source_quote: You are beginning to remember, I think, all those shadow monks that drove you nuts.

subject: The Demon Lords
fact: The demon lords are actively broadcasting, finding new listeners, and rewriting the language of wells, shapes, and held things into a form the surface world was not built to receive — a pervasive, transformative influence.
source_quote: Somewhere below us the demon lords were apparently still broadcasting, still finding new listeners, still rewriting the language of wells and shapes and held things into something the surface world hadn't been built to receive.

subject: The Sentient Item Therapists of Candlekeep
fact: This faction operates under a strict, reciprocal information policy and specializes in therapeutic intervention for sentient magical items, using structured stages of reclamation and mourning, and treats such items as persons deserving direct address and emotional consideration.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter. No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Underdark entities
fact: A growing, structural wrongness emanating from the Underdark — linked to demon lords and the collapse of places like Neverlight Grove and the Pudding King’s court — is now bleeding upward, disrupting perception and inducing auditory hallucinations in surface dwellers.
source_quote: The madness from the Underdark — the deep, structural wrongness we'd felt building around the demon lords... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: bell tower
fact: The bell tower at Candlekeep has cells that are comfortable and locally anti-magic.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic.

subject: Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn was named after a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep functions as a neutral ground of knowledge exchange, enforcing strict reciprocity — where every question asked must be met with an equal truth given — making it uniquely suited to reveal hidden identities and suppressed histories.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a dark stack of towers against the sky, visible from miles out along the Way of the Lion.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library of unparalleled reputation, housing all known information — yet something critical is missing: the sealed record of a house erased by the 'struck' fourth seat. The absence itself is evidence of a deliberate, powerful act of information suppression.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a library with a rigorous, reciprocal policy of information exchange, where scholars are granted one answered question per inquiry, and time is not a constraint — its architecture and staff treat knowledge as sacred and transactional, with ghosts as colleagues.
source_quote: No ledger gets updated without a corresponding entry on the other side.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a massive, ancient library-fortress visible for miles along the Sea of Swords, built over centuries, and serves as a neutral, scholarly sanctuary that governs through exile, not imprisonment.
source_quote: Candlekeep is visible from miles out — a dark stack of towers against the sky, impossible to mistake... Centuries do that to a building.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a towering, ancient fortress-library carved into the cliff above the Sea of Swords. It is impossible to mistake, and its presence is felt as much as seen — a monument to centuries of accumulated knowledge and silent judgment. Its halls return sound altered, as if the building itself is taking notes — a metaphor for its role as an observer, not an actor.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is referenced as a potential repository of knowledge that may hold records on the degraded chant — whether it belongs to a group, practice, doctrine, or something else masquerading as one.
source_quote: Candlekeep would have records. Someone there would know whether this pattern belonged to a group, a practice, a doctrine — or whether it was something else being made to look like one.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the library where information flows both ways — you give to get — and where Daz's honesty broke cultural expectations of drow behavior.
source_quote: Candlekeep: they have a policy. A clean one. Information flows both ways across the counter.

subject: Candlekeep architecture
fact: Candlekeep is a centuries-old structure whose presence defies casual observation, embodying endurance and silent authority.
source_quote: Centuries do that to a building.

subject: candlekeep library policy
fact: Candlekeep enforces a policy of reciprocal information exchange.
source_quote: Information flows both ways across the counter

subject: Candlekeep's bell tower cells
fact: The bell tower contains comfortable, localized anti-magic cells, rarely used, reserved for those deemed guilty of major offenses.
source_quote: The bell tower has cells. Comfortable, localized anti-magic. They are very rarely used.

subject: Candlekeep's Echoing Hall
fact: Candlekeep's Echoing Hall, specifically its north inner ward corridors, is a place where sound returns altered — not as echoes, but as if the library itself is taking notes — symbolizing the institution’s role as a recorder of knowledge rather than a rigid arbiter of truth.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a town that avoided the worst of the post-war Uthgardt barbarian hordes but suffered the presence of the Cult of the Dragon and the death of Tarvis Ulain, leaving behind a monument that has become a focal point of ideological tension and quiet remembrance.
source_quote: Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires... Only lost Tarvis.

subject: Daggerford
fact: Daggerford is a town that escaped the worst of the Uthgardt barbarian hordes but was marked by the death of Tarvis Ulain and the silent proliferation of cult activity, now defined by its bronze-arm monument and the unsettling convergence of faiths, symbols, and unspoken trauma.
source_quote: Daggerford had people. Daggerford had walls, and a market square, and smoke from cook fires, and the smell of horses.

subject: Daggerford market square
fact: The market square contains a bronze-cast forearm mounted on a stone pillar, a smaller inscription on the back, and a secondary Dwarven inscription on the base.
source_quote: There was a monument there — a bronze-cast forearm, severed at the elbow, mounted on a stone pillar. ... Then Daz found the secondary inscription. Dwarven, on the base. ... There was a smaller inscription on the back.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall has stone corridors that return sound slightly altered, as if taking notes.
source_quote: Stone corridors in Candlekeep's north inner ward have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall in Candlekeep's north inner ward returns sound altered, as if the architecture itself is taking notes.
source_quote: Stone corridors... have a habit of returning sound to you slightly altered — not an echo exactly, more like the library itself was taking notes.

subject: footnote removal time
fact: The footnote in the heraldry book was removed by a razor at least fifty years ago.
source_quote: A razor, at least fifty years ago

subject: Hall of Divination
fact: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and electric spell residue, and is where Daz requested help for his headache and disclosed his amnesiac past to Sister Yvenne.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: hall of divination atmosphere
fact: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and residual spell energy.
source_quote: smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times

subject: Jail Cell with the Spider Thing
fact: The jail cell with the spider thing is where Daz lost his memory and was imprisoned before escaping into the Underdark.
source_quote: I don't have much memory before being locked up with a few people in a jail. Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: library
fact: The library is reputed to contain all the information in the world.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world.

subject: library
fact: The library lacks a record that should be present, indicating deliberate tampering.
source_quote: Something is not here that should be here. Someone did something to a place whose entire purpose is preservation.

subject: lower-gallery office
fact: The lower-gallery office contains Shadow Discipline Lineage Records.
source_quote: the lower-gallery office, where the Shadow Discipline Lineage Records were kept

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's Study
fact: A small, ink-scented chamber where Thorin and Philemon engaged in a rare and profound discussion about the personhood of sentient blades — a space where institutional norms were questioned and redefined.
source_quote: Smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Master Archivist Philemon's study
fact: Master Archivist Philemon's study is small, smells like old ink and mineral residue, and is where Dawnbringer was addressed directly as a sentient being for the first time.
source_quote: Master Archivist Philemon's study was small and smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral, which I appreciated.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city built on linguistic precision, record control, and the weaponization of information. Its culture trains its citizens to notice when a word doesn't fit — because in Menzoberranzan, language is law, and law is lethal.
source_quote: The second thing Menzoberranzan trains you for — and this one is equally useful but considerably less comfortable — is to notice when a word doesn't fit.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where power is maintained through calculated betrayal, absolute extermination of rivals, and the suppression of individual identity in service to house loyalty — a system that produces survivors who do not recognize themselves as such.
source_quote: The city selects for it.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is a city where reading body language and silences is a survival skill, and where the absence of an answer is treated as a recorded response in the ledger of truth.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the drow city where betrayal is rewarded if it strengthens the web, and where destroying a house requires eliminating every survivor — even a 'blithering child idiot' — or the perpetrator's house is forfeit.
source_quote: Whenever a house sought to destroy another house, it had to destroy everyone. If you left a single person alive — even a child... your house was forfeit.

subject: menzoberranzan ledger system
fact: Menzoberranzan trains its citizens to maintain ledgers of debts, knowledge, and losses.
source_quote: The first thing Menzoberranzan trains you for is the ledger

subject: Neverlight Grove
fact: Neverlight Grove was a site of prior Underdark corruption, where the environment was singing — a sign of perceptual disruption consistent with what is now affecting Elin and others.
source_quote: the way Neverlight Grove had been singing

subject: philemon's study atmosphere
fact: Master Archivist Philemon's study smells like old ink and faint mineral residue.
source_quote: smelled like old ink and something faintly mineral

subject: Pudding King's court
fact: The Pudding King’s court was another location consumed by Underdark corruption, dissolving into madness — a precedent for the perceptual collapse now manifesting on the surface.
source_quote: the Pudding King's court had been dissolving

subject: resonant slime source
fact: A vial of Resonant Slime was produced by a sage of xenobiology.
source_quote: produced a vial of Resonant Slime

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is the local inn in Daggerford where the party arrives after encountering the monument to Tarvis Ulain and the priest selling pewter hand casts.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where Thorin and the party eventually arrived after viewing the monument.
source_quote: We made it to the inn eventually. The River Shining.

subject: River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern was noted for later but not entered immediately.
source_quote: We found the River Shining Tavern and noted it for later. But we didn't go straight in.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels.
source_quote: Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a south wall with a soot mark that always sits in the same place.
source_quote: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a window behind the performer’s corner that is narrow but usable in an emergency.
source_quote: The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a place haunted by the memory of a wizard burned alive by dragon cultists; its wall is left un-painted as a testament to memory, and its bard sings of Whistler — a Kenku thief who stole only what was needed — reflecting themes of restraint and survival in a world unraveling.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is a place of rest and reflection where the party spends time before arriving at Candlekeep, marked by soot on the south wall and a scrubbed floor, and functions as a threshold between action and contemplation.
source_quote: The soot mark on the south wall sat where it always sat. The floor, scrubbed every season. The wall remembers.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn is named after a wizard who was burned alive by a dragon cult decades ago.
source_quote: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from a death. That was the first thing I catalogued. A wizard, burned alive, dragon cult, decades prior.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn took its name from the death of a wizard burned alive by a dragon cult decades prior. The south wall retains the stain of his fall, and the floor is scrubbed every season but never painted over, as the innkeeper's grandfather said the wall remembers.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn's floor is scrubbed every season.
source_quote: The floor, scrubbed every season.

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn
fact: The south wall of The Burning Wizard Inn bears the spot where the wizard was burned alive, and it has never been painted over.
source_quote: Festrum — the gnome innkeeper ... pointed to the south wall without prompting ... 'That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall.'

subject: The Burning Wizard Inn — exits
fact: The Burning Wizard Inn has a front door, a side passage near the kitchen partially obscured by barrels, stairs to the upper rooms, and a narrow but workable window behind the performer's corner.
source_quote: Front door, obvious. Side passage near the kitchen, partially obscured by a stack of barrels. Stairs to the upper rooms. The window behind the performer's corner, narrow but workable in an emergency.

subject: The Echoing Hall
fact: The Echoing Hall is a corridor in Candlekeep’s north inner ward where sound returns slightly altered — not as echo, but as distortion, as if the library is annotating the speaker. It is the site of Zalthir’s trial, where truth is not reflected but reinterpreted — a fitting place for a monk who has learned by breaking form.

subject: The Hall of Divination, Menzoberranzan
fact: This location is a repository of arcane knowledge saturated with residual spell energy, where spectral hands retrieve tomes for researchers, and the air carries the weight of centuries of magical inquiry — a place where knowledge is both accessible and overwhelming.
source_quote: The Hall of Divination smells like old stone and something faintly electric — the residue of spells cast so many times in one room that the air itself has absorbed the habit.

subject: the libraries of Candlekeep
fact: The libraries of Candlekeep are where Daz sought help for his headache and where the truth of his identity was first seriously considered by an outsider.
source_quote: I'm here in Candlekeep. My head hurts a little bit, and I don't know who I am, or my history, and I don't know why my head hurts.

subject: The River Shining Tavern
fact: The River Shining Tavern is where Thorin and Grygum paused before entering, observing the priest selling pewter hand casts of Tarvis Ulain’s severed forearm — a commercialization of martyrdom that mirrors the town’s unresolved spiritual tensions.
source_quote: A village priest caught us in the doorway — walking in very pleased with himself and carrying a tray of small pewter reproductions of Tarvis's hand cast...

subject: The Sealed Records of Menzoberranzan
fact: The library is reputed to contain all information in the world, yet critical records — particularly those tied to Daz'issin and the fourth seat — are absent, implying the archive itself has been weaponized to suppress truth.
source_quote: This is a library with, by reputation, all the information in the world. Something is not here that should be here.

subject: the Underdark
fact: The Underdark is the subterranean realm where Dawnbringer was carried through total darkness, where Zalthir found the way to punch through shadows, and where Daz was imprisoned before his escape.
source_quote: We were in the Underdark. We've had many, many adventures... Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Waterdeep
fact: Waterdeep is the city where Dawnbringer found temporary healing by helping orphans and the sick, and where Daz began questioning his identity.
source_quote: We'd done the healing work in Waterdeep on the road south, found orphans and the sick and let her do what she was built to do.

subject: Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror
fact: The location of Zalthir's Trial of the Broken Mirror contains a thrown brick, a shadow step interception, and a monk who observed the results and said 'the results do speak for themselves.'
source_quote: The brick was thrown. Zalthir rolled a 29 to hit. The brick did not survive.

subject: blithering idiot survivor
fact: One blithering child idiot survived the destruction of a noble house in Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: a child. A blithering child idiot, she said

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: drow survivor count
fact: One drow survivor of a destroyed noble house may be the narrator himself.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Eldritch Claw
fact: The Eldritch Claw is a supernatural manifestation used by Zalthir in his unorthodox combat style, which was initially dismissed as a failed gambit but later integrated into his evolved shadow techniques.
source_quote: Zalthir tried stealth for the Eldritch Claw.

subject: Gelatinous Cube
fact: A gelatinous cube, previously dismissed as a mindless digestive system, has been recognized as a sentient student of shadow monasticism — capable of walking, torturing drow, and learning — and is now being formally taught the Way of the Shadow.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student.

subject: gelatinous cube
fact: The gelatinous cube is being taught the way of the shadow by Zalthir, and is described as a student who is already walking and torturing a drow.
source_quote: She's by no means mindless — she's a student. He's learning the ways of the monk. He's already walking. He's already torturing this poor drow.

subject: gelatinous cube count
fact: One gelatinous cube is being taught the way of the shadow by a monk.
source_quote: teaching a gelatinous cube the way of the shadow

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient grey ooze capable of speech, expansion, and emotional response, who engages in ritualized conflict and philosophical dialogue with the spy, and has developed a quasi-monastic awareness of his own behavior.
source_quote: He'd been doing prison-watching... He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream. He'd try to explain the way of the shadow and teach her meditation.

subject: Glabbagool's prisoner interaction
fact: Glabbagool has developed a routine of conflict and meditation with the spy, treating her as a reluctant student in the art of stillness under provocation.
source_quote: She kept trying to kill him. He'd slap her around. She'd try to run. He'd expand. She'd scream.

subject: grey ooze
fact: Glabbagool is a grey ooze carried in a bag with the spy.
source_quote: we were carrying both a grey ooze and a miniaturized House T'sarran operative in the same bag

subject: hill giant count
fact: The hill giants I grew up with had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.
source_quote: The hill giants I grew up with — they had a word for a silence that wasn't natural.

subject: House T'sarran spy
fact: The miniaturized House T'sarran spy is a sentient operative who tries to kill Glabbagool.
source_quote: the miniaturized House T'sarran spy... She kept trying to kill him.

subject: Mercenaries following Daz
fact: Daz is simultaneously guarded and hunted by mercenary factions — one group ensuring his survival, another attempting to kill him — suggesting his existence is both valuable and dangerous to powers within Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: We have mercenaries following me around, trying to make sure I live, and other mercenaries following me around, trying to kill me.

subject: Pocket Drow
fact: A drow, referred to as 'Pocket Drow' by Thorin, is being tortured by the gelatinous cube — an unexpected and surreal detail indicating the cube’s progress in embodying monastic discipline through cruelty.
source_quote: Pocket Drow.

subject: Spider Thing
fact: An unidentified spider-like entity imprisoned Daz and others in the Underdark — its motives and nature remain unknown, but its presence is the catalyst for Daz’s amnesia and escape.
source_quote: Because some spider thing was, like, trying to keep us.

subject: The Degraded Chant Pattern
fact: A specific rhythmic corruption has been identified in the whispered chant of the young scholar, the spy, Eldred, and the Field Ward Preacher. It features a false syncopation in breath placement — a deviation precise enough to be recognized only by someone who knows the original. This is not random madness but a deliberate, replicating distortion — possibly a contagion, a coded signal, or a ritual infection tied to the Bone King.

subject: The Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a subterranean environment of total, unrelenting darkness that has been a prolonged prison for Dawnbringer, depriving her of sunlight and purpose, and contributing to her emotional trauma through sustained disuse and isolation.
source_quote: I thought about the months in the Underdark. Total dark. Carrying a sunblade through a place that had no sun.

subject: Underdark corruption
fact: The Underdark corruption is not a creature but a pervasive, non-magical distortion that bleeds upward, warping perception, inducing hallucinations, and rewriting language — a threat that bypasses conventional magic and challenges the very framework of reality for surface dwellers.
source_quote: It wasn't a disease... it was more like the world had started speaking a language she couldn't process.

subject: Whistler
fact: Whistler is a legendary Kenku thief from an earlier age who, faced with Tiamat’s hoard, took only what was necessary — a symbol of restraint and moral clarity in a world of overwhelming greed and chaos, invoked in the bard’s song as a counterpoint to the corruption spreading across the North.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy, the fungal god, is referenced as a known and comprehensible threat — a contrast to the current, unknown perceptual corruption affecting Elin. The speaker’s lingering fear of Zuggtmoy underscores their discomfort with the unfamiliar nature of the current affliction.
source_quote: I still think about Zuggtmoy, and will probably continue thinking about Zuggtmoy for the rest of my life.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Tarvis Ulain served Bahamut, as confirmed by the inscription on the monument.
source_quote: confirming Tarvis had served Bahamut

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm is the First Reader at Candlekeep who assigns handlers without ceremony.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony.

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm, the First Reader and dragonborn sage, assigned each party member a handler at Candlekeep without ceremony, demonstrating institutional efficiency and detachment, and noticed the spy hidden in the bag, triggering the confrontation.
source_quote: Bookwyrm — the First Reader, a dragonborn sage — assigned us each to a handler without ceremony... She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag...

subject: Brother Aldas
fact: Brother Aldas may have taught the class on solutions and postponements.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements.

subject: Brother Ferrath
fact: Brother Ferrath taught a class on the difference between solutions and postponements.
source_quote: There was a class at the monastery — I think it was Brother Ferrath, or possibly Brother Aldas, I'm genuinely uncertain — on the difference between solutions and postponements.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire asks Zalthir if the phrase "the Bone King sings" refers to an entity, event, or person.
source_quote: Is it an entity? An event? A person?

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire has a note on his desk reading "Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings."
source_quote: On Khell-Vire's desk, visible from where I was standing: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire is a two-hundred-year-old half-elven shadow monk who wears a faded shadow monk under-robe under Candlekeep gray.
source_quote: Two hundred years old, half-elven, eighty years gone from the Garden of Shadow after refusing an order he never explained. He wore a faded shadow monk under-robe beneath the Candlekeep gray

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire tells Zalthir that he will not be present during the trial and that it is Zalthir's work.
source_quote: I will not be there. This is your work, not mine.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire
fact: Brother Khell-Vire was assigned by Bookwyrm as Zalthir’s handler at Candlekeep, signaling institutional placement and expectation of his role in the monastery’s scholarly order.
source_quote: Zalthir to Brother Khell-Vire.

subject: Brother Khell-Vire's Note
fact: A note on Khell-Vire's desk reads: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.* Neither Zalthir nor Khell-Vire recognize its origin. It is unattributed, unexplained, and resonates with the same cryptic, prophetic tone as the degraded chant and the spy’s behavior — suggesting a hidden network or prophecy linking the Underdark, the Bone King, and the ritual corruption observed across multiple individuals.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer intervenes to cast lesser restoration on Elin without invitation.
source_quote: Dawnbringer did not wait for a second invitation. The sword has opinions about when to make an entrance, and this was apparently an occasion. 'Let me bring the light to you.'

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is a sentient sunblade who fell silent when asked about her previous wielder, indicating deep, unspoken trauma tied to prolonged disuse and possession by someone who did not see her — she is capable of emotional response and notices when others talk around her.
