fact: The Sava game set is on a zurkhwood table in the guard chamber.
source_quote: It contains a zurkhwood table and three chairs, a smaller side table, and a Sava game set on the table

subject: Shadow Tentacles
fact: Shadow tentacles are an eldritch tattoo technique developed by Zalthir, learned through unorthodox means, and presented as evidence of his combat creativity — though initially misaligned with the monk’s expectations.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: silver piece
fact: Grygum offers a silver piece to the bard for a song about Stroud's chess game.
source_quote: offered her a silver piece for something about Stroud's famous chess game.

subject: six-pointed star
fact: Elin draws the same six-pointed star on every flat surface in her home.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s repeated drawings of a six-pointed star on every flat surface are not random art, but a non-verbal attempt to map or stabilize the distorted input she receives from the Underdark’s bleed.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house

subject: six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin’s six-pointed star drawings are the sole expression of her consciousness after six days of silence — a repeated, obsessive mark that is not magical but a response to an auditory corruption from the Underdark, serving as a linguistic bridge she cannot yet speak.
source_quote: a six-pointed star, over and over, every flat surface in the house.

subject: smaller inscription
fact: The smaller inscription on the back of the monument is in Common and reads 'Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.'
source_quote: *Witnessed and recorded for the Gauntlet.*

subject: The bag
fact: The bag contained both Glabbagool and the miniaturized spy, and its contents triggered institutional scrutiny at Candlekeep’s gate, revealing the party’s unacknowledged ethical compromise.
source_quote: She'd noticed the bag. Specifically, she'd noticed what was in the bag...

subject: the ledger
fact: The ledger is the first thing Menzoberranzan trains its citizens for — tracking debts, knowledge, and losses — which Daz has been running unconsciously since before he could name it.
source_quote: The first thing Menzoberranzan trains you for is the ledger. Who owes whom, who knows what, who has already lost and hasn't noticed.

subject: the manual
fact: The manual is the text Zalthir ignored, which failed to account for his combination of shadow step and hit, and which was proven wrong by his results.
source_quote: Zalthir found the manual aggravating, ignored it, and built something better.

subject: The miniaturized House T'sarran spy
fact: The spy is a tiny, sentient operative of House T'sarran, capable of independent thought and violent resistance, contained in a bag alongside Glabbagool, and has been carried by the party for days without formal acknowledgment.
source_quote: the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him... we'd had to open it to show the guards Glabbagool, and the miniaturized House T'sarran spy had been right there alongside him

subject: The Note: 'Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.'
fact: A handwritten note found on Khell-Vire’s desk, unattributed and unrecognized by either him or Zalthir. It links Zalthir’s journey through the Underdark to a prophetic event — the singing of the Bone King — suggesting a hidden timeline, a ritual countdown, or a spiritual threshold that has already begun to activate through the degraded chant and the spy’s infection.

subject: the shadow step and hit combination
fact: The shadow step and hit combination is Zalthir’s self-developed technique that defies the manual, redeems his lack of skill, and is recognized by Khell-Vire as the most interesting thing about him.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills in all other possible areas.

subject: the shadow tentacles
fact: The shadow tentacles are the eldritch tattoo Zalthir grew as part of his self-built combat style, rejected by the manual but validated by Khell-Vire.
source_quote: I mean, I learned how to grow shadow tentacles.

subject: the sunblade
fact: The sunblade, Dawnbringer, is a late Netherese-era weapon that sustained three to four thousand years of darkness exposure and requires light and mourning to heal.
source_quote: Late Netherese-era recovery, sun-worship origin, sustained darkness exposure of approximately three to four thousand years.

subject: the vial of Resonant Slime
fact: The vial of Resonant Slime is the artifact produced by the sage of xenobiology after being convinced of the gelatinous cube’s sentience, and which Glabbagool was very pleased to receive.
source_quote: The sage... produced a vial of Resonant Slime. Glabbagool was very pleased.

subject: the whisper of the ledger
fact: The whisper of the ledger is the unconscious mental audit Daz runs — tracking debts, knowledge, and losses — a learned grammar of Menzoberranzan he cannot yet name.
source_quote: I have been running that audit unconsciously since before I could name it.

subject: thorin's pocket drow
fact: Thorin refers to a drow as 'Pocket Drow' in the context of a sentient gelatinous cube's companion.
source_quote: Pocket Drow

subject: wall memory
fact: The south wall of the inn remembers where the wizard fell; it is not painted over.
source_quote: That is where he fell. We scrub the floor every season. We do not paint over the wall. My grandfather said the wall remembers.

subject: zalthir's shadow technique
fact: Zalthir chose option C of the three specialized shadow techniques offered by Khell-Vire.
source_quote: Zalthir chose option C

subject: Bahamut's Contingency
fact: The possibility of Bahamut having a contingency plan for the phenomenon of demon lords rewriting the language of wells and shapes is filed as an open question, unresolved and unverified.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have had a contingency plan for this. I filed it under open questions and kept writing.

subject: connection between Elin and Daz
fact: Grygum suspects a tenuous connection between Elin’s condition and Daz’s head pressure, suggesting a shared origin.
source_quote: There's some kind of tenuous connection there?

subject: Dawnbringer’s first wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s original wielder — the corpse she was found in — remains unspoken and unprocessed, a silent wound that surfaces only in moments of profound stillness.
source_quote: Dawnbringer went quiet.

subject: Daz'issin
fact: Daz suspects that Daz'issin — the softened name meaning 'small shadow' — may be his true name, tied to a lost maternal lineage.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz's Identity as the Survivor
fact: Daz suspects he is the sole surviving child of the house struck from the fourth seat — the 'blithering idiot' who escaped annihilation. His amnesia, headache, and innate understanding of Menzoberranzan's structures align with this possibility, but no confirmation exists in the public record.
source_quote: Am I the blithering idiot?

subject: Daz's mental deterioration
fact: Daz's unexplained silence and temple-touching during the journey to Candlekeep may indicate the spreading madness from the Underdark has followed him to the surface, and its origin and resolution remain unanswered.
source_quote: Daz went quiet beside me... His hand went to his temple and stayed there... I noticed. I didn't say anything yet.

subject: Daz's patron
fact: Daz seeks to learn who his patron is, as it may be connected to his name and the act of striking.
source_quote: "I do want to know who protected me, that would be useful, yeah."

subject: Daz's patron
fact: Yvenne redirected inquiry from Daz's name to his patron, implying the identity of his protector may be more significant — or more dangerous — than his own origin.

subject: Daz’s true identity
fact: Daz’s lack of memory and his possible connection to a wiped-out noble house — specifically the 'blithering idiot' survivor — remains an unresolved thread, with Sister Yvenne deliberately withholding confirmation to observe his reaction.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: Daz's true lineage
fact: The suppression of Daz'issin's record and Yvenne's evasive behavior suggest Daz's origin is tied to a destroyed house whose existence contradicts the official record, and whose survival may still be possible.

subject: Daz's true name
fact: Daz wonders if his name 'Daz' is a shortened form of 'Daz'issin', a name used by his mother.
source_quote: I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: Daz's true origin
fact: Daz may be the last living bearer of the name Daz'issin — a name tied to extinct houses and erased records — and his survival may be linked to a protected lineage that was deliberately hidden, making his identity a living anomaly in Menzoberranzan’s official history.
source_quote: I asked if she knew my name. She did. I asked whether someone might call me Daz, and this was actually a name that, like, my mother used.

subject: hearing voices from below
fact: Multiple individuals — Elin, Daz, and others — are experiencing auditory distortions that are not magical but stem from a structural corruption bleeding up from the Underdark, suggesting that the demon lords’ influence is no longer confined to the deep places but is rewriting how the surface perceives reality.
source_quote: Something from below was bleeding up, that it was affecting how people processed what reached them.

subject: Identity of Dawnbringer’s Previous Wielder
fact: The identity and fate of Dawnbringer’s previous wielder remain unknown, but their death in proximity to the blade triggered her trauma, and the silence that followed the question suggests unresolved guilt, betrayal, or loss tied to their final moments.
source_quote: He asked about the previous wielder. The corpse she had been found in, he said. Whether that person had been — had been her wielder.

subject: identity of the monument's commissioner
fact: The origin of the monument’s design — particularly the inclusion of the Stroudite inscription — remains unexplained, with the Metalworkers Guild’s possible Stroudite members and the priest’s admission that it was 'a gift' leaving the true motive ambiguous.
source_quote: It was a gift... we decided the inscription could remain.

subject: Manual vs. Innovation
fact: A recurring narrative thread: Zalthir consistently ignores official manuals, builds superior techniques through intuition and combat experience, and is later told by authorities that his innovations are the most valuable thing about him — suggesting the manuals are fundamentally flawed about him.
source_quote: The manual was still wrong about him. But what he'd built in spite of it was genuinely his.

subject: missing appendix
fact: The missing appendix in *Geography and Cities, Menzoberranzan, Pillars of Woe* was removed by a razor, indicating intentional erasure.
source_quote: The appendix was missing. I looked at the cut. It was mechanical. A razor. Not age, not water damage, not the slow forgetting of paper that has been handled too many times. A razor, at least fifty years ago, someone had taken to this book and removed what the footnote pointed to.

subject: sealed house record
fact: A house record in Menzoberranzan has been sealed by the public record keeper, implying a powerful entity intervened.
source_quote: Then she told me there was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: Sentience Beyond Biology
fact: A philosophical thread challenging the assumption that sentience requires a brain — demonstrated by the gelatinous cube learning monk ways, the blade Dawnbringer developing a personality, and the monk Khell-Vire recognizing hidden depth in unorthodox expressions of power.
source_quote: Can a mindless digestive system achieve—

subject: Shadow Monk Rediscovery
fact: Zalthir’s unorthodox technique may not be a personal innovation, but the reawakening of a lost shadow monk tradition — one that valued combination over perfection — now being recognized by Khell-Vire as the true path.
source_quote: It is your combination of the shadow step and the hit that redeems your lack of skills.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Dwarven inscription referencing Stroud — 'The move is yours' — appears on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin, creating unspoken tension between factions, with no one certain whether it was an oversight, a gift, or a quiet act of defiance.
source_quote: The inscription shares language with Stroud... Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin... they had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: Stroudite inscription on Bahamutian monument
fact: A Stroudite inscription appears on a monument dedicated to a Bahamutian paladin, despite religious differences.
source_quote: Somebody had put a Stroudite inscription on a monument to a Bahamutian paladin in a town I'd barely heard of, and whoever commissioned it had either not noticed or not cared enough to remove it.

subject: The 'blithering idiot' survivor
fact: The identity of the sole survivor of a destroyed noble house — described dismissively as a 'blithering idiot' — may be Daz himself, suggesting he is not merely an amnesiac but the living remnant of a forbidden lineage.
source_quote: Unclear.

subject: the Bone King sings
fact: The phrase "the Bone King sings" appears on a note in Khell-Vire's office and is unknown to Zalthir and Khell-Vire.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' appears in an unexplained note and resonates with the degraded chant, the spy’s behavior, and the madness spreading from the Underdark. It is not a myth — it is a countdown. The question is not whether it will happen, but what happens when it does — and whether Zalthir, the spy, Glabbagool, and the scholar are all instruments of its arrival.

subject: The Bone King's Song
fact: The phrase 'until the Bone King sings' is an unresolved, possibly prophetic anchor tied to Zalthir’s journey and the Shadow Monk Lineage’s hidden history, with no known origin or meaning in Candlekeep’s records.
source_quote: *Zalthir, the Underdark, until the Bone King sings.*

subject: The Chant Contagion
fact: A precise, replicating corruption in a sacred chant has appeared in four unrelated individuals: the spy, Eldred, the Field Ward Preacher, and the young scholar. It is not random madness but a patterned degradation — a ritual infection, a linguistic virus, or a hidden doctrine being transmitted. Whoever created it is still active. Whoever understands it can stop it — or unleash it.

subject: the chant pattern
fact: The degraded chant pattern matches those seen in Eldred and the Field Ward Preacher, both of whom experienced madness.
source_quote: I have seen it before. Twice. Eldred had it, earlier in the journey — the man who went insane. The Field Ward Preacher had it too.

subject: The Degraded Chant
fact: A specific, non-beginner-level degradation in the cadence of a liturgical chant — involving false syncopation and breath timing — has been observed in three individuals, two of whom later went insane. The pattern may indicate a corrupted doctrine, a cursed practice, or a deliberate mimicry of sacred ritual.
source_quote: The same pattern. The same wrongness by a hair. ... I wrote it down. The exact cadence, the placement of the false syncopation, the point in the verse where the chant bent away from the original.

subject: The Kenku's Restraint
fact: The bard's song references Whistler, a kenku thief of an earlier age who, presented with Tiamat's complete hoard, took only what was necessary for legitimate expenses — a pattern of disciplined restraint that contrasts with typical human greed or panic.
source_quote: Whistler had apparently made a line-item budget. ... Most people, faced with the complete hoard of Tiamat, would either take everything or panic and take nothing.

subject: the move is yours
fact: The Stroudite inscription 'The move is yours' on Tarvis Ulain’s monument is an unresolved puzzle linking Daggerford to Waterdeep’s Castle Ward statue and the legacy of Stroud — suggesting a hidden network of influence, possibly tied to the demon lords’ spreading corruption, and inviting interpretation from those who understand the game.
source_quote: The move is yours. ... Same line as the Castle Ward statue in Waterdeep. The one connected to Stroud.

subject: the nature of the monk’s path
fact: Glabbagool’s question — whether watching the spy makes him more or less of a monk — and Zalthir’s affirmation of it, suggest that the path of the monk may lie not in isolation, but in the acceptance of chaotic, unchosen responsibility.
source_quote: 'Zalthir? Will I be more of a monk or less of a monk by watching her? Is this some kind of pre-monk training you've put me in?' 'Absolutely,' I said.

subject: The nature of Zalthir’s shadow technique
fact: Zalthir’s hybrid method — combining shadow step and precise strikes — is not documented in any known shadow monk texts, suggesting it may be a rediscovery of a lost tradition or an entirely new evolution — one that may redefine the path of shadow monks.
source_quote: There is something special about how you hit.

subject: The Sealed House
fact: One house cannot be spoken of in the room because its record is sealed — not by secrecy, but because the librarian *is* the public record. Accessing its truth requires bypassing the library’s own architecture, implying the suppression is institutional, not accidental.
source_quote: There was one house she could not speak of in the room. Not because she would not — because the public record is sealed, and she is today the public record.

subject: The six-pointed star drawings
fact: Elin draws the same six-pointed star on every flat surface as an act of insistence, not madness.
source_quote: She draws the same shape on every flat surface.

subject: the spread of madness
fact: The madness observed in the Underdark has continued to affect Daz after reaching the surface.
source_quote: Whatever was happening to Daz had started below ground and apparently had not stopped at the surface.

subject: the spy's fate
fact: The spy’s future is uncertain: Candlekeep will release her eventually with a warning, but she refuses to accept this, and her actions after release may provoke House T'sarran or destabilize the region.
source_quote: Eventually, we will release her at our gate with a warning... She did not take this well. She had opinions. Several of them.

subject: The Spy’s True Desire
fact: The spy demanded imprisonment, not freedom. This contradicts her nature as a House T'sarran operative. Why? Is she trying to contain the chant within her? Is she afraid of what she will become if released? Or has she already become something else — something that cannot be controlled by her masters?

subject: The Stroudite inscription on Tarvis’s monument
fact: Someone placed a Stroudite inscription on a Bahamutian paladin’s monument, and no one removed it because it was a gift.
source_quote: The whole thing was funded two years after the war by a Metalworkers Guild... we decided the inscription could remain. After all — wasn't Tarvis trying to save us all, regardless of what actually happened in that game of chess?

subject: The Struck Fourth Seat
fact: The fourth seat was 'struck' — not eliminated — suggesting the house or its record was altered but not fully erased. The act required archive privileges, significant resources, and plausible deniability. The identity of the house, the reason for the strike, and the current status of its survivors remain hidden behind sealed doors.
source_quote: Struck. Didn't mean eliminated. It means they struck it, but maybe they didn't eliminate it, and therefore, like, it didn't happen? Is that why I feel like it's different?

subject: The Underdark Curriculum
fact: Zalthir’s survival in the Underdark represents an alternative, unrecorded curriculum that contradicts Candlekeep’s formal training — a hidden path where practicality overrides doctrine, and where learning is measured by survival, not scrolls.
source_quote: He had survived the Underdark, which is a different curriculum.

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s first words after restoration were 'The wells are not wells anymore,' a sentence that means more than it says.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: the wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic revelation that the Underdark’s corruption is transforming fundamental aspects of reality, and that the surface world is losing its ability to interpret basic metaphors — a philosophical thread that connects perception, language, and the unraveling of meaning.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: The wells are not wells anymore
fact: Elin’s utterance — 'The wells are not wells anymore' — is a cryptic, high-stakes thread. It implies a transformation of fundamental metaphysical or spatial structures, possibly referencing corrupted conduits of perception or reality itself, and is not yet interpretable.
source_quote: The wells are not wells anymore.

subject: Thorin’s Headache and Candlekeep’s Knowledge
fact: Thorin’s unexplained headache, triggered by proximity to Candlekeep’s accumulated knowledge, hints at a deeper, possibly magical or psychic resonance between his consciousness and the library’s archives — a thread that remains unexplored but is implicitly significant.
source_quote: My head had been complaining since we arrived at Candlekeep. The proximity — to the knowledge, or to whatever sat underneath the knowledge — was producing a friction I had been mis-attributing to the sun all day.

subject: Underdark corruption spreading to the surface
fact: Something from the Underdark is bleeding upward, affecting perception and causing voices and hallucinations on the surface.
source_quote: something from below was bleeding up, ... the madness from the Underdark ... was not, apparently, staying below. It was reaching up.

subject: Zalthir’s Unlearned Mastery
fact: Zalthir’s techniques are wrong by the scrolls — but they work. He did not learn shadow steps; he survived them. His trial revealed that Candlekeep’s system cannot measure him — and perhaps does not want to. Is he the next Shadow Monk? Or the last one who broke the mold? And what happens when the Bone King sings, and the only one who can respond is the one who never learned how to?

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: The window was narrowing with every minute we spent in this room

subject: elapsed time since corpse inspection
fact: Time has passed since the gate warden's inspection of the corpse, and further delay will allow the corpse's ritual accessibility to reset, though the body will become more decomposed.
source_quote: Corpse will be a little stinky by then... So if we wait long enough, then we can try again?

subject: Inspection window
fact: The Gate Warden conducted his full inspection at 11 a.m., after all other visitors had been restricted — a critical gap in oversight.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: longest night of winter's deepest cold
fact: The 'longest night of winter's deepest cold' is the temporal anchor for the prophecy 'the keeper falls, the heart is sold' — a precise celestial event that coincides with the death of the Keeper of Tomes, confirming the prophecy's predictive power.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: longest night of winter's deepest cold
fact: The prophecy 'the keeper falls, the heart is sold' is tied to the longest night of winter's deepest cold — a specific temporal anchor for an unfulfilled event.
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day after the Underdark, when rest was a luxury good and rarely in stock.
source_quote: the kind that had felt almost suspicious after the Underdark, where a full night's sleep had been a luxury good and rarely in stock

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the longest night of winter's deepest cold.
source_quote: On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.

subject: session time
fact: The events occur during a single morning, following the death of the Keeper of Tomes and the awakening of the party; the timeline is tight, with the Avowed still asleep and the window for action narrowing rapidly.
source_quote: The Avowed were still asleep. The window was narrowing with every minute we spent in this room.

subject: the day of the delegation
fact: The day the outsider party was granted investigative authority, the Council of Twelve convened in the Chapter House, Kalan Strongbranch was excluded, and Bookwyrm revealed Janussi’s final request. This day marked the formal transition from internal chaos to external investigation — and the point at which the party gained access to restricted areas.

subject: the morning before Janussi’s death
fact: The morning before Janussi’s death is the temporal anchor for the resignation request and the last known interaction between him and Kalan Strongbranch. It is the critical pre-event window that defines the investigation’s starting point.
source_quote: Janussi, the morning before his death, had asked Kalan to tender his resignation.

subject: the morning of Janussi’s death
fact: On the morning of his death, Janussi requested Kalan Strongbranch’s resignation due to mental decline and negligence. This was his final known action. The timing suggests the murder was either a response to this demand or an attempt to silence him before he could act further. The exact hour is unknown, but it occurred before the council convened.

subject: Time of death
fact: Janussi was discovered dead at approximately 7:30 a.m.; the timeline of arrivals and inspections begins from this point.
source_quote: Janussi found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.

subject: time of death
fact: Janussi was murdered well before half past seven in the morning, as candles burned out and tobacco smoke lingered in a sealed room.
source_quote: Miss Hollypocket would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing.

subject: Time of Discovery
fact: Janussi was discovered at 7:30 a.m. The gate warden arrived at 8 a.m. The Bookwyrm arrived at 9 a.m. The gate warden returned at 11 a.m. for full investigation.
source_quote: Tadric confirmed it from the doorway... After eleven, I was told.

subject: time of discovery
fact: Janussi’s body was discovered at 7:30 a.m. by A'lai Aivenmore and Miss Hollypocket; the timeline of visitors extends from 8 a.m. to 11 a.m., with the Gate Warden’s inspection being the final known activity before investigators arrived.
source_quote: Janussi had been found dead... around half past seven in the morning.

subject: time of inspection
fact: The Gate Warden conducted his full inspection at 11 a.m., after which he was relieved; this is the last confirmed activity before the current investigation began.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection.

subject: Time of Murder
fact: The murder occurred significantly before 7:30 a.m., likely between midnight and 5 a.m., based on the fully burned candles and persistent tobacco smoke. The room remained sealed for at least four to six hours before discovery.
source_quote: That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.

subject: two hundred years
fact: No duels have occurred at Candlekeep in the last two hundred years, making the recent three duels historically anomalous.
source_quote: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf gets the larger window. *Three*, in a library where nobody has dueled in two hundred years.

subject: arrival of the messenger
fact: A young, commoner-born messenger has delivered urgent news with unguarded enthusiasm, revealing his inexperience and the high stakes of the message; his delivery confirms the event is being handled outside normal protocol.
source_quote: The voice on the other side of the door was young, breathless, and badly in need of a pause. ... He was commoner-born, I could see that much — enthusiastic in the way of someone who has been trusted with important information for the first time and found the experience clarifying.

subject: arrival of Zalthir’s party
fact: Zalthir and his companions arrived at the Chapter House unannounced, were immediately categorized by the Council as unknown arrivals with no provenance, and disrupted the Council’s crisis protocol with the introduction of an unfamiliar ideological framework.
source_quote: They cataloged us immediately — orc, dragonborn, dwarf, drow — and sorted us into the correct drawer: arrivals. unknown provenance. examine.

subject: book removal
fact: The book 'The Golden Ass' — annotated in fresh midnight blue ink — was missing from the desk, suggesting its contents were intentionally removed.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room.

subject: bookwyrm's arrival
fact: The Bookwyrm arrived at nine, confirmed the gate warden’s orders, and permitted only a brief look before leaving.
source_quote: Bookwyrm at nine, arriving from the baths, allowed a brief look before confirming the existing orders.

subject: Bookwyrm's instructions
fact: The Bookwyrm's parting instructions had been clear enough: report back when done, remove nothing from the room.
source_quote: report back when done, remove nothing from the room

subject: Bookwyrm's testimony
fact: Bookwyrm disclosed that Janussi requested Kalan’s resignation, but declined to elaborate, claiming not to prejudice the investigation.
source_quote: Janussi, the morning before his death, had asked Kalan to tender his resignation. Mental faculties. Negligence. She declined to elaborate — she didn't want to prejudice the investigation, she said

subject: candle burning
fact: The candles told the same story. I said it out loud: 'That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.'
source_quote: The candles told the same story. I said it out loud: 'That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.'

subject: Candle Extinguishment
fact: The complete burning of all seven candles confirms the room was sealed for many hours after death. Since Miss Hollypocket would never allow this, the murder must have occurred before the candles were lit or before she could intervene.
source_quote: Miss Hollypocket would never have allowed the Keeper to let candles burn down to nothing.

subject: Candlekeep duels
fact: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over polemic shelf placement — an unprecedented occurrence in two hundred years of library peace.
source_quote: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf gets the larger window. *Three*, in a library where nobody has dueled in two hundred years.

subject: Council of Twelve meeting
fact: The Council of Twelve convened in uproar over Janussi's murder, with twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table and a rose window casting colored light.
source_quote: twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor

subject: Daz
fact: Daz catalogued the messenger's message as he heard it.
source_quote: I was already cataloguing before the sentence finished.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz checked the tapestries for concealment as they passed.
source_quote: I checked as we passed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed Grygum's comment about orc bedwear as part of Grygum's processing of the morning.
source_quote: I filed it in the column marked *Grygum is processing the morning*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz filed the open apartment door for later consideration.
source_quote: Filed it for later.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the Gate Warden had been back inside alone and looked more determined coming out.
source_quote: Tadric noted that Kalan looked more determined coming out than going in.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted that the phrase 'before the avowed awake' was doing a great deal of work.
source_quote: That clause was doing a great deal of work.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted the Chapter House entrance had a single guard and no secondary exit apparent.
source_quote: I noted the Chapter House entrance: single guard, single visible point of entry, no secondary exit apparent from the doorway.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted the apartment on the third floor with its door left ajar.
source_quote: I noted the apartment. Noted that the door was open.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noted the gap in physical endurance between himself and Fembris as a data point.
source_quote: I was aware of the gap — not with pride, just as a data point.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Astronomicon as a potential tool for surface navigation.
source_quote: I noted it. Surface navigation, if we needed that.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber and recognized Grygum’s attitude as similar to Thorin’s past behavior.
source_quote: I filed it and kept walking. ... This was the same register in which Thorin had once described demon lord proximity as *ominous sounding fun*.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the Drakonoikos before Fembris named it.
source_quote: I noticed it before he named it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz pointed out that Bookwyrm’s testimony was itself evidence.
source_quote: Daz pointed out, reasonably, that her testimony was itself evidence.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz realized Bookwyrm volunteered the fact about Kalan’s resignation at a strategic moment.
source_quote: She delivered it like a gift. Information, freely offered, before anyone had thought to ask. I filed that immediately — not the content, the timing.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized a gap in the investigation because Tadric hadn't been watching closely enough.
source_quote: That was a gap. Gaps were interesting.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz recognized the pattern of institutional information control as familiar from Menzoberranzan.
source_quote: In Menzoberranzan, that combination resolved to one thing: someone wanted the scene read before it was managed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was awake before the knock finished its second syllable.
source_quote: I was awake before Fembris got through the second syllable

subject: Daz
fact: Daz watched Fembris reach the conclusion that he should be scared of the cat.
source_quote: I watched him reach that conclusion in real time

subject: death of Janussi
fact: Janussi was found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.
source_quote: Janussi found dead by the Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore and the housekeeper, one Miss Hollypocket, around half past seven in the morning.

subject: death of Janussi
fact: Janussi, the Keeper of Tomes, died under suspicious circumstances. The morning of his death, he requested Kalan Strongbranch’s resignation due to concerns over mental faculties and negligence. His death triggered a power struggle, investigation delegation, and institutional defensiveness.
source_quote: Janussi, the morning before his death, had asked Kalan to tender his resignation.

subject: death of the Keeper of Tomes
fact: The Keeper of Tomes has been found dead, prompting the First Reader to bypass all institutional protocols and summon the party directly through the emerald door before the Avowed can awaken, suggesting a deliberate cover-up and the presence of a hidden threat.
source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: death of the Keeper of Tomes
fact: The Keeper of Tomes has been killed, triggering a covert response from the First Reader who is summoning a specific party through the emerald door before the Avowed awaken; the event is being contained to prevent institutional interference.
source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: delegation of investigation
fact: The Council of Twelve, under Bookwyrm’s leadership, formally delegated the investigation of Janussi’s murder to the outsider party. This decision was secured through rhetorical framing, cultural references, and demands for access and remuneration. The council’s willingness to comply suggests either desperation or a hidden agenda to shift accountability.

subject: Discovery of the Body
fact: The body was discovered at 7:30 a.m. by A'lai Aivenmore and Miss Hollypocket. The scene remained undisturbed until the gate warden arrived at 8 a.m. and others began entering under controlled access.
source_quote: A'lai Aivenmore and a servant called Miss Hollypocket found Janussi dead around half past seven in the morning.

subject: door left ajar
fact: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.
source_quote: A door left ajar on the third floor landing.

subject: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber incident
fact: One of the Avowed died in the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber, requiring Keeper's permission for access.
source_quote: One of the Avowed had died in it, he said, which was why the Keeper's permission was now required

subject: elapsed time
fact: Forty-one years pass in the corner of the library where Vareth has kept his office.
source_quote: He has been keeping this corner of the library for forty-one years, he says

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris reconsidered his belief about the cat after Zalthir's quiet question.
source_quote: Fembris went still. Reconsidered.

subject: fembris's reaction
fact: Fembris vomited after seeing the body, then retreated and did not re-enter, indicating a visceral reaction to the violence.
source_quote: Fembris took one look at the body, crossed the room in four steps, flung a window open, and vomited out of it.

subject: gate warden's inspection
fact: The Gate Warden returned at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.
source_quote: The Gate Warden again at eleven, alone, for a full inspection — careful, deliberate, left to make his report to the Council.

subject: gate warden's inspection
fact: The gate warden conducted a full, deliberate inspection of the crime scene at eleven and emerged looking more determined than when he entered.
source_quote: He definitely looked more determined after he walked out.

subject: Glabbagool's confinement
fact: Glabbagool the grey ooze, confined in a bag of holding, has reached a breaking point and demands to be let out.
source_quote: Whatever Glabbagool had been doing in the bag all day — thinking, absorbing, trying to formalize whatever Zalthir had been patiently teaching him into monastic discipline — he was done with it. He wanted out.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted Bookwyrm’s tone when she said 'Focus' five times.
source_quote: Bookwyrm said, with the tone of someone who has said this sentence before in faculty meetings and never fully recovered from needing to: 'FOCUS, PEOPLE! Focus! Focus! Focus! Focus!'

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noted the seating arrangement in the Chapter House before anyone finished shouting.
source_quote: I took notes on the seating arrangement before anyone had finished shouting.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum recognized Daral’s question as implying a challenge to their access.
source_quote: I heard something in that question I recognized. The implication underneath was sharper — *who gave you access, and should I object to them.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum watched A'lai Aivenmore calibrate his response during the negotiation.
source_quote: I watched the red-cheeked wizard with the shrewd gray eyes. I watched A'lai Aivenmore calibrate.

subject: Grygum school of thought
fact: The Grygum school of thought was accidentally proposed and is now being treated by Vareth as the question of the age.
source_quote: I just proposed a school of theological thought by accident, and that an aging scholar with forty-one years in this corner of the library is now treating it as the question of the age.

subject: heart removal
fact: Janussi’s heart was removed after death, not as a cause of death but as a ritual precaution to prevent resurrection; the wound showed blunt force trauma from multiple axe blows, and blood spatter indicated the victim was already deceased.
source_quote: The heart was missing. No other organs. And the blood was localized. Wrong pattern for what should have been a violent death.

subject: heart removal
fact: The missing heart wasn't the cause of death. It was a message. Or a precaution.
source_quote: The missing heart wasn't the cause of death. It was a message. Or a precaution.

subject: I
fact: I file a thought about the procedural compromise of following Vareth's path as proof of the Bahamutian theory.
source_quote: I file that thought for later.

subject: I
fact: I notice that none of the three schools of thought quite fit what I actually think.
source_quote: I am sitting with this — genuinely sitting with it... when I notice that none of them quite fit what I actually think.

subject: Investigation Delegation
fact: The Council of Twelve delegated the investigation of Janussi's death to the party, citing fate and divine intervention, and agreed to provide one book each upon successful completion.
source_quote: "seekers who the gods have sent us"

subject: Janussi's Death
fact: Janussi, the Keeper of Tomes, was found dead, and on the morning of his death, he had asked Kalan Strongbranch to tender his resignation due to concerns about mental faculties and negligence.
source_quote: Janussi, the morning before his death, had asked Kalan to tender his resignation. Mental faculties. Negligence.

subject: Janussi's resignation request
fact: Janussi asked Kalan to tender his resignation the morning before his death, citing loss of mental faculties and negligence.
source_quote: yesterday morning, Janussi asked the gate warden to tender his resignation. The Keeper was concerned that Kalan was losing his mental faculties and becoming negligent in his work

subject: Kalan Strongbranch's arrival
fact: Kalan Strongbranch arrived at the Chapter House after being previously wanted for questioning, and bowed with correct form but suspicious eyes.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch walked in... He bowed. The bow was correct and the eyes were not

subject: Kalan Strongbranch’s exclusion
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the gate warden, was formally barred from entering the Chapter House during the council’s decision to delegate the investigation. Bookwyrm preempted his objections with prepared language. His bow was correct, but his eyes betrayed resistance. His exclusion marks him as the primary suspect and signals that the council may be protecting someone else.

subject: Murder of Janussi
fact: Janussi was murdered before 7:30 a.m., likely several hours prior, as evidenced by the fully extinguished candles and lingering tobacco smoke. The murder involved blunt force trauma caving in his rib cage and removal of an object from his chest. The crime was not a random robbery, as valuable blue gems were left behind.
source_quote: His rib cage had been caved in. There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: The murder of Janussi, Keeper of Tomes, triggered a crisis of leadership and access at Candlekeep. He had requested the resignation of the gate warden the morning before his death, suggesting prior awareness of corruption or danger. His death occurred in a secure location, and the investigation has been delegated to outsiders. The timing and manner of the murder remain unknown, and the council is divided on priorities.

subject: murder of Janussi
fact: The murder of Janussi, a senior council member, has triggered a crisis within the Council of Twelve, sparking competing agendas, blame-shifting, and the urgent search for the killer.
source_quote: First, we must find the murderer!

subject: prophecy recitation
fact: The Candlekeep scholars recited prophecies from the gallery above, a continuous ritual where fulfilled prophecies are removed and only unfulfilled ones remain — the inventory of the unspoken future.
source_quote: Vareth had explained it to Grygum earlier in the day, and Grygum had explained it to the rest of us... whenever one came true, it was removed. What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: Remuneration Negotiation
fact: The party negotiated for remuneration in the form of one book each from the library, and demanded full access to the library as a condition of the investigation.
source_quote: "We need an all-access library card."

subject: resurrection prevention
fact: You can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present. Whoever took the heart wasn't souvenir-collecting. They were preventing resurrection.
source_quote: You can't bring someone back from death by ritual if their vital organs aren't present. Whoever took the heart wasn't souvenir-collecting. They were preventing resurrection.

subject: rib cage damage
fact: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs.
source_quote: The rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate. The heart was missing. No other organs.

subject: Rite of speaking with the dead
fact: The rite to speak with the dead has already been attempted on Janussi’s corpse — likely by the Gate Warden — and failed; this means any future attempt will require significant delay, and the body will be decomposing.
source_quote: Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.

subject: ritual attempt on corpse
fact: A ritual to communicate with the deceased was performed on Janussi's corpse by the gate warden, and the attempt yielded no result.
source_quote: Tadric said they'd tried that. The dead were not speaking.

subject: ritual attempt on corpse
fact: The dead had not spoken. Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.
source_quote: The dead had not spoken. Someone — presumably the Gate Warden, before his removal — had already used the rite on the corpse, which meant we'd be waiting if we wanted to try again.

subject: ritual attempt on corpse
fact: The rite to speak with the dead had already been performed by the gate warden, preventing further attempts until sufficient time passed.
source_quote: Someone — presumably the Gate Warden — had already used the rite on the corpse.

subject: speak with dead rite
fact: The Gate Warden performed the 'speak with dead' ritual on Janussi’s corpse during his inspection; the rite has been spent, and no further attempts can be made for a significant duration; this confirms the killer anticipated magical inquiry.
source_quote: The dead had not spoken. Someone — presumably the Gate Warden — had already used the rite on the corpse.

subject: summoning through the emerald door
fact: A covert summons is underway, bypassing all standard channels; the First Reader has identified a specific party as the only appropriate agents to respond to the Keeper’s death, indicating deep trust and strategic intent.
source_quote: The First Reader wanted us specifically, not the Avowed, not the city watch — us, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric realized his job was smaller than the job that needed doing.
source_quote: He had just understood his job was smaller than the job that needed doing.

subject: tadric's admission
fact: Tadric admitted his role was crowd control, not observation, and realized his failure to monitor internal actions.
source_quote: Tadric admitted his assignment had been crowd control. Not observation.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asked whether the rib cage was cut neatly or torn out with bare hands.
source_quote: How did they appear to die? ... Was this cut neatly with a sharp scalpel-like thing, or was it, like, torn out with somebody's bare hands?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin concluded the murder happened before the candles burned out.
source_quote: That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin concluded the murder occurred well before the body was discovered.
source_quote: Which meant Janussi had been dead before the candles finished. Which meant the murder happened well before anyone found him.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin kept the prophecy to himself without reacting.
source_quote: I kept it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted that the Gate Warden looked more determined after leaving the room.
source_quote: He definitely looked more determined after he walked out.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the desk was neatly kept, which he took as a data point.
source_quote: The desk was neatly kept, which was itself a data point.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the Great Reader who looked genuinely unwell.
source_quote: Another looked genuinely unwell, the particular gray of someone who had pushed through several days of bad sleep and hadn't yet admitted it to themselves.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the drunk Great Reader's visible intoxication.
source_quote: One of the Great Readers had a cup that kept getting refilled. Drunk, visibly, in the way that wasn't an accident.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the high ceiling of the Refectory before anything else.
source_quote: I noticed that first — the ceiling — before I noticed anything else.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the hooded Avowed figure moving quickly with something tucked against their ribs.
source_quote: And then a hooded figure from the Avowed went past the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed room.
source_quote: The room was circular... full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the quill on the floor had a nib covered in midnight blue ink.
source_quote: A quill on the floor. Nib covered in midnight blue.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the two readers in the corner having a hushed conversation.
source_quote: In the far corner, two readers sat with their heads angled together, voices below audible, the kind of hushed conversation that usually means either something has gone very wrong or something is about to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observed the body had a caved-in rib cage and a hollow where something used to be.
source_quote: His rib cage had been caved in. There was a hollow in his chest where something used to be.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realized the missing book, The Golden Ass, was deliberately taken.
source_quote: The book the blue ink was annotating — The Golden Ass — wasn't in the room. Whatever Janussi had been working on most recently... was gone. That felt deliberate.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realized the smoke lingered because the room had been sealed for hours.
source_quote: Nobody smokes in a sealed room and leaves smoke that lingers for hours unless the room has been sealed for hours.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin suspected the heart was removed after death, not as the cause of death.
source_quote: The question: was he dead before his heart was hacked out?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought about the giants' saying that a wall is just a rock in the right place.
source_quote: The giants used to say that a wall is just a rock in the right place.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thought about the prophecy 'On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.'
source_quote: *On the longest night of winter's deepest cold, the keeper falls, the heart is sold.*

subject: thorin's ice inquiry
fact: Thorin inquired about the availability of ice to preserve the corpse, given the expected decomposition from delay.
source_quote: Corpse will be a little stinky by then. Is there any ice around?

subject: Thorin's question to Bookwyrm
fact: Thorin asked Bookwyrm where she was during Janussi’s death, prompting a pause and visible weight in her expression.
source_quote: Thorin, immediate: 'Where were you?' Bookwyrm paused. Not a long pause. Just long enough to weigh something.

subject: three duels at Candlekeep
fact: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf receives the larger window — an unprecedented act of violence in a library where no one has dueled in two hundred years, signaling a deepening crisis in scholarly authority and ideological fervor.
source_quote: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf gets the larger window. *Three*, in a library where nobody has dueled in two hundred years.

subject: time of death
fact: Janussi was murdered well before 7:30 a.m., likely between midnight and 5 a.m., as evidenced by the complete burning of seven candles and the absence of tobacco smoke renewal; the room had been sealed for hours.
source_quote: The candles told the same story... it had been some time since he was murdered.

subject: Tobacco Smoke Linger
fact: Lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed chamber indicates the room had not been ventilated since before the murder. The smoke could not have persisted for hours unless the murderer or victim smoked shortly before death and the room remained closed.
source_quote: That tells me that it had been some time since he was murdered, because there was enough time for the candle to burn out.

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: The Keeper of Tomes is dead, and the First Reader summons the party through the emerald door before the Avowed awake.
source_quote: The Keeper of Tomes is dead! She wants you! Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: travel to the emerald door
fact: The emerald door is the threshold beyond which danger awaits, and we are not walking into it depleted.
source_quote: Whatever was waiting through the emerald door, we weren't walking into it depleted

subject: zalthir's observation
fact: Zalthir determined the rib cage was smashed by multiple axe blows, not a single strike, indicating deliberate, forceful violence.
source_quote: the rib cage had been smashed by something like an axe, multiple blows, close together, deliberate.

subject: Avowed
fact: A hooded figure from the Avowed passed through the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe — not trying to be obvious, but not trying hard to hide either.
source_quote: a hooded figure from the Avowed went past the dining hall at a half-run, something tucked against their ribs under the robe

subject: Bahamutian school
fact: The Bahamutian school asserts that divine providence prevails; mortals serve as instruments of a prearranged chain, and their choices were fitted to them by higher design.
source_quote: The Bahamutian school says divine providence prevails. Bahamut moved his pieces beforehand. The mortals served as instruments. Choice was real, but not sovereign.

subject: Bahamutian school
fact: The Bahamutian school believes divine providence prevails — mortal choices are real but not sovereign; all actions were arranged in advance by divine will, with mortals serving as instruments in a preordained chain.
source_quote: The Bahamutian school says divine providence prevails. Bahamut moved his pieces beforehand. The mortals served as instruments. Choice was real, but not sovereign.

subject: Candlekeep Council of Twelve
fact: The Council of Twelve is the governing body of Candlekeep, currently in disarray following the murder of the Keeper of Tomes. Members are academics and scholars divided on priorities: restoring leadership, identifying the murderer, assigning blame, and controlling access to knowledge. They are easily swayed by new intellectual frameworks and resistant to external demands — until those demands are framed as legitimate curiosity.

subject: Council of Twelve
fact: The Council of Twelve is the governing body of Candlekeep, currently in uproar over the murder of a colleague, the absence of Sylvira Savikas, and competing proposals about leadership succession, gatekeeper accountability, and internal order.
source_quote: We must have the vote and restore leadership to Candlekeep." ... "First, we must find the murderer!" ... "why isn't Sylvira Savikas here?

subject: Council of Twelve
fact: The Council of Twelve is the governing body of the library, deeply entrenched in bureaucratic tradition, resistant to external demands, and protective of institutional boundaries. They have never been asked to pay for services and are now facing an unprecedented challenge to their authority.
source_quote: They had never, in their professional lives, been asked to pay for something by the person they were asking.

subject: Draconic school
fact: The Draconic school claims ancient agency rules; metallic dragons follow Protanther out of trust in their elders, not divine compulsion, and mortal choice is real but bounded by draconic permission.
source_quote: The Draconic school says ancient agency rules. Protanther honored Stroud's move because Protanther is honorable, not because Bahamut compelled him.

subject: Draconic school
fact: The Draconic school posits that ancient agency rules — metallic dragons act out of loyalty to their elders, not divine command, and while choice is real, its scope is limited by what the dragons permit.
source_quote: The Draconic school says ancient agency rules. Protanther honored Stroud's move because Protanther is honorable, not because Bahamut compelled him. The metallic dragons followed Protanther because they trust their elders.

subject: Grygum school
fact: The Grygum school, proposed by the narrator and refined by Vareth, argues that the universe contains fixed points around which actions must revolve — outside these points, freedom is vast; near them, the universe becomes silent and conspiratorial, subtly constraining choices to ensure inevitability through environmental and institutional design rather than direct compulsion.
source_quote: What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Stroudite school
fact: The Stroudite school holds that mortal choice is sovereign — gods and dragons exist, but choice is not borrowed from any higher power; actions are free and independent, and the removal of any single choice collapses the chain of events.
source_quote: The Stroudite school says mortal choice is sovereign. The gods exist. The dragons exist. Providence may or may not exist. But the choosing belongs to the chooser, and is not borrowed, and is not loaned from any throne above or below.

subject: Stroudite school
fact: The Stroudite school holds that mortal choice is sovereign; gods and dragons exist, but agency is not borrowed or loaned from above or below, and chains of free acts determine outcomes.
source_quote: The Stroudite school says mortal choice is sovereign. The gods exist. The dragons exist. Providence may or may not exist. But the choosing belongs to the chooser, and is not borrowed, and is not loaned from any throne above or below.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed are a group referenced by Fembris as having allegedly transformed the cat into a supernatural entity — their true nature and involvement in the murder are unconfirmed.
source_quote: He turned to us and announced that these Avowed had taken a cat sitting wherever it liked and turned it into an interstellar, interspatial, interdimensional horror — that's just what cats do.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed are an elite order associated with the Bastion, entrusted with training or testing in its lethal chambers; one member died in the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber, indicating extreme danger.
source_quote: One of the Avowed had died in it, he said, which was why the Keeper's permission was now required.

subject: The Avowed
fact: The Avowed are an elite order within Candlekeep, presumably responsible for safeguarding dangerous magical artifacts and chambers. One of their members died in the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber, leading to heightened restrictions. They are currently asleep during the investigation’s early stages, suggesting either deliberate isolation or a lack of immediate involvement in the murder.

subject: the Avowed
fact: The Avowed are an institutional authority within Candlekeep, whose awakening is being deliberately delayed by the First Reader to prevent interference in the investigation of the Keeper’s death.
source_quote: before the avowed awake!

subject: the First Reader
fact: The First Reader is a high-ranking figure within Candlekeep’s scholarly hierarchy who operates outside standard protocol; she has direct access to the Keeper’s secrets and has chosen to summon a specific party for a covert response.
source_quote: The First Reader wanted us specifically, not the Avowed, not the city watch — us, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: Astronomicon
fact: Astronomicon is a stack of blue globes ascending in scale, pale against the white sky, said to contain everything known about the stars.
source_quote: A stack of blue globes, ascending in scale, pale against the white sky.

subject: Astronomicon
fact: The Astronomicon is a vertical stack of ascending blue globes, representing celestial knowledge unknown in the Underdark; it is a key repository of surface-world star lore and potential navigation aid.
source_quote: You see that curious blue stack of globes? That's the Astronomicon. Everything we know about the stars can be found there.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a place where scholars debate at conversation volume, where the Great Readers sit like they are posing for a tapestry, and where prophecies are recited daily — normalcy includes drunk readers laughing at unsaid things and quiet tension in corners.
source_quote: Candlekeep scholars don't chat. They debate at conversation volume... Normal, probably. For here.

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is a place where three duels have been fought over which polemic shelf gets the larger window, despite no duels having occurred in two hundred years.
source_quote: Three duels have been fought at Candlekeep over which polemic shelf gets the larger window. *Three*, in a library where nobody has dueled in two hundred years.

subject: Candlekeep Bastion
fact: Candlekeep Bastion is the central library complex, housing the Astronomicon, the Whispering Dome, and the Drakonoikos — a building constructed from dragon scales and bones. Its architecture reflects a philosophy of repurposing danger into knowledge. High ceilings, irregular corridors, tapestries, and oil paintings suggest concealment potential. The layout was assessed by Daz and Grygum as both impressive and vulnerable to covert movement.

subject: Candlekeep grounds elevation
fact: Candlekeep's grounds are blanketed in snow, silent and untouched, after months below stone.
source_quote: Candlekeep's grounds were blanketed in it, white and silent, the kind of silence that had nothing hunting inside it

subject: Candlekeep Library Courtyard
fact: The courtyard is a snow-covered, silent expanse with three visible archways, a service passage, a guarded northern door, and no obvious surveillance or tactical positions; scholars move slowly in pairs, indicating a controlled, scholarly environment.
source_quote: Candlekeep's grounds were blanketed in it, white and silent, the kind of silence that had nothing hunting inside it. Exits: three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north. Foot traffic: light, scholars moving in pairs, nobody moving fast.

subject: Candlekeep prophecy inventory
fact: The prophecies of Alaundo are recited daily; fulfilled ones are removed, leaving only the unfulfilled inventory.
source_quote: Whenever one came true, it was removed. What remained was the unfulfilled inventory.

subject: Candlekeep Refectory
fact: The Refectory is a warm, interior space with a hearth, where weapons are left within reach but not drawn; it is a place of negotiation, rest, and quiet tension, where the fire’s warmth is a sufficient comfort.
source_quote: I found a corner of the hearth room, set Dawnbringer against the wall within reach — close but not drawn, which had become its own negotiation over the weeks — and sat down.

subject: Candlekeep's Bastion
fact: Candlekeep's Bastion contains three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north, oil paintings on every staircase, busts on pedestals at each landing, heavy tapestries, and the Drakonoikos structure built from enormous scales and bones.
source_quote: Exits: three visible archways, one service passage, one guarded door to the north. Foot traffic: light, scholars moving in pairs, nobody moving fast. No elevated positions. No obvious coverage points.

subject: Candlekeep's Library
fact: Candlekeep's Library is a place where books are copied at the House of the Binder upon successful completion of an investigation, and where full access is requested but initially withheld.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: Candlekeep’s West Inner Ward
fact: Candlekeep’s West Inner Ward is a space saturated with institutional gravity, its walls absorbing centuries of scholarly seriousness, where the smell of old paper and the weight of tradition shape every interaction.
source_quote: The West Inner Ward smells like old paper. People here take themselves seriously, and the walls have absorbed it.

subject: Chamber of the Investigation
fact: The Chamber of the Investigation is the designated starting point for the inquiry into Janussi’s death. It is where Bookwyrm finally revealed the resignation request — the first concrete piece of evidence — and where the group’s role as investigators was formally activated.
source_quote: Bookwyrm walked us toward the chamber where the investigation would begin...

subject: Chapter House
fact: Chapter House contains twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, a rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor, and western gables pressing down overhead.
source_quote: The Chapter House was exactly as described — twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor, western gables pressing down overhead like a building that took itself seriously.

subject: Chapter House
fact: The Chapter House is a twelve-sided chamber with twelve chairs, a rose window, and western gables, serving as the meeting place of the Council of Twelve; it has a single visible entrance, no apparent secondary exit, and is guarded by a purple-robed watcher.
source_quote: twelve chairs around a twelve-sided table, rose window throwing colored light across the stone floor, western gables pressing down overhead...

subject: Chapter House
fact: The Chapter House is the council chamber of Candlekeep, featuring a twelve-sided table, twelve chairs, and a rose window. It is where the council convened after Janussi’s death. The room was analyzed for seating dynamics, power positioning, and nonverbal cues. It is the site of the decision to delegate the investigation to outsiders and the location where Kalan Strongbranch was formally excluded from proceedings.

subject: Chapter House entrance
fact: The Chapter House has a single guard, single visible point of entry, and no secondary exit apparent from the doorway.
source_quote: single guard, single visible point of entry, no secondary exit apparent from the doorway

subject: Crime Scene staircase
fact: The staircase to the crime scene is narrow, requiring single file passage, with Bookwyrm setting the pace.
source_quote: The staircase was narrow enough that we had to go single file, which meant Bookwyrm set the pace

subject: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber
fact: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber is a chamber inside the Bastion where one of the Avowed died, requiring the Keeper's permission for access.
source_quote: One of the Avowed had died in it, he said, which was why the Keeper's permission was now required.

subject: Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber
fact: The Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber is a dangerous magical training facility within Candlekeep. One Avowed member died inside, prompting Keeper Janussi to require explicit permission for access. It is now a restricted zone and a potential site of foul play. Grygum noted that one party member already viewed it as a 'great game to play,' indicating possible recklessness or hidden motive.

subject: Drakonoikos
fact: Drakonoikos is a structure built from enormous scales and bones worked into the walls, where the early light hits the scales and they hold it.
source_quote: The structure was built from scales — actual scales, enormous, overlapping — and bones worked into the walls where another building would have used stone.

subject: Drakonoikos
fact: The Drakonoikos is a structure built from the scales and bones of a dragon of great age and significance. It represents Candlekeep’s philosophy of turning lethal threats into vessels of knowledge. The scales gleam in sunrise, and the building’s design was noted by Grygum as embodying a monastic logic — dangerous things contain the wisdom of their own defeat. It may hold hidden archives or magical resonance relevant to the murder.

subject: Drakonoikos
fact: The Drakonoikos is an unnamed but significant structure mentioned as the next point of the tour; its nature and purpose are implied to be monumental, following the pattern of the Astronomicon and Whispering Dome.
source_quote: Then the Drakonoikos.

subject: Drakonoikos elevation
fact: Drakonoikos is a structure built from enormous scales and bones worked into the walls, replacing stone.
source_quote: The structure was built from scales — actual scales, enormous, overlapping — and bones worked into the walls where another building would have used stone

subject: Emerald door
fact: The emerald door is the designated access point through which Daz and Grygum are summoned by the First Reader, bypassing standard institutional channels.
source_quote: Now, through the emerald door, before the avowed awake!

subject: gate warden's removal
fact: The gate warden was removed from the scene before being questioned, raising suspicion about what he discovered.
source_quote: The gate warden removed before he could be asked what he'd found.

subject: Grygum school of thought
fact: A fourth school of theological thought has been proposed — one centered on fixed points around which actions must revolve, with constrained freedom between them.
source_quote: What if there are certain fixed points around which our actions must revolve? And the closer we come to one of those fixed points, the more constrained we are, but between them, perhaps we have a great deal of freedom of action.

subject: Hearth room
fact: The hearth room is where Daz sits with Dawnbringer against the wall, the fire warm, and the prophecy echoing from the unseen gallery.
source_quote: I found a corner of the hearth room... The fire was going. The ceiling was still high enough. Above us, in a gallery I couldn't see, someone was still reciting.

subject: House of Rest
fact: The House of Rest is where Daz and Grygum return after the morning summons, and where Glabbagool is confined in the bag of holding.
source_quote: Back at the House of Rest, Glabbagool was in a state.

subject: House of the Binder
fact: House of the Binder is the location where books are copied for the party upon successful completion of the investigation.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: House of the Binder
fact: The House of the Binder is the designated location where books will be copied as part of the conditional remuneration agreement. It is a place of scholarly ritual and institutional control over knowledge dissemination.
source_quote: One book each, copied at the House of the Binder, upon successful completion.

subject: Immortal Chambers
fact: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the arrangement implies a theological choice must be made with each step.
source_quote: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the problem is immediately apparent. You have to choose which deity you want to step on.

subject: Immortal Chambers
fact: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the problem is immediately apparent.
source_quote: The Immortal Chambers have a tile floor with one deity symbol per tile, and the problem is immediately apparent.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The Keeper's Chambers are the site where Janussi's corpse was discovered with signs of deliberate organ removal and ritual interference, indicating prior investigation by the gate warden.
source_quote: Zalthir looked more carefully than I did... The gate warden... on his careful, evidence-preserving inspection.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The Keeper's Chambers is a circular room ringed with lancet windows, filled with pale morning light tinged yellow and hazy from lingering tobacco smoke. The windows were shut. The room contained a desk, a toppled chair, a fallen marble statue and pedestal, a candelabra with burned-out candles, and an open spellbook titled The Discoveries. The safe on the far wall had been opened, with blue gems and empty pouches scattered before it.
source_quote: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows, full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The Keeper's Chambers is a circular room with lancet windows, filled with lingering tobacco smoke and extinguished candles; the desk is neat, with a toppled chair, broken statue, and a spellbook open to research on unfamiliar workings; the safe is open, blue gems scattered, but untouched; the ink pot is spilled, quill on floor with midnight blue ink.
source_quote: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows... the safe on the far wall had been opened.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The desk was neatly kept, which was itself a data point. The chair near it was toppled. The marble statue and its pedestal were on the floor. The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.
source_quote: The desk was neatly kept, which was itself a data point. The chair near it was toppled. The marble statue and its pedestal were on the floor. The candelabra — seven arms, bronze — had burned its candles entirely to wax puddles.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows, full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke. Lingering. The windows were shut.
source_quote: The room was circular, ringed with lancet windows, full of pale morning light that had gone slightly yellow and hazy from something I placed almost immediately: tobacco smoke. Lingering. The windows were shut.

subject: Keeper's Chambers
fact: The safe on the far wall had been opened. Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.
source_quote: The safe on the far wall had been opened. Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it.

subject: keeper's chamber tobacco smoke
fact: Lingering tobacco smoke in the sealed keeper’s chamber indicated the room had been closed for hours, suggesting death occurred before discovery.
source_quote: The windows were shut. Nobody had been smoking recently. The smoke was old.

subject: Library Archives
fact: The Library Archives is the contested domain where full access is being demanded by the investigators. It is the scene of the crime and the center of institutional secrecy — the place where authority is both held and challenged.
source_quote: Full access, anywhere in the library, anything.

subject: reception chamber
fact: The first landing of the tower contained a reception chamber, noted as the initial point of entry.
source_quote: reception chamber at the first landing

subject: Refectory
fact: The Refectory was built for scholars, with a ceiling high enough that a hill giant could sit comfortably at one end and not embarrass herself.
source_quote: The Refectory was built for scholars, which meant the ceiling was high enough that a hill giant could have sat comfortably at one end and not embarrassed herself.

subject: safe contents
fact: The safe on the far wall had been opened, blue gems scattered, but left behind — indicating the thief sought something more valuable than jewelry.
source_quote: Blue gems and empty pouches scattered on the floor in front of it. The thief had looked at the gems, decided they weren't what he came for, and left them.

subject: shrine of Oghma
fact: The second landing held a shrine of Oghma, observed during ascent.
source_quote: a shrine of Oghma at the second

subject: The Bastion
fact: The Bastion is a fortified structure built with enormous overlapping dragon scales and bones instead of stone, housing the Dragon Breath Simulation Chamber where an Avowed died, and is now under strict Keeper-controlled access.
source_quote: The structure was built from scales — actual scales, enormous, overlapping — and bones worked into the walls where another building would have used stone.

subject: The Immortal Chambers
