source_quote: Someone had struck him, broken his nose, waited or returned, killed him, rolled him over, taken his heart and one sapphire and a locket from his neck — and left the gold.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is identified as the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library, and is described by Hollypocket as having a face like thunder when seen on the steps.
source_quote: that the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the other key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library, alongside Janussi.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library, making him a critical figure in the mystery of the missing book and the deletion of its contents; his key is the only one not accounted for after Janussi’s death.
source_quote: the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the gate warden who holds the second key to the Hightower Library, the other being held by Janussi. His possession of the key suggests potential access to restricted materials and involvement in the theft or deletion of the book's contents.
source_quote: the other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is described by Hollypocket as having a face like thunder when passing her on the steps, and is identified by Fembris as the keeper of the second key to the Hightower Library.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was seen by Hollypocket on the steps with a face like thunder, nearly knocking over her tea tray shortly before Janussi's death.
source_quote: I was bringing the keeper his morning tea when I passed Kalan Strongbranch on the steps. He had a face like thunder, nearly knocked the tray out of my hands.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the gate warden, held the second key to the Hightower Library; he was seen with a 'face like thunder' on the morning of the murder, suggesting he was in conflict with Janussi over access or control of the library's secrets.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie assesses two-leggers as never licking themselves, and claims to have met cleaner dogs in her time.
source_quote: How would I know? I try to hold my breath whenever a two-legger passes. It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie believes Janussi carried the locket intimately and never took it off.
source_quote: The locket itself is intimate. He carried it all the time. He never took it off.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie believes good ticklers are the only good reason for disturbing her beauty sleep.
source_quote: Any good ticklers are the only good… and good ticklers are… tickles are only the good reason for disturbing my beauty sleep.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie demands that Daz leave and properly lick himself before returning.
source_quote: You may now leave," she said, "and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie describes a figure wearing Sylvira's shape but not her scent, calling her 'the torn demon lady' but noting, 'she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.'
source_quote: She'd prowled the nighttime cycle and seen *the torn demon lady* coming down the steps — Sylvira's shape — "But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though."

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie does not know what the locket was.
source_quote: I don't know what it was.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie finds two-leggers unclean because they hardly ever lick themselves.
source_quote: It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all. I've met cleaner dogs in my time.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie introduces herself as a five-year-old, sleet-grey cat entirely uninterested in being disturbed, and announces, 'I did not order any more ticklers!'
source_quote: The cat introduced herself, after a fashion. Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed. "I did not order any more ticklers!" she announced, stretching.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a five-year-old, sleet-grey housecat who resides in the tower and observes all movements with detached precision. She was napping in Janussi's armchair when awakened by Sylvira Savikas, later watched Daral carry away a book, and observed a figure impersonating Sylvira without her scent. She refuses to answer questions without tickles and has no interest in human politics or secrets.
source_quote: I did not order any more ticklers! Any good ticklers are the only good… and good ticklers are… tickles are only the good reason for disturbing my beauty sleep.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is a sleet-grey cat, five years old, who resides in the tower and observes two-leggers with detached precision, noting their gait, scent, and habits but not their secrets. She was awakened from naps by Sylvira Savikas and Daral, and witnessed the theft of a book, a locket, and a suspicious figure impersonating Sylvira.
source_quote: I did not order any more ticklers! Any good ticklers are the only good… and good ticklers are… tickles are only the good reason for disturbing my beauty sleep.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie is entirely uninterested in being disturbed.
source_quote: Queenie — five years old, sleet-grey, and entirely uninterested in being disturbed.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie refuses to answer more questions because there have been too few tickles and too many questions.
source_quote: There have been too little Tickles and too many questions.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie says, 'There have been too little Tickles and too many questions,' and refuses to be more generous until more tickles are given.
source_quote: "There have been too little Tickles and too many questions." I tickled. I tickled some more.

subject: Queenie
fact: Queenie tells Daz to leave and to give himself a proper licking before returning to her tower.
source_quote: "You may now leave," she said, "and please give yourself a proper licking before returning to my tower."

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who blasted the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light, waking Queenie from her nap.
source_quote: Sylvira Savikas, this is in the morning, blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling who had an on-again, off-again romantic relationship with Janussi. She is associated with bursts of force light and was witnessed impersonated by a figure that did not carry her scent.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is a tiefling with an on-again, off-again romantic relationship with Janussi. She attacked him with a lance of force during a lover's quarrel, and later appeared as a disguised figure wearing her shape but lacking her scent, suggesting impersonation or shapeshifting.
source_quote: blasting the armchamber with a lance of unerring force light.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas is described as screaming that Janussi was a traitor, nearly taking the door off its hinges, and was seen by Hollypocket at 2–3 a.m. with a glowing red face and carrying a lantern despite being a tiefling who can see in the dark.
source_quote: That devil woman! She gives me the heebie-jeebies!

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, Curator of the Infernal Fortress and a tiefling, had a volatile confrontation with Janussi during the day and was seen at 2–3 a.m. carrying a lantern despite having darkvision; her face glowed red in candlelight as she descended the stairs — a physical anomaly suggesting she was using the lantern to conceal her presence or illuminate something else.

subject: Sylvira Savikas
fact: Sylvira Savikas, the Curator of the Infernal Fortress and a tiefling, was seen raging at Janussi, accusing him of being a traitor, and was later observed carrying a lantern at 2–3 a.m. despite having darkvision — suggesting the light was not for her own use.
source_quote: That devil woman! She gives me the heebie-jeebies!… I swear I could see that devil woman's — Sylvira Savikas's — face glowing red in the candlelight… she was carrying a lantern.

subject: Tadric
fact: Tadric was visibly unnerved by Thorin’s warnings about the statue’s candle, demonstrating his vulnerability to psychological manipulation and fear of the unknown.
source_quote: He tried not to look at the candle and then could not stop looking at the candle.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is reported by Hollypocket to have shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during a meeting around the ninth bell.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during a heated exchange around the ninth bell, as overheard by Hollypocket despite claiming not to listen.
source_quote: I did hear Teles shout, *hypocrite*, at poor Janussi before he stormed out.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste shouted 'hypocrite' at Janussi during a heated meeting, indicating deep personal or ideological grievance; he was one of several Great Readers who argued violently with Janussi on the day of his death.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks, 'Wait, is that describing the type of writing?' and identifies the gift tag's script as 'grumpy' and 'cramped,' and later says, 'Okay, so yeah, there's definitely some sort of poison going on,' and 'Am I reaching too deep here?'
source_quote: Wait, is that describing the type of writing?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin asks, 'what was going on with those bolts of force, do we know why,' and later notes that the victim was still alive when Daral left.
source_quote: Thorin dug in — *what was going on with those bolts of force, do we know why* — and the answer arrived dressed as gossip: Sylvira the tiefling, and Janussi, an on-and-off-again relationship.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes a shapeshifter situation is going on.
source_quote: Oh, so we've got, like, a shapeshifter situation going on here," said Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the darts aimed at the chair were not meant for Janussi, since he bore no such marks.
source_quote: those darts never miss their mark, Thorin pointed out, and the man bore no such marks.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the gift tag supports his theory that Daral Yashenti gave Janussi a bitter gift.
source_quote: Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin identifies a 'shapeshifter situation' after Queenie describes a figure wearing Sylvira's shape but not her scent.
source_quote: "Oh, so we've got, like, a shapeshifter situation going on here," said Thorin.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin interpreted the gift tag’s cramped, grumpy handwriting as evidence of a bitter rivalry.
source_quote: It's, like, grumpy?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a rival of Janussi, suspected in the investigation due to his known hostility and the timing of events; he is one of the two individuals who simultaneously voiced the same line of inquiry, revealing a pattern of parallel thinking with Grygum.
source_quote: I'm sorry, but I didn't mean to stomp on you. Oh, I was gonna say, does he have any rivals?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is afraid the candle on the statue might be magically alive and could cause danger.
source_quote: I don't want it to wake up and attack us... I've had, you know, had bad experiences.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an investigator who declined tea and offered minimal commentary — his abrupt 'Nothing more' triggered Hollypocket’s realization about the thud, suggesting his words may have unintentionally guided the testimony.
source_quote: Nothing more," Thorin said.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an investigator who pushed Queenie for details on the shapeshifter and noted that Janussi was alive when Daral left. He recognized the implications of the force bolts and the shapeshifter.
source_quote: That explains the candle... But the victim was still alive when Daral left.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin mutters that he has the second-worst eye for detail in the room, implying he knows he’s bad at observation.
source_quote: Thorin muttered something about having the second-worst eye for detail in the room.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noted the chipped tooth was a recent injury and questioned whether it was tied to the murder or a prior event, contributing to the logical separation of two possible narratives.
source_quote: So either that was related to him being murdered, immediately as part of the murder, or it was something we need to investigate — how did he chip the tooth recently?

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin noticed the black residue on Janussi’s fingers and mouth was definitively not blue ink.
source_quote: What color was, like, on his fingers and mouth, was it black or red? Black. Definitively not the blue ink

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin observed the darts in the armchair and noted their target was not the body, suggesting an unexplained outburst of force; he raised concerns about the statue’s candle, revealing his superstition and fear of animated magic objects.
source_quote: I don't want it to wake up and attack us. I've had, you know, had bad experiences.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin repeatedly voiced fears about magical objects waking up, claimed personal bad experiences, and interpreted the gift tag as evidence of a bitter rival — though his interpretations were speculative and not confirmed by evidence.
source_quote: Are you sure this — is it true about candles? ... Okay, so that supports my theory. Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin suspects the missing comedy book may contain a cipher or replacement code.
source_quote: There's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book — or maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher. Some sort of replacement cipher, and there's, like, some sort of code that the book ends up being the key to.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin theorizes the comedy book is a cipher key and that Daral Yashenti may have given Janussi a bitter gift — the note found in the wastebasket supports his theory; he is the first to suspect a replacement cipher and the rival’s role.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir analyzed the ink sequence and parchment, determining Janussi’s final written act was research in *The Discoveries* using fresh blue ink; he questioned the nature of the black substance and connected it to possible magical poisoning; he noted the relevance of the tobacco pipe as a potential concealment tool.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the candlelight that lit Sylvira’s face came from the lantern, not a candle.
source_quote: The candlelight that lit her face had not come from a candle at all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed the poison and cipher could both be true, and that the missing book carried both.
source_quote: The poison and the cipher could both be true. The missing book carried both.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir connects the candle to the shapeshifter situation.
source_quote: That explains the candle," said Zalthir

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir despises the scholarly culture of Candlekeep for its hidden grudges and performative civility.
source_quote: I despise this whole place a little — not Candlekeep, Candlekeep's fine, the books are fine — but the *culture* of it, the scholars who keep grudges the way a dragon keeps gold, sitting on them for years, polishing them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir did not respond to Daz’s compliment on his thinking, silently considering both poison and cipher as possibilities.
source_quote: I said nothing to that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified the potential link between Glabbagool’s Underdark ingestion and the unidentifiable poison, providing the critical investigative angle that led to confirming the substance’s danger.
source_quote: Wouldn't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an investigator who actively engages with witnesses, seeks clarification, and connects clues — notably recognizing the significance of the lantern and Sylvira’s behavior.
source_quote: That explains the candle," said Zalthir.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is an observer who incorrectly identified the book as a TV but correctly linked the candle to the shapeshifter. They helped assemble the final picture despite flawed assumptions.
source_quote: Oh, it's a TV!

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is curious about what Janussi was writing in his final unguarded moment, believing the room reads better when you ask what a man was doing then.
source_quote: I'm curious… trying to understand what he was writing at the time of death. The room reads better when you ask what a man was doing in his last unguarded minute than when you ask who he was.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is methodical and observant, focusing on physical anomalies — ink, residue, smoke, and light — and connects them to the murder mechanism; he accepted tea from Hollypocket with unusual enthusiasm, perhaps to gain her trust or observe her reactions.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by the continuing speaker banner as the POV character who observes the ink and parchment clues, and who accepts herbal tea from Hollypocket with unusual enthusiasm.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Zalthir, Scene: Clues in the Ink and Parchment]

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir knew the locket was missing from Janussi’s neck and that it was significant.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Sylvira Savikas was carrying a lantern despite being a tiefling who can see in the dark.
source_quote: She was carrying a lantern. She's a tiefling, and she can see in the dark without any light at all.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the blue ink on the book captured both obscure spell notes and jokes.
source_quote: The blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir observes that the blue ink on *The Discoveries* was the last thing Janussi wrote, and that it came after ink on *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.*

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized Janussi had shifted from writing jokes to researching spells, based on ink drying patterns.
source_quote: Jokes first. The ink on those had dried. Then he'd flopped over into the spell research.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realized the smoke in the room was not meant to kill, but to hide the smell of poison.
source_quote: You don't fill a room with smoke to kill a man — you fill a room with smoke to keep him from smelling what's already there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes the bruise on Janussi’s nose must have occurred before death because corpses cannot bruise.
source_quote: Grygum, you've got the healer's eye, right? How does bruising work if he's dead? Like, I would assume you don't really. ... You don't — you don't bruise after you're dead.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled the Garden Shadow’s saying about absence, though he wasn't sure if it was the Garden Shadow or Brother Tharusk.
source_quote: The Garden Shadow had a saying about that — or possibly Brother Tharusk did, the tall one who always smelled of incense; I wasn't listening to either of them closely.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognized Daral Yashenti’s long-standing grudge as a vector of rage that had fully set.
source_quote: Rage that's had time to set is a vector. It points somewhere.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir says, 'That explains the candle,' after Thorin identifies the shapeshifter situation, and later incorrectly identifies the book as a TV.
source_quote: "That explains the candle," said Zalthir, and the picture began to assemble itself.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suggests Glabbagool might have ingested the black substance and could help identify it.
source_quote: Wouldn't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark?

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thinks the book is a TV.
source_quote: Oh, it's a TV!" said Zalthir

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that Daral Yashenti had unintentionally become the wall of suspicion.
source_quote: Daral Yashenti had just walked himself into being the wall.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that Janussi always wore the locket and never took it off.
source_quote: Janussi carried it always, all the time, never took it off.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understood that a room reveals itself most through what is missing.
source_quote: A room tells you most by what it is missing.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir wonders if the black substance on Janussi’s finger is like Dumbledore’s style, suggesting he’s making a pop-culture reference.
source_quote: Like, Dumbledore style? Or, like—

subject: blackened finger stain
fact: The black substance on Janussi’s left forefinger and lower lip is not ink — it is a poison unknown even to an ooze that has consumed the Underdark.
source_quote: That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*.

subject: blackened fingertip and lip stain
fact: The black stain on Janussi’s fingertip and lower lip was not ink, but a darker, unidentifiable substance, suggesting he ingested it while reading — possibly as part of a magical or toxic mechanism tied to the text he was copying.
source_quote: The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was not.

subject: black residue
fact: Black residue was found on Janussi’s fingers and mouth — definitively not blue ink — suggesting exposure to poison or a toxic substance, possibly concealed by tobacco smoke.
source_quote: Black. Definitively not the blue ink... The black on the man's mouth came from somewhere the blue ink did not.

subject: black residue
fact: Black residue was found on Janussi’s mouth and fingers — definitively not blue ink — suggesting ingestion of poison or a chemical agent; it was distinct from the ink used in the book's annotations and may be the key to identifying the murder weapon.

subject: black residue
fact: The black residue is described as being on Janussi’s fingers and mouth, definitively not from the blue ink, and associated with poison.
source_quote: Black. Definitively not the blue ink — Grygum had already settled that, checked it twice and certain.

subject: black substance
fact: A dark, unknown material that stained Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue; not ink, not poison easily identifiable even by Glabbagool; likely a magical toxin absorbed through contact with a cursed page.
source_quote: When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: blue ink
fact: The blue ink is described as capturing both notes on obscure spells and jokes, written in the same hand, with the joke annotations dried first.
source_quote: The blue ink captures both notes on obscure spells and jokes?

subject: blue ink in 'The Discoveries'
fact: The latest writing in Janussi’s hand was in blue ink on 'The Discoveries', recorded after notes in 'The Golden Ass', indicating his final intellectual activity was spell research.
source_quote: The blue ink on 'The Discoveries' had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. 'The Golden Ass.' 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: broken lead chain links
fact: Two broken lead links found on Janussi’s neck, worn from long-term use; evidence of a locket or amulet forcibly removed post-assault but pre-mortem.
source_quote: Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him.

subject: broken lead chain links
fact: Two broken lead links were found beneath the Keeper’s neck, indicating a locket or necklace had been forcibly removed after he was struck but before he died.
source_quote: The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain.

subject: broken lead chain links
fact: Two broken lead links were found embedded in Grygum's neck, with wear patterns indicating a long-held pendant or locket had been forcibly removed. The material and craftsmanship suggested it was not common jewelry but possibly a sacred or magical artifact.
source_quote: I have catalogued a great many sacred spaces in my time, and there is a particular grief in an empty setting where something belonged.

subject: chipped tooth
fact: Janussi’s front tooth was chipped from a fall face-first onto stone — a recent trauma occurring just before death, unrelated to the heart removal.
source_quote: A chip in one of his front teeth, the edge jagged. Recent. Not an old break worn smooth, but a fresh wound. He had fallen forward. Face-first. Chipped the tooth on the way down.

subject: comedy book cipher key
fact: The comedy book, *The Golden Ass*, may serve as a cipher key for hidden notes written within it.
source_quote: there's something written in the book that wasn't part of the original book... maybe he's using the book and the notes to do some sort of cipher... the book ends up being the key to.

subject: ebony pipe with cherry tobacco
fact: A finely carved pipe with cherry tobacco residue; likely used to mask the odor of the black poison, suggesting the killer or the victim anticipated or concealed magical toxicity.
source_quote: Tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: force darts (in chair)
fact: Three circular punctures in the armchair, with horsehair stuffing scattered and two holes punched clean through the back, indicate blasts of pure force. No such wounds were found on Grygum’s body, suggesting the darts were fired at the chair in rage or as a symbolic act — not an attack on the keeper.
source_quote: Why would you loose three darts of force at a chair?

subject: gift tag
fact: A gift tag in a cramped, resentful hand read: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival' — suggesting a bitter relationship, though its authenticity and intent remain unverified.
source_quote: *To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.*

subject: gift tag
fact: The gift tag is described as being written in a cramped, sour hand with the message: 'To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.'
source_quote: To Janussi, read it and weep, you old snob, a proper Dead Winter gift, your loving rival.

subject: Grygum's rivalry theory
fact: The rivalry between Janussi and Daral Yashenti is central to the investigation, with Daral being the one who called the sell swords.
source_quote: He's the one who called you sellswords.

subject: Hightower Library key (Janussi's)
fact: One of two physical keys to the Hightower Library, held by Janussi. Its location after his death is unknown, but it may have been taken along with *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: Hightower Library key (Kalan's)
fact: The second physical key to the Hightower Library, held by Kalan, the gate warden. Its status is unchanged, but access to the library may have been compromised through Janussi's key.
source_quote: The other key, I learned, rested with Kalan, the gate warden.

subject: hightower library key possession
fact: The key to the Hightower Library held by Janussi was the key that explained the deletion of forbidden text.
source_quote: That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: hypnotic block
fact: The hypnotic block is not a device — it is a book, 'The Golden Ass', that immobilizes and disinterests.
source_quote: Every time they open that block, they just sit there and don't tickle! The Golden Ass, the missing volume

subject: Keys to the Hightower Library
fact: Two keys grant access to the Hightower Library: one held by Janussi, the other by Kalan. Their possession implies authority over restricted materials and possible involvement in the theft or deletion of *The Golden Ass*.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys to the Hightower Library.

subject: lantern

subject: marble statue of hooded old man
fact: A three-foot-tall marble statue of a hooded, bearded man holding a candle aloft was toppled near the armchairs and tea table. The candle was intact when shaken, suggesting the statue was deliberately knocked over, not by accident or collapse. Its placement and condition imply ritual significance or symbolic desecration.
source_quote: Shake the candle.

subject: midnight blue ink stains on right sleeve
fact: Midnight blue ink stains on the right sleeve of Janussi’s tunic — the working hand — confirm he was actively taking notes at the time of death, suggesting he was interrupted while writing.
source_quote: Writing hand, fresh stains. A man interrupted at work.

subject: missing sapphire
fact: One sapphire was taken from the safe, while four others and a king’s ransom in gold, diamonds, and potions remained untouched — indicating the killer sought a specific component for a sapphire-based spell, not wealth.
source_quote: Someone is trying to build a sapphire spell, a spell that requires a sapphire.

subject: missing sapphire and spell parchment
fact: One sapphire and one parchment naming a spell were taken from the safe, while four other sapphires and numerous valuables remained untouched. The parchment likely contained components for a spell requiring a sapphire — possibly a high-level enchantment or ritual. The specificity of the theft indicates the killer sought not wealth, but a single arcane component.
source_quote: Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell.

subject: nose bruising
fact: The bruising around Janussi’s broken nose formed before death, as corpses cannot bruise — proving he was assaulted and injured hours before being killed.
source_quote: The bruising around the broken nose held its color, dark and settled, the way bruising only sits when blood was still moving when it formed. My focus narrowed and held, and the picture came clear and certain: this happened before he died. Not the fall. Earlier.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: statue of A'lai Aivenmore
fact: A three-foot marble statue of a hooded bearded man holding a candle, toppled near the armchair; it had been knocked over by A'lai Aivenmore upon discovering the body, not by magic or force.
source_quote: The Great Reader A'lai Aivenmore had knocked it over in shock when he found the body at dawn.

subject: Stonespeaker crystal
fact: The Stonespeaker crystal is described as granting Daz the ability to talk to beasts, and was used to initiate the cat interrogation.
source_quote: Talking to beasts, yeah. It's part of what the stone speaker crystal grants me.

subject: the black substance
fact: The black substance found on Janussi’s finger, lip, and tongue was not ink, not poison from his inkwell, and was unidentifiable even by Glabbagool, an ooze that has ingested the Underdark — indicating it was something uniquely dangerous and unnatural.
source_quote: Darkness than blue. That was the entire point of the long look — not that the finger was stained, but that the stain was *wrong*. Darker than anything in his inkwell. Zalthir, ever the auditor of other people's competence, pushed on it — *our great detective took his long, careful look and still can't tell us if it's ink?* No. That was exactly what I could tell. The skill wasn't in identifying the substance. It was in knowing, with certainty, what it was *not*. Would't Glabbagool have ingested, like, all sorts of different kinds of materials and poisons and goo in the Underdark? We gave him the substance. He gave it his best. It wasn't enough — a thin first effort, then a second pass with help, and still nothing he could name. But even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered.

subject: the comedy book
fact: The comedy book, *The Golden Ass*, was used by Janussi as a cipher key — annotated with both jokes and obscure spell notes in the same hand and ink; it was the only item physically removed from the room, suggesting it contained hidden knowledge worth stealing.

subject: the deleted book
fact: The book Janussi was studying was altered or removed from the library archives, likely because it contained sensitive or forbidden knowledge — the same knowledge that may have motivated his murder and the theft of the locket.
source_quote: that book that no one should have touched... why that stuff got deleted off the library.

subject: *The Discoveries*
fact: *The Discoveries* was a spellbook annotated in fresh blue ink with notes on unfamiliar spells and their casting — the final written work of Janussi before his death.
source_quote: The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book... The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: The Discoveries
fact: The spellbook *The Discoveries* was the last thing Janussi wrote in, with fresh blue ink noting unfamiliar spells, and its entries were newer than those in *The Golden Ass*, confirming it was his final act before death.
source_quote: In the middle of the desk sat a spellbook. *The Discoveries.* Beside it, blue ink, fresh enough that it had a sequence to it. There was more than one color on those pages, and I wanted the newest one isolated before anything else. The blue ink on *The Discoveries* had been laid down after the blue ink on another book. *The Golden Ass.* 'So that's the last thing he was writing?' Confirmation. The spell research was the final thing under his hand.

subject: the ebony pipe with cherry tobacco
fact: An ebony pipe with cherry tobacco was found on the desk, suggesting the killer may have used smoke to mask the odor of poison.
source_quote: A silver pedestal by the desk, an ebony pipe finely carved, cherry tobacco. Pretty, until Zalthir's instinct landed it — tobacco smoke would hide the smell of poison. Of course it would.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: *The Golden Ass* is a book that acts as a 'hypnotic block' — when opened, it renders a person motionless and uninterested in external stimuli. It was removed from the Hightower Library by Daral and is linked to the deletion of its contents.
source_quote: Every time they open that block, they just sit there and don't tickle!

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: *The Golden Ass* is a physical book, not a magical device, that induces stillness and disinterest when opened. It was the instrument used to disable observers and was stolen by Daral.
source_quote: A book. Not a device, not an enchantment — a book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat.

subject: *The Golden Ass*
fact: *The Golden Ass* was a comedy book annotated in blue ink with jokes Janussi found funny — the ink on these jokes had dried before he turned to spell research — and the book itself was missing from the chamber.
source_quote: Jokes first. The ink on those had dried. Then he'd flopped over into the spell research... the comedy book had walked out of the room.

subject: The Golden Ass
fact: The Golden Ass is a dull book that holds a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat, and was taken from the room under Daral's arm.
source_quote: "Every time they open that block," Queenie said, "they just sit there and don't tickle!" A book. Not a device, not an enchantment — a book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat. *The Golden Ass*, the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm.

subject: the golden ass
fact: The book, dull enough to hold a person motionless and uninterested in scratching a cat, is 'The Golden Ass', missing and carried by Daral.
source_quote: The Golden Ass, the missing volume, walking out of the room under Daral's arm

subject: the Hightower Library keys
fact: Two keys exist to the Hightower Library — one held by Janussi (now missing), and one held by Kalan, the gate warden; the deletion of content from the book suggests the killer sought access to restricted materials, requiring one or both keys.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys of the Hightower Library... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: the lantern
fact: Sylvira Savikas was seen carrying a lantern at 2–3 a.m., despite being a tiefling with innate darkvision; the lantern's light was not for illumination but to obscure or reveal something — possibly the poison’s residue, the missing book, or the locket’s contents.

subject: the locket
fact: A locket or necklace was torn from Janussi’s neck, leaving broken lead links and worn impressions where it had hung, suggesting it was a personal, long-carried item of significance.
source_quote: The neck told us more. The impression of a chain on the back and sides, and beneath it two broken lead links. Something had hung there, and someone had torn it off him. A locket, a necklace — gone, snapped at the chain. I have catalogued a great many sacred spaces in my time, and there is a particular grief in an empty setting where something belonged. The links were worn where it had hung. Whatever it was, he'd carried it a long time.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket is described by Queenie as intimate, carried all the time, never taken off, but its nature is unknown to her.
source_quote: The locket itself is intimate. He carried it all the time. He never took it off." "I don't know what it was.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket was worn by Janussi and taken after his death; its absence is a key indicator that the killer sought not just to kill, but to remove a physical object tied to the library’s security system or personal significance.
source_quote: The locket was missing. Off Janussi's neck.

subject: the locket
fact: The locket, always worn by Janussi, was missing from his neck after death; it may have contained a key, message, or magical component tied to the Hightower Library's second key or the cipher in the comedy book.

subject: the missing sapphire
fact: One sapphire was missing from the safe, while four others remained sealed in pouches, indicating the thief sought not treasure but a specific component for a spell requiring a single sapphire.
source_quote: But one sapphire was missing. One parchment. 'Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell,' he said, 'a spell that requires a sapphire.' And here is where the room stopped making sense as a robbery. Because still inside the safe were four sealed pouches, each with its sapphire — and beside them a figurine of a raven, a potion of supreme healing, another of water breathing, five diamonds each worth a fortune, a heap of platinum and gold, a small treasury left untouched.

subject: tickles count
fact: There have been too little Tickles and too many questions — Queenie's final assessment of the interrogation.
source_quote: There have been too little Tickles and too many questions.

subject: tobacco smoke
fact: The chamber was thick with tobacco smoke, a habitual habit of Janussi’s to medicate his failing lungs — which would have masked the smell of poison, making it an ideal concealment method for his murder.
source_quote: A man who fills his own room with smoke as a habit... The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: Candle Reference
fact: Zalthir linked the candle to the shapeshifter situation, implying the candle may have been used in the disguise ritual or as a magical trigger. Its nature and origin are unexplained.
source_quote: That explains the candle.

subject: Cat’s Final Insult
fact: Queenie’s final assessment — that two-leggers rarely lick themselves — is a cryptic, culturally loaded judgment. It may hint at a deeper truth about hygiene, magic, or ritual practices among the suspects.
source_quote: It's clear that you hardly ever lick yourselves at all.

subject: cause of Janussi's death
fact: Janussi was alive when Daral left with *The Golden Ass*. The exact mechanism of death remains unconfirmed, but the book's removal and the deletion of records suggest a targeted act of sabotage or ritual.
source_quote: But the victim was still alive when Daral left.

subject: Daz's disinterest
fact: Daz paid no attention to Hollypocket’s emotional breakdown and only resumed listening after the lantern revelation — suggesting he may have prior knowledge or a hidden agenda regarding Sylvira or the murder.
source_quote: Daz, I noticed, was paying the weeping woman no attention whatsoever… Hmm," said Daz, suddenly listening after all.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The killer had intimate knowledge of the safe’s combination, access to the chamber, and a specific goal — to silence Janussi permanently and steal a single sapphire for a spell; they struck before death, returned after, and were patient enough to desecrate the body without haste.
source_quote: Who had been certain enough to want him silent on both sides of death.

subject: identity of the killer
fact: The killer had no need to force entry, knew the safe’s combination, carried a method to mask poison, and took only a single arcane component. The assault on Grygum’s nose, the removal of his necklace, and the force darts aimed at the chair suggest personal motive — not mere theft. The killer may be someone connected to Grygum’s research, or a rival spellwright seeking to complete the sapphire spell before him.
source_quote: Daz's reading and Zalthir's logic only got us to the moment of death. I had the part before it.

subject: identity of the rival
fact: The gift tag suggests a bitter rival, but no name or further evidence is provided — the rival’s identity and motive remain unknown.
source_quote: Some sort of rival gave him a gift, but it was sort of like a bitter thing.

subject: Janussi’s locket
fact: The locket was always worn by Janussi and never removed, making its absence significant.
source_quote: Janussi carried it always, all the time, never took it off.

subject: Locket’s Purpose
fact: The locket carried by Janussi was never identified. Its absence after his death raises questions: Was it stolen? Does it contain a key, message, or magical component tied to the library or book?
source_quote: I don't know what it was.

subject: locket's significance
fact: The locket Janussi never removed may contain a clue to his relationship with Sylvira Savikas or the source of her wrath — its absence or condition after death may be critical to the investigation.

subject: nature of the black substance

subject: purpose of the erased records
fact: Records within the Hightower Library were deleted, possibly to conceal knowledge tied to *The Golden Ass*, the locket, or the shapeshifter. The nature of the erased data is unknown.
source_quote: That might explain why that stuff got deleted off that book that no one should have touched.

subject: purpose of the sapphire spell
fact: The stolen sapphire was likely for a spell capable of binding, silencing, or reanimating the dead — possibly to prevent Janussi’s soul from answering questions beyond death, aligning with the heart’s removal.
source_quote: Whoever had done this had not wanted Janussi answering questions on the other side of the veil.

subject: shapeshifter identity
fact: A shapeshifter impersonating Sylvira Savikas was observed, suggesting an agent working in the shadows to conceal their involvement in the theft, deletion, and murder.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: Shapeshifter Identity
fact: The figure impersonating Sylvira Savikas without her scent suggests a shapeshifter is active in the tower. Their identity, motive, and connection to Daral or the book's deletion remain unknown.
source_quote: But she didn't smell like the demon lady, though.

subject: source of the poison
fact: The black residue on Janussi’s mouth and the concealment by tobacco smoke imply poisoning, but the substance, delivery method, and agent remain unidentified.
source_quote: The one thing that tobacco smoke would do is hide the smell of poison.

subject: Sylvira's lantern
fact: The presence of a lantern carried by Sylvira Savikas — a tiefling with darkvision — suggests the light was meant to illuminate evidence, a body, or a hidden object, and may be central to determining the method or timing of the murder.
source_quote: That explains the candle," said Zalthir.

subject: The black substance
fact: The black substance is unknown but potent enough that even Glabbagool, an ooze that has eaten the Underdark, cannot identify it.
source_quote: Even his failure carried a verdict: there was *something* about the black, something that mattered. When even a creature that has eaten the Underdark can't place a poison, you've learned the poison is worth being afraid of.

subject: the candle statue's meaning
fact: The toppled statue of the hooded old man holding a candle may represent a deity, patron, or symbolic figure in Grygum’s practice. Its deliberate toppling, coupled with the untouched candle, implies a ritual act of defiance, mourning, or power transfer. The statue’s identity and its connection to the missing necklace or sapphire spell remain unknown.
source_quote: Shake the candle.

subject: the cipher in the comedy book
fact: The comedy book contains a replacement cipher — jokes and spell notes written together suggest a code where each joke maps to a spell component; the book's disappearance implies the cipher was the target, not the book itself.

subject: The darts at the chair
fact: The three darts of pure force fired at the chair have no clear motive, and their purpose remains unexplained.
source_quote: Why would you loose three darts of force at a chair?

subject: the glowing red face
fact: Sylvira Savikas’s face glowed red in candlelight at 2–3 a.m. — an unnatural phenomenon suggesting magical interference, poison residue, or a hidden spell; her lantern may have been used to trigger or conceal this effect.

subject: the housekeeper’s testimony
fact: The housekeeper, Hollypocket, has not yet been interviewed, but her knowledge of what is normally present in the quarters is the next critical step — she may reveal what else is missing beyond the locket and the book, exposing the true scope of the theft.
source_quote: go find, say, the housekeeper, and ask her, what is missing or out of place.

subject: the identity of the killer
fact: The killer acted with calm precision, showed no urgency, and performed a ritualistic desecration — suggesting a person with intimate knowledge of magical protections and a motive beyond simple murder.
source_quote: Whoever did this had not been in a rush. He had not been trying to kill. He had been desecrating a corpse at his leisure, with nowhere to be.

subject: the midnight thud
fact: Hollypocket heard a thud at midnight, coinciding with Janussi’s death; it may have been the victim falling, the book being removed, or a struggle — and it occurred after Sylvira’s suspicious presence, suggesting she was involved in the act.

subject: the missing book’s contents
fact: The deletion or removal of the book’s contents remains unexplained; its connection to the locket and the keys suggests it contained a cipher, a map, or a key to a hidden archive — a secret that someone killed to protect or steal.
source_quote: Some sort of cipher... the book ends up being the key to.

subject: The missing comedy book
fact: The comedy book was the only thing missing from the room, and its absence was the central clue.
source_quote: And now it was gone, and it was the only thing gone.

subject: the missing key
fact: One of two Hightower Library keys is missing — Janussi’s — while Kalan holds the other; the locket may have contained the key or a duplicate; whoever stole the book may also have stolen the key to access restricted archives.

subject: The missing locket
fact: The locket or necklace taken from Janussi’s neck is unidentified, but its removal suggests personal or symbolic significance.

subject: The missing sapphire and parchment

source_quote: Somebody is trying to build a sapphire spell, a spell that requires a sapphire.

subject: the reading poison mechanism
fact: The pattern of black substance on finger and lip suggests Janussi was wetting his fingertip to turn pages — and that the pages themselves may have been the source of the poison, implying a magical or sentient text that consumes those who read it.
source_quote: Turning pages, wetting the fingertip the way readers do without thinking, a hundred times an hour, never once considering that the page might be the thing reading them.

subject: The rivalry between Janussi and Daral Yashenti
fact: Daral Yashenti and Janussi had been at each other's throats for years, with Daral harboring deep resentment.
source_quote: Those two have been at each other's throats for years.

subject: The two keys to the Hightower Library
fact: One key was around Janussi’s neck and missing; the other was held by the gate warden, Kalan.
source_quote: Janussi held one of the two keys... the other key is heralded by the gate warden, Kalan.

subject: drow poisoning timeline
fact: The poison was transferred via a book licked by the killer, and the act occurred during a day of drugging and emotional distress.
source_quote: I was drugged. I was upset. I don't know what I was thinking.

subject: eight o'clock meeting
fact: Kalan met with Janussi at eight o'clock to request additional watchers, and was refused; this refusal may have triggered the murder, as Janussi was aware of security vulnerabilities; the timing suggests the killer acted within hours of this confrontation.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: eight o'clock meeting with Janussi
fact: Kalan met with Janussi at eight o’clock to request more watchers and was refused — a key event in his timeline before the murder.
source_quote: The eight o'clock meeting where he'd pressed Janussi for more watchers and been refused.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: midnight curfew
fact: Daral will be kept under watch until midnight, when a cleric and sword capable of drawing poison are within arm's reach.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight — a cleric who could draw poison out, and a sword that could do the same, both within arm's reach.

subject: midnight deadline
fact: Daral Yashenti is to be held under surveillance until midnight, when a cleric and a sword capable of drawing poison will be brought to his side. If he dies after that hour, it will be interpreted as evidence that he was the poisoner — the poison was meant to kill only if he were innocent. The timing is a ritualistic test of guilt.
source_quote: We'd keep Daral close until midnight.

subject: morning of the murder
fact: On the morning of the murder, Kalan conducted an inspection just after eight, established a cordon, posted a watcher, and doubled the guard at the High Tower Library — all documented to establish his whereabouts.
source_quote: The morning of the murder: the inspection just after eight, the cordon, the posted watcher...

subject: night of the murder
fact: The murder occurred on the night of the incident, with Janussi consuming the poison during the day and dying at midnight; Kalan’s timeline places him at the Chamber of Lost Lore, visiting Sylvira Savikas at quarter-past-ten, and inspecting the High Tower before the murder; the impersonation of Sylvira Savikas occurred during this window.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas
fact: Kalan visited Sylvira Savikas at 10:15 for a cosmological question — later revealed to have been an impersonator, undermining his alibi and timeline.
source_quote: The quarter-past-ten visit to Sylvira Savikas over some cosmological question.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the investigation phase of Chapter 54, following the Candlekeep Murders. No specific calendar date is given, but the narrative implies immediate post-crime activity, with the body being removed and the investigation initiated without delay.

subject: session date
fact: The events occur in the context of a murder investigation at Candlekeep, with no explicit in-world calendar date provided.

subject: session date

source_quote: The eleven o'clock meeting came out without resistance

subject: session date
