source_quote: 'Jezebel! Organize the chamber's seats in front of me!' The familiar moved with an efficiency that told me this was not the first time Sylvira had directed operations from a sickbed.

subject: Kaelira
fact: Kaelira is the source who previously revealed that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand, establishing the long-term mystery tied to A'lai.
source_quote: My training ran toward the opposite: know where every debt is, who holds it, what it costs. The patron entry had been blank for months. Every time I thought I was close to something, it receded. Now there was a compromised drow scholar who might represent the first real lead I'd been offered since Kaelira laid the problem out for me plainly.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is identified as the party wronged, with standing and motivation to be thorough, and the one to whom the evidence should be handed.
source_quote: Kalan was the party who had been wronged, Kalan had standing, Kalan was presumably motivated to be thorough.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan is the wronged party with standing in the investigation, whose motivation and thoroughness make him the natural candidate to receive and act upon the collected evidence. His position as the moral center of the group is unchallenged.
source_quote: Kalan was the party who had been wronged, Kalan had standing, Kalan was presumably motivated to be thorough.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan, the man who had been fired, stood outside during Alkrist’s confession and now holds a complete and unfiltered account of the plot’s mechanics.
source_quote: Kalan had been standing just outside through all of it, which meant the man who'd been fired now held a rather complete account.

subject: Kalan
fact: Kalan, the recently fired staff member, was present during the assassination and now holds the most complete account of the events; he is the designated party to inherit the investigation and clean up the aftermath.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is referenced by Sylvira as the one who requested intercession with Janussi to keep his job.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch had come to her before Deadwinter evening, asking her to intercede with Janussi on his behalf, to keep his job

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the First Reader who developed the Threefold Proof methodology, which was rejected and dismissed as solipsism by Janussi; his professional credibility is tied to the very framework now used to investigate the murder.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch. The First Reader. The one with the truth-seeking spell that had already anchored the investigation once.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the First Reader whose criminal investigation methodology, the Threefold Proof, was formally rejected by Janussi and later used by Kalan as the basis for his own investigative authority.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it. ... Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime, the Threefold Proof, the methodologies, the framework we'd been handed as a legitimate investigation tool, had been blocked by the man who was now dead.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch requested Sylvira’s intervention to retain his position under Janussi; his proposal for investigative controls was deemed insane by Sylvira and opposed by Bookwyrm; his research was considered third-rate by Sylvira; he was dismissed by Janussi and later died under mysterious circumstances involving midnight tears.
source_quote: He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch sought Sylvira’s intervention to retain his position, which she declined to pursue; his proposal for investigative controls was deemed absurd by Bookwyrm and rejected by Janussi.
source_quote: He asked her to intercede with Janussi on his behalf... she never brought it up.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies was rejected by Janussi as solipsism and dismissed as a vanity project; Kalan then presented that same framework as his operating methodology to the investigation team, despite having been professionally humiliated by the victim.
source_quote: Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal for new criminal investigation methodologies, found it to be solipsism, and had blocked it. He wasn't interested, he wrote, in creating all these rules and procedures so that Kalan could go detect a murder mystery.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch, the First Reader, is the only known caster of the truth-seeking spell that previously anchored the investigation, and his current absence has become a critical point in the group’s operational split.
source_quote: Who can cast the truth spell? Yeah — Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch title
fact: Kalan Strongbranch is the First Reader.
source_quote: Kalan Strongbranch. The First Reader.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani holds a credible, long-standing resentment toward Sylvira and Janussi, with apparent capability to act on it.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani: resentment credible enough to survive scrutiny, long-standing grudge, apparent capability.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani is a former romantic partner of Janussi who resented Sylvira for replacing her, and is identified by Sylvira as a suspect with motive rooted in academic jealousy.
source_quote: That bitter old hag... who always resented Janussi for ditching her in favor of me. ... This was my fault.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani is a former romantic partner of Janussi, replaced by Sylvira; Sylvira implicated her in the framing out of long-standing resentment, breaking down emotionally while doing so.
source_quote: That bitter old hag, who always resented Janussi for ditching her in favor of me.

subject: Kazryn Nyantani
fact: Kazryn Nyantani is referenced by the narrator as having credible resentment and a long-standing grudge.
source_quote: Kazryn Nyantani: resentment credible enough to survive scrutiny, long-standing grudge, apparent capability

subject: Lilith
fact: Lilith is referenced by the narrator as the sick tiefling in the too-hot room, grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved.
source_quote: And a sick tiefling in a too-hot room, shivering despite the fire, grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved

subject: nobody drow evoker
fact: A nameless drow evoker is being kept alive and functional through payments to Menzoberranzan, and their existence is tied to the hidden payer and A'lai’s knowledge-based terms.

subject: Orrin Glass
fact: Orrin Glass is referenced by Alkrist as arriving with Irony with a basin of water for supper while he was burning the vial’s label.
source_quote: He was burning the label when Irony and Orrin Glass arrived with a basin of water for supper

subject: people involved in Janussi's death
fact: There are at least 3 people involved, at least.
source_quote: Yeah. There's 3 people involved, at least.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira anticipated being asked whether she called Kalan a genus traitor, which suggested she had prepared for the question.
source_quote: The word "never" had a specificity that suggested she'd anticipated being asked.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed jealousy was a powerful motivator for revenge and murder.
source_quote: Jealousy is a powerful motivator, she said. For revenge. Murder.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira believed that anyone claiming to have seen her after 12:30 was lying, and named Teles Ahvoste as a hostile party.
source_quote: it would be members of the avowed who had long nurtured hostility toward her. Great Readers included. She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira considered Kalan Strongbranch's proposal insane and believed Bookwyrm had pushed hardest against it.
source_quote: his proposal, which she called insane, all sorts of investigative controls and restrictions. When Janussi had raised it at some point, it was Bookwyrm who'd felt it was absurd. Bookwyrm who had pushed hardest against it.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had been trying to coax her son back into the Mordenkainen's Mansion she built for his protection.
source_quote: She'd been trying to coax him back into it.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira had never drunk honey and felt genuine offense at the suggestion.
source_quote: Honey? I would never drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira insisted she had never called Kalan Strongbranch a genus traitor.
source_quote: But she had never, she insisted, called him a genus traitor.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a feverish tiefling who once promised to intercede for Kalan Strongbranch but never followed through; she dismissed him as incompetent and later claimed to have never called him a genus traitor; she has a son born in the Abyss whom she constructed a Mordenkainen's Mansion to protect and has been trying to coax back into it; she insists she was with her son after 12:30 and was infected with an abyssal plague by him; she named Teles Ahvoste as a long-term enemy who may have framed her; she rejected honey as a substance and expressed outrage at the suggestion she drank it.
source_quote: I did sneak out. To visit my son.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling abyssal spawn researching infernal domains, currently under suspicion for a 'horrible tragedy' she claims she did not commit, and believes she has been framed.
source_quote: I'm willing to collaborate with anything, and I'm delighted — delighted — that you are leading the investigation.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling and abyssal spawn accused of murdering Janussi; she is feverish, framed, and believes she is being impersonated — she has critical knowledge about her research, rivalries, and final conversation with the victim.
source_quote: I'm willing to collaborate with anything... I'm delighted that you are leading the investigation.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling researcher framed for Janussi's murder, suffering from a fevered illness while under investigation, and revealed she was the target of prejudice due to her infernal research and relationship with Janussi.
source_quote: Sylvira was framed for the murder and dying slowly under the poison's effect. ... Her area of research was the infernal domains, which compounded the prejudice. The relationship with Janussi had probably offended someone else on top of that.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is distraught and feverish, grieving the last argument she had with Janussi, and claims to have been with her son after 12:30 AM, returning to her chambers alone before succumbing to an abyssal plague.
source_quote: I returned to my chambers around 12:30... and saw no one.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is referenced by Daz as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Sylvira might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira is the subject of an unresolved anomaly: a lookalike has been sighted in two locations within a timeframe that defies standard polymorph spell duration, indicating deception beyond simple magic.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira knew her field and dismissed Kalan Strongbranch's research as third-rate at best.
source_quote: Janussi was right to want him gone. He was a clown, a boar, and his research was third-rate at best.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was framed for the murder and is dying slowly under the poison's effect; she had every reason to tell everything she knew and no reasons left not to; she is bedridden and shuddering under fever but still capable of running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room, indicating she is not incapacitated.
source_quote: The door opened before I knocked. A mage hand, which was interesting: she was bedridden and shuddering under a fever, and still running a familiar and a mage hand from across the room.

subject: Sylvira
fact: Sylvira was grieving the last argument she had had with her son.
source_quote: And a sick tiefling in a too-hot room, shivering despite the fire, grieving the last argument she'd had with someone she'd loved.

subject: Sylvira's son
fact: Sylvira's son was born in the Abyss and lives in a Mordenkainen's Mansion she constructed for his protection.
source_quote: born in the Abyss, living in a Mordenkainen's Mansion she'd constructed specifically for his protection

subject: Sylvira's species
fact: Sylvira is a tiefling and technically an abyssal spawn.
source_quote: people look at a tiefling and assume she's an abyssal spawn. She happened, technically, to be an abyssal spawn

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste harbored a two-decade institutional grudge against Janussi, having been passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older and more skilled, and Sylvira suspects Teles of fabricating sightings of her after the plague set in.
source_quote: If anyone claimed to have seen her after that, it would be members of the avowed who had long nurtured hostility toward her. Great Readers included. She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste held a two-decade grudge against Janussi, having been passed over for Keeper of Tomes despite being older and more skilled; Sylvira identified him as a persistent enemy who may have fabricated evidence against her; he is a Great Reader and harbors institutional hostility toward Sylvira.
source_quote: She named Teles Ahvoste directly.

subject: Teles Ahvoste
fact: Teles Ahvoste is named by Sylvira as having held hostility toward Janussi for nearly twenty years and being passed over for Keeper of Tomes.
source_quote: Teles Ahvoste directly

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin advocates for collecting physical evidence (books per suspect) and pushing Kalan to take charge, while also entertaining blackmail as a tool — his position reflects pragmatic institutional thinking.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes the team should give the evidence to Kalan so he can clean house.
source_quote: I think we go to the guy that was fired, give it to him, let him clean house.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insists on acquiring a book per suspect and suggests handing the evidence to Kalan to clean house.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin insists the team should get a book per suspect as compensation.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a meticulous investigator who has observed the pattern of those who share critical information immediately before healing, and is concerned that Daral will disappear once restored.
source_quote: The ones who ran the moment they felt better were usually the ones who'd shared their most valuable information right before the healing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is an absent colleague of Daz, currently preparing to make Alkrist uncomfortable; he does not offer emotional support to Sylvira.
source_quote: Thorin wasn't in the room to offer the easy sympathy.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is assembling a framework for truth-seeking based on fixed facts over magical deception, rejecting the myth that the dead or magic reveal truth transparently, and values convergence of physical, testimonial, and procedural evidence.
source_quote: You cannot rely on magic to make evidence meaningful. It makes evidence adversarial.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is concerned that Daral, once restored, would disappear and become difficult to locate because he might have already shared his most valuable information.
source_quote: The concern was that Daral, once restored, would discover pressing business elsewhere and become difficult to locate. The ones who ran the moment they felt better were usually the ones who'd shared their most valuable information right before the healing, because they knew they wouldn't be around to see how you used it.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced as absent from Sylvira's interview, presumably preparing to confront Alkrist, and thus not present to provide emotional support during her testimony.
source_quote: Thorin wasn't in the room to offer the easy sympathy. He was off somewhere getting ready to make Alkrist very uncomfortable.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Grygum as the investigator who struggled to reconcile the sapphire and the locket as evidence and proposed that one person could have stolen both.
source_quote: Thorin proposed that one person could have done both: stolen the locket, then taken the sapphire to close off pursuit.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is referenced by Zalthir as the one who conducted the interrogation of Alkrist and confirmed the presence of a truth spell.
source_quote: Thorin responded with something about being happy to help for the right remuneration... Kalan was outside the door. As of right now, Alkrist could not lie

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the group’s pragmatic strategist, consistently pushing for actionable outcomes — whether extracting books from suspects or framing blackmail as a career path. His instincts align with material gain and control, making him the most vocal advocate for exploiting the evidence.
source_quote: I have a mission in mind.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is the lead investigator in the party, specializing in logical puzzles and forensic contradictions. He is deeply troubled by the impossibility of stealing a locket from a living person and suspects two perpetrators. He is methodical, persistent, and understands that magic does not resolve contradictions—it creates them.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin realizes that magic like Speak with Dead cannot be relied upon because the dead are still themselves and may misremember or misattribute events.
source_quote: Well, I'm interested — even if we were able to actually cast Speak with Dead, how do you know they're a reliable narrator? What are their motivations after they're dead? We don't know. Because they're dead.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recalls that in the Underdark, the only thing that didn't lie was terrain — the fixed physical world.
source_quote: In the Underdark, the one thing that didn't lie was terrain. You couldn't trust what you were told. You couldn't trust what you saw. But the ground under your feet was fixed.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that giants taught him the principle that a rock's meaning depends on its placement — not its nature.
source_quote: Giants taught me that without ever writing it down. A rock in the wrong place is just a rock. A rock in the right place is a wall.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin thinks the poison book method was too elaborate, which is exactly why it worked.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understands that the myth of the person — the assumption that death brings transparency — is false.
source_quote: The myth of the person. The assumption that death is a transparency, that the dead have shed their performances and will now simply tell you what's true. They don't. They're still themselves.

subject: Varath
fact: Brother Varath is one of the two possible instructors who taught the cohort the art of the urgent errand, though the speaker is uncertain whether it was Heslin or Varath.
source_quote: Brother Heslin, or possibly Brother Varath, I'm genuinely uncertain which, had devoted an entire season to teaching our cohort the art of the urgent errand, the clean dispatch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed he could use the dragonborn conversational bond with Alkrist.
source_quote: I knew I could.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believed that what you find in someone's room tells you more than what they'd ever say with their face.
source_quote: I had been in Alkrist's chambers earlier, moving through the dark in a way I was reasonably confident he hadn't noticed. The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to. There was a class at the monastery, Brother Essivhan, possibly, or the quiet one with the ink-stained hands, about what you find in someone's room telling you more than what they'd ever say with their face.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes blackmail is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.
source_quote: It is not expressed in gold... It is the most reliably underpriced resource in the world, especially in the hands of someone who desperately needs it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes his training requires knowing where every debt is, who holds it, and what it costs.
source_quote: My training ran toward the opposite: know where every debt is, who holds it, what it costs.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir believes the most dangerous person in a room is the one who has already decided they've won.
source_quote: The most dangerous person in a room isn't the one with the blade drawn. It's the one who has already decided they've won.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir confirms the obvious at every turn, supports handing authority to Kalan, and implicitly endorses the idea that the real power lies not with the blade but with the one who has already decided victory is assured.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir considers A'lai the first real lead he's been offered since Kaelira laid out the problem.
source_quote: Now there was a compromised drow scholar who might represent the first real lead I'd been offered since Kaelira laid the problem out for me plainly.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir finds it uncomfortable to be the unknown variable in his own accounts.
source_quote: It is not comfortable to be the unknown variable in your own accounts.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir had not flagged the detail about what Alkrist burned at the feast.
source_quote: I hadn't flagged that one.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been maintaining a column since Kaelira told him someone powerful was paying to protect a man he couldn't understand.
source_quote: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been quiet because he is working through a problem until it is finished.
source_quote: Zalthir had been quiet for a while, which with Zalthir means he's working something through until it's finished.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir has been unable to name the entity behind the patron entry in his column for months.
source_quote: The patron entry had been blank for months. Every time I thought I was close to something, it receded.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir identified a temporal inconsistency in Sylvira’s appearances — a two-hour gap between sightings — and deduced that a polymorph spell alone cannot explain it, indicating the use of something more complex or multiple applications of magic.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a key observer who correctly identified the separation between the apothecary intrusion and the heart looting, and is aware of Glabbagool’s capabilities but chose stealth over brute force in the investigation.
source_quote: Zalthir had been in Alkrist's chambers. He'd asked Glabbagool whether Glabbagool could squeeze through the crack.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a quiet but perceptive member of the party who deduced that the Sylvira lookalike's appearances span a two-hour window, exceeding the duration of a standard polymorph spell. He suspects a more complex or repeated magical effect is at play. He is analytical, observant, and unafraid to challenge assumptions with physical evidence.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is dragonborn and recognizes the unspoken rapport between dragonborn that bypasses performative introductions; he intends to leverage this dynamic during the Alkrist interview.
source_quote: Dragonborn to Dragonborn? Intimate... yeah, I'm fine with that.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the speaker who confirms the presence of Kalan and the validity of the investigation's conclusion, stating 'He's here.'
source_quote: Zalthir confirmed the obvious. "He's here."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced as the speaker who initiated the investigation into Janussi's chambers and recognized the significance of the wrapping paper trail from the poisoned book.
source_quote: We had three problems and roughly the same number of people willing to go chase them. The third-story apartment in Janussi's chambers was still unvisited. We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there, and we hadn't gone back.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by Grygum as the individual who observed Glabbagool could eat through walls and noted that the safe had not been opened.
source_quote: Zalthir had been in Alkrist's chambers. He'd asked Glabbagool whether Glabbagool could squeeze through the crack. Glabbagool had made the distinction between a gap that admitted a gelatinous cube and a gap that did not.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is referenced by the narrator as the one who insisted on pinning timelines to the minute and interrogated Alkrist under truth spell.
source_quote: Zalthir's instinct would have been to pin the timing down to the minute... So I asked it in his place

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the group’s confirmatory voice, repeatedly validating emerging conclusions with minimal elaboration. His role is to reflect consensus rather than drive it, lending credibility to the group’s direction.
source_quote: That's where I was.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is the investigator who failed to flag the feast-burning detail about Alkrist, but later recognized Grygum’s insight as a critical missed observation.
source_quote: I hadn't flagged that one. I had been working through the zone-of-truth timing, the dragonborn opening, when Kalan would arrive. The feast detail had been sitting there, unflagged. Grygum had read it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted that Daz was the natural choice to interview Sylvira because he knew how to make someone talk and was drow.
source_quote: I noted this and did not say it aloud.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed that Fembris operated with monastic commitment to immediate tasks.
source_quote: There is something almost monastic about how Fembris operates: the total commitment to the immediate task, no friction between decision and movement.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed the dragonborn quality in Alkrist the way he notices the size of a room before noticing the people in it.
source_quote: I noticed this the way I notice the size of a room before I notice the people in it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes that the Sylvira lookalike's appearances create a two-hour gap that cannot be explained by a single polymorph spell.
source_quote: The Sylvira lookalike had been seen in the kitchens around one in the morning. She'd been seen coming down the stairs between two and three. That's a minimum two-hour gap. A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recalled Brother Heslin or Brother Varath teaching the art of the urgent errand.
source_quote: Brother Heslin, or possibly Brother Varath, I'm genuinely uncertain which, had devoted an entire season to teaching our cohort the art of the urgent errand, the clean dispatch.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes that A'lai needs discretion above all else.
source_quote: He needed, above all other things, discretion.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir refuses to punch the safe because they were trying to be sneaky, not destructive.
source_quote: If the goal was to be destructive, I could've just punched the safe. But we were trying to be sneaky.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembers that Brother Quellin or possibly Brother Harren said 'They all stabbed him.'
source_quote: Brother Quellin had said this. Or possibly Brother Harren, I was never certain of the attribution.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir silently approved of Grygum's decision to investigate the third-story apartment.
source_quote: I approved of it silently.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects A'lai constructed a narrative of administrative efficiency to justify Janussi’s death.
source_quote: The man who treats blackmail as a kind of career knows how to make his own history sound administrative.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir suspects something more than a simple polymorph — or repeated use of it — is involved in the Sylvira lookalike sightings.
source_quote: Something more is going on here.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir thought the apartment in Janussi's chambers held evidence about Kalan that didn't need an interview to yield.
source_quote: There was still evidence about Kalan we hadn't turned over. The kind of thing that didn't need an interview to yield.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir was working through the zone-of-truth timing and dragonborn opening when Kalan would arrive.
source_quote: I had been working through the zone-of-truth timing, the dragonborn opening, when Kalan would arrive.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: Alkrist possessed a copy of 1001 Tashalian Nights, which he had read and bookmarked at the 'Midnight Tears' passage; the book contained annotated instructions for the poison’s use; it was not the murder weapon but the source of the method; it was found in his chambers, indicating premeditation.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked... Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked.

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The book 1001 Tashalian Nights was bookmarked at the section describing midnight tears, annotated by Alkrist.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to. Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked

subject: 1001 Tashalian Nights
fact: The book 1001 Tashalian Nights was found bookmarked in Alkrist’s chambers, and the marked passage was known to contain dangerous or subversive material, suggesting Alkrist had studied it with intent.
source_quote: The book was on a shelf, bookmarked. I had read the section it was bookmarked to.

subject: abyssal plague
fact: An abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, was transmitted to Sylvira by her son, causing fever and physical deterioration, and serves as her alibi for post-12:30 AM.
source_quote: Her son... had infected her with an abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, which has consequences.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe is referenced by Grygum as the unopened container that remains a mystery and was later considered penetrable by Glabbagool.
source_quote: open threads: Alkrist's safe, unopened. ... I guess I could have eaten through the safe. It would have taken a while.

subject: book identity
fact: The book used to plan the poisoning was 1001 Tashalian Nights, bookmarked at 'Midnight Tears'.
source_quote: 1001— whatever it is, Nights? Tashalian Nights... bookmarked at the midnight tears part

subject: book value
fact: Thorin insists we get a book per suspect.
source_quote: I'm gonna insist that we get a book per suspect.

subject: Chalice
fact: The chalice was a hidden vessel with a secret purpose, likely used to conceal the transformation mechanism or the final trigger for Janussi’s death, known only to an unknown third party.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason.

subject: chalice
fact: The chalice was known to conceal something only someone with specific reason would look inside, and its knowledge was not possessed by Alkrist.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist

subject: cheese
fact: Cheese is referenced by Glabbagool as the lost food item he remembers with genuine longing.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese. Perhaps if we had some cheese.

subject: evidence collected
fact: We had a confession, a poisoned book reclaimed from Daral, Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper, and a note in Janussi's own hand found on the third floor.
source_quote: We had a confession, a poisoned book reclaimed from Daral, Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper, a note in Janussi's own hand found on the third floor.

subject: Fembris Lancer's notes
fact: Fembris Lancer's notes are referenced by Glabbagool as the non-nutritious material that was handed over and evaluated.
source_quote: He handed them over. Glabbagool examined them with professional detachment: the focused, slightly acidic attention he gives to anything he's evaluating for nutritional content. 'This is not nutritious.'

subject: Fembris's notes
fact: Fembris's notes contain his intellectual and spiritual reflections on the quadrangle issue, and are ultimately deemed non-nutritious by Glabbagool, symbolizing the futility of his scholarly effort.
source_quote: This is not nutritious.

subject: gift-wrapped book
fact: The gift-wrapped book was coated in midnight tears and carefully re-wrapped after Daral's present was poisoned.
source_quote: Daral's present, unwrapped and coated in midnight tears and carefully re-wrapped

subject: gift-wrapped book
fact: The gift-wrapped book was concealed with wrapping paper bearing a deliberate straight cut and two sets of tears — one intentional, one incidental — indicating it was prepared in advance by someone who planned for Janussi's death and the subsequent disposal of evidence.
source_quote: Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents, and tied the bow, and handed it to Janussi, or left it on a table, or had it carried by someone who had no idea what they were carrying.

subject: gift wrapping
fact: The wrapping paper for the deadly book had been discarded in the dining hall trash.
source_quote: a piece of paper, crumpled and retrieved from a trash bucket in the dining hall. Wrapping paper.

subject: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper
fact: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper is a recovered artifact, possibly containing hidden markings or evidence.
source_quote: Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper

subject: Grygum's reassembled wrapping paper
fact: Grygum reconstructed wrapping paper from the book’s packaging — its pattern and seal suggest tampering prior to delivery, providing forensic evidence of premeditation and access control breaches.

subject: honey
fact: Honey is denied by Sylvira as something she would never drink, and its mention was a trivial misrepresentation.
source_quote: Honey? I would *never* drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: lilac robes
fact: Sylvira wears lilac robes that fail to protect her from an internal cold, symbolizing her vulnerability despite her outward composure.
source_quote: the lilac robes she'd wrapped herself in accomplishing nothing against a cold she clearly felt in her bones.

subject: locket
fact: The locket is a personal item that cannot be stolen from a living person who holds it. Its presence on the victim implies the victim was already dead when it was taken. This creates an irreconcilable contradiction with the assumption that the locket was taken during the attack, forcing the conclusion that two separate actors were involved—or that the locket was planted post-mortem.

subject: locket
fact: The locket is referenced by Thorin as the object that cannot be stolen from a living person in possession of it.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it.

subject: magical book
fact: The magical book was used to frame a colleague by poisoning those who handled it. It was retrieved by Daral, who licked his fingers while handling it, thus ingesting the poison. The book is not merely a weapon—it is a trap designed to punish curiosity and meticulousness. Its mechanism mirrors the moral economy of the investigation: care leads to self-harm.

subject: Midnight tears
fact: Midnight tears is a deadly poison, applied to a book and later transferred to Janussi’s body, leaving traces on the margins of Tashalian Nights and on Alkrist’s hands.
source_quote: Midnight tears. Tidy, annotated, marked: the margins of a man who had been studying rather than reading.

subject: midnight tears vial
fact: The midnight tears vial had its label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration.
source_quote: The vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration

subject: midnight tears vial
fact: The vial of midnight tears was stolen from the Oak Tree Apothecary; its label was torn off and tied to the Dead Winter tree as decoration; the vial itself was discarded or destroyed after use; the substance is lethal when ingested and requires precise application.
source_quote: The vial's label torn off and tied to the back of the Dead Winter tree as decoration.

subject: note from Janussi
fact: The note from Janussi, found in the third-story apartment, contained a scholarly dismissal of Kalan Strongbranch's criminal investigation methodology as solipsism and revealed Janussi's contempt for the institutionalization of detective work.
source_quote: The opening line landed like a thrown stone. 'Oh boy, this starts out with some real academic insult.' ... Janussi had reviewed Kalan Strongbranch's proposal... found it to be solipsism... as though the investigation of crime were an indulgence, a hobby, a *conceit* Kalan was pursuing for his own entertainment.

subject: note in Janussi's hand
fact: A handwritten note found on the third floor contains Janussi’s final thoughts — possibly a list of targets or a confession — and is the only personal artifact directly tied to his awareness of the plot against him.

subject: note in Janussi's hand
fact: A note in Janussi's own hand was found on the third floor and contains direct evidence of his final thoughts or actions.
source_quote: a note in Janussi's own hand found on the third floor

subject: note in Janussi's own hand
fact: A handwritten note found on the third floor contains Janussi's final thoughts or instructions, potentially implicating others or revealing his awareness of the conspiracy. It is a key piece of documentary evidence.
source_quote: ...a note in Janussi's own hand found on the third floor.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book is referenced by Daral as the object that was retrieved from the apothecary and touched with a licked finger.
source_quote: Daral had taken it back, as men who give gifts sometimes do when the recipient fails to appear sufficiently grateful. In the process of reclaiming it, he had licked his finger, licked the book, then licked his finger again.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book is the primary frame in the murder, used to implicate a colleague and disappear evidence — a method deemed overly elaborate yet effective, and central to Elian’s proposed investigative thesis.
source_quote: Poisoned book, frames a colleague, and disappears the evidence. Too elaborate. Which is exactly why it worked.

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was a weapon used to kill or incapacitate Janussi, later reclaimed from Daral. It was central to the murder plot and remains a tangible piece of evidence linking suspects to the crime.
source_quote: We had a confession, a poisoned book reclaimed from Daral...

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was reclaimed from Daral and is a key piece of physical evidence in the investigation.
source_quote: a poisoned book reclaimed from Daral

subject: poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book, originally from Janussi’s research, was laced with a slow-acting toxin and delivered to him under false pretenses; it is now evidence of premeditated murder and a symbol of intellectual betrayal.

subject: poisoned book value
fact: The poisoned book was wrapped in paper that was taken to the third-story apartment.
source_quote: the wrapping paper from the poisoned book

subject: polymorph spell
fact: The polymorph spell has a known duration of one hour, which is insufficient to explain the two-hour gap between sightings of the Sylvira lookalike, indicating the use of something beyond standard magic.
source_quote: A polymorph spell lasts an hour.

subject: sapphire
fact: The sapphire is a magical item that reveals the location of a lost locket. It is useless if the locket is still in possession of a living person. Its presence in the case suggests the locket was taken from a corpse or hidden object, not a living victim. It is a tool of discovery, not theft, and its existence contradicts the assumption that the locket was stolen from the living.

subject: sapphire
fact: The sapphire is referenced by Thorin as the object required to locate a lost locket, and not useful for stealing one from a living person.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: sapphire and locket
fact: The sapphire and locket are linked artifacts in the investigation, with the locket being in the possession of a living person and the sapphire required to locate a lost locket — suggesting the two are mutually exclusive tools in the thief’s methodology.
source_quote: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.

subject: sapphire and locket value relation
fact: You can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it; you need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost.
source_quote: you can't steal a locket off someone who's alive and holding it. You need the sapphire to find a locket that's already lost

subject: Tashalian Nights
fact: Tashalian Nights was the book used to conceal the poison, specifically marked at the 'midnight tears' passage, annotated and bookmarked by Alkrist as a reference point for his plan.
source_quote: Tashalian Nights," he said. "Yes, yes, yes — that would, that would exactly—

subject: the poisoned book
fact: The poisoned book was the medium through which the poison was delivered to Janussi and later reclaimed by Daral, becoming the catalyst for his self-contamination.
source_quote: The book had delivered the poison to Janussi, and Daral had taken it back, as men who give gifts sometimes do when the recipient fails to appear sufficiently grateful.

subject: third-story apartment
fact: A third-story apartment with an open door in Janussi’s chambers was unvisited and contained his private notes; it was the location where the wrapping paper and damning critique of Kalan were discovered.
source_quote: There's something listed as a third-story apartment with an open door we haven't gone into. I'm gonna go look into that.

subject: Threefold Proof
fact: The Threefold Proof is Kalan Strongbranch's criminal investigation methodology, formally rejected by Janussi as solipsism, yet still used by Kalan as the operational foundation for the current investigation.
source_quote: Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime, the Threefold Proof, the methodologies, the framework we'd been handed as a legitimate investigation tool, had been blocked by the man who was now dead.

subject: Threefold Proof methodology
fact: The Threefold Proof is Kalan Strongbranch’s formalized framework for criminal investigation, now being used by the party to solve Janussi’s murder — despite having been rejected by the victim as solipsism.
source_quote: Kalan's entire proposal for dealing with crime... had been blocked by the man who was now dead.

subject: wrapping paper
fact: The crumpled wrapping paper, retrieved from the dining hall trash, bore a clean, ruled edge inconsistent with casual unwrapping, suggesting it was reused or deliberately altered to conceal its origin and purpose.
source_quote: A straight edge where there shouldn't be one. Someone had taken something sharp to this paper...

subject: wrapping paper
fact: The wrapping paper that had enclosed the poisoned book was brought to Janussi’s chambers and had not been retrieved as evidence; it was found on the third floor, linking the murder weapon to the location of Janussi’s critical notes.
source_quote: The paper that had wrapped the poisoned book had been brought here, and nobody had retrieved it. Evidence doesn't improve with age.

subject: wrapping paper from dining hall trash
fact: Crumpled wrapping paper, retrieved from the dining hall trash, was found to have two sets of tears: ragged from unwrapping and one clean, straight cut indicating deliberate re-sealing; it had been used to wrap the poisoned book; the paper was later restored by a Bahamut cantrip, revealing the tampering; it was discarded in the dining hall to avoid detection in Janussi’s rooms.
source_quote: A straight edge where there shouldn't be one... Someone had taken something sharp to this paper, and then wrapped it back around the contents.

subject: wrapping paper from poisoned book
fact: The wrapping paper that concealed the poisoned book was brought to Janussi’s third-floor chambers and has not been recovered; it may contain trace evidence, handwriting, or magical residue.
source_quote: We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there.

subject: wrapping paper from the poisoned book
fact: The wrapping paper from the poisoned book was transported to the third-story apartment in Janussi's chambers and remained uncollected, serving as the primary physical trail leading to the discovery of Janussi's note.
source_quote: We knew the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there, and we hadn't gone back. ... There was still the matter of the wrapping paper. The paper that had wrapped the poisoned book had been brought here, and nobody had retrieved it.

subject: wrapping paper reassembled by Grygum
fact: The carefully reassembled wrapping paper is a symbolic artifact — evidence of obsessive attention to detail, possibly containing hidden messages or serving as a metaphor for reconstructing truth from fragments.
source_quote: ...Grygum's carefully reassembled wrapping paper...

subject: wrapping paper value
fact: The wrapping paper from the poisoned book was taken to the third-story apartment as evidence.
source_quote: the wrapping paper from the poisoned book had been taken there

subject: zone of truth
fact: The zone of truth is a magical mechanism that worked without waste and was used to verify statements during the investigation.
source_quote: We had the zone of truth as a mechanism, which had worked without waste

subject: A'lai's knowledge
fact: A'lai possesses knowledge of the patron behind his protection, the nature of the funding, and possibly the identity of other drow agents in Candlekeep — this knowledge is the only currency worth collecting.

subject: Alkrist's burning
fact: Grygum sought to know whether Sylvira knew anything about Alkrist burning something at the feast; she responded with diplomatic silence, suggesting either non-witness status or irrelevance.
source_quote: She received it with the diplomatic silence of someone choosing not to comment on something they either hadn't witnessed or had already assessed as irrelevant.

subject: Alkrist's feast burning
fact: There is an unflagged item in the list regarding what Alkrist burned at the feast; Grygum recalled this detail and recommended asking about it, suggesting a potential link between ritual destruction and the investigation.
source_quote: When you talk to Alkrist, there's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast — you should ask about that.

subject: Alkrist's motive
fact: Alkrist resented Janussi for dismissing his germ warfare research and denying his leadership potential, but the full extent of his grievance remains unexplored.
source_quote: dismissed, told his germ warfare research was dangerous and should be stopped, told he showed no leadership potential.

subject: Alkrist's safe
fact: Alkrist's safe remains unopened and is a persistent unresolved thread, with multiple characters (Zalthir, Glabbagool, Grygum) recognizing that Glabbagool’s ability to consume matter could bypass it — though the method was never employed.
source_quote: open threads: Alkrist's safe, unopened.

subject: blackmail as a career
fact: The group has identified blackmail not as a crime of opportunity but as a sustained profession — potentially practiced by A'lai. This thread suggests a deeper, systemic corruption within Candlekeep’s hierarchy, where assassination is masked as administrative action.
source_quote: In these murder mysteries, you often find somebody who treats blackmail as a kind of career.

subject: blackmail as career
fact: The idea that blackmail is not a crime but a profession — practiced by drow, librarians, and hidden powers — is now a recognized pattern in the investigation, and may be the key to understanding the broader conspiracy.

subject: Bookwyrm's involvement
fact: Bookwyrm argued with Alkrist after learning of the poisoning and stormed off, but her subsequent actions and knowledge of the chalice remain unexplained.
source_quote: She went somewhere. He went home. Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: Brother Quellin's quote
fact: The phrase 'They all stabbed him' — attributed possibly to Brother Quellin or Brother Harren — frames Janussi’s death as the result of collective betrayal, not individual action.
source_quote: They all stabbed him, came the answer.

subject: collective betrayal
fact: Janussi’s death was not the act of one killer, but the culmination of multiple independent motives converging — a model of political assassination where the victim becomes the architect of his own demise.
source_quote: Janussi had spent his last day in a library full of people who had already decided, and he had offered each of them one more reason on his way through.

subject: column status
fact: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand had one entry.
source_quote: The column I had been maintaining since Kaelira told me bluntly that someone powerful was paying to protect a man she couldn't understand. That column had one entry

subject: connection between Alkrist and the book
fact: Alkrist possesses a copy of the 1001 Tashalian Nights with a dangerous passage bookmarked, but his knowledge of its contents and his relationship to the gift-wrapped book remain unconfirmed under truth spell.
source_quote: I had read the section it was bookmarked to. There was a class at the monastery... about what you find in someone's room telling you more than what they'd ever say with their face.

subject: continuity of the missing man
fact: A prior party member, similar to Daral in behavior, was previously sent away, creating a pattern of post-healing disappearance that Grygum recognizes as recurrent.
source_quote: Didn't we have somebody like that with our party anyhow? Did we already send him away? Oh, that's the same guy.

subject: counterfactual thesis
fact: A counterfactual thesis is proposed — that the murder techniques *would have* helped even if unsolved — challenging the assumption that academic value requires resolution, and introducing epistemological ambiguity into the investigation.
source_quote: Counterfactual, but I think that's a different thesis, so...

subject: frumpy old boar
fact: Sylvira’s cryptic reference to 'a frumpy old boar' during her emotional breakdown may hint at an unspoken rival or symbolic figure in her academic circle.
source_quote: Something about a frumpy old boar.

subject: honey sighting
fact: A witness claimed to have seen the murderer near the kitchen with honey; Sylvira vehemently denies ever consuming honey, calling the claim nonsense, and this detail undermines the credibility of the sighting.
source_quote: Honey? I would *never* drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: identity of Daz's patron
fact: The identity of the patron paying to protect a man unknown to Kaelira remains unresolved. This thread has persisted for months, with every lead receding — until A'lai, a compromised drow with Underdark connections, emerged as the first plausible conduit to the truth.
source_quote: The patron entry had been blank for months. Every time I thought I was close to something, it receded.

subject: identity of the gift-giver
fact: The gift-wrapped book was delivered in a manner that ensured Janussi would not suspect its danger, and the wrapping paper was discarded where no one would look — indicating the perpetrator never entered Janussi’s rooms and planned for the aftermath of his death.
source_quote: Someone had walked out of Janussi's rooms, or never entered them at all, carrying discarded wrapping paper they felt was safe to throw away in the dining hall, because who looks at trash?

subject: identity of the honey-drinker
fact: Someone was seen near the kitchen drinking honey; Sylvira vehemently denied ever consuming honey, expressing genuine outrage at the claim; the true identity of the honey-drinker remains unknown, and the detail may be a red herring or a clue to another suspect.
source_quote: Honey? I would *never* drink honey. What kind of nonsense is this?

subject: impersonation mystery
fact: Someone is magically impersonating Sylvira to commit crimes — the method, identity, and purpose of the impersonator remain unknown, and may be tied to the Menzoberranzan thread or Janussi’s enemies.
source_quote: Who is impersonating me.

subject: Kalan's motive
fact: Kalan’s professional humiliation by Janussi may be the root motive for the murder — his entire life’s work was dismissed, yet he continues to operate under that same framework, suggesting deep unresolved resentment.
source_quote: He built his whole methodology in the wreckage of the man who told him he was wrong.

subject: Menzoberranzan thread
fact: A Menzoberranzan thread was running under all of the events in the investigation.
source_quote: the Menzoberranzan thread running under all of this

subject: mind control claim
fact: Alkrist claims he was under mind control during his confession, a claim that was acknowledged but not verified, leaving the authenticity of his testimony in ambiguous territory.
source_quote: I am under mind control, and everything I have said is so true.

subject: missing party members
fact: The absence of four key party members during the colloquium went unremarked upon by Fembris Lancer, suggesting a prior separation or concealment that remains unexplained.
source_quote: Where are the four of you? Who were the rest of you? I didn't see you at the talk.

subject: monograph authorship
fact: A persistent thread in the narrative is the tension over scholarly credit — whether co-authorship, introductions, or prefaces constitute legitimate academic contribution — reflecting deeper institutional values at Candlekeep.
source_quote: Prefaces are decorative. Introductions frame the argument.

subject: murderer's identity
fact: Multiple suspects exist: Teles Ahvoste (motive, institutional hatred), Bookwyrm (obstruction), Kalan (rejected proposal), Kazryn (resentment), and Daral (motive but dismissed execution); Sylvira’s alibi is verifiable but her testimony is filtered through grief and illness.
source_quote: It was enough to work with.

subject: mysterious payer to Menzoberranzan
fact: An unknown entity is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional, and the identity of this payer is the focus of A'lai’s knowledge-based payment.

subject: patron entry status
fact: The patron entry had been blank for months.
source_quote: The patron entry had been blank for months.

subject: stature and falling
fact: Grygum reflects on the nature of scholarly stature, linking it to personal history — specifically Velkynvelve — where prestige is built on repeated failure and resilience rather than external recognition.
source_quote: Whatever stature looked like from the outside, it was built on a lot of falling first.

subject: Sylvira’s son’s role
fact: Sylvira’s son, born in the Abyss, infected her with an abyssal plague; she claims to have been with him after 12:30, providing an alibi; his presence and condition may be connected to the plague’s origin, but his motives, awareness of the murder, and possible involvement remain unknown.
source_quote: Her son, it emerged, had infected her with an abyssal plague, born in the Abyss, which has consequences.

subject: the burned object
fact: The object Alkrist burned at the feast may be a key piece of evidence — potentially Kalan’s rejected proposal, a personal token, or a magical artifact — and its destruction may be linked to the murder or the framing.
source_quote: There's something in the list about what Alkrist burned at the feast.

subject: The chalice's origin
fact: The identity of the person who knew about the chalice and its hidden purpose remains unknown.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: the cheese
fact: Glabbagool’s memory of cheese represents a persistent, emotionally resonant loss from the past, one that underscores his non-human but deeply felt inner life.
source_quote: I remember when there was cheese.

subject: the locked safe
fact: Alkrist’s locked safe remains unopened, and its contents are unknown. Though Glabbagool could have eaten through it, the party never considered his capability as a viable investigative tool. The safe symbolizes the failure to think outside conventional methods—and the cost of underestimating non-human agents.

subject: the missing truth spell caster
fact: Kalan Strongbranch’s absence creates a critical gap in the investigation, as he is the only known caster of the truth-seeking spell that previously anchored the case, and his location is now the focus of Fembris’s mission.
source_quote: Who can cast the truth spell? Yeah — Kalan Strongbranch.

subject: the monograph obsession
fact: The repeated attempts by Fembris and Elian to co-author a monograph reveal a deeper institutional truth: Candlekeep values documentation over resolution. The real mystery may not be the murder—but the system that rewards academic credit even when the truth remains hidden.

subject: the myth of the person
fact: The myth of the person is the false assumption that death strips away deception, bias, and performance—that the dead speak only truth. Elian and Grygum reject this, asserting that the dead retain their motivations, memories, and lies. Magic that summons the dead does not reveal truth—it reveals a new kind of adversary.

subject: the Sylvira anomaly
fact: A mystery persists regarding the Sylvira lookalike: her appearances violate known magical constraints, suggesting the use of an unknown or repeated magical effect, and remains unresolved despite the group’s growing understanding.
source_quote: Something more is going on here.

subject: the two-perpetrator theory
fact: The contradiction between the locket and the sapphire, the timing of the Sylvira appearances, and the separation of the poisoning from the looting all point to two perpetrators. One handled the poison and the apothecary intrusion; another handled the theft of the heart and locket. The investigation is not failing—it is revealing complexity.

subject: unknown orchestrator
fact: Someone else — not Alkrist, A'lai, or Bookwyrm — knew about the chalice’s hidden purpose and likely orchestrated the final transformation, suggesting a fourth or higher-level conspirator.
source_quote: Someone had known about the chalice: what it was for, what could be hidden inside it, why no one would think to look there without specific reason. That someone was not Alkrist.

subject: unknown patron
fact: An unidentified patron has been paying Menzoberranzan-level fees to protect A'lai for months — this is the central unresolved thread, and the only lead since Kaelira first raised the question.

subject: unpublished research
fact: Sylvira may possess unpublished research that could be the real motive behind the framing, though she has not yet disclosed it.
source_quote: Something she'd found and hadn't published yet.

subject: what to do with the evidence
fact: The central unresolved question is not who killed Janussi, but what should be done with the evidence — whether to expose, bury, or weaponize it — and this question now defines the future of the investigation.

subject: wisdom vs. intelligence
fact: The group distinguishes between intelligence — knowing what options exist — and wisdom — knowing which ones ensure survival. This thread underpins the entire investigation, framing Janussi’s death as a failure of wisdom and A'lai’s survival as an exercise in it.
source_quote: Intelligence tells you what the options are. Wisdom tells you which ones you survive.

subject: Zalthir's alternative proposal
fact: Zalthir is considering an alternative proposal where A'lai pays not in gold or books, but in information about the patron funding his survival.
source_quote: I had an alternative proposal forming. It was not finalized. But the terms were these: A'lai does not pay in gold, and does not pay in books. A'lai pays in what he knows. And what he knows about whoever is paying Menzoberranzan rates to keep a nobody drow evoker alive and functional: that is the only price I am interested in collecting.

subject: Zalthir's mission
fact: Zalthir has a mission in mind involving A'lai and the patron behind the unknown entity, but has not yet finalized the terms.
source_quote: I have a mission in mind.

subject: after the naming
fact: The official trial and judgment of Alkrist will occur after the naming ceremony, when the new head of the Avowed assumes power — delaying accountability and ensuring Bookwyrm’s influence endures.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: elapsed time
fact: An hour passes between two events in the session.
source_quote: An hour later

subject: evening in Deneir's Sanctum
fact: The events in Deneir's Sanctum occur during the evening hours, following the opening of the safe; the group waits until later this evening before being escorted to their chambers.

subject: naming ceremony
fact: The formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Candlekeep Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, marking the critical turning point in the political maneuvering around Bookwyrm’s fate.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occur during the ongoing session following the restoration of Daral and preceding the ambush — a single narrative unit with no external calendar reference.
source_quote: Combat?" Zalthir said. Yes. Combat.

subject: session date
fact: The events described occurred during a single session of roleplay, culminating in the strategic planning phase and the tense confrontation with Bookwyrm — no calendar date is given, but temporal continuity is maintained.
source_quote: I wrote it down either way.

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred during the continuation of a campaign session following the healing of Daral and the discovery of the helmed horrors’ ambush.
source_quote: [Continuing — Speaker: Grygum, Scene: Waiting in Deneir's Sanctum]

subject: Session date
fact: The events occurred during the ongoing session, following the ambush of the helmed horrors and preceding any further investigation into the key’s origin.
source_quote: Quiet, then. Glass on the floor, dust settling...

subject: Session Date
fact: The events occurred on the day of the naming ceremony, immediately preceding the formal transition of leadership in the Avowed.
source_quote: That will be done after the naming, by the new head of the Avowed.

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493 DR.
source_quote: On the 5th day of the 2nd Tenday of Taraskh 1493

subject: session date
fact: The session occurs on the day of the ambush in Deneir's Sanctum.
source_quote: ## Thorin — Ambush of the Helmed Horrors

subject: tomorrow
fact: The naming ceremony for the new head of the Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, marking the next critical turning point in the political maneuvering surrounding Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Tomorrow there will be a naming ceremony.

subject: Academic principle vs justice
fact: The group debated whether academic rigor (requiring three evidentiary types) outweighs practical justice (concluding guilt from confession and context).
source_quote: What matters more to an academic? Putting the murderer in jail, or being true to their academic principles and their research proposal?

subject: accusation of accomplices
fact: The group publicly acknowledged the existence of accomplices without naming Bookwyrm.
source_quote: Yeah — we know there are accomplices

subject: A'lai's political position
fact: A'lai will not be named the new head of Candlekeep — suspicion extends to him as well.
source_quote: A'lai won't be named either.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist confessed to killing Janussi under Kalan's spell, and the confession was deemed insufficient by academic standards despite being legally valid.
source_quote: Alkrist had confessed. Kalan Strongbranch hadn't yet come back into the room, and we knew there was a thread running from all this back to A'lai.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist publicly confessed to murdering Janussi under magical compulsion, ending the investigation and shifting responsibility to Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: Alkrist's confession
fact: Alkrist's confession under the Zone of Truth spell provided the first concrete breakthrough in the case, but lacked corroborating evidence to identify the mastermind behind the murder.
source_quote: Alkrist had said it out loud, in the room, with Kalan's spell still holding him honest — he'd killed Janussi.

subject: ambush of the helmed horrors
fact: An unexpected ambush occurred in Deneir's Sanctum, where three helmed horrors attacked the party, targeting Daz repeatedly, forcing the group to adapt tactics after realizing the creatures lack minds and respond only to force.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors breached Deneir's Sanctum through windows, targeting Daz and later Grygum upon key transfer, ultimately destroyed by coordinated party efforts after revealing their mechanical, non-sentient nature.
source_quote: Glass and wood came in at the same time, from three directions, and for a breath none of us had moved.

subject: Ambush of the Helmed Horrors
fact: Three helmed horrors breached the chamber through the windows, targeting the key in Daz’s pocket, and were systematically destroyed after shifting focus when the key changed hands.
source_quote: Three suits of murderous plate had come through the windows to die for it.

subject: Bookwyrm's potential dismissal
fact: Bookwyrm may be dismissed from her position due to suspicion, with the new head of Candlekeep likely to demand a Zone of Truth as her first act.
source_quote: The new head may give Bookwyrm one of two choices: continue as a member of the Avowed, or submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Bookwyrm's relief
fact: Bookwyrm was relieved, not heartbroken, upon learning of Alkrist's confession.
source_quote: Alkrist. I could never have imagined it.

subject: Candlekeep naming ceremony
fact: A formal naming ceremony for the next head of the Avowed is scheduled for tomorrow, and Kalan believes the suspicion surrounding Bookwyrm will ensure she is not chosen — making her vulnerable to post-ceremony scrutiny and potential removal.
source_quote: Tomorrow morning's naming ceremony clearly will not name her.

subject: combat outcome
fact: The helmed horrors were destroyed through coordinated attacks using fire, acid, brute force, and tactical positioning, leaving only rusted wreckage.
source_quote: The suit came apart where it stood, and the last of them folded down into piles of rust and loose plate, like they'd never been anything but junk somebody stacked up.

subject: Dawnbringer’s Lesser Restoration
fact: Dawnbringer performed a lesser restoration on Daral, curing his illness and triggering his epiphany about magical swords — an event that awakened the sword’s sentience and began a new dynamic between scholar and weapon.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it.

subject: Dawnbringer's psychic communication
fact: Dawnbringer communicated telepathically with the narrator, expressing a need for further therapy sessions after a productive first session, and the narrator acknowledged her as 'she' despite uncertainty.
source_quote: *I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.*

subject: Dawnbringer's Restoration of Daral
fact: Dawnbringer is used to restore Daral from sickness, causing him to straighten, breathe, and become ecstatic, which triggers his sudden scholarly obsession with the sword's sentience and beauty.
source_quote: The blade lit, poured into Daral, and took the sickness with it. He straightened. He breathed. In the space of a heartbeat he was a well man, and he was ecstatic. ... 'I shall do all kinds of new research on magical swords,' he announced, 'with the sentience and the beauty of Dawnbringer. I intend to make it an area of active research.'

subject: Dawnbringer's telepathic communication
fact: Dawnbringer communicates telepathically — her voice clicks inside the speaker’s skull like a palm slapping stone.
source_quote: And then a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone, whatever that was supposed to mean.

subject: Dawnbringer's telepathy
fact: Dawnbringer demonstrated the ability to communicate telepathically with the narrator, producing a distinct mental sound like a palm slapping stone, confirming her non-human nature.
source_quote: a click inside my skull, a sound like a palm slapping stone, whatever that was supposed to mean.

subject: Dawnbringer's therapy request
fact: Dawnbringer requested therapy — she said, 'I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive.'
source_quote: She spoke up in my head. *I'm not leaving here without the therapy. That first session was actually very productive. I really feel we need to—*

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the woman was delighted to have them wrapped up and out of everything.
source_quote: Daz found the other half, the half I only saw land on his face: she was delighted to have us wrapped up and out of everything, no more heads poking anywhere.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the woman was not sad but relieved.
source_quote: Daz caught it too — I saw him go quiet and still, the way he does when he's found the seam in a thing. She was not sad. She was relieved.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to touch the cup of tea.
source_quote: Daz did not touch the cup in front of him.

subject: Daz's contingency plan
fact: Daz's contingency plan is to 'start hacking and slashing' if things go sideways — a comfort, not a strategy.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Daz's floor strategy
fact: Daz provides a floor — hacking and slashing — as a fallback when all strategy fails.
source_quote: If things go sideways, we can always start hacking and slashing.

subject: Fembris Lancer's expected election
fact: Fembris Lancer is expected to be elected the new Avowed, replacing Bookwyrm due to suspicion.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer will probably get elected the new avowed.

subject: Fembris's punishment
fact: Fembris Lancer was assigned to keep the adventurers company as his penance.
source_quote: Fembris Lancer was already in there, serving out his own punishment by keeping us company.

subject: food taster protocol
fact: The group established an informal food taster protocol using Fembris Lancer, with Daz's '118' signaling his selection; he ate without harm, reinforcing the group's survivalist pragmatism.

subject: Glabbagool's satisfaction
fact: Glabbagool was pleased with the stolen potion of flying and deemed it a good skill.
source_quote: I like the flying skill. That was a good skill.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum handed the key back to Daz after it had been passed to him.
source_quote: When Grygum handed the key to Daz — who saw it?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum kept his feet steady as the last helmed horror reached for him, refusing to be moved.
source_quote: Grygum kept his feet like the floor was the one thing he wasn't giving up.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum lifted the cup and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down his throat.
source_quote: I lifted the cup, tilted it to my mouth, and let the tea run down into Glabbagool instead of down my throat.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum marked in the margin that they had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment.
source_quote: I only took notes and marked, in the margin, that we had come all this way to convict a woman not of murder but of embarrassment

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Daral had stopped bragging and was complimenting the party up and down.
source_quote: He'd stopped bragging. That was new. He was complimenting the party up and down, which for Daral was a kind of surrender.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed Fembris Lancer had no reservations about the food.
source_quote: Fembris, on the other hand, had no such reservations — come, come, come, already reaching, all appetite and no suspicion.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed that the helmed horrors went for Daz first, then for him when the key changed hands.
source_quote: The suits had gone straight for Daz, then straight for Grygum the second the key changed hands.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the room stopped looking at the safe and started looking at each other after finding the red herring coin.
source_quote: The whole room understood that at once, and at once stopped looking at the safe and started looking at each other.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the woman said 'beloved by all'.
source_quote: Did she actually say 'beloved by all'? Of course she did. Beloved by all.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum noticed the woman was sincerely afraid something would happen to them.
source_quote: I looked at her while she said it and found, underneath, that she meant the worry. It was real — she was sincerely afraid something would happen to us.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum realized the woman did not have the sapphire when the spell found nothing.
source_quote: I reached out with the spell and found nothing where the sapphire should have been. Bookwyrm did not have it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum stepped up and unleashed a burst of clean light that caught two helmed horrors at once.
source_quote: Grygum stepped up and let go a burst of clean light that caught two of them at once, both flinching under it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum understood that Daz's number '118' meant Fembris had been promoted as taster.
source_quote: Daz offered, which meant nothing to Fembris and everything to us

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's Glabbagool arm swiped the potion of flying off the table.
source_quote: While she was talking, I had my Glabbagool arm swipe the potion of flying off the table.

subject: House arrest avoidance
fact: The adventurers were not under house arrest, but were escorted to Deneir's Sanctum for protection.
source_quote: No, no, no. You currently hold the most important evidence... I'm simply doing this to protect you.

subject: Infamous definition clarification
fact: The term 'infamous' was questioned and confirmed to mean 'extra famous' — a bad joke that earned a half-groan.
source_quote: Infamous," I said. "You know that's supposed to mean extra famous.

subject: Janussi’s murder investigation
fact: The investigation into Janussi’s murder has reached a turning point: Alkrist has confessed under magical compulsion, the heart was moved to a statue’s chalice, and Bookwyrm is the prime suspect for concealment — but no physical evidence directly ties her to the crime, forcing the group to rely on strategy over proof.
source_quote: You have a confession, a heart, and a cleaver.

subject: Kalan reinstated
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was reinstated as head of the Avowed after the investigation.
source_quote: Would you be so willing as to take your position once more?

subject: Kalan's firing
fact: Kalan Strongbranch was dismissed from his position prior to solving Janussi’s murder, making the resolution of the case both a redemption and an ironic twist.
source_quote: Kalan had gotten fired. That's the terrain — a man told he was done, standing next to a case he couldn't crack, that we cracked for him.

subject: Kalan's moral compromise
fact: Kalan plans to give Bookwyrm a chance to decline the Zone of Truth — knowing refusal implies guilt, making her politically untenable.
source_quote: We will give her the opportunity to decline. Her declining will further weaken her support among the other Avowed.

subject: Kalan's offer to give full report to Bookwyrm
fact: Kalan offered to give Bookwyrm a full report of the evidence against her, to pressure her into declining the position — thus implying guilt without direct accusation.
source_quote: I will give it to Bookwyrm herself.

subject: Kalan's patient strategy
fact: Kalan advocates patience — letting suspicion and the naming ceremony do the work instead of direct confrontation.
source_quote: Sometimes the clever play is to be patient.

subject: Kalan's refusal to sneak
fact: Kalan refused to cast the Zone of Truth spell covertly again, insisting on a public, bold demand for submission — a shift motivated by fear of future consequences rather than principle.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan's shift from stealth to open confrontation
fact: Kalan changed from covert casting of Zone of Truth to demanding open submission — motivated by fear of future repercussions.
source_quote: I will not sneak this time. We will walk in, and we will boldly demand that she submit to a Zone of Truth.

subject: Kalan's shift to patient strategy
